# Mirror's Edge Catalyst: research notes for the Cinematic Tools

The research notes written while building the Cinematic Tools for Mirror's Edge Catalyst in October and November 2026, in one file. Each set of notes is under its own heading, oldest first, so a later one can correct an earlier one. Test logs and working bookkeeping are left out.

- Addresses are in the game's image (base `0x140000000`) of its current PC build (PE timestamp `0x5762E3B7`, 2016-06-16; the one installed in late 2026).
- "Offline" means read from the game's files or its decrypted image; "live" or "in game" means read from or seen in the running game, read-only.

# 1. CT_MirrorsEdge.dll: reverse notes for porting to the CinematicTools template

Source: static disassembly of `CT_MirrorsEdge.dll` (build 2018-02-10, image base `0x180000000`).
Target: `Cinematic Tools/` template in https://github.com/Hattiwatti/CinematicTools.

> **Status:** everything below comes from reading the code.
> Items marked *(unverified)* are interpretations, not facts read straight from the code.
> Section 6 is implemented in `CT_MirrorsEdge/` (see `README.md` next to this file).

---

### 1. Signatures

The DLL scans `MirrorsEdgeCatalyst.exe` (falls back to `MirrorsEdgeCatalystTrial.exe`).
The scanner has the same semantics as the template's `util::offsets::Scan()`:

* **ref**: the pattern contains `[ ?? ?? ?? ?? ]`, and the result is the rel32 target (`match + refOff + 4 + rel32`).
* **abs**: no brackets, and the result is the address of the first matched byte.

No signature uses an add-offset, so the template's `AddOffset` is always `0`.

| Name | Pattern | Type | Hardcoded fallback (abs) | RVA for template |

| `OFFSET_DXRENDERER` | `48 8B 0D [ ?? ?? ?? ?? ] 48 8B 53 10 43 8D 04 76` | ref | `0x142563300` | `0x2563300` |
| `OFFSET_GAMERENDERER` | `48 8B 0D [ ?? ?? ?? ?? ] 48 8B 01 31 D2 FF 50 60` | ref | `0x142563A10` | `0x2563A10` |

Notes:

* MEC's hardcoded table holds **absolute** addresses that assume the exe loads at `0x140000000`. The template's `m_HardcodedOffsets` expects **module-relative** values, which is why the last column exists. The fallbacks only match the exact exe build the tool targeted, so prefer the scanned results.
* `OFFSET_CAMERAMANAGER` and `OFFSET_GAMERENDERER` fall back to the **same** address. "CameraManager" here is really the GameRenderer singleton, seen through a different code site.
* Most "ref" results point at a **static pointer**: callers do `*(T**)GetOffset(...)`. The hook targets (`CAMERAUPDATE`, `VISUALENVUPDATE`) are function addresses. `3PTOGGLE` resolves to a vtable whose slot 0 gets called.
* The DLL also writes the scanned results to `Offsets.txt` in `("NAME", 0x...)` form. If the old tool still injects, that file gives you the live addresses for your exe.

### 2. Camera hook (the important one)

The DLL detour is `sub_180008140`, and the trampoline lives at DLL global `+0x2B890`. It does this:

```cpp
__int64 hCameraUpdate(RenderView* rv /*rcx*/)
{
  __int64 r = oCameraUpdate(rv);              // call the game first
  if (g_freeCamEnabled)
  {
    GameRenderer* gr = *(GameRenderer**)GetOffset("OFFSET_CAMERAMANAGER");
    if (rv == *(RenderView**)((char*)gr + 0x58))
    {
      memcpy((char*)rv + 0x00, &g_camMatrix, 64);   // LinearTransform
      memcpy((char*)rv + 0x40, &g_camMatrix, 64);   // LinearTransform (same matrix written twice)
    }
  }
  return r;
}
```

* The game calls this once per rendered frame on its own thread. That makes it the right place to apply (or evaluate) a keyframe track.
* The detour only touches `rcx` before calling the original, so `rdx/r8/r9/xmm0-3` pass through untouched. The real function may take more arguments than one *(unverified)*, so declare the C++ detour with 4 integer args and forward all of them.
* Matrix layout: 4 rows of `float4` = **right, up, forward, translation(w=1)**. This is the same layout `XMMatrixRotationQuaternion` + `r[3] = position` produces, so the template's `Camera::Transform` drops straight in.
* `rv + 0x70` (the translation row of the `+0x40` matrix) is the current camera world position. The DLL reads it for `lockToPlayer 0`.

### 3. Game structure offsets

```
GameRenderer*        gr  = *(void**)OFFSET_GAMERENDERER        (== OFFSET_CAMERAMANAGER)
  gr  + 0x58  -> RenderView*  rv
  rv  + 0x00  float4x4  camera transform  (overwritten)
  rv  + 0x40  float4x4  camera transform  (overwritten); +0x70 = position xyz

GameRenderSettings*  grs = *(void**)OFFSET_GAMERENDERSETTINGS
  grs + 0x14  float  resolutionScale
  grs + 0x54  float  ForceFov (degrees; -1 = no override, per the readme)

GameTimeSettings*    gts = *(void**)OFFSET_GAMETIMESETTINGS
  gts + 0x48  float  timeScale (0 = frozen, 1 = normal)   <- DELETE hotkey toggles 0 / 1.0

WorldRenderSettings* wrs = *(void**)OFFSET_WORLDRENDERSETTINGS
  wrs + 0x48  int    shadowMapResolution
  wrs + 0xB0  int    worldViewMode

ClientGameContext*   cgc = *(void**)OFFSET_CLIENTGAMECONTEXT
  cgc + 0x68 -> +0x568 -> +0x14A0   local player controllable; non-null once spawned
      vtable + 0xC0  GetTransform(LinearTransform* out)   (used for lockToPlayer)
  cgc + 0x78 -> A;  A + 0xE0 -> B;  B + 0xD8 -> P (pointer pair)
      P[0] + 0x40/0x44/0x48  float  player position   (copied to the free cam on enable)
      P[0] + 0x150           ptr    set to 0 while free cam is on, restored from P[1] on disable

Main*                main = *(void**)OFFSET_MAIN
  main + 0x50 -> +0x2E0  int  game state; camera thread skips work when it's 0xF or 0x10 (likely loading/menu, unverified)

DxRenderer*          dx  = *(void**)OFFSET_DXRENDERER
  dx + 0x7E0 -> +0x5C   byte  window active/focused (input only polled when non-zero)

InputSystem*         sys = *(void**)OFFSET_SYSTEM
  vtable + 0x08  int GetDeviceCount()
  sys + 0x40     Device*[]   ; Device vtable + 0x18 = const char* GetName() -> "Keyboard" / "Mouse" / "Gamepad"
  Gamepad: [dev + 0x28] + 0x10, 0xE0 bytes = pad state (the controller hook zeroes it to block the pad)

3PTOGGLE: obj = (*(fn*)OFFSET_3PTOGGLE)();  obj + 0x28 = 0xF2 on enable, 0x00ED00ED on disable
          (probably switches Faith to the 3rd-person body so she's visible from the free cam, unverified)
```

### 4. Other hooks

| Hook | Detour | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `OFFSET_VISUALENVUPDATE` | `sub_180008210` | `int f(void*, void*)`; applies the visual overrides from shared memory before and after calling the original. |
| `OFFSET_CONTROLLERINPUT` | `0x180008270` | If *disableGamepadInput* is on, zero the gamepad state buffer (see above), then jump to the original. |
| `OFFSET_ENTRYINPUT` | `0x180008250` | If *disableAllInput* is on, `return 0`, otherwise jump to the original. This is how player input is blocked. |
| `OFFSET_UPDATELIGHT` | (called, not hooked) | Used by the LightManager pipe commands. |
| `OFFSET_DOFFIX` | byte patch | "Sprite DoF" patch; not needed for the camera. |

### 5. How the old free cam works (for reference)

* A separate thread (`sub_18000d3a0`) computes `dt` with `steady_clock` and runs `Sleep(1)` in a loop. It does **not** run on the game frame, which is why playback driven from that thread would stutter.
* Rotation is stored as **Euler doubles** (pitch, yaw, roll in radians) and built with `XMMatrixRotationRollPitchYaw`. Rotation input is smoothed with a 50-sample moving average.
* Position: `pos += (right*inX + up*inY + forward*inZ) * dt * MoveSpeed`. W/S give `inZ` = −1/+1, so the view direction is −forward (row 2).
* HOME toggles the byte at `UISettings + 0x48` (HUD), END toggles *disableAllInput*.
* Hotkeys come from `GetAsyncKeyState`: `INSERT (0x2D)` toggles the camera, `DELETE (0x2E)` toggles time freeze.
* There is **no FOV in the DLL's camera state**. The GUI sends `camera fov <deg>` over the pipe and the DLL writes it to `GameRenderSettings + 0x54`.

DLL globals (RVA from the DLL base), useful only if you want to poke the old tool externally:

| RVA | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x2E710` | byte | camera enabled |
| `+0x2E711` | byte | time frozen |
| `+0x2E712` | byte | lock to player |
| `+0x2E713` / `+0x2E714` | byte | gamepad / keyboard drives camera |
| `+0x2E715` / `+0x2E716` | byte | disableAllInput / disableGamepadInput |
| `+0x2E720` | double[3] | position |
| `+0x2E738` | double[3] | pitch, yaw, roll (rad) |
| `+0x2E750` | float[3] | MoveSpeed, RotationSpeed, RollSpeed |
| `+0x2E7A0` | float[16] | output matrix copied by the hook |
| `+0x2E7E8` | double | dt |
| `+0x2E7F8` | double[3] | move input right / up / forward |

Pipe protocol, GUI to DLL (`\\.\Pipe\MECMessageSender` / `MECMessageReceiver`), space separated:
`camera enable|disable|movementSpeed v|rotationSpeed v|rollSpeed v|keyboard 0/1|controller 0/1|timeFreeze 0/1|lockToPlayer 0/1|disableGamepadInput 0/1|disableAllInput 0/1|fov v`,
`misc worldViewMode v|gameTimeScale v|shadowMapResolution v|resolutionScale v|fixLOD 0/1`,
`visuals reset|getData`, `LightManager CreateSphereLight|CreateSpotLight|RemoveLight|MoveToCamera|Color|...`.
Shared memory `PamplonaSharedMemory` carries only the camera speeds and the visual overrides, not the camera position.

Set `g_gameHandle` from `GetModuleHandleA("MirrorsEdgeCatalyst.exe")`, falling back to `"MirrorsEdgeCatalystTrial.exe"`.

#### 6.2 `Util/Hooks.cpp`

```cpp
typedef __int64(__fastcall* tCameraUpdate)(__int64, __int64, __int64, __int64);
typedef __int64(__fastcall* tEntryInput)(__int64, __int64, __int64, __int64);

tCameraUpdate oCameraUpdate = nullptr;
__int64 __fastcall hCameraUpdate(__int64 pRenderView, __int64 a2, __int64 a3, __int64 a4)
{
  __int64 result = oCameraUpdate(pRenderView, a2, a3, a4);

  CameraManager* pCameraManager = g_mainHandle->GetCameraManager();
  if (!g_shutdown && pCameraManager->IsCameraEnabled())
  {
    __int64 pGameRenderer = *(__int64*)util::offsets::GetOffset("OFFSET_GAMERENDERER");
    if (pGameRenderer && pRenderView == *(__int64*)(pGameRenderer + 0x58))
    {
      DirectX::XMFLOAT4X4 const& transform = pCameraManager->GetTransform();
      memcpy((void*)(pRenderView + 0x00), &transform, sizeof(transform));
      memcpy((void*)(pRenderView + 0x40), &transform, sizeof(transform));
    }
  }
  return result;
}

tEntryInput oEntryInput = nullptr;
__int64 __fastcall hEntryInput(__int64 a1, __int64 a2, __int64 a3, __int64 a4)
{
  if (g_mainHandle->GetCameraManager()->IsKbmDisabled())
    return 0;
  return oEntryInput(a1, a2, a3, a4);
}

// in util::hooks::Init()
CreateHook("CameraUpdate", util::offsets::GetOffset("OFFSET_CAMERAUPDATE"), hCameraUpdate, &oCameraUpdate);
CreateHook("EntryInput",   util::offsets::GetOffset("OFFSET_ENTRYINPUT"),   hEntryInput,   &oEntryInput);
```

`GetTransform()` is a one-line accessor you add to `CameraManager` that returns `m_Camera.Transform`.

#### 6.3 `Camera/CameraManager.cpp`

* **ToggleCamera / ResetCamera:** seed the camera from the game's current view instead of the player entity:

  ```cpp
  __int64 pGameRenderer = *(__int64*)util::offsets::GetOffset("OFFSET_GAMERENDERER");
  XMFLOAT4X4* pView = (XMFLOAT4X4*)(*(__int64*)(pGameRenderer + 0x58) + 0x40);
  m_Camera.Position = XMFLOAT3(pView->_41, pView->_42, pView->_43);
  XMStoreFloat4(&m_Camera.Rotation, XMQuaternionRotationMatrix(XMLoadFloat4x4(pView)));
  ```

  If Faith's body is missing or the game camera fights you, mirror `sub_1800034c0`: call the `3PTOGGLE` function, set `+0x28` to `0xF2`, and null `P[0]+0x150`, restoring both on disable.
* **FOV:** while enabled, write `m_Camera.FieldOfView` to `GameRenderSettings + 0x54` every update. Write `-1.0f` when disabling. MEC starts at 60°, the template defaults to 50.
* **Axes:** *(corrected after reading the old tool's key handling, `sub_180003190`)* W subtracts 1 from the Z input, D adds 1 to X and Space adds 1 to Y. So the camera looks down **−row 2**, with row 0 = right and row 1 = up. The template's `dZ = Backward − Forward`, `dPitch = PitchUp − PitchDown` and `dYaw = YawLeft − YawRight` already match that, so no sign changes are needed.
* **Time freeze:** `GameTimeSettings + 0x48` = `0.0f` / `1.0f`.

#### 6.4 Keyframes (TrackPlayer)

The template's `TrackPlayer` already does Catmull-Rom interpolation on position, rotation (quaternion) and FOV, and `CameraManager::UpdateCamera` already calls `PlayForward(dt)`. Once 6.1–6.3 are in, add three hotkey actions: *add node*, *delete node*, *play/stop*. Watch out for these template bugs:

* `m_SelectedTrack` is never initialised in the `TrackPlayer` constructor. Set it to `0`.
* `if (m_CurrentNode - 1 >= 0)` is always true because the value is `unsigned`, so playing backwards past node 0 underflows. Use `if (m_CurrentNode > 0)`.
* `DrawNodes()` dereferences a null `PrimitiveBatch`. Don't call it (or finish it) until the overlay exists.
* Node timestamps are hardcoded to `previous + 1.0s`. Expose them, or use the "Time multiplier" field for overall speed.
* Before storing a new node, flip its quaternion if `dot(prev, new) < 0`. Otherwise Catmull-Rom on quaternions can spin the long way round.
* **Smoothness:** the template updates the camera on its own loop, like the old MEC thread. For recording, evaluate the track inside `hCameraUpdate` (once per game frame, ideally with a fixed dt such as 1/60 when frame-dumping) so playback is frame-locked.

#### 6.5 What's still unknown

* **ImGui overlay:** the MEC DLL never touches D3D11, so it gives no swapchain offset. Either grab the `Present` vtable from a dummy device/swapchain created at init (the standard trick, no game offset needed), or find the swapchain under `DxRenderer + 0x7E0` (Screen) at runtime. Until then, drive everything with hotkeys.
* The extra arguments of the camera-update function, the meaning of the `+0x00` vs `+0x40` matrices, the `3PTOGGLE` mode values, and the game-state values `0xF`/`0x10` are inferred, not confirmed.
* The hardcoded fallbacks only match the exe build the 2018 tool targeted. The signatures are what matter.

---

### 7. Visual environment overrides (findings after the first port)

The old GUI (`MEC Cinematic Tools.exe`, .NET) and the DLL share a 4 KB file mapping
(`PamplonaSharedMemory`). Its layout comes from the GUI's `MappedMemory` IL (view accessors) and from
each component class's `Write` method (per-field offsets):

| Shared memory | Contents | Game state offset |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x0` | 3 bools: CameraEnabled, TimeFrozen, VisualsReady | |
| `+0x3` | 12 override bools: outdoor, enlighten, tonemap, colorcorrection, sky, fog, wind, dynamicao, dof, vignette, filmgrain, characterlighting | |
| `+0x10` | OutdoorLight | `+0x000` |
| `+0x1E0` | Tonemap | `+0x1D0` |
| `+0x340` | ColorCorrection | `+0x330` |
| `+0xA60` | DoF (0x60 bytes), then DofMethod at `+0xAC0` | `+0xA50` |
| `+0xAD0` | Vignette | `+0xAC0` |
| `+0xB10` | FilmGrain | `+0xB00` |
| `+0xF58` | Camera speeds | |

The game state is `[[[[*OFFSET_MAIN + 0x50] + 0x90] + 0x1C0] + 0x30] + 0x85470`. The DLL's
VisualEnvironment hook (`OFFSET_VISUALENVUPDATE`, detour `sub_180008210`) copies each enabled
component from shared memory into that state, before and after the game's update. DofMethod goes to
`[manager + 0x138] + 0x154` (int) and `+0x247` (bool, method == 1). The per-field offsets are in
`CT_MirrorsEdge/Visuals/VisualsManager.cpp`. They were checked against a running game: color
correction reads 1 / 1 / 1.1, sun color is near white, vignette opacity is 0.15, film grain has its
texture pointer at `+0x20`.

*Sprite DoF fix* (`OFFSET_DOFFIX`): the original patched 13 bytes with a jump to a stub that always
continues at `+0x7E`, skipping the game's "DoF settings unchanged" checks. The port writes
`EB 7C` (`jmp +0x7E`) instead.

### 8. Light manager

The original builds the game's light entities in its own memory (`sub_18000a8e0` sphere,
`sub_18000abc0` spot) and calls `OFFSET_UPDATELIGHT(entity)` after every change:

* Entity (0x250 sphere / 0x270 spot): vtable `base+0x1BFF178` (sphere) or `base+0x1BFF240` (spot),
  `+0x18 = 0x121E`, `+0x28 = light data`, `+0x40` transform, `+0x80 = 0xFFFF`, `+0xA0 = 0x0101`,
  `+0xA4 = 1`, `+0xA8 = 1.0`, `+0xB0 = base+0x1BFF168`, a table of pointers into the data at
  `+0xC0 … +0x248`, `+0x206 = 0x3F80`, `+0x20C = 3`.
* Light data (0x110): vtable `base+0x1BFA8F8` (sphere) or `base+0x1BFA930` (spot), `+0x20`
  transform, Color `+0x70`, EnlightenColor `+0x80`, ParticleColor `+0x90`, Intensity `+0xA8`,
  AttenuationRadius `+0xAC`, AttenuationOffset `+0xB0`, ShadowDimmer `+0xCC`, Dimmer `+0xD0`,
  Diffuse `+0xE1`, Specular `+0xE2`, CastShadows `+0xE3`, Radiosity `+0xE5`, and for spots DiscRadius
  `+0xF0`, InnerAngle `+0xF4`, OuterAngle `+0xF8`.
* Remove: clear entity `+0xA0 … +0xA3`, then update once more.
* The vtables are hardcoded with no signatures, so the port only enables the light manager when the
  PE timestamp is `0x5762E3B7` and the vtables point into the exe.

### 9. Other findings from running the port

* **DRM:** the Steam / EA app exe is wrapped by EA's OOA DRM (`.ooa` section, scrambled section
  names, encrypted code). The code is only decrypted during start-up, so signatures must be scanned
  after that. Its PE timestamp is still `0x5762E3B7` (2016-06-16), the build the original tools
  supported, and every signature resolves to the original hardcoded addresses.
* **Loading without an injector:** on disk the exe only imports `Core/Activation64.dll`. The DRM
  resolves the real imports after decrypting (CRYPT32, DINPUT8, IPHLPAPI, MSVCP120, MSVCR120,
  NvCameraSDK64, OLEAUT32, PSAPI, SHELL32, SHLWAPI, USER32, USP10, VERSION, WINMM, WS2_32, WSOCK32,
  WTSAPI32, bcrypt, d3d11, dwmapi, dxgi, ole32, urlmon). By then the EA overlay (`igo64.dll`), EA's
  `steam_api64.dll` and Steam's `steamclient64.dll` / `tier0_s64.dll` have already loaded the
  system `VERSION.dll`, `WINMM.dll` and `IPHLPAPI.DLL`, so proxies with those names are skipped.
  `USP10.dll` is first loaded by the game's own imports (seen in the process's module list, which
  is in load order). On Windows 10/11 all 44 of its exports are forwarders to `GDI32`, so the
  proxy is just a `.def` of forwarders. MSVC's linker only accepts `X=GDI32.X` if an import library
  defines `X`, and the SDK's `gdi32.lib` doesn't, so the loader builds one from
  `gdi32_forward.def` first.
* **Hook memory:** after start-up the game's heap fills the whole ±1 GB around the exe, so MinHook
  1.3.3 fails with `MH_ERROR_MEMORY_ALLOC` (0x9). The nearest free block was about 1.6 GB away.
* **RenderView:** besides the transforms at `+0x00`/`+0x40`, there's a third copy at `+0x130`. The
  near plane is at `+0xEC` (0.06) and the far plane at `+0xF0` (25000). `+0xE4` is the vertical
  field of view in radians (1.0472 with ForceFov 60), `+0xE8` 0.9599 (55 degrees, maybe the
  default), `+0xF4` the aspect ratio. The view matrix is at `+0x2A0`
  and the projection at `+0x360` (`[0][0]` = cot(30) / aspect, `[1][1]` = 1.73205,
  `[2][3]` = -1: view space looks down -Z, like the camera transform's row 2 points backwards).
* **MeshSettings:** `+0x20` is 0 by default on this build, not the -1 the original restored.
* **Faith's position:** the entity the original seeded the camera from (`…+0xD8 → [0] + 0x40`)
  holds zeros on this build. The soldier at `ClientGameContext + 0x68 → +0x568 → +0x14A0`
  has `GetTransform(out)` at vtable `+0xC0` (it uses `movaps`, so the output must be 16-byte
  aligned). It reads `r9 = [soldier + 0x38]`, slot `(byte[r9+9] + 2·byte[r9+0xA]) · 0x20`, and
  the matrix at `r9 + slot + 0x10`. The translation is at Faith's feet.
* **Type info:** Frostbite's reflection data is in the decrypted exe. Field records are 0x18
  bytes: name pointer, uint16 flags, uint16 offset at `+0xA`, then a type pointer. Search the
  image for the field name string, then for 8-byte pointers to it, and read the offset.
* **Motion blur** (WorldRenderSettings, `*OFFSET_WORLDRENDERSETTINGS`): `MotionBlurScale +0x78`
  (0.5), `MotionBlurFixedShutterTime +0x7C` (0.008), `MotionBlurMax +0x80` (0.1),
  `MotionBlurRadialBlurMax +0x84` (0.06), `MotionBlurNoiseScale +0x88` (1), `MotionBlurQuality
  +0x8C` (int, 1), `MotionBlurMaxSampleCount +0x94` (int, 48), `MotionBlurEnable +0x145` (bool).
  `ShadowmapResolution` at `+0x48` (3072) confirms the class. There's also a visual environment
  `MotionBlurComponentData` (Enable `+0xA4`, Scale `+0x84`, radial blur fields), not used yet.
* **Finding a field's class:** walk back from the field record to the start of its array (the
  first record some 8-byte pointer in the image points to). The `ClassInfoData` holding that
  pointer has the class name pointer just before it. Field arrays of different classes sit next to
  each other, so walking records alone runs into the neighbouring classes.
* **Culling and distance** (live values on the Steam build):
  * WorldRenderSettings (`WorldRenderSettingsBase`) `CullScreenAreaScale +0x10` = 5.0 (Frostbite's
    default is 1), `MinShadowViewCoverage +0x14`, `ShadowmapViewDistance +0x64` = 200. Lowering
    `CullScreenAreaScale` keeps small objects drawn further away ("Show small objects far away").
  * Sun shadows (WorldRenderSettings, live): `ShadowmapViewDistance +0x64` = 200 m from the camera,
    `ShadowmapResolution +0x48` = 3072, `ShadowmapQuality +0x4C` = 1, `ShadowmapSliceCount +0x54` = 4
    cascades, `ShadowmapSliceSchemeWeight +0x5C` = 0.88, `ShadowmapFirstSliceScale +0x60` = 1,
    `ShadowmapExtrusionLength +0x68` = 1000, `ShadowmapViewDistanceScaleEnable +0x133` = 1,
    `ShadowmapAdjustFarPlane +0x135` = 1. A camera more than ~200 m above the ground leaves it
    outside every cascade, so "Shadow distance" overrides `+0x64` every frame. Resolution and
    cascade count aren't touched: the shadow maps are probably only made at start-up.
    "Adjust the shadow layers" overrides `ShadowmapTransitionBlendAmount +0x6C` (the fade between
    cascades) and `ShadowmapSliceSchemeWeight +0x5C` (log / even cascade split blend).
  * Outdoor light shadow fields (`OutdoorLightComponentData`, state offset = data offset - 0x80,
    which matches every field the original GUI used): `ShadowSunRotationX +0x8C` (0),
    `ShadowSunRotationY +0x90` (60), `SkyEnvmapShadowScale +0xA8` (1), `SunShadowHeightScale +0xAC`
    (1), `SunShadowFilterType +0xB0` (int 0), `SunShadowForwardQuality +0xB4`, `SunPcssInitialSampleCount
    +0xB8` (8), `SunPcssMaximumSampleCount +0xBC` (32), `SunPcssShadowFilterScale +0xC8` (1),
    `ShadowSunRotationEnable +0x119` (0), `CloudShadowStartFade +0xEC`, `CloudShadowsFadeDistance
    +0xF0`. The original GUI's "Shadow follows sun rotation" at `+0x119` is
    `ShadowSunRotationEnable`, so it's the other way round: on = shadows use their own direction.
  * GameRenderSettings: `NearPlane +0x4C`, `ViewDistance +0x50` = 25000, `ForceFov +0x54`,
    `FovMultiplier +0x58`, `EdgeModelScreenAreaScale +0x60`, `EdgeModelViewDistance +0x64` = 150,
    `EdgeModelForceLod +0x68`, `EdgeModelLodScale +0x6C`, `StaticModelPartOcclusionMaxScreenArea
    +0x70`, `LockView +0xCD`, `SecondaryStreamingViewEnable +0xD0` = 1.
  * MeshSettings: `ForceLod +0x20`, `GlobalLodScale +0x24`, `ShadowDistanceScale +0x28`,
    `LoadingEnabled +0x54`, `LodFadeEnable +0x56`. Fix LOD writes 0 / 100000 / 100000 (both scales,
    like the original tools), and works in game.
  * `CameraParamsComponentData` has its own `ViewDistance`, `ForceLod`, `ShadowDistanceScale` and
    `CullScreenAreaScale` (+0x84 - +0x98), for the game's scripted cameras.
* **Streaming:** the city is streamed by `ZoneStreamerEntity`, which loads the grid zones its
  foci are in, plus their neighbours. Its default focus is the game camera (camera registry entry
  0, 0), which stays with Faith while the free camera is elsewhere. That's why props close to a
  far-away free camera can be missing even with Fix LOD. The tools add a second focus at the free
  camera, see section 10. The `ClientSecondaryStreamingViewEntity` /
  `SecondaryStreamingViewEnable` path wasn't needed.
* **Time of day:** taken from MEC-TC (Mirror's Edge Catalyst Time Changer, .NET):
  `[[[base + 0x255C2F8] + 0x8] + 0x28] + 0x30`, float seconds 0 - 86400, about 20 game seconds
  per real second. Its "frozen TOD fix" writes `65700 + 15` whenever the clock reads 65700.
* **Interpolation:** plain Catmull-Rom moves the camera between two identical keyframes
  once a third keyframe is elsewhere. The port uses time-aware tangents clamped to
  3× each segment's slope, which keeps it still and is identical for evenly spaced keyframes.
* **Time of day keyframes:** the clock is interpolated on unwrapped values around each segment's
  first keyframe (each step is forward through midnight, or backward when the keyframe says so),
  with the same clamped Hermite as everything else, then wrapped to 0 - 86400. A playing track's
  value is written in the camera hook and again in the visual environment update, before the
  frozen-clock and stuck-clock writes.
* **Mouse wheel:** the game's window gets no `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` (it reads the mouse as raw input)
  and the tools' DirectInput mouse sees no wheel either (`lZ` stays 0), although x / y work. A
  `WH_MOUSE_LL` hook does see it; it's only set while the menu is open, on its own high-priority
  thread, so gameplay mouse input never waits on it. Wheel and `WM_CHAR` input are handed to
  ImGui on the render thread at the start of a frame: written from the window thread they could
  land mid-frame and be cleared by `EndFrame` unused.
* **Controller scan:** `XInputGetState` on empty slots and DirectInput `EnumDevices` are slow and
  share locks with the game's own input; the template ran both every second without a controller.
  Now XInput is checked every 3 s and DirectInput every 30 s.
* **Two crashes:** both access violations in game code with no tools frame
  on the stack. One (`+0x1A9DC69`): a loop at `0x142FC2C34` calls `vtable[0](obj, 0xC390A20F)` on
  each object of a list (an interface query), and one object's vtable led into reflection string
  data. The other (`+0x300341E`): a hash lookup on an object whose first field was garbage. Both look
  like a freed or overwritten object. At the `+0x1A9DC69` crash the game camera was at (0, 1, 0), so the free
  camera and Faith's body switch had just been turned on outside normal play. Changes since:
  the body switch saves and restores the exact `+0x150` link and only on the same player entity,
  it's skipped when the game camera isn't in the world, the fake focus vtable has 16 no-op slots,
  and a crash writes `[CRASH]` lines to the log (the previous log is kept as `CT.previous.log`).

### 10. Zone streaming

Read from the decrypted exe (PE timestamp `0x5762E3B7`). Addresses are absolute, base `0x140000000`.

**Reflection data.** Class info records are 0x38 bytes: `+0x00` name, `+0x08` flags (u16),
`+0x0A` size (u16), `+0x10` module, `+0x1A` field count (u16), `+0x20` super class, `+0x28`
create function, `+0x30` field array. Value types (flags `0x29`) have their field array at
`+0x28` instead. Each class also has a static `TypeInfo` whose first qword points to that record.
`getType()` is vtable slot 0 (`lea rax, [TypeInfo]; ret`), so a vtable can be found from the
`getType` that returns its class's TypeInfo.

| Data class | Fields |
|---|---|
| `ZoneStreamerEntityData` (0xA0, super `SpatialEntityData`) | `Transform +0x20`, `Info +0x60` (`ZoneStreamerInfo`), `ClientSideOnly +0x90`, `EnableDefaultFocus +0x91` |
| `ZoneStreamerInfo` (0x30) | `GridResource +0x0`, `SubLevelPath +0x8`, `ZoneInfos +0x10`, `BundleParents +0x18`, `BundleNames +0x20`, `RegionSuperbundles +0x28` |
| `ZoneStreamerZoneInfo` (0x10) | `Neighbours +0x0`, `HasBundle +0x8` |
| `ZoneStreamerFocusEntityData` (0x70) | `Realm +0x18`, `FocusPoint +0x20` (LinearTransform), `AutoEnabled +0x60` |
| `ZoneStreamerQueryEntityData` (0x70) | `FocusPoint +0x20`, `Mode +0x60` (FocusPoint / AllStreaming / AllFoci / AllFociAndStreaming), `IncludeNeighbours +0x64` |
| `ZoneStreamerSettings` (0x38) | debug drawing, `TestZoneHeights +0x28`, `PinVisitedZones +0x29`, `PauseAll +0x2A`, `SelectedStreamer +0x20` |
| `SecondaryStreamingViewEntityData` (0x20) | `Enabled +0x18`, `PauseCubemapUpdates +0x19`, `UseForCubemapPriorities +0x1A` |

**Runtime classes.**

| Class | Size | Vtable | `getType` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ZoneStreamerEntity` | 0x708 | `0x141CFE290` (more at `+0x30`, `+0x248`, `+0x260`) | `0x143C7FD70` |
| `ZoneStreamerEntityBase` | 0x268 | `0x141CFE190` | `0x143C7FD90` |
| `ZoneStreamerFocusEntity` | 0x58 | `0x141CFE460`, focus interface at `+0x40` (vtable `0x141CFE528`) | `0x143C7FDA0` |
| `ZoneStreamerQueryEntity` | 0x90 | `0x141CFFD00` | `0x143C86810` |

**ZoneStreamerEntity.** `+0x28` data, `+0x280` focus list, `+0x2D8` zone grid, `+0x2F0` zone
table (8 bytes per zone, parent zone at `+6`), `+0x700` / `+0x702` state bytes. Streamers register
with one of two per-realm managers at `[0x1425A3FC8]` / `[0x1425A3FD0]` (index
`ClientSideOnly == 0`). The manager's update (`0x143C80F40`, vtable `0x141CFE270`) walks its
`+0x28` list (0x10 bytes per entry: streamer, frame interval, counter, accumulated dt) and calls
the streamer update `0x143C81900(streamer, dt)` (`OFFSET_ZONESTREAMERUPDATE`). That update does:

1. `0x143C81850(list)`: for each focus record, `focus->vtable[0](focus, key, &cache[i])`. A record
   with flag bit 0 (removed) gets the default instead: position `FLT_MAX`, direction `(0, 1, 0)`.
2. `0x143C82060(streamer)`: for each record, looks up the grid zone containing the cached
   position (point in polygon on X/Z, `0x143C7FA60`, or `0x143C7FB40` with `TestZoneHeights`).
   When it changes it calls `0x143C810D0` (reference the new zone and its neighbours) and
   `0x143C81240` (release the old ones) through the streamer's `+0x30` interface, then stores the
   zone in the record. `FLT_MAX` is in no zone, so a removed focus releases what it held.
3. `0x143C7F570(list)`: drops removed records (swap with the last one, count - 1).

**Focus list** (`streamer + 0x280`): `+0x00` the default focus provider (owned), `+0x08` / `+0x10`
/ `+0x18` record vector, `+0x28` / `+0x30` / `+0x38` cache vector (0x20 bytes per focus: position
float4, direction float4), `+0x48` record count (u32). A record is 0x18 bytes: `+0x00` key (passed
back to the focus), `+0x08` focus object, `+0x10` current zone (-1 = none), `+0x14` flags.

* Add: `0x143C7E7C0(list, key, focus)` (`OFFSET_ZONEFOCUSADD`) appends an enabled record with zone
  -1, growing both vectors with `0x143C813F0`.
* Remove: `0x143C81390(list, key, focus)` (`OFFSET_ZONEFOCUSREMOVE`) sets bit 0 on the first
  enabled record matching both. If there's none it writes the flag at index -1, so only call it
  for a focus that's there.
* `ZoneStreamerFocusEntity` makes those calls with key 0 and `entity + 0x40` on its Enable /
  Disable events (`0x143C7F420`, event hashes `0x8BA423E4` / `0xF90216B1`). Its focus function
  `0x143C7F9A0` returns `FocusPoint`'s translation and forward rows.

**Default focus.** `0x143C7F2B0` creates the list's provider at `list + 0x00`:

* If `[0x14253AC70]` is set, which it always is (a static initialiser at `0x14327D870` points it
  and `[0x142415E50]` at the camera registry at `0x142415E60`): provider vtable `0x141CFE118`,
  focus function `0x143C7F840`. It looks up the registry entry with ids (0, 0) (`0x143279950`)
  and calls its vtable `+0x08`, which copies the entry's transform at `+0xD0` under the lock at
  `+0x30`. It uses translation (`+0x100`) and forward (`+0xF0`), unless the translation is zero or
  equal to `[0x14253AF00]`.
* Otherwise, when `0x14311E890()` returns 1 and `[[0x14253D670] + 0x70] + 0x46D4` is set
  (probably "this is a server"): provider vtable `0x141CFE140` (focus function `0x143C7F910`),
  which listens for the messages `0xF5E71A27` / `0x1708637D` that every `ServerConnection` sends
  when it starts and stops (`0x1433CD2F0`), and uses `connection + 0x4490 → +0x70[0]`, the
  client's view position.

The camera registry entries (vtable `0x141B17D28`, created by `0x143273E20`, ids at `+0x10` /
`+0x14`) are updated by `0x14327BA00`. It takes the active game camera, copies its two transforms
to `entry + 0x90` and `+0xD0`, and sets up a render view at `entry + 0x1140` (which calls
`OFFSET_CAMERAUPDATE` through `0x14352D4C0`). The free camera only overwrites the render view,
never this transform, so the streaming focus keeps following the game camera, that is, Faith.

**What the tools do.** They hook `0x143C81900`. Before the game's update, they look for their own
focus in the streamer's list and add or remove it with the game's own functions, the same way a
`ZoneStreamerFocusEntity` is enabled or disabled. The focus is a static object in the tools'
DLL whose vtable slot 0 copies the free camera's translation and forward (written each frame
from the camera hook) into the cache entry. It's added while *Load the world around the camera*
is ticked and the free camera is on, and removed otherwise. The game's own focus stays, so the
zones around Faith remain loaded.

**More foci.** There are now 32 static focus objects (`{ vtable, index }`, slot 0 reads
`g_FocusResults[index]` under an SRW lock): 0 the camera, 1 a look-ahead point (camera position
plus its smoothed velocity × 2.5 s, at most 400 m, reset on jumps over 50 m in a frame), 2 - 31
points along the selected track (keyframes and every 150 m between them, straight lines, points
within 1 m merged). The camera hook publishes positions and a wanted flag per focus; before each
streamer update the tools remove the ones no longer wanted, then add the new ones, using the
game's add / remove (remove only for foci found enabled in the list). The look-ahead focus stays in
the list while it's on (it sits on the camera when it's still), so zones aren't referenced and
released over and over around a speed threshold. Now 72 foci: 0 camera, 1 ahead, 2 - 41 rings
around the camera (stream distance, centred on a 100 m grid point), 42 - 71 track points.

**Zone slots, and the crash they caused.** Each `ZoneStreamerEntity` has 128 slots for loaded
zones at `+0x2F8` (8 bytes each). A zone table entry (`+0x2F0`, 8 bytes per zone) has flags in
byte 0 (bit 2 set when it has a slot, bit 3 checked when zones are released) and its slot number
plus one in the word at `+2`. The slot search in `0x143C80180` loops `cx` over 0 - 0x7F looking
for an empty one; when there's none it falls through with `dx` holding a garbage value, writes
the zone's object to `streamer + 0x2F8 + dx * 8` (far past the table) and stores `dx + 1` as the
slot. The release loop in `0x143C81E60` later reads `slot - 1` back: with a slot word of 0 that's
`0xFFFF`, i.e. `streamer + 0x7FFF8 + 0x2F8`, and it passes the null it finds to `0x143C81600`,
which reads `[rdx + 0x10]` (the crash at `+0x3C8160A` reading `0x10`, stream
distance 575 m). The out-of-bounds writes corrupt whatever follows the streamer, so earlier
crashes elsewhere can have the same cause. The tools now count used slots (non-null entries)
before each update, add at most one of their foci per update and only below 84 used, and above
100 remove their least important one (rings outer first, then track points, then the look-ahead
point; never the camera's own).

That budget alone wasn't enough: with 544 m the game crashed at `+0x3576AA5`
(function `0x1435763F0`). It loops over 32-byte instance records (`[obj + 0x278]`, position and
radius) and writes a closest distance into a per-mesh table (`[obj + 0x270]`, 0x350 bytes per
mesh, value at `+0x288`); the read was for mesh index 17761 and the loop counter was
`0xD430F1A1`, so the object was already corrupt. Zone slots are only filled as zones load, so a
count of used slots runs behind what was asked for, and adding foci on every update could still
ask for more than 128. Now a focus is only added once the slot count has stood still for 0.75 s
(and 0.75 s after the last one), below 96 used, two are removed above 104, and the stream distance
is capped at 400 m. The mesh streaming may have a limit of its own (Fix LOD was on in both
crashes). The game's own crash handler then crashed in its allocator, which is what the dump's
exception shows; the first exception's CONTEXT was found on the stack (`ContextFlags 0x10005F`).

### 11. Entities: class tree, instance lists, transforms

Read from the decrypted exe and the `.data` it was dumped with (taken in-game, so heap pointers
in it are from that moment), then checked read-only against the running game (*Live census* below). Addresses
are absolute, base `0x140000000`. `Pam` is the prefix of Catalyst's own classes.

**Runtime ClassInfo** (the static `TypeInfo` object `getType()` returns, see section 10):

| Offset | Field |
|---|---|
| `+0x00` | class info record (name at `+0`, size at `+0xA`, section 10) |
| `+0x08` | next type (one list of every type) |
| `+0x10` | u16 runtime id |
| `+0x18` | super class (ClassInfo) |
| `+0x28` / `+0x2A` | u16 class id / last subclass id (an `isKindOf` range) |
| `+0x30` | first subclass |
| `+0x38` | next subclass of the same super class |
| `+0x60`, `+0x70`, `+0x80`, `+0x90` | instance lists (first link) |

**Instance lists.** Entity constructors register the new entity with its exact class: `lea rcx,
[entity + 0x40]; mov r8, entity; lea rdx, [ClassInfo]; call 0x1431661F0`. That function links it
into `ClassInfo + 0x60 + (flags & 1) * 0x10` when the entity's flags (`+0x18`) have bit `0x10`.
`0x1431665B0` (vehicles, the player / look-at / target cameras, spawn and team entities) also sets
bit `0x20` and uses `+0x80` / `+0x90` when `0x10` isn't set. The lists are intrusive: the head
holds the first link, and a link (`entity + 0x40`) is the next link, then the address of whatever
points to this link (the head, or the previous link). So `entity = link - 0x40`, and a linked entity
has `*link[1] == link`. Each class lists only its own instances, plus unnamed subclasses that don't
override `getType` (9 vtables share ClientPhysicsEntity's); subclasses have lists of their own. In
the dump, the `+0x60` lists of ClientDynamicModelEntity, ClientStaticModelEntity,
ClientStaticModelGroupEntity, PamClientCharacterEntity, PamClientStaticModelEntity, SwarmEntity and
VisualEnvironmentEntity were in use. The code that unlinks an entity when it's destroyed wasn't
found (it isn't a plain copy of the insert).

Game code checks exact types by calling `getType` and comparing with the ClassInfo address, for
example `0x1432D1080` (a ClientVehicleEntity gives `[vehicle + 0x430] + 0xC0`).

**Transforms.** vtable `+0xC0` is `0x1432E1440` in every class above (in SpatialEntity it's still
pure virtual, `0x143C8845D`), the same function Faith's soldier has (section 9): `r9 = [entity +
0x38]`, the matrix at `r9 + 0x10 + (byte[r9 + 9] + 2 * byte[r9 + 0xA]) * 0x20`. Byte `+9` looks
like the number of components (0x20 bytes each, from `+0x10`), followed by the transforms.

**Live census** (2026-10-18, read-only, Faith on a rooftop in the first open-world area). Walking
every class's four lists and keeping only entries whose vtable's `getType` points back to that
class: ClientStaticModelEntity 2106, PamClientStaticModelEntity 701, ClientStaticModelGroupEntity
44, PamClientUIMapEntity 21, PamClientCharacterEntity 23 (Faith and NPCs, each NPC listed twice at
the same spot: two entities per character), SwarmEntity 17, VisualEnvironmentEntity 67,
PamClientMagropeEntity 33, plus the server-side copies (PamServerCharacterEntity 23,
ServerStaticModelEntity 2104, ...). No ClientVehicleEntity, ClientDynamicModelEntity,
ClientBangerEntity or drones there. Data classes have other things at `+0x60`, so the check on
`getType` matters. Picking from ClientPhysicsEntity's subclasses only (no
static models) therefore only ever found characters (seen in game).

**Swarms: traffic and crowds.** Catalyst's cars, flying traffic and crowds are members of
`SwarmEntity` (ClientGameComponentEntity's subclass, size 0x870), not entities.
`BoidsNetworkNodeEntityData` (`Position +0x20`, `Facing +0x18`, `IsTrafficSignal +0x71`,
`TrafficGreenDuration +0x3C`, `Connections +0x68`, ...) is the road network they drive on;
`SwarmEntityData` has `MaxAgentCount +0x84`. Every swarm in the census had 5 components (entries
of `[swarm + 0x38]`, 0x20 bytes each from `+0x10`, the component at entry `+0x10`, count at byte
`+9`): CrowdPlacementComponent, CrowdVariationComponent, ClientAppearanceComponent,
CrowdRenderComponent (0x9150 bytes) and CrowdBoidsComponent (0xB8). CrowdBoidsComponent:

| Offset | Field |
|---|---|
| `+0x00` / `+0x38` | vtables `0x141CCE7F8` / `0x141CCEA08` (constructor `0x143B8F4C0`) |
| `+0x10` | CrowdBoidsComponentData |
| `+0x50` / `+0x58` / `+0x60` | a vector of 8-byte elements, allocator at `+0x68` |
| `+0x70` / `+0x78` / `+0x80` | the members: begin / end / capacity, allocator at `+0x88` |
| `+0xA0` | u32, 413 for 425 records (live members?) |

Each member record is 0x20 bytes: two float4 positions (w = 0) about 0.3 m apart, which look like
this frame's and the last. In a road traffic swarm only x and z change; in another one x, y and z
do (flying traffic, around y = 60 - 100). The block after the swarm's own transform in its
component allocation also has one float4 per member (w = 0.008), close to the record's second
position, maybe what gets drawn. Sampled every 15 ms: each record stays the same
member and moves smoothly, about 0.5 m per change for a car; the first position is the newest
and the second one is exactly the first one of the change before. Records change about every
30 ms, every other sample, so the tools interpolate between the two positions over the measured
interval. In one swarm (1300 records) ground traffic sat at y = 0.1 - 0.3.

**What the tools do** (*Attach to what the camera looks at*, `Camera/AttachTargets.cpp`). The pick
runs in the camera hook, on the game's thread:

1. ClientPhysicsEntity's ClassInfo is found by going up the super classes of Faith's class (her
   vtable slot 0 is `48 8D 05 rel32 C3`, decoded instead of called), or at its address on this
   build (`0x1427EE290`), checked by name either way. Its subclasses are collected through `+0x30`
   / `+0x38`, leaving out static model groups, terrain, water, AppearanceEntity, the map screen,
   bullets and held weapons. ClientPhysicsEntity's own lists are left out too. SwarmEntity is
   found among the subclasses of ClientPhysicsEntity's super class.
2. Every instance list of those classes is walked (at most 20000 links each, inside `__try`). An
   entity counts when its vtable's `getType` decodes to the list's class and its slot `+0xC0`
   has `0x1432E1440`'s first 28 bytes. Its transform is then read straight from memory. For a
   swarm, its CrowdBoidsComponent is found among its components by `getType`, and every member
   record (at most 8192) is a candidate.
3. Candidates must be within 12 degrees of the middle of the view, or 1 m of the line of sight, up
   to 1000 m in front (aiming 1 m above a character's or crowd member's feet, 0.6 m above
   traffic). The view
   direction is minus the camera's row 2 (W moves the camera that way). Faith (her soldier
   pointer, or an entity exactly where she is) is skipped. The best 48 are kept, and the best 48
   static models apart from them.
4. A quarter of a second later (real time, so it doesn't depend on the frame rate) every
   candidate is read again. Static models that haven't moved 2 cm are
   dropped, so buildings are never picked, and swarm members that haven't moved rank as if they
   were about 6 degrees further out (a record left over from a member that's gone stays still).
   The best of the rest is followed, and with *Put the camera next to what I pick* the camera is
   placed 3.5 m behind and 0.6 m above a person (8 m and 2.5 m for anything else), looking at it.

The FOLLOW tab's *Nearby* list uses the same walk with a radius instead of the view cone, once a
second while the tab is drawn: everything within it, nearest first (at most 300 rows), characters'
second entity at the same spot dropped, static models only once they've moved in the last 30 s
(compared with the previous scan). The rows shown are only replaced every 30 s, on Refresh, or
after the range changes, and not while the mouse is over the list. Live check of the traffic /
crowd split: a 1300-member swarm at y = 0.4 with 0.88 m average steps (road
traffic), 425 members at y = 71 with 0.34 m (flying traffic), and 700 - 900-member swarms at ground
level with 0.045 m (crowds). Listed positions are read again every frame for the markers,
projected with the camera transform and the render view's `+0xE4` / `+0xF4`. A swarm is traffic
when its moving members' average step is over 12 cm, a crowd otherwise.

Every frame the followed entity must still have the vtable it had when it was picked, `*link[1] ==
link` (and `next[1] == link`), and a finite transform. A swarm member's swarm must also still have
the same CrowdBoidsComponent (same vtable) and a record at its index. Its transform is built from
the record's first position, facing the way it moved (first minus second position, smoothed, kept
while it stands still); following only uses how the transform changes, so a heading that's
backwards wouldn't matter. A jump of more than 100 m in one frame (15 m for a swarm member, whose
record may be given to a new member somewhere else) also ends it. Nothing on the target is ever
called.

**What things are, by name** (2026-10-22, read-only, Faith on a rooftop at about -60 61 62).

- *Static models*: `ClientStaticModelEntity + 0x30` is its StaticModelEntityData (2071 of 2071;
  PamClientStaticModelEntity's is PamStaticModelEntityData, 686 of 686, a subclass; super class at
  ClassInfo `+0x18` works for data classes too). StaticModelEntityData: `Mesh +0x98` (MeshAsset),
  `Visible +0xDC`. Asset: `Name +0x10`. The mesh's local box is at entity `+0x100` / `+0x110` (two
  float4 corners), sane on 2754 of 2757. Moving ones in the whole level: the monorail trains
  (`objects/props/monorail/monorail_train_01`, `monorail_trainwagon_01`, and
  `objects/props/monorailtrain_01/monorailtrain_01a`, `01b`, 34 carriages, 85 - 135 m/s, one jumped
  756 m in a second: its route starting again), `objects/props/backdrop/bd_airplane_01` (5, one
  flying at 1796 1507 222, 46 m/s), `objects/props/construction/blimpcallaghan01` (3, y 213 - 244,
  1 - 6 m/s), `objects/architecture/backdrops/animated/bd_animated_csg_elevator_01` (21 lifts on
  backdrop buildings) and `objects/props/louver/louver_facade01/...` (320 facade shutters, a few cm a
  second; 24 of them made up most of what moved near Faith). Still: `vehicles/vtol/vtol_backdrop`
  (3 parked VTOLs), `backdrop/bd_boats/...` (6). No bird meshes anywhere.
- *Security cameras*: `objects/props/missionitem/securitycamera01/securitycamera_body_Mesh`, 23
  ClientStaticModelEntity within 150 m of Faith. None moved or turned in 2 s. Box (-0.11 -0.10
  -0.19) to (0.11 0.30 0.70): 0.9 m long along +Z (its forward row), the lens end 0.7 m in front of
  the origin. Most have forward (0.20 -0.95 0.22), i.e. 72 degrees down with no roll; a few 15
  degrees down. (`magrope_camera1/2` are the mag rope gadget, not cameras.)
- *Swarms*: CrowdVariationComponent `+0xA8` / `+0xB0` is a vector of 0x10-byte entries, the first
  qword a CrowdAppearanceItemData (an asset; the second qword's low byte looks like the variation
  index). Its names, e.g. `Levels/SP/SP_MainCity/Crowds/Cars/CarBackdropSport_01`, give the folder:
  Cars (VehicleTruck_01_crowd_Yellow, CarBackdropSport_01 and colours, MotorcycleCrowdSport_01: one
  1300-record swarm, avg step 1.09 m), Drones (DroneNews / DroneSnooper / DroneVTOL_Helicopter_01:
  the 425-record flying traffic at y 74, and 32 drones at y 236 - 501), Boats (Boat_01 / 02, 32 at y
  -1, about 1 km away), and the people: LowCaste, MidCaste, HighCaste, Pedestrian, Enforcer,
  Construction_Worker (several of them stand still on balconies, so moving or not can't tell
  people from traffic). People swarms also lead to MasterSkeletonAsset / SkeletonAsset
  (`Characters/Skeletons/...`), vehicle swarms don't. Which member uses which item wasn't found:
  no per-member vector in the components; a byte table of values 0 - 6 at CrowdVariationComponent
  `+0x1FA0` has 1216 entries, not 1300, so it isn't known to be that.
- The Nearby list kept the nearest 300 of everything and only then applied the menu's filters, so
  unticked groups (crowds near a street) took the places of what was ticked.

**Not used.** The physics raycast: the instance lists made it unnecessary, and from a hit you'd
still have to get from the physics body back to its entity.

**Sound listener** (2026-10-22, read live, read-only). The sound system is `[0x1423DD580]` (vtable
`0x141ABD460`; SoundEntity's vtable `0x141AD0338` slot 4 gets its voice from it with `+0x40`). Its
slot 1 gives the listeners: `[0x1423E29B8] + 0x30` (begin / end, one listener in the city, vtable
`0x141ACFA78`). Listener: transform rows at `+0x10..+0x4F` (slot 0 sets them, `0x14301DBC0`; slot 1
gets `+0x10`), velocity `+0x50` (slot 2 sets it, `0x14301DCA0`), flags `+0x60` (bit 0 transform
changed, bit 1 velocity changed), its source `+0x70` (slot 6, the camera). Nothing else uses those
two setters. Once a frame `0x1432C1350` (frame time in xmm1) does, for each listener: the source's
transform (its slot 1), rows 0 and 2 negated; times a transform from `[0x142409C08]` (its slot 8,
then `0x1432A6B90`) if that is set (the load at `0x1432C1494`; an earlier note said 0x14240A608,
a miscalculation, and that address was read instead); velocity = (new position - the listener's stored one) / dt, set; transform
set; then CameraData's SoundOcclusion (+0x40, to the sound system's slot 0x19), SoundListenerRadius
(+0x44, listener slot 4) and SoundListenerFov (+0x48, slot 7). Checked live: the listener's rows
were exactly the render view's (+0x40) with rows 0 and 2 negated, the same position. The tools
hook the two setters: the free camera's transform made the same way, and a velocity from its own
movement (the game's would be the jump from the free camera back to its camera).

Voices: the sound system's slot 8 (`0x142FE2EE0`) is `mov rcx, [0x1423E29B8]; jmp 0x143019860`
(rdx = the sound asset, e.g. SoundEntityData.Sound `+0x18`), which builds a voice (vtable
`0x141ACFAD0`, its 3D state at `+0x28`, null for one heard the same anywhere; slot 13 `0x14301DC30`
copies 4 rows there; slot 0 fires an event). SoundEntity's event handler (its slot 4, `0x14301A170`)
makes the voice on its first event, places it (`0x143021540`, ending in voice slots 15/16 and 13)
and fires the event. A sound log (the tools' diagnostic, 2026-10-22, Faith walking up to traffic)
gave: district ambiences from `0x1432BC569` (hundreds of voices a second, placed at the origin
first); traffic (`ME_Spot_Traffic_Heavy_02`), crowd spots and the club music
(`ME_Music_Diegetic_Club2`) from SoundEntity events sent by the level's logic: an event queue in
`0x14347995F` (up to 15 a frame, a ring of 128) through `0x14347C480` (vtable `0x141B94710` slot 9)
and `0x1431C7F00`; the announcements (`VO_Propaganda_DownTownStage1..3`, `AnchorStage1..2`)
through `PamObjectCastEntity` (`0x1439581B0`, a type cast in the logic); KrugerSec chatter
(`VO_AI_DistantAmbient`) from the voice system `0x143047B90`, updated right after the listener in
`0x1432C1350`. All positional at their real places. With the free camera far from Faith they don't
start: what starts them reacts to her.

---

Analysis script: `ctdis.py` (Python with `capstone` + `pefile`) indexes the DLL's functions from `.pdata`, finds xrefs, and annotates strings, e.g. `Bin().dis_func(0x180008140)`. Set `CTDIS_DLL` to the path of the original DLL. The tool folder's `CT_MirrorsEdge.dll` gets replaced when you install the port; the original is in `CT_MirrorsEdge_20180210-1c6115.rar` (password `CinematicTools`).

#### Instance lists (the third streaming crash)

A third crash came with only 77 of 128 zone slots in use: `+0x35554EB` reading `0x4`, in
`0x1435554B1`, which takes an instance handle (bit 31 a flag), indexes a 32-byte record list at
`[manager + 0x350090]` (null at the time) and clamps the mesh index it finds to `0xFFF`.

* The mesh streaming manager is at `[0x142563410]`. `+0x50` / `+0x58` is its mesh table (0x350
  bytes per mesh), `+0x350070` and `+0x350090` are two model instance vectors (begin, end,
  capacity, allocator; 32-byte records), `+0x386480` its `MeshStreamingSettings`.
* `0x143554B10` (called only from `0x1432F2AC9`, which sets up the streaming pools for a level)
  reserves the two vectors with `MeshStreamingSettings + 0x58` (`ReservedPositionedInstanceCount`)
  and `+ 0x5C` (`ReservedDistancedInstanceCount`) through `0x143554510`, which reallocates when
  asked for more than the current size.
* `0x1435454F0` copies both vectors' begin pointers and counts into a job context (`+0x278`,
  `+0x280`, `+0x214`, `+0x218`, mesh table at `+0x270`) and the job (`0x1435763F0`, the second
  crash) loops over them later. When more instances register than were reserved, a vector moves,
  and a job still holding the old pointer reads freed memory: garbage counts, indices (17761) and
  null lists.
* The tools now read both vectors every frame. Above 80 % full they add no more zones, above 90 %
  they take two away, and with *Load the world around the camera* on they set the two reserve
  counts to four times the game's, which the game uses from the next level load. When a vector
  moves anyway, the log says "The game outgrew its ... model instance list".

#### The mesh table (the actual limit)

The instance lists turned out to have plenty of room (65536 positioned, 0 in use at load), and
the fourth crash was the mesh job again (`+0x3576AA5`), a few seconds after Fix LOD was turned
off. The mesh table is an `eastl::fixed_vector` with room for 4096 meshes inside the manager:
the constructor `0x14353B8F0` sets begin and end to `manager + 0x70` and capacity to
`+0x70 + 0x350000` (`0x14353B963`). With more than 4096 meshes it moves to the heap, and grows
again from there, while the jobs (which copied the begin pointer into `+0x270`) still read the
old storage: index 17761 was far past it. Extra zones around the camera bring in many different
meshes, so the tools now budget by the mesh count (`([manager + 0x58] - [manager + 0x50]) / 0x350`):
no more zones from 3300, two taken away from 3500, and from 3700 (or once the table has left
the manager) the camera's own zones go too. Zone slots: add below 96, two away above 104. (4000 meshes was too close: one zone can bring in a few hundred at once, and a crash came at 3877.) The menu and the crash note show the count.


### 12. Interiors are sublevels (2026-10-19)

Read live (read-only) with the free camera inside the train station and Faith in Anchor, about
410 m apart. The city has three `ZoneStreamerEntity`s, all on the manager at `[0x1425A3FD0]`:
`CentralCityProps_ZS` (238 zones), `CentralCityBuildings_ZS` (83) and `Ground_ZS` (17). Their zones
are tall prisms (e.g. -354 .. 485), and the zones under the camera were loaded (slot set, refs > 0).
`ZoneStreamerSettings` (`[0x1425A3FA8]`) had `TestZoneHeights` 1 (the update picks `0x143C7FB40`).
Focus records: 0 the camera registry focus (vtable `0x141CFE118`), 1 a `ZoneStreamerFocusEntity`
(interface vtable `0x141CFE528`) near Faith, then the tools' own.

Interiors and district content are sublevels. The level (`[[0x14253D670] + 0x30] - 0xF0`, name at
`+0x118`) has its description components at `[[level + 0x108] + 0xB8]` (count at `-4`), among them
`PamSubLevelLoadTriggersComponent`: `LoadTriggers +0x10`, 86 entries of 0x40 bytes (`Assembly +0x00`,
an expression over `Inputs +0x10` (progression flags), `InstallGroupHash +0x18`, `Area +0x20` (Vec3
array, 16 bytes each, tested on X / Z by `0x14330D8C0`), `AreaHeight +0x28` (from `Area[0].y`, 0 = no
limit), `SubLevelPath +0x30`, `HeapType +0x38`). Districts (Downtown, Anchor, TheView, Construction
and their CityAlert versions), Trainstation (+ pre / post raid props), BaubleMall / Destruction /
Ruins, Jukebox, LairCharacters, mission sets (Icarus, Nomad, Birdman, ...) and the open-world
character sets. Only the level-load path reads it: `0x1432E2370` calls the pointer at `0x1424A9B90`
(`0x143A243F0`), which tests the start point (`0x143A224D0`: the transform at `[0x14257C9D8] + 0xA0`)
with `0x143A20170` and queues the sublevels; `0x143A21440` / `0x143A2150D` run the expression.

During play the level's own area triggers load them, and those react to characters, not cameras.
A count of the sublevel names in the game's private memory (`name_scan.py`) gave 7 - 20 copies
for Faith's (Anchor, AnchorArea1, Anc_OM_Characters_Area01) and 1 (just the trigger list's string)
for Trainstation, BaubleMall and Jukebox, so the camera's interior wasn't loaded. The tools leave it
at that: the menu and README only say some safe houses may or may not load with the setting. `ServerSubLevelEntity` (ClassInfo
`0x1427FD4C0`) and `ClientSubLevelEntity` (`0x1427EE1F0`) had no instances in their lists.

### 13. Vistas, the zone table's flags, and the CinematicSettings mod (2026-10-20)

**Vistas.** `VISTA_CityBuildings` is a `ZoneStreamerVistaEntity` (vtable `0x141CFFF88`, its
listener interface at `+0x30` with vtable `0x141D00040`). It registers that interface with the
buildings' zone streamer (`0x143C856F0`: pushed onto the vector at streamer `+0x38`/`+0x40`, and
vista `+0x50` = the streamer; `0x143C860F0` takes it off and zeroes the states). Vista `+0x28` is
its data (ZoneInfos at `+0x18`: VistaZoneInfo, Neighbours and Objects; ControlEntity `+0x20`),
`+0x48` the object entities made once at setup (`0x143C86E90`, `+0xD0` = 0 on each, hidden),
`+0x58` 8 bytes per zone (word first object, word object count, byte focus count, word flags),
`+0x60` the zone count (83, one per buildings zone: vista zone k is the low-detail copy of
buildings zone k).
- On every focus's zone change the streamer calls its listeners (`0x143C7ED80` ends with
  `[streamer+0x30]` vtable 0); the vista's (`0x143C87630`, this = vista + 0x30) takes 1 off the
  count of each vista neighbour of the old zone and adds 1 to each of the new zone's (clamped
  0 - 127), then runs `0x143C881C0`.
- `0x143C881C0`: flag 2 set: objects hidden (`+0xD0` = 0), flag 1 cleared; flag 1 set and count 0:
  `0x143C87F60(vista, zone, 0)`, flag 1 cleared; flag 1 clear and count > 0: `0x143C87F60(vista,
  zone, 1)`, flag 1 set. `0x143C87F60` writes `show` (or 0 when vista `+0x41` is 1) to `+0xD0` of
  each object of the zone of the right class.
- Flag 2 is set once (`0x143C86870`, guarded by vista `+0x40`) on the zone at streamer `+0x278`
  and its streamer neighbours, never cleared: the game hides those vistas for good.
- **The vista listens to the client's copy of the buildings' streamer**, a `RealmProxy` (ClassInfo
  `0x14289EEA0`, a ZoneStreamerEntityBase like ZoneStreamerEntity `0x14289EC20`; vtable
  `0x141CFE7C0`; its instances in the ClassInfo's `+0x60` list, link at entity `+0x268`, next link
  first). Its listener vector is at `+0x38` too; its `+0x28` data has the same SubLevelPath, but
  `+0x2D8` / `+0x2F0` aren't the grid and zone table. The three server ZoneStreamerEntity have no
  listeners at all (seen 2026-10-20: vista `0x634B1730` on proxy `0x1F102E4F0`, 83 zones, 31 shown,
  11 hidden for good, 76 objects). The link function (`0x143C85780`) looks through
  ZoneStreamerEntity's instances, then RealmProxy's, for the one whose data GUID matches.
- The tools hook `0x143C87F60` (signature `48 89 5C 24 18 56 41 54 41 55 41 56 41 57 48 83 EC 20 89
  D0 45 31 ED 45 0F B6 E0 4C 8D 3C C5 00 00 00 00 48 8B 41 58`) and pass 0 for zones they hold
  back; to apply a change they call the original for zones with flag 1 (and not 2).

**Zone table flags** (streamer `+0x2F0`, 8 bytes per bundle, as many as BundleNames: zones then
regions): byte 0 bit 0 = load asked (refs 0 -> 1), bit 1 = unload asked (refs -> 0), bit 2 = loading
(set with the slot in `0x143C80180`, cleared in `0x143C816D7` once the slot object's state is 3 or
more, or unload is asked), bit 3 = available (the parent chain's bit 3 and the region checks,
`0x143C81B46`/`0x143C81BCC`; a zone only gets a slot with it). Word `+2` slot + 1, cleared at
release (`0x143C81E60`); word `+4` refs; word `+6` parent.

**CinematicSettings.fbproject** (Frosty project, "hyper+ kekuGraphic 1.0"; read with a custom EBX
reader, `ebx.py`, `fbp_zones.py`): about 366 assets, mostly FX and visual
environments. Streaming:
- `CentralCityBuildings_ZS`: every one of the 83 zones has Neighbours = all bundle indices 0 - 94
  except 57 (so the 12 regions too), zone 25 none. Loading any building zone loads all of them.
- `VISTA_CityBuildings`: all 83 VistaZoneInfos emptied (no neighbours, no objects).
- Props (238 zones, up to 30 neighbours, 2799 in all) and Ground (17 zones) look like the game's
  own; not compared with the original.
- The region indices as neighbours stay inside the zone table (it has 95 entries). Its crashes
  are most likely the same limits the tools watch (the draw batch's 1748 chunks, the 4096 meshes),
  which the mod's loads don't go through.

### 14. The game's own replay (runner ghosts), first look (2026-10-20)

Classes: `PamClientReplayRecordingComponent` (TypeInfo `0x1428567B0`, vtable `0x141C48CD0`),
`PamClientReplayPlayerComponent` (`0x142856800`, vtable `0x141C48A28`), `PamClientReplayEntity`
(`0x142856990`, vtable `0x141C48960`), `PamServerReplayEntity`, `PamServerReplayPlayerComponent`,
`PamClientReplayMarkerEntity`; messages PamReplayRecordingStarted/Stopped, PamReplayReplayDone,
PamReplayStartPreview/StopPreview/StopReplay; `PamUseRunnersGhostShader`. Data:

batch then went held back 88k -> taken away 97k -> all taken away up to 106001 (95 %) -> everything

### 17. Present and the other mods' hooks (2026-10-22, live, read-only)

The menu and the mouse look once failed to start although every hook was in place: the Dx11 interfaces
were never retrieved. Following the jumps at dxgi's Present (dxgi.dll+0x19000 in the dxgi.dll
version that was read):

```
dxgi Present: jmp -> Clarity relay -> DINPUT8.dll (Catalyst Clarity) detour
  Clarity's trampoline -> a jmp stub next to EA's trampoline -> Steam overlay relay -> gameoverlayrenderer64 detour
  Steam's trampoline -> igo64.dll (EA app overlay) detour
  EA's trampoline = dxgi's own first 0x13 bytes, then dxgi Present+0x13
```

The tools' own MinHook slot (in a block below dxgi) was still there: relay to hIDXGISwapChain_Present,
trampoline to the same stub as Clarity's. So both trampolines were built from the same bytes, and
Clarity's jump was written last: Clarity's Present hook went over the tools' one and passes on to
what was there before it. Why (a hook created early and enabled late, or disabled and enabled again)
isn't known; Clarity's code wasn't read. Clarity's SetCursorPos / ClipCursor hooks were made after
the tools' and do pass on to them. Also in the process: `igo64.dll` (EA app overlay),
`gameoverlayrenderer64.dll`, `NvCameraSDK64.dll`, and `NoclipInjectedDLL.dll`; none of those three is on the
Present chain.

**The game's swapchain:** `[OFFSET_DXRENDERER] + 0x7E0` = Screen, `Screen + 0x280` = the
IDXGISwapChain. Its table is dxgi.dll+0xCD688, entry 8 = Present. In the dxgi.dll file three more places
hold Present's address (+0xCDA90, +0xCDDD8, +0xD0690); which tables they belong to wasn't checked.
DxRenderer + 0x750 / + 0x758 hold two other dxgi objects (tables dxgi+0xCED80, +0xCB020).

**Fix:** the tools also put hPresentFromTable in that table entry (the tools' thread, once a
second until the swapchain is there, only if the entry holds the Present the tools found). The game
calls through the table before any jump, so other mods' hooks can't leave the tools out. A
thread_local flag makes a call that passes both the table and the jump count once.

### 18. The whole city: what it runs into (2026-10-22, live read-only and offline)

Snapshot (Faith in the city, camera off, `city_limits.py`): Ground 17 zones (9
loaded), Buildings 83 (14), Props 238 (16); meshes 2183 in use (table end 3672 this level, room
4096); positioned model instances 78373 of 262144; render arena 19 of 64 MB; the draw batch of
renderer 0 category 0: 1597 chunks, the others small.

**Draw batch handle (a game bug).** The add (`0x1436C3960`, its caller `0x1436C8B70`) writes an
instance's handle as `category << 28 | chunk` (`0x1436C3AC8`); the update (`0x1436C8CF3`) and the
take-out (`0x1436D27E8`) decode `chunk = h & 0x3FF`, `batch = h >> 16 & 0xFFF`, `category = h >>
28`, then look for the instance's key (`desc + 0x70`) among the chunk's entries (`chunk + 0x540`,
0x40 apart). For chunk 1024 and up they look in chunk - 1024, don't find it and return: those
instances are never taken out. Live: chunks 0 - 1023 had 38750 instances (418 chunks empty),
chunks 1024 - 1596 had 36638, every one of their keys in unreadable (freed) memory, the low ones'
readable. Those are the only two `and ..., 0x3FF` with a `>> 0x1C` near them in the game's code
(`find_handle_decode.py`; the third hit, `0x143837C89`, is something else). The two helpers called
before them (`0x1436C30A0`, `0x1436C3140`) read a different 64-bit record whose low 10 bits index
the category header's `+0x10` array (a spatial tree's root cells, 3-bit child steps), not chunks.
The other batch users (`0x1436C4840`, `0x1436D1DD0`, the jobs from `0x1436C6339` into
`0x1436D1230`) go by the chunk count. Fix: both masks to 0x7FF (one byte each).

**Batches.** The renderer's constructor (`0x1436C1680`) zeroes 4 categories inline at renderer +
0xA0100 (0x28980 each, pointers at +0x90), puts a 0xA8-byte header object at category + 0 and sets
the batch count (+0x28978) to 1. Nothing else writes the count, and the add always uses the
category's first batch. Live: everything after batch 0 (147824 bytes per category) is zero in all 8
categories. The readers loop over the count, and the job table (`0x1436C63B7`: + 0x3784, 9 slots per
category) has room for 9 batches. So 8 more batches per category are there unused: the way to more
than 2048 chunks, if the add can be made to fill them (the handle already carries the batch; the
header object at batch 0 + 0 is per category and re-made every frame, `0x1436C8C58` /
`0x1436C3230`).

**Mesh index cap.** `0x1435554B1` reads the mesh index as a 16-bit word (record + 4) and caps it
with `min(index, 0xFFF)` (0xFFF from `0x90C3A20F + 0x6F3C6DF0`), not a 12-bit field. The table
itself is an inline array of 4096 (CameraManager.cpp, MeshTableOffset).

**Batch spread, 2026-10-22** (`[Misc] BatchSpreadChunks`, 400 chunks a batch): the
add's hook (`hBatchAdd`) put category 0 into 4 batches (400, 400, 400, 195 chunks); batch 3
emptied again when zones went, batches 1 - 2 filled and emptied while flying; every key
readable in every batch, the header copy at each batch's start current. The renderer's teardown
(`0x1436C1E20`) cleans only each category's own header (`0x1436C2E70` on category + 0, 4 times), so
the copies are never freed. The 11 batch readers outside the renderer (`0x143048E50`,
`0x143179BC0`, `0x14323C3A0`, `0x14325EC90`, `0x143338DE0` + 4 like it, `0x143C2C420`,
`0x143C53070`) all loop over the count, stride 0x4808, chunk pointers at fill - 0x4004. Nothing
looked wrong in game; people and cars were missing in the camera's districts (not yet checked whether
that's the spread or the level only making them near Faith, which it does for their sounds).

**Mesh table, what else is sized for 4096** (manager `[0x142563410]`, constructor `0x14353B8F0`):
- The add (`0x143551D50`): an existing mesh keeps its index (`[rbp + 0x18]` word); else the first
  free record (first qword 0) in [begin, end), else end += 0x350 and the record is zeroed; no
  capacity check. It pushes the new index (u16) onto `+0x384230` (begin) / `+0x384238` (cursor) /
  `+0x384240` (end), an inline buffer at `+0x384250` of 0x2000 bytes (4096 entries), no check.
- `+0x386250`: a bitset of 0x200 bytes (4096 bits), by mesh index, in `0x143550870` (4 uses, each
  behind `cmp index, 0x1000; jae` skip): meshes from 4096 never get their bit.
- `0x1435554B1`: `min(index, 0xFFF)`.
- A record's `+0` is the MeshSet (TypeInfo `0x142835050`); MeshSet `+0x20` -> resource, `+0x58` the
  full name (`mesh_census.py`). Live with the camera's zones (Ground 14/17, Buildings 28/83, Props
  42/238): 3519 in use, 1808 `objects/props`, 1357 `objects/architecture` (366 downtown, 323 anchor,
  218 modules, 167 theview, 144 backdrops, 85 unique), 68 `levels/sp`.
- Every 0xFFF / 0x1000 in the mesh code (`find_4096.py`, 0x143530000 - 0x143580000) and the
  renderer: mesh-number ones are the bitset's four checks (`0x143550B09`, `0x143550C93`,
  `0x143550ED0`, `0x143550FA0`) and three `min(record + 4 word, 0xFFF)` caps before indexing the
  table (`0x1435554D4`, `0x1435555E9`, `0x1435556F9`, disguised constants). The rest are buffer
  sizes (`0x143541280` max(count, 0x1000) for an allocation, `0x143579xxx` 4 KB blocks,
  `0x143564FF0`), flags, or the batch handle's 0xFFF.
- The bitset (`0x143550870`, the streaming pass): a mesh gets its bit when it's in this pass's
  request list (`+0x386880`, 0x14 bytes each, mesh word at `+0xC`, count `+0x386800`); later the bit
  decides whether a request is kept. From 4096 the check jumps to the not-set path, so their
  requests would be treated as no longer wanted.
- Only the constructor writes the table's begin / end / capacity (`0x14353B967` - `0x14353B975`)
  and the add moves the end (`0x143551E42`); nothing clears or moves it, so the table lives with
  the manager and is never emptied. The add takes the manager's lock (`+0x10`, `0x142A9F970`). The
  new-mesh list's cursor is also written at `0x143551C0C` / `0x143551CEA` (in `0x143551BDE`,
  `0x143551C24`).
- Readers don't check for an empty record: `0x1435554B1` reads `[record + 0]` then `[+0x20]`.

**Street traffic and crowds away from Faith** (2026-10-22): with the camera 784 - 927 m from her,
918 - 1144 swarm members within 250 m of it, 0 moved in 5 s with the spread on, 18 with it off
(camera flying); seen in the game with the spread off: highway traffic moves, street traffic and
crowds stand still and aren't drawn. So it isn't the spread; the game only runs them near Faith
(or its own camera).

**Room for 16384 meshes** (`Hooks.cpp` EnlargeMeshTable / hMeshManagerCtor):
right after the code is readable (with the arena patch), if `[0x142563410]` is still null and every
site's bytes match: a 0x800-byte bitset and a 4 KB block within 1 GB of the exe (its first qword =
the bitset's address, then four stubs); the clear (`0x143550A21`) becomes `mov rcx, [slot]` with
size 0x800; the four checks 0x4000; the four uses jump to stubs (`push rax; mov rax, [slot]; or
[rax + r8*8], rdx; pop rax` / `mov rdx, [slot]; mov rdx, [rdx + rax*8]`) and back; the three caps
0x3FFF. Then the constructor (`0x14353B8F0`, called once from `0x1435744A6`, the global stored at
`0x1435744B1` after it returns) is hooked: after it, the table (record 0 only) is copied into a
16384-record block and the new-mesh list pointed at a 32768-entry one. The manager is made in a
module's init (`0x143574140`, vtable entry `0x141BC4238`); whether the tools get there first is
logged. Read back offline (the same changes applied to a copy of the image and disassembled).

**Zone slots, 512 per streamer** (`Hooks.cpp` EnlargeZoneSlots): the 128 slots
(`+0x2F8`) are used only by the constructor `0x143C7DB00` (clears 0x400 bytes; called for
ZoneStreamerEntity, vtable `0x141C6E2E8`, from `0x143A20AA9`, and for its base from `0x143C7F27E`;
RealmProxy has its own layout), the load's search (`0x143C80255` `mov r8d, 0x80`, the compare
`0x143C80264`, the write `0x143C80280`; with none free it writes slot 0xFFFF), two readers
(`0x143C81703`, `0x143C81C97`) and the release (`lea rbx, [rsi + rax*8]` at `0x143C81F46` /
`0x143C81FD8`, then `[rbx + 0x2F8]`). The release (`0x143C81E60`) and the load pass
(`0x143C81D20`) gather the zones they handle (zones only, below the ZoneInfos count; regions are
handled one at a time from the top) into a 128-entry u16 array on their stack (`rsp + 0x30`, the
cookie at `+0x130`) with no check; they're called from the update (`0x143C81A12` / `A1A`), the step
(`0x143C81CD0`) and `0x143C81732` / `73A`. A second call with the same request bits would handle
a zone twice (the release with slot + 1 = 0 reads slot 0xFFFF). Live before: 19, 64 and 102 slots in
use (ground, buildings, props).

**Whole city, first limit: the renderer's instance list** (every district Always, BatchSpreadChunks
1700): every bundle got a slot (20 / 95 / 253), slot blocks consistent; 65 of 83 building and 126 of 238
prop zones loaded, the rest still loading, when the game crashed at `+0x36C4135` reading 0x2FC7B6758, in
the renderer's instance add (`0x1436C40B0`): it pops the free list's head (`renderer + 0x142908`) from
the u32 array at `renderer + 0x142768` (made by `0x1436BFC90`: next[i] = i + 1, the last -1, 200000 long,
with a u64 array beside it; size `0x90C3050F + 0x6F400831` = 0x30D40). At the crash the fullest category
had 191325 instances in 2990 chunks: the list ran out; -1 as the index read and wrote 16 GB past it
(r8 0x3C2D6ADA came from there) and the next add faulted. The batch spread's room (9 x 1700 x 64)
was far above the list, so the tools didn't hold back. Fix: 1000000 (and
`0x1436BFD62` / `0x1436BFD99`'s sizes x 4 / x 8), the tools count each renderer's instances (all
categories) against its array's length; render memory 128 MB; model instance room 8x the game's.

**Whole city, second limit: the instance record pool:** with that, it crashed twice at
`+0x35777D4` with 260645 / 263790 renderer instances (meshes 5530 / 5617, model instances 244k of
524288, arena 48 MB of 128). `0x143577780` hands out 0xA0-byte instance records from blocks of
0x28000 (1024 records; size `0xC390A20F + 0x3C71DDF1`, end `add rax, 0x28000` at `0x1435777E6`),
the blocks' addresses in room for 256 at pool + 0 (count `+0x800`, block `+0x808`, cursor `+0x810`,
end `+0x818`, allocator `+0x820`), no check: block 257 is written over the count. The pool is at +0x40
of an object made by `0x143567680` (it clears the 256 slots, 0x800 bytes; records list `+0x868`, free
records `+0x888`); its only grower is called from `0x14356ACD3`. Fix tried: blocks of 0xA0000
(4096 records, 1048576 in all); the tools count min(instance list, records) as the renderer's room.
**Correction, the same day:** the bigger blocks crashed at once (`+0x357B9C8` writing
0x1D6A0, 1339 instances): a record's number picks its block as number >> 10 and its place as number
& 0x3FF (`0x14357B9B7` / `0x14357B9AE`, in `0x14357B970`: blocks at pool + number >> 10 * 8, record at
block + (number & 0x3FF) * 0xA0), so record 1024 was looked for in a block that didn't exist. Taken
out; the tools count the records' room (262144, less 32768 margin) instead. More records would need
the 256 block pointers (pool + 0 .. + 0x800, the count right after) moved, and every place that reads
them by number found.

**Whole city, held at the record pool** (every district Always): no crash. The tools held back at
180043 of 229376 records and took zones away at 198887; then Ground 16/17, Buildings 25/83, Props
115 + 25 loading of 238, 193524 renderer instances, 4818 meshes, arena 36.7 MB. The record pool is the
last limit seen. Reads of a record by number (`[pool owner + (n >> 10) * 8 + 0x40]`): `0x14356AE3E`,
`0x1435730E4`, `0x1435735B9`, `0x1435736C6`, `0x1435737BF`, `0x14357392A`, `0x14357B9AE`,
`0x14357BA32`, `0x14357BB1E` (from `find` of `and 0x3FF` + `shr 0xA` + `[.. * 8 + 0x40]`; loops over all
blocks not searched yet).

**Past the hold-back:** the tools hold at about 185000; with *Unrestricted* on (crash note: "UNRESTRICTED", renderer instances 263078 of 229376) the game crashes at
`+0x356AF57` (writing 0x0), in the record pool's add: the pool runs out, as expected.

**Record pool moved** (`Hooks.cpp` EnlargeRecordPool / hRecordOwnerCtor): the owner is
made once (`0x1431A10E7` -> `0x143567680`, kept at `0x142563A30`; checked null at start-up). Every use
of the block list (a search of every `[x + y*8 + 0x40]` in 0x143567000 - 0x14357C000 and in the 81
functions that reach the global; the two others are an allocation size and another structure): the

**Record pool, two misses** (a crash at `+0x357333D` reading 0x79A52000 =
the end of the tools' 8 KB block list): a tenth read `add rdx, [rsi + rcx*8 + 0x40]` at

**Whole city, done:** every zone loaded (17 / 83 / 238, nothing loading for 20 s),

**Crash, Never while loading.** Default switched Always -> Never 3 s after it went
back to Always (a ground zone had just been asked to load again): `+0x3C7FCA4` reading 0x10, from
`0x143C81C40` (in the streamer update `0x143C81900`, before its step): for each bundle with flag 4
(loading) and not 2 (unload asked) it asks the loader about slot (word + 2) - 1 (the tools' reader 2
stub); the slot word was 0 (rax 0xFFFF), so the slot was null. `0x143C81C40` also drops flag 4 of a
bundle asked to unload, before the game's step. The tools' Never code runs the step (`0x143C81CD0`,
release then load pass, then the request bits cleared) from the update hook, which comes before
`0x143C81C40`: it asked the still-loading zone to unload, the release took its slot and left flag 4.
Fix: MarkNeverZones leaves a loading zone until it has loaded, and before the tools' step
any bundle with flags 2 and 4 drops 4 (as `0x143C81C40` does). Old bug of the Never districts, not of
the whole-city patches.

**The reflection volume limit, where it's used (offline).** `0x1436F02E0` (called once per view and frame from
`0x14372E950` in `0x14372D9B0`, rcx = `[0x142568CE0]`, the frame allocator) makes a 0x630-byte tile object
from the frame allocator and copies the tile pass's limits from WorldRenderSettings (r8), each
min(setting, 0x200 fixed at `0x1436F03C6`), each 0 when its Enable is off: +0x2F4 -> obj +0x54C (enable
+0x46C), +0x2F8 -> +0x550 (+0x46D), +0x2FC -> +0x554 (+0x46E), +0x300 -> +0x558 (+0x46F), **+0x304
MaxLocalReflectionVolumeCount -> obj +0x55C** (TilePassLocalReflectionVolumeEnable +0x470), +0x308 next.
`0x143624D10` (from `0x14362DA60`, called through a pointer, rip ref at `0x143623421`): allocates obj +0x5A8
pointers, gathers (`0x143625120`) into r8's struct, then **count +0x10 = min(count, obj +0x55C)** at
`0x143624DA3` and allocates count * 0xB0: past 512 the rest are dropped without a word, in gather order.
`0x1436314E1` clamps another count the same way ([rbp - 0x10]), +0x560 for the next. So: 512 local
reflection volumes per view and frame at most, the code's own ceiling as well as the setting. The live
count only exists inside a frame (frame-allocated object), so reading it needs a hook in the DLL (after
`0x143625120` returns in `0x143624D10`: [r8 + 0x10] before the clamp). GenericEntityMaxVisibleEntityCount
(+0x1C0): not traced (the offset is common, 52 hits in 0x1435 - 0x1439).
