# 3. Replaying KrugerSec fights 1:1: the AI system and how to get it into the replay

2026-10-23. Research for the replay (REPLAY tab, FaithReplay). Offline disassembly of the game image plus read-only live reads (Faith's pose, a census of the level's characters). Addresses are for the game build 0x5762E3B7. Where something isn't known yet, it says so.

### 1. The one approach that can be 1:1

There are two ways to replay a fight:

- **Run the AI again from the same start.** That can't be made 1:1. The AI reacts to physics, timing, randomness and to the real Faith, who stands still during playback. The game has no deterministic replay: its own replay component records only Faith's pose.
- **Record what the fight shows and play that back.** That's how the replay already works for Faith, doors, elevators and KSec bodies. Every visible or audible output of the fight is recorded, and the live game's own versions are kept out of the way while it plays.

So the plan below covers each output of a fight: what produces it in the game, and how it gets recorded and played.

### 2. What a fight is made of in the game

| Part | The game's classes (client side unless said) | What's known |
|---|---|---|
| Guard bodies | `PamClientCharacterEntity` (body = ANT animatable at +0x248); skeletons of 163 / 162 / 169 bones; pedestrians 82 | Posed by our override (done). The update gates are described in section 3. |
| AI brain | `PamServerAIBrainComponent` / `PamClientAIBrainComponent` (client slot 65 = 0x1439336D0) | The client brain turns the body's "always update" off once the guard dies (0x143981A80); 0x143936820 turns it on. |
| AI behaviour | `PamAIState*` and `PamAIAction*` (e.g. `PamAIStateGoDespawn`: MinPlayerDistance +0x28, MinPlayerAngle +0x2C, LookForDespawnAS +0x30) | Server side; not needed for a recorded-output replay. |
| Spawning | `PamServerAIAutoSpawnCoordinator` (vtable 0x141C431B0), `PamServerAIAutoSpawnGroup` (0x141C432A8; data: MaxContextualDistance +0x60, MinContextualDistance +0x64, MaxContextualAngle +0x68, Enabled +0x6C), `PamServerCharacterSpawnEntity`, `PamServerAIAirSpawnPointProvider` | The open-world KSec groups. A group took all its guards out at once when Faith ran off, past the auto-despawn hold (seen in game). A diagnostic in the tools logs which call does it. |
| Auto despawn | `PamServerAIAutoDespawnManager` slot 26 0x143982AE0, base 0x142CB2FE0 | Held while the replay holds people (done). It saw no removals (seen in game). |
| Guns | `PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity` (an actor: data Mesh +0x90, MoveAnimatableWithActor +0x98, WeaponDrop +0xA0) | Its transform code is the static models' getter (slot 24 0x1432E1440) plus its own setter (slot 25 0x143903F10 -> 0x1438FB260 -> 0x1432E8300). Whether a held gun follows the replayed hand is **not known**: that needs a live look during playback. |
| Shooting | Fire managers `PamClientAIFireManagerBase` -> `PamClientAIBurstFireManager` -> heli / drone variants; `PamClientWeaponFiringComponent`; bullets `PamClientBulletEntity` -> `ClientBulletEntity` -> `ClientProjectileEntity` | Muzzle flashes, tracers and impacts are made per shot. Not traced yet. |
| Drones | `PamClientDroneActorEntity` (an actor; data: KillForce*, UnspawnWhenKilledTime +0xB0, MinPlayerDistance +0xB4, MinPlayerAngle +0xB8), `PamServerDroneActorEntity`, `PamServerDroneEnemyManager`, drone AI states | Not traced live (none in the level during the census). |
| VTOL | `PamClientAIHeliFireManager`, `PamClientAIAirLoco` (a locomotion component, so a character-like AI), `PamAIStateHeliFlyOffAndDespawn` | Likely an AI character with air locomotion, which our people recorder may already catch if it's within 40 m. **Not checked live.** |
| Faith's health | `PamServerHumanHealthComponent` slot 32 0x143923EA0 (the AI's health is another class) | Hooked: no damage while a replay plays. |
| Sounds | The existing replay sound hooks (voices, sound entity events) | Records Faith's sound entities only, so far. |

### 3. Why the dead stayed dead (done) and what's left of it

A body is only updated when its update job (0x1432DE310 on animatable + 0x70) finds it needed. That's when 0x1432E86D0 sees one of these, and update mode 4 never qualifies:
- +0xFC set, or
- +0x5C0 set, or
- "always update" (+0x5C3) set with an update mode ([+0x118] + 0x10) other than 1 or 3, or
- AntSettings' ForcePoseUpdate.

A guard's AI turns "always update" off a few seconds after he dies. From then on his ragdoll body is never updated, so an override on it does nothing.

- The replay turns it back on, with the game's own switch (0x1432E7EA0), for bodies the replay poses. When the replay stops, it puts their own pose back and turns the switch off again.
- It does the same for a body whose update stops *during* playback: a guard killed near the end of the recording is let go by his AI only once playback has begun.

### 4. The plan, part by part

Each part comes with its record and playback steps and what it needs first.

1. **Keep every recorded guard in the level** (blocker for everything else). A diagnostic logs the game code on the stack whenever a character is destroyed while the replay holds people. From that, the group-release call gets the same kind of hold as the auto-despawn. Needs: one recording in which Faith runs off from a group.
2. **Guns.**
   - If held guns already follow the replayed hand, there's nothing to do.
   - If they don't, record each gun's transform at Faith's samples (getter slot 24) and set it while playing, the way doors are moved. A setter that only moves what's drawn may be needed, as for the doors; to be checked.
   - Dropped guns move by physics; recording their transform covers those too.
   - Needs: a live read while a replay with guards plays.
3. **Shots: muzzle flash, tracer, impact, gunfire sound.**
   - Record each shot of a recorded guard: time, gun, muzzle transform, direction.
   - Play it back through the same visual-only client code. Client bullets don't do the damage; the server does. That's to be confirmed before anything is built.
   - Needs: tracing the client shot path (the fire manager -> the bullet entity's creation), offline first.
4. **Guard sounds** (voice lines, gunfire, footsteps, gear).
   - Widen the replay's sound recording from Faith's sound entities to the entities of the recorded guards, guns, drones and VTOL.
   - Play them back the way hers are played. While it plays, the live guards' sounds are silenced.
   - Needs: knowing which sound entities belong to a guard (by owner, or by attachment to the body).
5. **Drones.** They're actors, so treat them like guns: record the transform, plus the pose if they're animated, and play it back. Their AI and shots come under items 3 and 4. Needs: a drone in the level.
6. **VTOL.**
   - If it's a character with a body, the people recorder takes it, with a larger radius for it (it's big and flies above).
   - If it isn't, record it as an actor.
   - Guards it drops are characters that appear during the recording; the recorder's time windows already handle those.
   - Needs: a VTOL in the level.
7. **The live game under the replay.** Already in place:
   - non-recorded people near the replayed Faith are hidden;
   - Faith takes no damage;
   - the auto-despawn is held.

   Still open: the live guards keep shooting and shouting at the real Faith while it plays. Item 4's silencing covers the sound. Their bodies are hidden or posed, so their shots are the only thing left to see. A full pause of the live AI would need hooking its update. That's possible, but its side effects are unknown, so it isn't planned until items 1-6 are done.

### 5. What needs the game in a certain state (live, read-only)

Everything below is read with targeted reads; nothing is written from outside.

- **Guns:** a recording with guards kept, played on loop, with the guards in view. Each gun's place is read against the replayed hand.
- **Drones / VTOL:** a recording with a drone or a VTOL. With the game left in the encounter, their classes, bodies and transforms are read.
- **Removal path:** one recording in which Faith runs off from a group. The diagnostic's log then names the call.

<a id="n4"></a>

# 4. Replay sync research: KrugerSec, elevators, doors, the MagRope line (2026-10-23)

Goal: while the replay plays Faith's recording, the world around her plays along: the
KrugerSec she fought, the doors and elevators she used, and the MagRope's line.

What the replay does today (`Camera/FaithReplay.cpp`): it records Faith's pose (every bone, 30 times a
second) and plays it back on her own body through the animation system's pose override (the Dash
ghost's way). Faith herself stays where she is, so nothing in the world reacts: doors stay shut,
elevators stay put, KrugerSec stand where they are, and the MagRope's line isn't drawn.

Everything below was read from the game's code in `game_image.bin` (offline). Nothing was read live.
**Verified** means read in the code; **to check** means it needs a live read or a test first.

### 1. Doors and elevators: the level's timelines

There's no door or elevator entity type in the game (no type name with Door, Elevator or Lift). The
level moves such things with the generic **TimelineEntity**: a time that runs and tracks of values
(`TransformPropertyTrackData`, `TransformPartPropertyTrackData`, float, bool and event tracks) linked
to the parts it moves. The 21 moving backdrop elevators (`bd_animated_csg_elevator_01`, census
2026-10-18) are static models that something moves; the doors are likely the same.

**Verified (code):**
- TimelineEntity: TypeInfo `0x14283BEB0`, vtable `0x141BEAB28`, constructor `0x14368D590`
  (vtable put in place at `0x14368D5BE`; the other `lea` is at `0x14368DC83`, likely the destructor),
  event handler slot 4 `0x14368FD20`.
- TimelineEntityData fields: TimelineData +0x20, BlendInTime +0x28, BlendOutTime +0x2C, InitTime +0x30,
  StartTime +0x34, EndTime +0x38, JumpTime +0x3C, PlaybackRate +0x40, **ExternalTime +0x44**,
  UpdatePassFlags +0x48, AutoPlay +0x4A, UseRealTimeClock +0x4B, AutoInitConnectedProperties +0x4C,
  ResetTimeOnStarted +0x4D, AllowAnimationCarryForward +0x4E, SyncTimelines +0x4F,
  RuntimeFramerate +0x50, Looping +0x51, Infinite +0x52.
- The entity's own copies, read in the constructor: property refs (each {link, the data's value}) at
  +0x30 StartTime, +0x40 EndTime, +0x50 PlaybackRate, +0x60 ExternalTime, +0x70 Looping, +0x80
  Infinite. Its time is at **+0x98** (and +0x9C, the time before), set from `0x143690A50` (the start
  time). Its **CurrentTime** output is the connection at +0xB0 with its value at +0xB8.
- **SetTime: `0x143691120` (timeline, float time in xmm1, bool force in r8b).** Without force it does
  nothing while ExternalTime is linked (+0x60 not null). It writes +0x9C, +0x98, +0xC8 and clears
  +0xCC, after `0x14369E5B0` / `0x1436926C0` (likely the tracks being evaluated, to check). The
  game calls it from the timeline's event handler (`0x14368FECF`, seeking to StartTime) and with
  force from `0x14325CCFB`.
- Restart (vtable slot 13, `0x143692100`): sets +0x400 = 1, then the start time into +0x98 / +0x9C
  / +0xC8 / +0xBC / +0xC0, clears +0xC4 / +0xCC.
- Property names are hashed with `h = 5381; h = h * 33 ^ c`. The hashes are loaded split (`mov r9d, a;
  lea r9d, [r9 + b]`). Offline tools: `hashrefs.py` finds the code for a field name,
  `hashname.py` names a hash.

**How the replay could sync them:**
1. Note every TimelineEntity as the game makes and removes it (hook the constructor and destructor,
   with byte checks, like the sound entities).
2. While the replay records, keep each timeline's time (+0x98) once per replay frame, but only for
   the timelines whose time changes during the recording.
3. When playback starts, save each recorded timeline's live time. During playback, call SetTime with
   force for each one, every frame, with the recorded time. When playback stops, give back the saved
   live times.

**To check before building:**
- Which timelines move a door or an elevator. A live watch while Faith opens a door and rides an
  elevator, logging which timelines' +0x98 changed, would show it (read-only).
- Whether SetTime with force moves the linked parts the same frame, and whether it fires the event
  tracks between the old and new time. Event tracks could start the level's logic again: alarms,
  scripted scenes, sounds. If it does, sync only timelines with no event tracks, or look for a
  SetTime that doesn't fire events.
- Moving platforms Faith stands on are physics. Moving one under the frozen real Faith could push
  her.
- Other movers that may be involved: `PamClientMoverEntity` (TypeInfo `0x14285EBB0`, vtable
  `0x141C61F48`; its data has only Realm, so it's driven by what's linked to it) and
  `ClientSyncedSequenceEntity` (`SyncedSequenceEntityData` + 0x58 InterpolateTime).

### 2. The MagRope's line

**Verified (code):**
- The line is drawn by **PamClientMagropeRenderEntity** (TypeInfo `0x142854230`, vtable
  `0x141C410F8`, constructor `0x14391DCD0`). It's a subclass of **PamClientRopeRenderEntity**
  (TypeInfo `0x14285E770`, vtable `0x141C5DFE0`, constructor `0x1439AB3F0`), whose data is
  `PamRopeRenderEntityData`: Model +0x18, Skeleton +0x20. So the line is a skinned model whose joints
  run from Faith's hand to the anchor (`PamMagRopeRenderJoint`).
- The render entity's properties, from its constructor: **Anchor** (property ref at +0x130, accessor
  `0x144794BD0`), a transform it hands out at +0x140 (hash 0x45F8E9D1, no name string in the game),
  and **TargetTransform** at +0x148. Its fields +0xC8 to +0x150 are zeroed.
- The anchors in the world are **PamClientMagropeEntity** (TypeInfo `0x14285ED90`, vtable
  `0x141C619E0`; 33 of them near Faith on 2026-10-18).
- **PamClientMagRopeVisualizerEntity** is the swing hint. Its data (`PamMagropeVisualizerData`) has
  MapSplineMeshEnter +0x18, Scale +0x20, PlayerHandPosition +0x30, ClosestMagRope +0x40,
  MapSplineMeshExit +0x50, IsPlayerSwinging +0x58 and isMagRopeInRange +0x59. Its accessors are
  `0x14477F930` / `0x14477D6E0` / `0x1447807A0`, all three called from `0x143942xxx`.

**How the replay could sync it:**
1. Note the MagRope render entity (constructor hook).
2. While recording, keep each frame whether the line is shown, plus its two ends (Anchor and the hand
   side), or the joint transforms it builds.
3. During playback, show it with the recorded ends while the recording had it shown. The cleanest
   way is to hand its Anchor / target properties the recorded transforms, the same trick as the
   crowd tracker hook (`out = { null, &recorded }`). The line would then follow Faith's replayed hand.

**To check:** how the line is shown and hidden (a flag in the render entity, or the entity being made
and removed for each swing), and which transform is the hand. A live read during one swing would
settle both.

### 3. KrugerSec encounters

**Verified (code, earlier research):** KrugerSec are **PamClientCharacterEntity**, the same class as
Faith. There are two entities per character and 23 near Faith in one census. The replay's pose
override works on any **ClientAntAnimatableEntity** (TypeInfo `0x1427EEE10`): the pose handle is
`[[animatable + 0x158] + 0x118]`, and the pose manager comes through animatable + 0x1B8. That's how
the Dash ghost runners are posed.

**How the replay could sync them:**
1. While recording, also record the pose (every bone) of each character within, say, 60 m of Faith.
   It's the same sampling as Faith's, per character, keyed by the character entity.
2. During playback, hand each one an override of the recorded pose, with a slot of its own in its
   pose manager, as for Faith. Their bodies then act out the fight where it happened (the root bone
   carries their world position).
3. Their sounds come along with the same "replay sounds" code: their SoundEntities' voice events,
   with the filter widened from Faith's sound names to theirs (`ME_Sound/Character/AI/...` and their
   VO).

**To check:**
- How to reach an NPC's animatable. Faith's comes through her recording component (soldier +
  `SoldierRecordingComponentOffset`, then + 0x50), which NPCs may not have. Other routes: the
  character's component list, or the soldier + 0x340 box animatable as on Faith (`characters_near.py`
  lists them, read-only).
- Whether their weapons follow the overridden pose (they're attached to a hand bone) and what
  ragdolls (KOs) do with an override. Muzzle flashes, tracers and impacts aren't part of a pose, so
  they won't play.
- Their AI keeps running in the real world (they may attack the frozen Faith). Playing the replay
  with the fight over, or with them out of combat, avoids that.

### 4. Order of work

1. A read-only diagnostic: constructor/destructor registries for TimelineEntity, the MagRope
   render entity and the characters, and a 30 s log of which timelines move and what the rope
   entity's fields do.
2. Timeline sync (recorded times, SetTime with force, live times given back at the end).
3. The MagRope line (recorded ends handed to its properties).
4. KrugerSec poses (the pose override per character), then their sounds.

### 5. Camera improvements that could be made (not in the menu now)

Judged from the tools' options today: free camera, tracks with keyframes, Follow / Nearby, the replay,
motion blur, field of view, smoothing, freeze time, HUD, time of day, VISUALS' DoF settings.

1. **Look-at mode**: the camera flies freely or along a track but keeps aiming at Faith or a Nearby
   object (Follow moves with the target; this would only turn).
2. **Autofocus and keyframed focus**: DoF focus distance taken from what the camera aims at (the aim
   pick exists) or from the followed target, and kept per keyframe on tracks.
3. **Track timing**: constant speed along the path instead of time per keyframe, and easing (ease
   in / out) per keyframe.
4. **Handheld shake**: procedural noise on rotation and position, with amplitude and frequency, also
   per keyframe.
5. **Slow motion**: only Freeze time exists. A game time scale (0.1x to 1x) needs research.
6. **Near clip plane**: getting very close to objects without them being cut. The render view's
   near plane needs finding (the far plane is already written).
7. **Composition overlays**: a rule-of-thirds grid, letterbox bars (2.39:1, 1.85:1), safe frames.
8. **Orbit mode**: the mouse circles the camera round Faith or a target at a set distance.
9. **Several replay takes at once**: more than one recorded Faith playing together. The game's ghost
   runners can do it, and their red look is the character data's PamUseRunnersGhostShader (+0xE8),
   which can be cleared.
10. **World sync for the replay** (sections 1 to 4 above).

# 5. How Mirror's Edge Catalyst makes its shadows

2026-10-23, game build 0x5762E3B7. Offline disassembly of the decrypted game image, checked against read-only live reads of the running game (Faith near (-157, 78, 23) in the city, then (438, 98, 276)). Each claim says how it's known:

- **[live]** read from the running game;
- **[code]** read from the disassembly;
- **[notes]** from the earlier offline work in MEC_Reverse_Notes.md (2026-10-22), not re-checked this time;
- **[not traced]** known to exist, not followed.

This is research only. Nothing in the game or the tools was changed.

### 1. Where everything lives

| What | Where | How known |
|---|---|---|
| World renderer | `[[0x142563A10] + 0x1E8] + 0x30`. The tools' `VisualsManager::GetStateManager` (`[[[[0x142142A48] + 0x50] + 0x90] + 0x1C0] + 0x30`) is the same object (0x1F95D4190), so it's the world renderer, not a visual-environment manager. | [live] |
| Views | count at world renderer + 0xA94 (1 now); **view state i = world renderer + 0xB00 + i * 0x89400**. | [code] 0x14374B862, [live] |
| Main camera view | view state + 0xBD0 (a view object, layout below); a second copy at view state + 0x10F0 (the one the cascade code copies). | [code], [live]: both at the camera, FOV 1.5708, near 0.06, far 25000 |
| Settings used by the view | `[view state + 0x882B8]`: the world renderer's copy at + 0x118 (or + 0x110, picked per frame at 0x14372E0B0). The world renderer also holds the global at + 0x120. | [code] 0x14372E0C7, 0x14374FD8E; [live] |
| Global WorldRenderSettings | `[0x14240C2B8]` (what the tools write). | [live] |
| Visual environment values in the view state | CameraParams block at view state + 0x85520: SunShadowmapViewDistance + 0x8552C, ShadowDistanceScale + 0x85534. | [code] 0x143735CCD, [live] |

**Correction to the notes.** The earlier notes and `shadow_live.py` read "near / far" at "VE manager + 0xCBC / + 0xCC0" and found zeros. Those offsets belong to the view state (world renderer + 0xB00). The main view's near is at world renderer + 0xB00 + 0xCBC, and its far at + 0xCC0.

**The settings copies: refreshed from the global every frame [code, live].**

- The world renderer's constructor (0x14371CFF0) clones the global into + 0x118 and + 0x110 (`0x142A861D0`).
- Every frame, the world renderer's frame (0x14372D9B0, at 0x14372DAD7 / 0x14372DAFF, on every path) calls **0x143759730(global, copy, ...)** for each copy. That function:
  1. clones the copy as "before";
  2. copies the whole global into the copy (`0x142A871D0(copy, global)`);
  3. forces some fields (below);
  4. compares about 120 fields with "before", among them ShadowmapResolution, SliceCount, ShadowmapsEnable, the 16-bit formats, MaxShadowCount and the spot shadow settings, and returns whether any changed. That result goes back to the frame (r14b), which reads like "render resources must be rebuilt"; what the frame does with it wasn't read.
- **Live:** a hook on the copy's + 0x64 saw it follow the tools' Shadow distance slider (the tools write only the global).

Fields forced in the main (+ 0x118) copy [code]:
- MaxShadowCount to 1..42;
- MaxLocalPlanarReflectionCount at most 6;
- MaxSpotAndPointLightShadowmapCount = 1 when ShadowOptimisationEstimateEnable;
- SkyEnvmapSidesPerFrameCount = 6, SkyEnvmapResolution a power of two ≥ 16, LocalIBLResolution a power of two ≥ 8;
- MultisampleCount must be 1, 2 or 4 (else 1), MultisampleQuality = 0;
- ShadowmapResolution rounded up to a multiple of 8 when TransparencyShadowmapsEnable and TransparencyShadowmapsHalfRes;
- a few GPU-dependent switches.

These explain all six dwords where the live copy differed from the global (+0x8 is the object's header).

The + 0x110 copy (5th argument 1; the local-IBL / reflection captures) also:
- takes ShadowmapSliceCount = LocalIBLShadowmapSliceCount and ShadowmapResolution = LocalIBLShadowmapResolution;
- has no transparency shadows and no cascade transition blend;
- turns off motion blur, sub-surface scattering, split lighting and others.

The constructor also clears the global's LightTileUseCsIndirectClears (+0x42B) on NVIDIA GPUs (vendor 0x10DE).

#### A view object (from its setters, 0x143536A70 - 0x143536F10)

| Offset | Field |
|---|---|
| +0x00 .. +0x3F | world matrix (rows; + 0x30 = position) |
| +0xE0 | projection type (1 = orthographic) |
| +0xE4 | FOV |
| +0xEC | near |
| +0xF0 | far |
| +0xF4 | aspect |
| +0xF8 / +0xFC | ortho width / height |
| +0xE8 | **reference FOV for LOD: 0.95993 rad = 55°**, set by the view constructor (0x14352CB10, `mov [rcx+0xE8], 0x3F75BE0C`) and copied with the view; no other writer found [code; 0.9599 live] |
| +0x120 | dirty flags |
| +0x290 | from the FOV setter 0x143536A90 (FOV and aspect) |
| +0x294 | 1 / (2 · tan(FOV / 2)) |
| +0x298 | **the LOD factor = tan(FOV / 2) / tan(55° / 2)** (0x143537B50; maths call identified as tan from the live values) |
| +0x29C | the LOD factor squared |

The LOD factor is the one the shadow caster cut uses (3.6). Live: FOV 1.5708 (90°) gives 1.921, matching the read value exactly. FOV is the view's +0xE4, a vertical FOV: the setter derives the other axis with the aspect.

### 3. Sun shadows, step by step

The world renderer's frame (its vtable slot at 0x141BFAC98 = 0x14372D9B0) calls 0x14374B750. That function calls, for each view, **0x1437356A0(world renderer, ..., view state)**, the shadow setup, which handles the sun, the dynamic envmap's shadow and the spot lights. r14 is the view state and r15 the settings copy. [code]

#### 3.1 On or off [code]

Sun shadows are made only when all of these hold:
- OutdoorLightEnable (+0x419) is set;
- view state + 0x88273 is set;
- the range d (3.2) is above **0.2 m** (0x141A1198C);
- the sun vector at view state + 0x845F0 has a squared length of at least **0.0001**.

Otherwise the 4 matrix slots are filled with a neutral matrix (0x1437369E9).

#### 3.2 The range: how far from the camera the cascades reach [code 0x143735CA1, live]

```
d = min(main view far - near, ShadowmapViewDistance)     // 25000 - 0.06 and 200 -> 200
d = max(d, 0)
if CameraParams.SunShadowmapViewDistance >= 0: d = it    // the visual environment: 125 here -> 125
if ShadowmapViewDistanceScaleEnable: d *= view state + 0x26C8    // 1.0 here
if ShadowmapViewDistance < 0: d = -ShadowmapViewDistance  // a negative setting wins over everything (no scale)
```

Live, at both places read: **d = 125 m**, the level's visual environment.

**What the two view state values are [code, live].** View state + 0x26C8 (the range scale) and + 0x26CC (the cascade minimum FOV) come from the view descriptor's + 0x1BE8 / + 0x1BEC. The game's render view carries them at + 0x1100 / + 0x1104; the descriptor builder 0x1431E66A0 takes them from there at 0x1431E6C0D. The camera code **0x143277100** fills the render view from the active camera:

- **render view + 0x1100 (→ + 0x26C8)** = `[[camera + 0xF8] + 0x3C]` = the camera's **CameraData.ShadowViewDistanceScale**; 1.0 without a camera. The render view's constructor (0x143195C80) defaults it to 1.0. Live: 1.0.
- **render view + 0x1104 (→ + 0x26CC)** = −1 by default (off). When the camera says so (its vtable + 0x48), it's (its vtable + 0x40 value + an offset read from the caller's object + 0x1B80) × π × 1/180: a camera FOV in degrees turned into radians. The setup uses it, else ShadowmapMinFov, as the cascade frustum's minimum FOV. Live: −1.
- + 0x1108 (→ + 0x1BF0) = `0x143328E80(camera)`, else 1.0; + 0x10FC = camera + 0x108, else −1. These two aren't used by the sun setup as far as read.

- **The tools' Shadow distance has no effect where a visual environment sets SunShadowmapViewDistance.** It writes a positive ShadowmapViewDistance (+0x64), and the visual environment's value replaces that.
- **A negative ShadowmapViewDistance is the one value that wins everywhere.** The last line of the code above makes d its absolute value, whatever the visual environment says.
- d is a **depth along the camera's view direction**, from its near plane. It is not a height or a distance on the ground. Nothing in this code reads the camera's height.

#### 3.3 The cascade splits [code 0x1437264A0, live]

With n = ShadowmapSliceCount, w = ShadowmapSliceSchemeWeight and near = the view's near:

```
split_i = w * near * (d / near)^(i / n)  +  (1 - w) * (near + (d - near) * i / n)
split_0 = near; split_1 *= ShadowmapFirstSliceScale; split_n = d
```

This is the standard parallel-split scheme: log and even splits blended. Live (near 0.06, d 125, w 0.88): **0.06 / 4.1 / 9.9 / 27.5 / 125 m.**

#### 3.4 Each cascade's light view [code 0x1437264A0, 0x143725DE0; live]

For each slice, 0x1437264A0 does the following:
1. It copies the main view (`0x14352D4C0`), sets its near and far to the slice's splits, and takes its 8 corners (`0x143537730`).
2. It turns the corners into light space and takes their box. Slice 0's box also takes in a point 0.2 m along the view, from the global float 0x142111AF0 = -0.2.
3. If ShadowmapMinFov is set (> 0), a view narrower than it is widened to it (0x143536A90).

0x143725DE0 then makes the slice's orthographic shadow view:
- **Near plane:** the box's light-space top, moved ShadowmapExtrusionLength (1000 m) toward the sun. So anything up to 1000 m sunward of the slice can cast into it.
- **Depth:** box depth × ShadowmapSizeZScale + the extrusion; with FixedDepth, a fixed depth.
- **Position:** with ShadowmapFixedMovementEnable, the width, height and centre are snapped to whole texels of ShadowmapResolution (`0x142A665A0`), so cascades don't shimmer as the camera moves.
- **Texture matrix:** the projection's 0.5 scale-and-bias, with a reversed-depth variant picked by `[[0x142563300] + 0x5C]`.

After the slices, one more view over the whole range (near to d) is built the same way: the "cull volume" view.

Live slices:

| Slice | Ortho size | Far | Distance from the camera |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 16.4 m | 1008 m | about 1000 m toward the sun |
| 1 | 39.4 m | 1017 m | about 1000 m toward the sun |
| 2 | 109.5 m | 1048 m | about 1000 m toward the sun |
| 3 | 497.2 m | 1223 m | about 1000 m toward the sun |

All four have near 0.5 m.

#### 3.5 Where the cascades go [code 0x143736593 - 0x1437369E7]

- **Slice views:** three copies each, at view state + 0x7B7B0 + i × 0x1C20 (+ 0xF0, + 0x610, + 0xB30). Each slice's viewport is x = ShadowmapResolution × i, width and height = the resolution, so the slices sit side by side in one strip.
- **Texture matrices:** view state + 0x7B6B0 + i × 0x40, copied to the shader constants at view state + 0x844A0 (4 slots; unused ones neutral).
- **Shader constants:** + 0x84630 holds the resolution and 1 / resolution; + 0x84688 the slice count; + 0x8468C the 32-bit slice count.
- **Shadow map textures** are allocated per slice (+ 0x7B640 / + 0x7B660 / + 0x7B680). The shared accumulation targets are used instead when ShadowmapAccumEnable and ShadowmapAccumReuseEnable are set.
- **Culling:** each slice is added to the frame's view list with flag 8 (shadow view), plus flag 0x10 when view state + 0x88274 asks for transparency shadows. The scene is then culled once per shadow view.

**The other cascade builder.** 0x143727470 is a separate builder used only when settings + 0x484 is set and view state + 0xAF0 == 1, with + 0xAF8 deciding per face. The class dump names + 0x484 LocalIBLShadowmapFaceMerging, so this is likely the local-IBL (reflection probe) capture views. It isn't used for the main camera. [code]

#### 3.6 Which meshes cast into a cascade [code, re-checked 2026-10-23; numbers live]

**Per-view mesh settings, 0x143710230.** It's given the cull context (rcx), the view's descriptor (rdx) and an output (r8). A shadow view is a view type of 2 or 3 (`1 << type & 0xC`).

For a shadow view:
- **the reference view is `[context + 8] + 0x610`.** The context is set up in the shadow setup at 0x14373775C, where `[context + 8] = view state + 0xAE0`, the main camera's own descriptor. So the reference view is the main camera's (view state + 0x10F0), not the cascade's.
- output + 0x00 = its position (+ 0x70); output + 0x44 = its LOD factor (+ 0x298);
- output + 0x40 (the scale) = context + 0x30B0 if it's ≥ 0, else MeshSettings + 0x28;
- the shadow view's own position and direction go to output + 0x20 / + 0x30, used for LOD picking in shadows.

The same setup copies the view state's CameraParams into the context (0x143737822 - 0x143737849):
- ForceLod (+ 0x85530) → + 0x30B8;
- CullScreenAreaScale (+ 0x85538) → + 0x30B4;
- **ShadowDistanceScale (+ 0x85534) → + 0x30B0.**

For any other view the reference is the view's own + 0x610, and output + 0x40 = 0, so there's no shadow cut.

**Per mesh, 0x1437110D0 / cut at 0x1437111B0:**

```
dist = max(|bounding sphere centre - main camera| - radius, 0) * LOD factor
if mesh ShadowDistance (mesh + 0x2C8) * scale > 0 and dist > it: not drawn in this shadow view
```

Live: the LOD factor is 1.921 at FOV 1.5708, and the scale is 5.0 (CameraParams' is -1). That gives, by ShadowDistance class:

| ShadowDistance | Cut past (distance − radius) | Loaded meshes with it |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | never cut | 2022 of 2863 architecture, 2763 in all |
| 25 | 65 m | |
| 30 | 78 m | |
| 40 | 104 m | most props |
| 50 | 130 m | 523 architecture |
| 80 | 208 m | 195 architecture |
| 100 | 260 m | |

The LOD factor is tan(FOV / 2) / tan(55° / 2), so the camera's FOV changes these distances. Cut distance (beyond the radius) = ShadowDistance × scale / LOD factor; with scale 5:

| Vertical FOV | LOD factor | ShadowDistance 40 | ShadowDistance 50 | ShadowDistance 80 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 55° | 1.000 | 200 m | 250 m | 400 m |
| 60° | 1.109 | 180 m | 225 m | 361 m |
| 70° | 1.345 | 149 m | 186 m | 297 m |
| 90° | 1.921 | 104 m | 130 m | 208 m |

With a scale of 1 instead of 5, divide by 5 (40 at 70° → 30 m).

The test is 0x1437110D0 (re-read): `dist = max(|sphere centre − output + 0x00| − sphere radius, 0) × output + 0x44`. In a shadow view, if mesh + 0x2C8 × output + 0x40 > 0 and dist is larger, it returns "not drawn" (0x1437111C8).

The LOD settings (GlobalLodScale, Lod1..6Distance, ForceLod) only pick which LOD a caster draws with, from 0x1437112B3 on, not whether it casts.

Not traced: GameRenderSettings StaticModelPartShadowCullEnable (+0xC8) and ShadowOcclusionCullingEnable (+0x43B).

#### 3.7 Which surfaces get the shadow

A surface is shadowed by the sun only if its depth along the camera's view is within d (125 m here), the range the cascades cover. Past that it's lit as if nothing were in the way. Inside it, a caster only shows if it passed 3.6.

### 6. For the community question: SunShadowmapViewDistance vs ShadowDistance

1. **They're separate.**
   - SunShadowmapViewDistance (CameraParams, a visual environment component) only sets how far the sun's cascades reach, as depth along the camera's view. It replaces WorldRenderSettings' ShadowmapViewDistance (200) whenever it's ≥ 0, with no cap (0x143735CA1).
   - ShadowDistance (MeshLodGroup, per mesh) is the caster cut.
   - Nothing in the cascade or cut code compares against 200 m. 200 is only WorldRenderSettings' default range.
2. **The cut:** `(distance from the camera to the mesh's bounding sphere − its radius) × LOD factor > ShadowDistance × scale` means the mesh casts no shadow. The scale is CameraParams.ShadowDistanceScale if it's ≥ 0, else MeshSettings.ShadowDistanceScale (5.0 in MEC). The LOD factor is tan(FOV / 2) / tan(27.5°). ShadowDistance 0 means never cut.
3. **The link: the same CameraParams component.**
   - A CameraParams with ShadowDistanceScale ≥ 0 replaces MeshSettings' ×5 for every mesh. With 1.0, a ShadowDistance-40 prop stops casting at about 30 m at a 70° FOV (149 m with ×5).
   - So an edited or added CameraParams that sets SunShadowmapViewDistance and also has ShadowDistanceScale ≥ 0 would cut casters 5× nearer.
   - In the city, live: SunShadowmapViewDistance 125, ShadowDistanceScale −1, so ×5 applies.
4. **The other effect of a big range.**
   - The 4 cascades are spread over it: 6.4 / 15.1 / 41.2 / 200 m for 200 m; **30.6 / 66.8 / 167.5 / 1000 m for 1000 m**.
   - Past the first cascade the shadow map covers far more ground per texel, so small casters' shadows thin out. That's a loss of resolution, not a cut.
5. **The LOD settings don't help.** GlobalLodScale, Lod1..6Distance and ForceLod only choose which LOD the caster draws with.
6. **The FOV matters.** A wider camera FOV cuts every caster nearer: ×1.92 at 90° compared with 55°.
7. **Editing ShadowDistance:** the cut reads the value from the runtime mesh itself (mesh + 0x2C8, inside an inline copy of its LodGroup at mesh + 0x298; read live from 6143 meshes). So what counts is the value the mesh holds. Whether a change to the LodGroup asset after the mesh is loaded reaches that copy isn't known; a value in the data before the mesh loads would be the safe case.
8. **BF4:** not checked (another engine build).

# 6. What removes KrugerSec, and whether the replay can spawn stand-in guards

2026-10-23, offline disassembly only (game build 0x5762E3B7). Background (seen in game): a whole KSec group was taken out of the level at once while Faith ran off, past the auto-despawn hold. Where something isn't known yet, it says so.

### 1. Short answer

- **Every removal path traced ends in one call:** the generic "destroy this entity" request, **0x143167700**. That covers:
  - the level's own "Unspawn" events, through the guards' spawner;
  - the AI's despawns through the AI coordinator, including the auto-despawn we already hold.
- So the replay can keep the recorded guards by catching that one call, but only for them, and handing it back to the game when the replay lets go of the recording. A per-path hold isn't needed.
- **Stand-in guards aren't worth it.** The only way the game spawns a guard is through a level spawner. That makes a live, armed AI guard that counts in the encounter, and nothing found makes it a harmless puppet. Details in section 4.

### 2. The removal paths, traced

**Spawners.** `ServerSpawnEntity` has its event handler in vtable slot 4 (0x143383D40, vtable 0x141B4DDB0). The KSec spawners override it: `PamServerCharacterSpawnEntity` 0x143958790 → `ServerCharacterSpawnEntity` 0x143382D20. Both pass every event except "Spawn" down to the base with a tail jump (0x143382EA1).

On **"Unspawn"** (name hash 0xCE486545, h*33 ^ c), the base handler, when the spawner is active (+0x2A4):
1. tells its listeners (list at +0x180, each listener's vtable +0x28);
2. copies its list of spawned characters (vector at +0x148 / +0x150);
3. calls **0x143167700(character, [character + 0x28])** on each (loop at 0x143383F48).

**AI groups.** `PamServerAIAutoSpawnGroup` (vtable 0x141C432A8) → `PamAIGroup` (0x141C42618) → `ServerAIGroup` (0x141A57798).
- The group's handler is slot 4: the Pam override 0x14392F280 handles "Spawn", then the base 0x142C91560.
- On "Unspawn" the group calls 0x142C97130. That sends "Unspawn" to every spawner linked to the group (pairs at +0x68 / +0x70, each one's vtable +0x18) and empties its member list (+0x40 / +0x48).
- **No game code builds an "Unspawn" event for a group.** The only code that builds one is 0x142C97130 itself, sending to its spawners. So whatever unspawns a group does it through the level's own event links, which are data. That fits the whole group going at once when Faith ran off. Which level link it was isn't known, and doesn't need to be.

**AI despawns.**
- The AI auto-despawn managers keep a pointer to the AI coordinator at +0x50. Both constructors set it from the global **[0x142548710] − 0x30**: 0x142CAE37D, and 0x142CAF51F (the Pam one, from 0x14397D534).
- The coordinator is a `PamServerAICoordinator` (vtable 0x141C424F0; base `ServerAICoordinator` 0x141A57428, built at 0x142C8CA00).
- Its **slot 24, 0x143933580**, despawns an AI: `0x143167700([ai + 0xD0], [[ai + 0xD0] + 0x28])`, i.e. the AI's character.
- The despawn check we already hold (0x143982AE0) calls it. Other callers go through stored pointers too, so they can't be listed offline. A stack log would show which one fired.

**The destroy request, 0x143167700(entity, owner):**
- if the entity's +0x18 bit 10 is set (already being destroyed), it returns;
- otherwise it jumps to `[owner]`'s vtable slot 2 with the entity: the owner queues it for destruction.

It has 84 direct callers; it's how entities in general ask to be destroyed.

### 3. Keeping the recorded guards: what to build

- **Hook 0x143167700.** While the replay holds people (as now: recording, or a recording with people kept), check each request:
  - Is the entity a `PamServerCharacterEntity` (vtable 0x141C3FCB0)?
  - Is it where one of the recorded guards is, within about 3 m? The server character's place reads the same way as the client's: `[entity + 0x38]` components, translation at `+0x40 + (byte 9 + 2 · byte 0xA) · 0x20`. The despawn check reads its AI's place exactly like this, at 0x143982B03.

  If both hold, don't pass the request on: keep (entity, owner) in a list. This needs FaithReplay to share the recorded guards' current places each frame, behind a lock, since the request can come from another thread.
- **When the hold ends** (recording forgotten, people turned off), hand each kept request to the game: call the original 0x143167700 with it. The game then removes the guard as it meant to.
- **Safety:**
  - If a kept guard is destroyed some other way meanwhile (a level unload), its destructor (server slot 7, 0x14391F540, already hooked for the diagnostic) takes it off the list. A stale pointer is never handed back.
  - A request for an entity already on the list isn't added twice.
- **What changes in the live game while a guard is kept:** the guard stays, with his AI running, though the group thinks he's gone.
  - His spawner still counts him (its list is kept by the destruction itself), so it doesn't spawn more in his place.
  - He may walk back or keep searching. While a replay plays, Faith takes no damage.
- **Unknowns:**
  - Whether anything removes characters without 0x143167700. The level unloading may well; that's fine, it isn't something to block.
  - How far apart the server and client places of a ragdolled guard drift; hence the 3 m.

A stack log taken while Faith runs off from a group would show the path in that case and check the above.

### 4. Stand-in guards: why not

- **The only way a guard gets spawned** is the spawner's "Spawn" (0x143383DB4). It checks that the spawner is active and within its limits (0x1433804A0, 0x143388DD0), then queues the spawn (0x143174360). The guard is made from the spawner's data: `CharacterSpawnReferenceObjectData` Template +0x198, at its ControllableTransform +0xA0, within its MaxCount +0x144 / MaxCountSimultaneously +0x148.
- **What that gives the replay:** a new live KSec at the spawner's place, with his AI, weapons and collision. He would fight the real Faith, be counted by the encounter and the coordinator (combat state, music, the AI's other guards), and stand at the spawner, not where the recorded guard was. Making him a pure body would need:
  - stopping his AI, for which no switch exists: `IsAiEnabled` is only read when a level sets up its AI (0x143343622);
  - keeping his collision out of the way;
  - removing him after, and "Unspawn" on that spawner would remove every guard it has.
- **A body without AI, made on the client alone:** not found. The game's characters are server-run, and the client copies are made from the server's.

So keeping the real guards (section 3) is the safer path. It changes the live game only by leaving guards in the level that it wanted gone, and hands them back after.

# 7. The video billboards and how they play (2026-10-24)

Read from the game's code and data files only (offline, read-only). Nothing here was read live.

### 1. What they are (verified)

- The city's video screens use **LinearMedia** ("LMS"). It is separate from the RW movie player (`MoviePlayer2`, VP8 / WebM) that plays the menu and cutscene movies.
- **The data.** Each video is an `LMSBillboardAsset` under `linearmedia/sequences/...`, for example `LinearMedia/Sequences/NewsCast/NewsCast_02`.
  - It has five Resources, one per LOD. Each is a "configuration" res (resType `0x86521D6C`) named `<name>_configuration`, then `...lod1` to `...lod4`.
  - Its BaseTexture is a still image, used when the video doesn't stream.
- **A configuration** holds:

| Part | Contents |
|---|---|
| Header | 1-second segments, frames, chunk count |
| Segment table | 30 frames each, `999 999 990` ns |
| Frame table | 0x18 bytes a frame: offset, size, `33 333 333` ns |
| Chunk index | |
| Chunk ids | 20 bytes each (16-byte guid + `0x200000`) |

- **The frames** are in 2 MB data chunks. Each frame is a u32 length, a 4-byte zlib-packed header, a u32 length, then a **VP6** frame (On2 VP6, version 7). The decoder is the LMS "RegularGrid" with `LMSRegularGridVp6CodecRuntime`, with job labels `lMSRGDecFrm`, `lMSRGDecSeg` and `lMSRGUpload`.
- **Real sizes, read from the first keyframe of every LOD of all 81 videos.** All play at 30 fps, and each LOD halves width and height:

| LOD | Most videos (31 + 15 turned) | 16:9 ones (8 + 3) | Others |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1440 x 720 | 1280 x 720 | 1280 x 432, 1024 x 512, 1280 x 640 |
| 1 | 720 x 368 | 640 x 368 | |
| 2 | 368 x 176 | 320 x 176 | |
| 3 | 176 x 96 | 160 x 96 | |
| 4 | 96 x 48 | 80 x 48 | |

- **Data rate.** For NewsCast_02, LOD 0 is 105 chunks (about 0.9 MB/s; keyframe 87 KB, other frames about 40 KB), and LOD 4 is 3 chunks.

### 2. The entities (verified field offsets)

| Class | Fields |
|---|---|
| LinearMediaBillboardFeedEntityData (one video) | EmittingChannel +0x18, TextureCodes +0x20, LinearMediaBillboardAsset +0x28, NumSpeakers +0x30, ExternalTime +0x34, SubresourceIndices +0x38, StartOnLoad +0x40, Loop +0x41 |
| LinearMediaBillboardClientEntityData (one screen) | ReceivingChannel +0x18, **SizeInMeterSqr +0x1C**, FallbackTexture +0x20, MeshLookAtDirection +0x28, isDynamicObject +0x2C, disableLOD +0x2D, useSecondTextureStream +0x2E, EnabledOnStartup +0x2F |
| LinearMediaBillboardSettings (TypeInfo 0x142847730) | SkipLOD +0x10, MaxActiveFeeds +0x14, LODScreenSurfaceScale +0x18, DebugEntityLogicUpdateEnable +0x1C (the update runs only while set), StreamingEnable +0x1D, SupportTexture2Enable +0x1E, SupportEmissiveEnable +0x1F, ForceLowestMipDynamic +0x20, DownscaleOnOverloadEnable +0x21, DisableLODBlendOnOverloadEnable +0x22, LODBlendingEnable +0x23 |
| Other classes | LinearMediaBillboardProviderEntity, LinearMediaBillboardOverrideFeedEntity (ChannelsToOverride +0x48), LinearMediaSettings (pools, job and message limits) |

- The manager keeps up to **32 feeds** (`[+0x468]`, `LMBBD_MaxSupportedBillboardFeeds`). Its settings are at `+0x458`.

### 3. A frame of the manager (verified in code)

The manager's update job is `0x1437DEB30`, registered as a job batch by `0x1437E1430`. Each frame it runs these steps:

1. **`0x1437DF8D0`:** each feed's current textures, put into a 32 × 0x40 table. Each entry's screen size (+0x10) is set to 0.
2. **`0x1437E2190`: each screen's size on screen.**
   - The camera is the **camera registry entry (0, 0)**, `[0x142415E50]`. Its transform comes from `0x143278E40`, which reads `[+0x208]` + 0x50 when there is an override, else +0xD0. The frustum comes from `0x143278C30`, with the FOV from slot 3 `0x143279C00`.
   - For each client: `s = SizeInMeterSqr / (distance² × 1.4)`, with distance² at least 1e-9.
   - Facing away (direction to the camera · look direction < -0.1): `s = min(s × 0.5, 0.005)`.
   - Not in the frustum (unless the feed already had a screen in view): `s = min(s, 1) × 0.15`.
   - A feed takes the largest `s` of its screens.
3. **`0x1437E1FE0` and `0x1437E0AF0`:** bookkeeping, not traced.
4. **`0x1437E2760`: the LOD.** For each feed, `v = s × LODScreenSurfaceScale × overload factor`. The LOD is the first row that passes:

| v at least | and SkipLOD below | LOD |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 0 | 0 |
| 0.25 | 1 | 1 |
| 0.1 | 2 | 2 |
| 0.025 | 3 | 3 |
| 0.005 | 4 | 4 |

   - Below that, the feed gets LOD 4 if ForceLowestMipDynamic is set, else **255: no stream, the still BaseTexture**.
   - StreamingEnable 0 makes SkipLOD 255, so every feed ends in that last case.
   - The LOD goes to feed +0x398, the screen size to +0x39C, and the blend flag to +0x284.
   - **Overload** (DownscaleOnOverloadEnable): the manager counts feeds still catching up (feed +0x248 ≠ +0x24C).
     - With 2 or more catching up for 0.8 s, the factor (`+0x448`) drops 0.0025 per frame, down to 0.45. At 0.45, DisableLODBlendOnOverloadEnable switches blending off.
     - With none catching up, it climbs 0.006 per frame back to 1.
     - With exactly one catching up, it stays.
     - The blend flag is also ANDed with LODBlendingEnable.
5. **The feeds' update (`0x1437DE7B0`):**
   - It switches the LOD (`0x1437E0210`).
   - It advances the play time by **the update's frame time** (dt × 1e9 ns, `0x1437E29F0`). With **dt 0 the feeds don't move**, so a frozen game clock freezes the billboards.
   - A feed with an external "PlayPosition" follows it, and resyncs after a jump of more than 0.5 s.

**What the game's settings give.** The game's values are SkipLOD 0 and scale 1 (read live on 2026-10-21).
- **The game never shows LOD 0 (1440 × 720).** The best it shows is LOD 1 (720 × 368), and only when `s ≥ 0.25`.
- For a 100 m² screen, that is within 12 m. LOD 2 (368 × 176) is reached by 19 m, and the still image beyond 120 m.

### 4. Findings for the tools' Billboard quality

- **The LOD is measured from the game's camera, not the free camera.**
  - The free camera only writes the render view, never the camera registry's transform (verified 2026-10-2x for the zone streaming focus). So distance, facing and view are all taken from Faith's camera.
  - Screens near the free camera but far from Faith get low LODs or the still image, whatever the tools' quality is set to. Screens behind Faith's camera lose a further × 0.15.
- **Zoom doesn't count.** The size is distance only, so a narrow free-camera FOV gets the same LOD as a wide one.
- The dropdown's levels, with the real sizes:
  - **Default** tops out at 720 × 368.
  - **Sharper** (scale 4) reaches 720 × 368 at `s ≥ 0.0625`, about 24 m for a 100 m² screen.
  - **Much sharper** (SkipLOD -1, scale 4) allows 1440 × 720 from `s ≥ 0.125`, about 17 m.
- The overload drop (down to 0.45) can still push the higher levels down when several feeds fall behind.

### 5. Improvements, best first

1. **The LOD from the free camera.**
   - Hooks: a hook on `0x1437E2190` sets a thread-local flag for its run (it runs in job threads). Hooks on `0x143278E40` (transform) and `0x143279C00` (FOV) return the free camera's transform and FOV while the flag is set and the camera is on.
   - Why this way: nothing shared is written, and every other user of the camera registry keeps the game camera.
   - The rows: the tools' `m_Camera.Transform` uses the same rows as the entry's +0xD0 (translation +0x100 / row 3, forward +0xF0 / row 2), as the zone focus already relies on.
   - To check live first: whether slot 3 returns the vertical FOV in degrees. The frustum code multiplies it by π/180.
2. **Zoom-aware.** While the free camera is on, multiply the scale the tools write by `(tan(game FOV / 2) / tan(camera FOV / 2))²`, so a zoomed shot gets the sizes it shows.
3. **A "Maximum" level.** SkipLOD -1, a very large scale and DownscaleOnOverloadEnable off: every screen in view at its full size, for stills.
   - The cost: one 1440 × 720 VP6 decode per feed per video frame, up to 32 feeds. Videos may fall behind and stutter while many play.
4. **Keep far screens playing.** ForceLowestMipDynamic on gives LOD 4 instead of the still image. The game's value isn't known; read it live first.
5. **The tooltip:** the real sizes from §1, replacing "the videos' sizes in pixels aren't known".

### 6. Not known

- The game's live values of ForceLowestMipDynamic, StreamingEnable, LODBlendingEnable and DisableLODBlendOnOverloadEnable.
- Where MaxActiveFeeds (-1 live) is used: no reader was found in the manager's code range.
- What `0x1437E1FE0` and `0x1437E0AF0` do.
- How long a LOD switch takes: it has to start streaming another file.
- Whether the frame time the feeds get follows the tools' slow motion: it comes from the entity update. Freezing does stop them (dt 0).

# 8. The game's data: KrugerSec types, weapons and settings (2026-10-24)

Read from the game's own data files: `Data` and `Patch` under
`<game folder>`. Everything was read only, and nothing was written or downloaded.
"Verified" means read from the files with the parser checked against known values (see §1).

### 1. The format, and the tools (offline, `fb\`, read only)

- **Bundles.** `Win32\*.sb` (and `levels\...`) are Frostbite DbObject data, not obfuscated. Each bundle lists its `ebx` / `res` / `chunks` assets by name, SHA-1, size and originalSize. The `.toc` files and the catalogs start with a signed 0x22C-byte header (`00 D1 CE 01`); after it they are plain.
- **Archives.**
  - `Win32\gameconfigurations\<package>\cas.cat` holds "NyanNyanNyanNyan", u32 entries, u32 patch entries, then 36-byte entries (SHA-1, offset, size, ?, archive number → `cas_NN.cas`).
  - The patch catalogs end with 60-byte records of three SHA-1s: the result, then most likely the base (it parses as EBX) and the delta.
  - Asset data is in blocks: u32 BE size out, u16 BE type (0x09xx = LZ4, 0x02xx = zlib, 0x00xx = stored), u16 BE size in.
- **EBX** (magic 0x0FB2D1CE, its type info inside):
  - The instances come after the strings (absStringOffset + lenString), and the arrays after the instances.
  - Each instance is aligned so that its own start, 8 bytes before its stored data, falls on the class's alignment. Then come its GUID (the first numGUIDRepeater groups only) and its data without the first 8 bytes (the DataContainer header). Field offsets count from that start.
  - A class's super class (`$`) sits inline at the same start.
  - Checked on airanged_firesettings: every value is sensible, and the transforms in the weapon blueprint come out as identity.
- **Tools:**
  - `dbobj.py`: the DbObject reader.
  - `cas.py`: the catalogs, archive reads, and a pure-Python LZ4 decoder.
  - `ebx.py`: the parser.
  - `ebxlist.py`: writes `ebx_index.tsv`, 43,704 assets; the Patch version wins.
  - `show.py`: prints the assets you name.
  - `dump.py`: dumps the assets matching a pattern, with other files' references resolved to names.
- **Not done:** applying the patch deltas. Four assets (the base Protector template and three SubProtector ones) were patched with a delta, so for them the **pre-patch** version was read and is marked so below.

  - The EffectComponent (an effect file, at most 1 instance) is started by the weapon's interface and prefab events (2089401213 / 230748069), not by each shot. Probably a laser sight or idle effect; not checked.

### 5. What this gives the replay, and what it doesn't yet

- **Shots can be described exactly**:
  - A guard's shot is a client bullet flying at 150 m/s for at most 1.5 s, carrying its trail effect (the tracer), plus the shot sound started by the firing component's event.
  - So a replayed shot is one sound and one tracer along the recorded line.
  - Still missing: the game's code that spawns that bullet, or starts its trail, on the client. No vtable slot of PamClientWeaponFiringComponent reads the projectile (+ 0x78) directly. The live counting-hook step is still the way to find it.
- **Shot sounds** may already be in the replay's sound recording, since they are ordinary SoundEntity sounds on the gun. Shot sounds near Faith would show up in the replay's recorded sound events. Not checked.
- **Labelling each recorded KrugerSec by type** (Enforcer, Sentinel, …) in the log or the UI: the spawn template's AISpecialization is an instance of the type's class (e.g. AIRanged_Enforcer). At runtime a character points to it somewhere, and finding where takes one read-only live look. Then the label is its class: the TypeInfo objects are in `Research_KSec_Types_2026-10-24.md` §1.
- **Melee guards** (Sentinel, Protector, ShockProtector) have no gun, so the gun fix and gun replay concern only the ranged types, the cutscene baton Enforcer, and the baton- or knife-carrying melee types. Whether batons and knives (wepbp_baton / wepbp_knife) are the same kind of weapon entity as the gun is not checked. If they are, the replay records them as it does guns (it records any PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity), and the gun fix covers them too.

# 9. The game's ghost (runner replay) system, its guns, and what they mean for the tools' replay (2026-10-24)

Everything here was read offline from the game's code (the Steam exe image; the game wasn't
running). "Verified" means read from the code. "Not known" means it needs a live read. The earlier ghost notes
(`MEC_Reverse_Notes.md` §14 and §15) are folded in where they were checked again.

### 1. Short answer

The game's ghost is an ordinary character. It is drawn wherever the recording says, while its entity stays parked, and it does
two things every frame:
1. It registers a pose override with all its bones (0x142FCEE50). The tools' replay already does this for Faith and the KSec.
2. **It sets the pose's world placement itself**: 0x142FD8F20(pose, 4x4, 0), with the recorded root. **The tools' replay never
   does this** (no reference to 0x142FD8F20 in the source).

For a body the game updates, the game does step 2 itself in the body's update job, from the entity's transform. That is why the
live KSec work: the replay moves their entity to the drawn root.

For a body the game doesn't update (a downed KSec), step 2 never happens. The replay also holds that body's
update gate, so the game's pose job doesn't run for it either. That job and the placement setter are what fill the render-side
matrices ([page + 0x40], §6). The replay's own writes go to other buffers of the slot. So the screen keeps showing the body as
it lay. That fits what was seen in game (downed KSec invisible and not alive) and is the best lead found. It is not confirmed: it needs a live read
during playback (§7.1).

For a dropped gun, the game takes the body's transform from its **physics part** when it has one, not from the entity rows the
replay moves. That fits dropped guns being drawn 1.5–5.4 m off (seen in game, 2026-10-23).

### 2. The ghost, part by part (verified)

#### Player component (PamClientReplayPlayerComponent, vtable 0x141C48A28)
Made by 0x143944860. Its layout:

| Offset | What |
|---|---|
| + 0x000 | the component's vtable |
| + 0x038 | the replay core (vtable 0x141C48C28). It advances and samples with 0x1439729F0(core, dt, time scale) |
| + 0x180 | the sampled bones (0x20 a bone: translation x y z 1, rotation quaternion) |
| + 0x1A8 | network state (vtable 0x141C48C48). Slot 2, 0x14394BDE0, reads from a bit stream: the time scale (+ 0x2E0), two counts (+ 0x5C / + 0x60), a state byte (+ 0x2E4 = whether the state equals + 0x200), and a bone list into [+ 0x180]. So ghost poses can also come from the server (a PamServerReplayPlayerComponent exists) |
| + 0x1C0 | the override listener (vtable 0x141C48C68). Slot 3, 0x14394D6B0, calls 0x142FCEE50(manager + 0x1D0, descriptor + 0x1D8, handle) |
| + 0x1C8 | the owner animatable |
| + 0x1D8 | the override descriptor (+ 0x1F0 weight, + 0x1F8 handle, -1 at first) |
| + 0x200 | the bone count |
| + 0x2A0 | a placement transform (identity at first; PamReplayEntityData has OverrideTransform at + 0x20) |
| + 0x2E0 | the time scale (1.0) |
| + 0x2E4 / + 0x2E5 | gates for the copy below (meaning not traced: + 0x2E4 is set from the network state, see + 0x1A8) |
| + 0x2E6 | use the frame's second dt, and put the root straight from + 0x2A0 |
| + 0x2F8 | an output property: progress = [+ 0x60] / [+ 0x5C], written through 0x142A430F0 |

Other slots:
- Setup, slot 37, 0x14394CAC0 (§14).
- Teardown, slot 23, 0x14394C7D0.
- Slot 38, 0x14394D780: when [+ 0x10]'s slot 4 returns 2, it calls 0x14346CD00(arg, + 0x1A8, 0). This most likely subscribes the network state (not traced).

#### Its per-frame update
- Updaters: two singletons, [0x142578588] (pass 6) and [0x142578590] (pass 5). Both have vtable 0x141C49190 and are named "PamClientReplayPlayerComponent".
- Their slot 2, 0x14394DA40, calls **0x1439501A0(component, frame)** for each registered component.

0x1439501A0 does, in order:
1. Takes dt from frame + 0 (or frame + 4 when + 0x2E6), then calls 0x1439729F0(core, dt, + 0x2E0): the ghost's clock and sample.
2. If + 0x2E4 and + 0x2E5: sets the weight to 1.0 and copies + 0x200 bones from [+ 0x180] into the override buffer [+ 0x1D8].
3. If + 0x2E6 isn't set: puts the root (bone at + 0x20 of the buffer) through the + 0x2A0 transform and builds a 4x4 (16-byte-aligned, on the stack). Then calls **0x142FD8F20([[+ 0x1C8] + 0x158], &m, 0)**.
4. If + 0x2E6 is set: puts the root override straight from + 0x2A0 (0x142A63A30, matrix to rotation + translation).
5. Writes the progress output.

#### Recording
- The recording component is made by 0x143949120 (vtables 0x141C48CD0, listener 0x141C48ED0).
- Its setup, 0x14394CD80, registers it with the updater [0x142578A68] (vtable 0x141C48CA0, made by 0x143945FF0, "PamClientReplayRecordingComponent", pass 1), with a frame interval.
- The updater's slot 2, 0x14394DAC0, works on entries {component, u16 interval, u16 counter}:
  - every entry whose [component + 0x19] & 1 is set gets its counter increased;
  - every interval frames it calls **0x143974390(recorder = [component + 0x48], {dt × interval}, reader = component + 0x58)**, which records one frame into the player's recorder (§14: a ring of 450 frames × 0x2F0).
- That ring is Faith's only. KSec are never recorded by the game.

### 3. How the game places a body each frame (verified)

The body update job is 0x1432DE310 (body = animatable + 0x70, vtable 0x141B34500 slot 3):
- It sets + 0x5C1 = 0 and calls the gate 0x1432E86D0.
- **Skipped:** it calls 0x142FD1B00([body + 0x2F8], ..., body) if + 0x5C0 is set or the body has a pose slot, sets + 0x5B0 = 0, and **nothing else**. No placement.
- **Updated:** it sets + 0x5C1 = 1, then calls:
  - 0x1432EAD70 (the pose update interval);
  - **0x1432EA220 (placement)**;
  - 0x142FD3F30, whose result is copied as a 4x4 into body + 0x530 to + 0x560 (meaning not traced);
  - then 0x1432EB3B0 or 0x1432EB4B0.

0x1432EA220(body, frame):
- If body + 0xB8 is 0, it calls 0x142FD0830(pose) and nothing else.
- Otherwise it takes the transform from **0x1432E06B0(body)**. That function copies body + 0x50 to + 0x80 (the body's own rows). When the body has a part at [body + 0xC0] / [body + 0xC8], it computes the transform from that part instead (a physics or attachment part: what a dropped gun has is not known for certain).
- Then, by the mode at body + 0x90:

| Mode | What it calls |
|---|---|
| 1 | 0x142FD8C30(pose, m, 0, bone) with a bone from [body + 0x598] + 0x58 / + 0x60 at index + 0xB0 |
| 2 | 0x142FD8C30(pose, the rows + velocity (+ 0xA0) × dt, 1, -1) |
| 3 | 0x142FD8F20(pose, m, 0) |
| 4 | 0x142FD8C30, and/or 0x142FD8F20 |
| other | 0x142FD0830 |

The pose world-transform setter, 0x142FD8F20(pose = animatable + 0x158, const 4x4*, bool):
- turns the matrix into a rotation and a translation (0x142A63A30), with a fixed extra rotation when pose + 0x1E0 is set;
- writes the root into the skeleton's storage;
- sets pose + 0x131;
- calls 0x142B50E70 with [pose + 0x28];
- writes the descriptor buffers from [pose + 0x20] + 0x80;
- calls **0x142FD8840(manager [pose + 0x1B8], handle [pose + 0x118], 3x4, the root bone [[data + 0x48]], flag)**. If manager + 0x2B8 is set, this writes the root's 3x4 into the per-slot buffers at [page + 0x40] + slot × 0x20 (+ 0x08 always, + 0x00 only with the flag; the entry is on when + 0x14 is set);
- calls 0x142B15260([[[pose + 0x28] + 0x20] + 0xD0]) and 0x142B6E6F0 (most likely the scene / culling placement; not traced).

**The replay writes different buffers.** For bodies it draws itself, it writes page + 0x00 / + 0x08 / + 0x10 / + 0x18 (see FaithReplay's RawRestore). It doesn't write the [page + 0x40] per-slot buffers, and it doesn't do the scene update. Which of these the renderer and the culling use is **not known**.

### 4. Guns (verified unless marked)

- **The gun:** PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity (TypeInfo 0x14284FB60, vtable 0x141C33FE0, getType 0x1438FEC20).
  - Its data is PamCharacterWeaponEntityData (0xB0): WeaponDrop at + 0xA0.
  - PamCharacterWeaponReferenceData has AutoSpawn at + 0xA0.
  - Its body is at + 0x100 (26 bones) and its owner at + 0x120 (2026-10-23, live).
- **Dropped guns:** see 0x1432E06B0 in §3. The replay's MoveActorDrawn writes the entity rows (the setter body with the physics and queued bits off). That reaches body + 0x50 at most, never the part the transform is read from.
- **AI firing:**
  - The fire managers are entities: PamClientAIFireManagerBase (vtable 0x141C536F8), PamClientAIHeliFireManager (0x141C53F30; slot 26 0x14398C640 → 0x14398D780 each update) and PamClientAIDroneFireManager (0x141C53A70; slot 26 0x14398BE10).
  - Their data: PamAIFireManagerBaseData (WeaponTransform + 0x20, AimAtBone + 0x60) and PamAIHeliFireManagerData (HeliWeapons + 0xB0, InsertionWeaponEnabled + 0xB8, HoverWeaponEnabled + 0xB9). So the VTOL's guns are switched on separately for the drop-off and for hovering.
  - PamWeaponFiringComponentData has AIProjectile at + 0x78.
  - **Aim:** 0x143982F60 works out an aim point and hands it to 0x143903CB0. That stores it at + 0x40, sets + 0x50 = 1, and writes it to a property connection at + 0x68 (0x142A430F0). This is aiming, not the shot.
  - **Where the client makes a shot's flash, tracer and bullet: not found yet.**
- **VTOL drop-off:** HeliDropOffASData has MaxContextualDistance + 0xB0, MinContextualDistance + 0xB4, MaxContextualAngle + 0xB8, ApproachAltitude + 0xBC, DropOffAltitude + 0xC0 and ContextualActivation + 0xC4. The AI states are PamAIStateApproachHeliDropOff and PamAIStateHeliDropOff. A drop-off is an AI state of the VTOL (and the KSec). The VTOL hovers at DropOffAltitude.

### 5. KSec

- **Server brain:** PamServerAIBrainComponent (vtable 0x141C42848). Its slots 48 to 60 are all small (at most 50 instructions, except slot 49, 0x143932080, which has 308 instructions and 35 calls). No code refers to either copy of its class name string (the replay components name their updaters this way, so the brain doesn't register an updater by name). Where its per-frame update runs is not known. **The hunt fix still needs the live counting-hook test from `Research_KSec_Systems_2026-10-24.md` §4.1.**
- **Close-camera vanishing:** no character "hide near camera" setting was found. The CameraFadeStart / CameraFadeLength fields are a rendering component's data (the record is shared by the sky, sun flare, outdoor light, screen-space raytrace and fog component classes), not a character's. Culling from a stale placement (§3) is the leading candidate.

### 6. Ragdolls, and what the replay's draw really reaches (verified unless marked)

**Classes and data.**
- RagdollPhysicsComponent: TypeInfo 0x1428302B0, vtable 0x141BA9BD8, getType 0x1434DD0F0. Made by 0x1434D7870 and 0x1434D7DE0, with sub-objects at + 0x20 (vtable 0x141BA9E58) and + 0x28 (0x141B2D4B0).
- RagdollPhysicsComponentData (0xA0): BodiesNamesHashes at + 0x90.
- RagdollAsset (0x28): MaterialPair + 0x18, Resource + 0x20.
- UseServerRagdoll is at + 0x90 of EACharacterPhysicsComponentData (ClientAuthoritative + 0x91, EffectsWorldOnly + 0x92). These offsets are from this report's field records; that they belong to EACharacterPhysicsComponentData is from §16 of the notes.
- PhysicsSettings has RemoveRagdollWhenWoken at + 0x36.
- The messages are JuiceSoldierRagdollActivateMessage and JuiceSoldierRagdollDeactivateMessage.
- Havok's hkaRagdollInstance is there, and so are the behaviour nodes hkbPoweredRagdollControlsModifier, hkbRigidBodyRagdollControlsModifier and hkbCheckRagdollSpeedModifier. So the ragdoll reaches the pose through the animation graph.

**Where the ragdoll's pose gets into the body.** No code in the ragdoll component's range (0x1434D7000 to 0x1434E3000) writes a pose slot. Its only call into the pose code is 0x142FCAAF0, from 0x1434E26B0, which looks like a bone-name setup (not traced).

Taken as (consistent with live samples from 2026-10-24, not proven): the ragdoll's pose is the animation graph's output, written by the ANT pose job 0x142FCC7C0. That job runs only for a body the update job lets through (§3). This is why holding the gate stopped the flicker (seen in game).

**What the screen gets.**
- The pose job checks the slot's render-side entry, [page + 0x40] + slot × 0x20 (+ 0x14 on, manager + 0x2B8), and passes that on into its work (0x142FC9B80 and on; the write itself is not traced).
- The placement setter writes the root into the same entry (0x142FD8840, §3).
- So the render-side matrices come from the pose job and the placement, both of which run only for a body the game updates.
- The replay holds the gate for the bodies it draws itself (FaithReplay.cpp:1861) and writes page + 0x00 / + 0x08 / + 0x10 / + 0x18 / + 0x20. The page + 0x10 matrices are a different buffer, behind a different flag (manager + 0x2B9).

**What this explains.**
- Before the hold, the per-frame + 0xFC flag let the update through for part of each frame. The pose job then sometimes took the replay's pose and sometimes the ragdoll's: the flicker.
- With the hold, the pose job never runs for them. The render-side matrices keep what was last there (the body lying where it fell), and the replayed guard isn't shown: **downed KSec invisible and not alive**.
- This fits what was seen in game both before and after the hold. That it is what happens is not proven yet; the reads in §7.1 would settle it.

### 7. Fixes, best first

1. **Get the replayed pose into the render-side buffers of the bodies the replay draws itself, and place them the ghost's way.**
   - **Step 1, read-only, live:** for one body the game updates and one the replay draws, read the entry at [page + 0x40] + slot × 0x20: + 0x00 and + 0x08 (pointers), + 0x14 (on). Compare its per-bone 3x4s (0x30 a bone, as 0x142FD8840 writes them) with the world pose (page + 0x08) and the page + 0x10 matrices, to learn what they hold.
   - **Step 2:** every frame, write those buffers from the drawn world pose, and call 0x142FD8F20(pose, drawn root 4x4, 16-byte aligned, 0) for the placement and the culling. Keep the gate held, so the ragdoll's pose job doesn't run.
   - **At stop:** give the bytes back as RawRestore does now, plus the placement through 0x1432E06B0(body, &m) → 0x142FD8F20(pose, &m, 0).
   - This covers downed KSec, and maybe the up-close vanishing.
   - Risk: none of this runs the animation graph (that is what crashed earlier). What the scene update inside 0x142FD8F20 does on a body that is partly torn down is not known.
2. **Dropped guns:** the same call, with the recorded gun root, after the game's own placement each frame. The order has to be checked live: if the body job runs after the replay's call, the game's placement wins. The diagnostic: set it, then read it on the next frame.
3. **Shots:** find the client's per-shot function with a temporary counting hook on PamClientWeaponFiringComponent (0x141C34518) and the fire managers' slots during a fight. Then record (time, weapon, origin, direction) and replay only what the client makes. The open question is whether the client bullet does damage. Frostbite usually does damage on the server, but for this game it isn't checked, and neither is which side the replay's HumanDamage hook is on.
4. **The hunt:** unchanged (§5).

<a id="n10"></a>

# 10. Faith's on-screen hit effects, and the characters' culling box (2026-10-24)

Read from the game's code and data files only (offline, read-only). Nothing here was read live.

### 1. On-screen hit effects (verified in code and data)

**What they are.**
- `characters/faithcharacter` imports `FX/_Old/VisualEnviroments/Fullscreen/Faith_HitEffect_Prefab`.
- The prefab holds six visual environments. Its logic switches them on through `Enabled` and fades them through `Visibility` (sequences 400 to 600 ms).

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| VE_FS_Damage | The red frame (screen effect, shader SS_Screen_Damage) and a vignette |
| VE_FS_Damage_Add | Colour correction and tonemap (exposure) |
| VE_FS_Damage_Sub | Desaturation |
| VE_FS_Critical | The low-health frame (SS_Screen_Critical), looping |
| VE_FS_Critical_Sub | Colour change while health is low |
| VE_FS_Shield | A screen effect (SS_Screen_Shield) and a vignette |

- The electric fence's hit is `FX/VE/Combat/General/VE_Hit_Tazer_Additive` (the Flytrap fence prefab).
- The melee and knockout flashes are visual environments inside effects. They belong to Faith's own attacks, not to her being hit.

**How the game mixes them.**
- The manager is at `[0x142568CD8]`. Its update, `0x143705B30`, runs in the client update (the game thread). It calls `0x143703D60(view, ...)` for each of its views (`[+0x2358, +0x2360)`).
- A view is mixed only while its `+0x3F00` is set. The mix clears it at the end.
- The view's list `[+0x530, +0x538)` holds one record per VisualEnvironmentEntity (vtable `0x141AFA440`), at entity `+0xA0`:

| Offset | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+0` | Visibility |
| `+4` | The future visibility |
| `+0xD` | Set: left out of the mix (the constructor writes `!Enabled` there) |
| `+0x30` | Blend mode |
| `+0x38` on | Its components |

- An environment made from a reference object keeps that object at entity `+0x60`. The object's Blueprint is at `+0x18`; the blueprint's Name is at `+0x10`.

**The fix.**
- A hook on `0x143703D60`. Its byte checks cover:
  - the mix itself;
  - its dirty-flag check and clear;
  - its skip check;
  - the constructor's writes to `+0xAD` and `+0x60`.
- While the tools' camera is on, the hit environments get `+0xD` set for the mix. The game's value goes back right after, wherever ours is still there.
- A view is marked to be mixed again when the camera goes on or off.
- Log line: "Free camera: Faith's hit effects are left out of the picture (first: name)".

**Not covered.**
- The HUD's health lens: it's UI, and the tools' "Show HUD" hides it.
- Faith's movement environments (speed, fall, wall run and heavy landing blur): they are not hit effects.

### 2. The characters' culling box (verified in code; the cause is inferred)

**The box.**
- PamClientCharacterEntity gives it in slot 23 (`0x14390FDE0`):
  - rows at `+0x2D0`, `+0x2E0` and `+0x2F0`, and the centre at `+0x300`;
  - the corners at `+0x310` and `+0x320`, around the centre;
  - 4 m or 2 m added on each side (which one depends on `[+0x1D8]` slot 15).
- With no box (`+0x2F0` all zero), it gives its physics bounds or a fixed box instead.

**How the game makes it.**
- `0x14391C700` makes it. Its only caller is slot 84 (`0x143919040`), from the character update.
- It uses the BoundingBoxBones (data `+0xE0`), in the character's own frame.
- Each bone is where the **PamMovementImpactManager** (`[0x14257C180]`, the footstep manager) last had it:
  - its map is keyed by the pose `[+0x340]+0x158`;
  - each entry holds the previous position, the current position and a time step.

**The cause (inferred, not read live).**
- The manager's positions follow the game's own updates of the body.
- A body the replay draws itself isn't updated by the game, so its box stayed where it lies. With the camera close, that box was out of view and the body was culled.
- This matches Faith's own vanishing, fixed when her box pose got the replay. The dead KSec's bounding box was also its body's pose (seen in game).

**The fix.**
- A hook on `0x14391C700`. Its byte checks cover:
  - the function itself and its corner writes;
  - the getter's first read;
  - the tail jump;
  - vtable slots 23 and 84.
- For each character it draws, the replay writes a box around the drawn pose:
  - axis aligned;
  - around bones 1 to 3 and every bone built from its parent;
  - at most 20 m on a side.
- The box is written when the replay draws the body, and again right after the game makes its own.
- The game's box goes back when the body isn't drawn any more, and at stop. This is the box as it was at the replay's first write.
- The client character destructor is now hooked on its own, not only with the diagnostic. It drops the box, so none is written into a destroyed character.
- Log line: "its culling box goes with the drawn body (size; the game's was N m from it)". That distance tests the theory.

### 3. Sounds

- At playback, all the recorded voices were there; the 192 limit wasn't reached (seen in game).
- The real loss was elsewhere: past 64 events in one frame, the rest were dropped. Now a frame plays up to 128 events, and the rest wait for the next frame.
- Still not recorded:
  - KSec voice lines;
  - KSec footsteps and gear;
  - Shock Protector, hunter drone and VTOL shots.
- Their sound names haven't been seen yet; a fight's sound log would show them.

# 11. The hunter drone: its sounds, effects and AI (2026-10-24)

Read offline and read-only: the game's data (`characters/enemy/dronesecurity/aidrone`) and its code. Nothing was read live. Event and field names come from hashes resolved against the game's own strings. Ones that didn't resolve are given as hashes.

**Parser fix first.** The EBX reader drifted by 16 bytes in some large files.
- The cause: an exported instance's GUID is aligned to its type's alignment, and the instance base is aligned after it. The old reader aligned the base 8 bytes after an unaligned GUID.
- `fb/ebx.py` is fixed. It now reads aidrone, faithcharacter and vtol cleanly.
- Re-dumping the 55 KSec files with the fix changed values in four: `aimelee_echo`, `standardai_enemy_additional`, `pf_helilandanddeploy` and `vehicles/vtol/vtol`.
- The earlier reports drew nothing from the misread values, except that the VTOL's weapon was "not found". See §6.

- The hunter drone is `Characters/Enemy/DroneSecurity/AIDrone`.
  - Its mesh is `drone_hunter_mesh`, its AI specialisation `AIDrone`, its skeleton `masterdronesecurity_ske`.
  - The city alert's air pathfinding layer (`cityalert/layer0_airpathfinding`) and `exitstrategy` place it.
- `AIDrone_NoAI` is a scripted copy (benefactor, the Family Matters drone loop). It uses the same taser sounds.
