# 20. The hang when a mission started during a replay recording (2026-10-25)

### What was seen

- The replay was recording Faith when the mission set the clock (seen in game). In the same second the tools'
  catch-up started (bounce light solve time 5 -> 20 ms, exposure at once, a whole cubemap captured in a frame),
  Enlighten light map ids were refused (whole city loaded, more coming in), and the sun shadows got new views 3, 4,
  5 (the extra reflection faces of that frame, "far - near 10 m" each; views are 0x89400 apart). Nothing came
  after that, and no crash. The replay's sub-level hold kept nothing, so this isn't the fast travel hang.
- The hung game, read read-only from outside (OpenProcess QUERY | VM_READ, GetThreadContext without suspending,
  dbghelp StackWalk64 with the tools' PDB, no writes, only the threads' own stacks read): six game
  threads at 100% CPU, all in a SwitchToThread loop; two job workers asleep; no thread inside the tools' code
  (only the tools' own idle threads: Main::Run in SleepEx, the thunder thread on its condition variable); no
  thread waiting on a lock (no RtlAcquireSRWLock / critical section waiter).

Every one of the six had the same innermost frames:

```
SwitchToThread <- 0x142FB9370 (in 0x142FB9250) <- 0x142FB9051 (in 0x142FB8F20) <- 0x142FBA03B (in 0x142FB9F00)
  <- 0x142FBB3B6 (in 0x142FBB2F0) <- 0x142FB9E7A (in 0x142FB9DB0)
```

Above that: one was the main loop (0x142A2D470 -> 0x1431A40E0 waiting on the render job, "waitRenderSync",
0x1431A4E6E -> 0x142A9AED0); one a worker running the particle emitter cull (0x143106880, job "emitterCull",
its parallel-for 0x142A999B0 -> 0x142A9A4F0 kicking its pieces at 0x142A9A90A); one a Havok thread
(0x142DFDCC0 -> 0x142DFD9B0 -> 0x142E00230, kick at 0x142E00333); three workers (0x142FBB040
loop) that had just finished a job.

### The game's job system (offline)

- The job system object is `[0x142373E70]` (stored at 0x142A948A7; the emitter parallel-for reads it at 0x142A9A578,
  the waits at 0x142A9AF71); its `+0` is the job manager (0x142FBA974), and the manager's `+8` is the system again
  (ctor 0x142FB7890 at 0x142FB78C6). Made once at start-up by 0x142A94750 -> 0x142FBA890 -> 0x142FB7890 from a
  settings block (defaults 0x142FB8010).
- **The global queue** (jobs any thread may run): manager `+0x20`, set up by 0x142FBA9B0(queue, room, extra, ...):
  `+0x00` how many are in it (lock inc on push 0x142FBC153, lock dec on take-out 0x142FBC0A7), `+0x08` the slots
  (16 bytes each, room + 8 x extra), `+0x10` the room, `+0x14` the extra, `+0x20` a lock-free stack of free nodes
  (one per slot, node `+0` its slot index, 0x142FBAA9F loop), `+0x30` the nodes. **Room: 1024** (0x142A94841
  `mov r8d, 0x400` -> 0x142FBBC20 writes settings `+0x30`; the default is 0x80), extra 0.
- Push 0x142FBC0C0(queue, job): takes a free node (0x142C32AF0, 0 when none), writes the job into its slot
  (cmpxchg16b), returns the index, or -1 when no node is free (the queue is full).
- Take-out 0x142FBBEF0: 0x142FBA210 scans all room + 8 x extra slots for the best match (priority byte), so its
  cost grows with the room (one reason the fix doesn't make the queue bigger).
- Finishing a job: 0x142FB9DB0 runs it (0x142FBAEE0; jobs with flag 0x100 run on their own fiber), then 0x142FBB2F0
  takes its list of waiting jobs and 0x142FB9F00 calls each one's continuation; for a job that's now ready,
  0x142FB8F20 puts it in its thread's queue (manager `+0x928`, 0xF0 each, `+0x950` how many) or, for any thread,
  through **0x142FB9250**: push; when full, if the manager's **help byte** `+0x8F0` is set, run one queued job
  first (0x142FB8800 a context from the pool at manager `+0x240`, 0x142FBB400(context, 0xFF, 0xFF) runs one,
  0x142FBA400 gives the context back; the same three the game's waits use, e.g. 0x142A9AF60), then a watchdog
  callback past a time limit, SwitchToThread (0x142C79070), try again (0x142FB937E `js 0x142FB92D0`).
- The help byte is settings `+0x10`, set to 1 only when 0x142C77DC0 returns 2 (0x142A94851 `cmp eax, 2`). That
  function caches field `+0x20` of a 48-byte block filled by an import: the shape of GetSystemInfo, i.e. the
  processor count. (The import's name isn't in the dumped image, which has only the DRM's import table.) So the
  game runs a job itself when the queue is full only on 2-processor PCs. Other readers of `+0x8F0`: 0x142FBA460 (a
  getter), used by 0x142C30C00 and the waits 0x142C3E690 / 0x142C3E740 (a helping wait 0x142FBC460 vs 0x142FBBC50).
  `+0x8F1` (0x142FB8F20, 0x142FB9EB2) runs ready jobs inline; `+0x8F2` (default 1) is the multi-thread switch.

### The cause

The global queue was full and every running thread was trying to put a job into it (0x142FB9250, help byte 0),
so nobody took one out: a deadlock. The stuck threads' registers agree: rbp = the manager in the
0x142FB9250 frames, r9 = manager + 0x40 (the free node stack) left over from 0x142C32AF0. Not read:
the queue's count itself. So "full" is inferred from push failing
(no free node) at all six threads at once, not seen as 1024. A node leak would look the same; the count tells
the two apart (full events with the count at the room, vs. failures with a low count).

What filled it: the mission's clock change started the tools' catch-up in the same second, with the
whole city loaded:
- Enlighten's update (0x143793670) makes jobs from the scheduler's lists (0x143790F40: systems while jobs out
  < JobCount 64 and the solve time lasts, then light probe tasks on what's left): per system about 2 jobs
  (0x143793F70 / 0x143793FDB), per 20 probe tasks 7 (two sync jobs 0x14379413B / 0x1437941AB, three groups of up to
  8 0x143794312, 0x1437943BB, 0x14379443A), released together when the job they wait for ends. Up to 2252
  probe tasks were measured in one update at 20 ms with the whole city: about 790 + 130 jobs,
  against ~200 + 130 at the game's 5 ms.
- 6 reflection faces in one frame (views 3, 4, 5) instead of 1: each face is a render view with its own
  culling jobs (the stuck emitterCull handles views per type, 0x143106C9D / 0x143106D27).
- The mission's own loading (light map id requests: 1912 more in one second).
Which of these pushed it over isn't known; together they did. **An earlier freeze** (Enlighten
catch-up at 128 ms and 512 jobs) had the same frames ("0x142FB9051 -> 0x142FBC0E4"): the same deadlock.

### The fix

`Util/Hooks.cpp`, "The game's job queue": `HookJobQueueHelp` checks the code (0x142FB9250's start, both pushes
and their `jns` / `js`, the help byte's `cmp` / `je` at 0x142FB92D0, the three help calls, the caller
0x142FB904C, the build stamp) and puts a cave at 0x142FB92D0 via MinHook (threads held while it's written): `lock
inc` a counter, jump to 0x142FB92D9 (the help). So on a full queue a thread runs a queued job itself, as the game
does on 2-processor PCs; nothing else changes, and the help byte stays the game's (the two waits that read it
keep their behaviour). Log: "Hooked JobQueueHelp at 0x142FB92D0 ...", "The game's job queue (jobs for any thread)
has room for 1024", "up to N of 1024 jobs waiting at once" (from half full on, each further tenth; sampled every
pass of the tools' loop, ~5 ms), and "[WARNING] The game's job queue was full (1024 jobs): N times a thread ran a
queued job itself to make room ..." (at most every 5 s).

Not done, and why: a bigger queue (patching 0x142A94841 before 0x142A94750 runs) costs every take-out a longer
scan (0x142FBA210), and whether the tools get there before the game makes its job system isn't known.
Turning the help byte on also changes two waits. Cutting the catch-up back would lose what it's for and wouldn't
cover the other bursts.

Risks, not seen: a thread running a job inside the push nests job runs (as the game's waits do); a long chain of
full-queue nestings could use a lot of stack. The game takes the same path on 2-processor PCs; MEC's minimum
spec is most likely (not checked) a 4-thread CPU, so that path may hardly ever have run on PC.

### The queue's room and peaks, seen in game (2026-10-25)

- The room read live through [[0x142373E70]] + 0x30 is 1024, which confirms the offsets decoded offline.
- A time-of-day jump with no recording: the catch-up's burst alone took the queue to 666 of 1024 jobs waiting at
  once, 65 % of its room.
- A mission's clock change while recording (catch-up, the game's own reset, a loading screen), with the city's
  loading settled (no flood of new light map ids), didn't fill the queue: **no hang**.
- So bursts reach 2/3 of the room, which supports the cause. This doesn't show the fix getting the game out of a
  full queue.

### Peak after each time jump

`util::hooks::NoteTimeJump(from, to)` (called by VisualsManager::CatchUpBounceLight at every jump it detects, the game's
thread, atomics only) opens a window in the tools' loop (SampleJobQueue, ~5 ms); 10 s after the last jump LogJobQueue
writes "The game's job queue after the time jump from A to B[, N jumps in a row]: at most M of 1024 jobs waiting at once
(P %), T s after it (sampled every ~5 ms by the tools); found full K times". Only with "Light catches up with time
jumps" on (the jump detection is part of it). [not verified in game]

### The help hung the game itself

Seen in game: Release's loading screen while the replay recorded (bundles streaming in while it recorded, the
mission's time of day jumping twice). The queue was found full again and again (up to 1024 of 1024
waiting); the last warning says 0 waiting; then the game drew no frame. The process still ran, two
threads at about 100 % CPU each. Read live, read-only
(OpenProcess query + read, GetThreadContext without suspending, StackWalk64):

A worker (innermost first):

    SwitchToThread <- 0x142A9B02F (0x142A9AFF8's wait loop: 0x142FBB400 to run a job, 0x142A637F0 to yield,
    0x142FBAB50 whether the waited-for job is done) <- 0x142A9AEFF <- 0x1435FE81A <- 0x143595156 <- 0x143743491
    <- 0x14373EAC8 <- 0x1431D8948 <- 0x143578840 <- 0x143579051 (the job run in another's place)
    <- 0x142FBB01E <- 0x142FB9E2E <- 0x142FBB5FA <- 0x142FBB4A5 <- 0x142FB92FE (the help's call 0x142FB92F9 ->
    0x142FBB400: reached only through the tools' cave, the help byte is 0 except on 2-processor PCs) <- 0x142FB9051 (0x142FB8F20's
    push, 0x142FB904C -> 0x142FB9250) <- 0x142FB89FB <- 0x1435CE4D3 <- 0x1435D026D (the job being run)
    <- 0x142FBB01E <- 0x142FB9E2E <- 0x142FBB786 <- 0x142FBB08A <- 0x142C7895B (the worker's loop)

Another thread: SwitchToThread <- 0x142A9B07C (the same wait loop) <- 0x142A9B11F <- 0x143575230 <- 0x1431A4843
<- 0x142A2E069 <- 0x142A315B5 <- 0x142A2923C <- 0x142A6342B <- 0x142C7884D.
Three more workers wait on their events (0x142FBB9D9): the queue is empty.

An earlier hang on quit had a thread with
0x142A9B02F, 0x142A9B11F, 0x143575230, 0x1431A4843 and the push frames 0x2FBC0E4, 0x2FB994A, 0x2FB908D on its stack.

So the job run in another's place waits for a job that can't finish while the thread under it is stuck in the help:
most likely the job being handed on (it is never pushed until the help returns) or one that needs it. Running a job
inline in the middle of a hand-on is what the game does only on 2-processor PCs.

### The fix now: the full queue's jobs kept [not verified in game]

- 0x142FB9250 (push, try again while full) has one caller: 0x142FB904C in 0x142FB8F20 (hand a job on: the per-group
  queue, the main thread's lists or the global queue by the job's + 0x80 / + 0x38, then 0x142FB97F0 wakes an idle
  worker: cmpxchg [worker + 0x5C] 0 -> 1, SetEvent). Nothing reads what 0x142FB9250 returns. No thread-local state
  in 0x142FB8F20 or 0x142FB97F0.
- The cave at 0x142FB92D0 (as before: the help byte's cmp, reached the first time the push finds the queue full and
  after each failed try): lock inc [count]; KeepJob(rbp = manager, r15 = job); a kept job leaves through
  0x142FB9384 (the push's own way out: rsi, rdi, rbx, xmm6, xmm7 back from the stack, ret); one that couldn't be kept
  (no memory) goes to the trampoline (the cmp and je: the game's own code).
- A tools thread (HandOnKeptJobs) wakes on KeepJob's event, and while any are kept, hands the oldest on with
  0x142FB8F20(manager, job) once the queue has 16 free (ReadJobQueue), else sleeps 1 ms. A hand-on that finds the
  queue full again is kept again (at the end). The thread never stops (the game may wait for a kept job while it
  closes).
- Bytes checked before hooking (IsJobQueueCode): the push and its tries as before, the way out at 0x142FB9384 (42
  bytes), 0x142FB8F20's prologue, its push call (mov rcx, rbx; call 0x142FB9250) and its wake call at 0x142FB9088.
- A bigger queue was looked at: the room is cfg + 0x30 (0x142FBBC20, set to 0x400 at 0x142A94841 before
  0x142FBA890 makes the manager; the default 0x80 from 0x142FB8010). The queue is a node pool (free list at queue +
  0x20, nodes at + 0x30, slots at + 8), any size works, but every take (0x142FBBEF0) calls 0x142FBA210, which looks
  through all slots for the best match, so each take would get slower with it. Also the tools patch after the code
  is decrypted, racing the game's start.

<a id="n21"></a>

# 21. The MagRope system, and how to put it in the replay (2026-10-25)

Offline research only: the saved decrypted game image (`game_image.bin`) and the game's data files on
disk (the `fb` parser). The live game wasn't read. No code was changed.

Each claim is marked:
- **[code]**: read in the game's code.
- **[data]**: read in the game's data files.
- **[not verified]**: inferred, not checked.

### 1. In short

- The MagRope's line is one entity on Faith's character: a **PamClientMagropeRenderEntity**. It
  exists all the time. It only has a mesh while Faith's animation is in a MagRope state.
- Faith's animation (ANT) turns the line on and off. Entering one of three tagged animation states
  shows it, and leaving the state hides it.
- Showing the line does three things:
  - it creates the rope mesh `objects/rope/magrope_skinned`;
  - it adds the line to a MagRope update list;
  - it starts two effects, FX_MagRope_Muzzle at the hand and FX_MagRope_Impact at the anchor.
- Every frame, the line is a **straight polyline** with no sag or physics:
  - first the anchor (an animation game-state value);
  - then three points on Faith's right hand and forearm: the index finger twice, then the forearm
    gauntlet.
- The game spreads that polyline evenly over the rope mesh's **201 joints**. It then builds their
  skinning matrices and the rope's culling box.
- **Why the replay has no line today:** during playback the real Faith isn't in a MagRope animation
  state, so the line has no mesh. The MagRope sounds and effects are already caught by the replay's
  filters (section 5).
- **Proposed fix:**
  - Record the 4 polyline points while the line is shown (64 bytes per sample).
  - During playback, give Faith's line entity its mesh with the game's own create function.
  - Feed it the recorded points through the game's own points-to-joints function, called from the
    game's own update pass for that entity.
  - Remove the mesh with the game's own destroy function.

### 2. The classes

| Class | TypeInfo | vtable | Constructor | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PamClientRopeRenderEntity (base) | 0x14285E770 | 0x141C5DFE0 | 0x1439AB3F0 | class ids 0x4EA..0x4EC **[code]** |
| PamClientMagropeRenderEntity | 0x142854230 | 0x141C410F8 | 0x14391DCD0 | id 0x4EC **[code]** |
| PamClientGameSplineRenderEntity | 0x1428542D0 | 0x141C40F68 | 0x14391D7F0 (size 0x110) | id 0x4EB, the zip-line cable **[code]** |
| PamClientMagropeEntity (anchors in levels) | 0x14285ED90 | 0x141C619E0 | | **[code]** |
| PamClientMagRopeVisualizerEntity (swing hint) | 0x142855900 | 0x141C46B18 | | **[code]** |

- Both render subclasses also set a second interface vtable `0x141C41030` at +0x30 **[code]**.
  - Slot 0 (0x143920400) gives the rope's bone count.
  - Slot 6 (0x1439AD8C0) gives an identity transform and the box at +0xA0/+0xB0.
- **Correction to an earlier note:** the function `0x143926830` with the whip wave belongs to the
  **game-spline (zip-line) cable**, not the MagRope **[code]**.
  - The constructor at 0x14391D7F0 lays out +0xC8 points, +0xE8 a float, and +0xF0/+0xF0+0x10 the
    ends. Its data is PamGameSplineRenderEntityData (StartOffset +0x28, EndOffset +0x2C, Scale +0x30).
  - Its update list is at [0x142577778], with updater slot 2 = 0x143925B30.
  - The MagRope has no throw animation of its own (section 4).

### 3. The game data (Faith's character, `characters/faithcharacter`) [data]

**The line entity: PamMagropeRenderEntityData #1685**
- Model: `objects/rope/magrope_skinned`.
- Skeleton: `animations/skeletons/magrope_ske`, with **207 bones**:
  - Reference, AITrajectory, Trajectory, TrajectoryEnd, Connect, ConnectEnd;
  - then **joint1 .. joint201**.
- Scale: **0.15**.
- Joints (`PamMagRopeRenderJoint`: Offset float3 at +0x00, BoneId at +0x10 **[code + data]**):
  1. BoneId **135** = RightHandIndex1, offset (0.005, 0.025, 0.01)
  2. BoneId **135** = RightHandIndex1, offset (0.01, 0.03, -0.055)
  3. BoneId **152** = RightForeArmRoll2, offset (0, -0.033, 0.007)

  The bone names come from `characters/skeletons/skeleton_faith`, which has 182 bones.

**Its connections**

| From | To |
|---|---|
| ReadAntGameStateEntityData #1730, output 0xEEF3B93F (ReadVector3TransformGameState #1753) | the line's **Anchor** |
| link: the line's **Animatable** (hash 0xBF40C871 = "Animatable") | Faith's AntAnimatableEntityData #179 |
| the line's output 0x45F8E9D1 (anchor turned toward the hand) | EffectComponent #78 (`fx/weapons/magrope/fx_magrope_impact`) Transform |
| the line's output TargetTransform (hand turned toward the anchor) | EffectComponent #80 (`fx/weapons/magrope/fx_magrope_muzzle`) Transform |
| the line's event 0xFC689444 | Start on #78 and #80 |
| the line's output 0x0BFB1618 (bool) | WriteAntGameStateEntityData #1919 (WriteBoolGameState 0xEDBC1501) |

**Show and hide events**

AntEventEntityData #182 has 3 animation tags. Entering a tag shows the line; leaving it hides it:

| Tag id | Enter event → line | Leave event → line |
|---|---|---|
| 0x7BF26E77 | 0x5D8CF5C8 → 0x8E85640C | 0x5187615B → 0x7FC6CF83 |
| 0xD81C8A20 | 0x8B40885F → 0x15F909DB | 0xD50E3CCC → 0xE665D554 |
| 0x8C1C4370 | 0xC5D1793B → 0x2E52663F | 0xA1F2BA48 → 0x7C6662B0 |

- The game data doesn't name the tags. Three tags matching the three MagRope kinds (Swing, Pull up,
  Pull down; `FBMagropeType_*`) is **[not verified]**.

**The in-game names** (from each asset's Name field)
- Effects: `FX/Weapons/MagRope/FX_MagRope_Muzzle` and `FX/Weapons/MagRope/FX_MagRope_Impact`.
- Sounds: `ME_Sound/Gadgets/MagRope/MagRope`, `…/MagRopeWhipCord`, `…/MagRopeAttach`,
  `…/MagRopeGenElements`, and about 25 more under `me_sound/gadgets/magrope/`.

**The anchor props**
- `MagRope_Camera1/2` are plain PamStaticModelEntityData (physics, health). Their prefab adds a
  lens flare.
- What turns them toward Faith isn't in these two files **[not verified]**.

### 4. How the line works [code]

**Fields** (PamClientMagropeRenderEntity; the base class owns +0x30 .. +0xB0)

| Offset | What |
|---|---|
| +0x28 | data (PamMagropeRenderEntityData) |
| +0x58 | the rope mesh entity (0: not shown) |
| +0x60 | skinning matrices, 3 float4 per bone |
| +0x80 | skeleton |
| +0x38 | rest segment lengths (bones − 6) |
| +0x88 | rest length |
| +0x90 | the mesh's interface |
| +0xA0 / +0xB0 | culling box |
| +0xC8 | input points (joints + 1 = 4) |
| +0xE8 | input segment lengths (3 floats) |
| +0x108 | output points (bones − 6 = **201**, 16 bytes each) |
| +0x128 | Faith's pose object (ref-counted) |
| +0x130 | Anchor property {connection, default} |
| +0x140 / +0x148 | the two output transforms |
| +0x150 | the bool output |

**Spawn: slot 15, `0x143924E90`**
- Sizes +0x108 to bones − 6, +0xC8 to joints + 1, and +0xE8 to joints.
- Writes the bool output +0x150 = **false**, after an integrity-check compare. It's the only writer
  of +0x150 in the MagRope code.

**Events: slot 4, `0x143921D90`**
- 0x2E52663F, 0x8E85640C, 0x15F909DB, 0x71D9CEFD go to slot 23 (**show**).
- 0x8A18A372, 0xE665D554, 0x7C6662B0, 0x7FC6CF83 go to slot 24 (**hide**).

**Show: slot 23, `0x143926160`**
1. Base slot 23, `0x1439B2D00`: if +0x58 is 0, it creates the mesh entity from data Model
   (0x1431C4830, identity transform). It registers the line's +0x30 interface on the mesh
   (+0xC0 slot 7), sets +0x90 to the mesh's interface (TypeInfo 0x1427EE7A0), and positions the
   mesh (0x1431CAFE0).
2. `0x1439200A0(this + 0xC0, 1)`: lazily makes the MagRope updater (global **[0x142577788]**,
   vtable 0x141C410C8, named "PamClientMagropeRenderEntity") and adds the line with interval 1
   (0x143174420).
3. Finds the linked "Animatable" (it must be a ClientAntAnimatableEntity). Stores its pose object
   at +0x128 (from [animatable + 0x158], via 0x14324BF80).
4. Writes the two output transforms:
   - +0x140: at the anchor, facing the hand point;
   - +0x148: at the hand point, facing the anchor.

   The hand point is the last joint's bone with its offset.
5. Fires event 0xFC689444, which starts the two effects.

**Hide: slot 24, `0x1439267E0`**
- Base `0x1439B3300` unregisters the interface, calls DestroyRequest on the mesh (0x143167700), and
  sets +0x58 and +0x90 to 0.
- `0x143174D30([0x142577788], this)` queues its removal from the updater.
- Fires event 0xAA8ECFFC ("OnStop"), which isn't connected in Faith's data.

**Per frame**

The updater's slot 2, `0x143925C10`, calls `0x143926CE0(line, dt)` for each line on its list.

1. It needs a mesh (+0x58), a valid pose object (+0x128, byte +0x68), and an Anchor connection
   with flag bit 6. Without the mesh or pose object, it removes itself from the updater. Without
   the Anchor connection, it skips the frame.
2. in[0] = the anchor's position.
3. in[1..3] = each joint's bone transform with its offset rotated by the bone, plus the bone's
   position. The bone transform comes from `0x142FD2B00(pose, bone, out, addRoot = 1)`: entries of
   0x20 bytes at [pose + 0x50] (position + scale, then a quaternion), plus bone 0's position.
4. Segment lengths go to +0xE8. The total is the sum.
5. Resampling, for k = 0 .. 200: the point at fraction k / 200 along the polyline's length, by
   cumulative segment length and a linear blend. The results go to +0x108.
6. `0x1439B3350(line, +0x108 points, 201, data Scale 0.15)`.

**Points to joints: `0x1439B3350(entity, points, count, scale)`**
1. Requires +0x58.
2. The box = the points' min/max ±1 m, written to +0xA0/+0xB0. This matches what was seen in game:
   one box corner sat at the anchor ±1 m.
3. Sets the mesh's transform (mesh vtable +0xC8).
4. For bones 0..5 and then each rope joint: an orientation along the points, built with the bind
   pose from skeleton +0x30 (0x142D25B60). Writes three rows per bone into +0x60.
5. Hands `{current length ÷ rest length, 1, 1, 1}` to the mesh's interface (0x1431E55A0). This is
   likely a stretch value for the shader **[not verified]**.

**So the rope never "flies" out.**
- It appears at full length the frame the animation state is entered, while the muzzle effect (with
  a ribbon emitter, `em_magrope_muzzle_ribbon`) and the impact effect play.
- That the ribbon makes the "shot" look is **[not verified]** visually.

### 5. What the replay already has [code: the tools' Hooks.cpp]

- **Sounds:** `IsFaithOwnSoundName` takes `ME_Sound/Gadgets/`, so the MagRope's sound entities are
  recorded and played as Faith's own. That they are hers (owned by her character) is
  **[not verified]**; they were found near her and at the anchor (seen in game).
- **Effects:** `IsGunEffectName` takes `FX/Weapons/`, so FX_MagRope_Muzzle and FX_MagRope_Impact are
  recorded within 80 m of Faith and played again. Both are effect components of Faith's character,
  so they go through the effect function the replay hooks (0x14329B860) **[not verified live]**.
- **The line itself:** not drawn. The rope registry exists already: the hRopeCtor / hRopeDtor
  hooks, `g_WorldRopes`, 32 entries. It's only read by the world log today.
- **Anchor props turning, and the swing-hint meshes:** these are static models moved by the level.
  The moving-models replay (ReplayModels) likely covers them when near Faith **[not verified]**.

### 6. Proposed implementation

**Recording** (with each replay sample, 30 Hz)
1. Find Faith's line: the registry entry whose mesh (+0x58) is set and whose in[1] point is within
   about 2 m of Faith.
2. Keep its data pointer [+0x28], to find her line again after a respawn. Faith's data instance is
   shared by every Faith, which is **[not verified]**.
3. Each sample while its mesh exists: copy the 4 input points (+0xC8). That's 64 bytes, read-only,
   inside `__try`. A sample without it means the line is hidden.

**Playback**

Over the samples where the recording had the line:
1. Find Faith's live line by the kept data pointer.
2. If the game shows it itself at that moment (+0x58 set, not by the replay), the real Faith is
   using her rope (Faith control during playback). Leave it alone.
3. Otherwise mark it replay-driven and add it to the MagRope updater with the game's own call,
   `0x1439200A0(line + 0xC0, 1)`.
4. **New hook on `0x143926CE0`** (MagRope-only code). For a replay-driven line:
   1. If it has no mesh, call the base create `0x1439B2D00(line)`. Don't call slot 23: that would
      start the two effects a second time, since the effect replay already plays them.
   2. Interpolate the recorded 4 points to the replay's time, resample them to the line's output
      count (read from +0x108..+0x110, 201), and call `0x1439B3350(line, points, count, scale)`.
   3. Return without the game's own update.

   This runs in the game's own update pass for that entity, which is where the game itself creates
   and poses it.
5. When the recording's line ends, or on stop, a loop or a seek out of it: call the base destroy
   `0x1439B3300(line)` and the updater removal `0x143174D30([0x142577788], line)`. These are slot
   24's calls, without its OnStop event.
6. The tools' DestroyRequest hook only holds server characters, so the mesh's destroy goes through
   **[code]**.

**Why recorded points, not the replayed pose**
- The game's own update takes the hand from Faith's pose object (+0x128).
- Whether that object reflects the replay's pose override is **[not verified]**.
- Recorded points match the recording exactly and don't depend on the live ANT, whose anchor game
  state is stale during playback.

**Risks**
1. Creating the mesh from a hook: it's done where the game itself does it, in the entity's update
   on the game thread, but outside an animation event.
2. Faith's rope after a respawn: picking the line by data pointer needs a live check.
3. Faith control during playback: the hook keeps the game's own update off a replay-driven line.
   If the real Faith starts a rope at the same time, the replay's rope is skipped (rule 2).
4. 0x1439B3350 indexes the skinning buffer by count, so it must get exactly the line's own count
   (read +0x108..+0x110 each time).

### 7. Still open

- The names of the three animation tags, and which ANT states use them.
- What turns `MagRope_Camera1/2` toward Faith, and whether ReplayModels catches it near her.
- Whether Faith's rope data pointer stays the same after a respawn, and whether NPC MagRopes
  (Icarus, `icarus_magrope`) share it.
- The meaning of output 0x0BFB1618 (the game state written false at spawn) and output hash
  0x45F8E9D1. Neither matters for the replay.
- The zip-line cable wobble (PamClientGameSplineRenderEntity, `0x143926830`) could be replayed the
  same way later. It has its own updater at [0x142577778].

### 8. Addresses

| What | Address |
|---|---|
| MagRope render: constructor / spawn / events / show / hide | 0x14391DCD0 / 0x143924E90 / 0x143921D90 / 0x143926160 / 0x1439267E0 |
| per-frame update | 0x143926CE0 |
| rope base: constructor / create mesh / destroy mesh | 0x1439AB3F0 / 0x1439B2D00 / 0x1439B3300 |
| points to joints | 0x1439B3350 |
| MagRope updater: global / add / remove / update all | [0x142577788] / 0x1439200A0 → 0x143174420 / 0x143174D30 / 0x143925C10 |
| bone transform from a pose object | 0x142FD2B00 |
| pose object from an animatable | 0x14324BF80 |
| zip-line cable: constructor / update / updater | 0x14391D7F0 / 0x143926830 / [0x142577778], 0x143925B30 |

The scripts used:
- `dfr.py`: a branch-following disassembler;
- `callers.py` / `leas.py`: raw-byte reference scans over the code sections;
- `strs.py` / `hashfind.py`: strings and hash names.

The game data parser is `fb\wiring.py` / `fb\show.py`.

<a id="n22"></a>

# 22. Missions' time of day, weather and Faith's look, and replays (2026-10-25)

Offline research (the decrypted game image, the `fb\` game data parser).
Nothing here was checked in game yet. Unverified points are marked **[not verified]**.

### 1. How missions set the time of day (verified in data and code)

#### In the game data
- **`gameplay/logic/pf_settimeofday`**: a LogicPrefab that missions and story beats use.
  - Its TimeOfDay field goes to a **TimeOfDayClockControllerEntity** (TimeToSet; data TimeToSet + 0x18,
    TimeScaleMultiplier + 0x1C, ControllerId + 0x20).
  - It also goes to a progression flag (the time saved with the game).
  - Its other events start or stop the clock.
  - Also in the data: `gameplay/logic/pf_timeofdayskip`, and the clock's own prefab
    `levels/sp/sp_maincity/lighting/visualenvironments/timeofday/timeofday` (TimeOfDayManagerEntity, see
    Research_TimeOfDay_Jump_2026-10-25.md).
- **`gameplay/progression/timeofday/*`** (about 50, e.g. `0630_to_0900`, `2100_to_0500`): PamFlagsCollectionAssets
  holding two flag values in seconds, e.g. 23400 and 32400 = 06:30 and 09:00.
  - **[not verified]** These look like the story's time windows. What reads them wasn't traced.

#### In the code
- **ServerTimeOfDayClockEntity**: vtable 0x141CD8438, getType 0x143BC4E00 -> TypeInfo 0x142896A70, a
  TimeOfDayClockEntity. This is the tools' clock (`[[[OFFSET_TIMEOFDAY] + 8] + 0x28]`).
  - Its constructor 0x143BC3AA0 sets:
    - **+ 0x30 the time** (data DefaultTime + 0x1C);
    - **+ 0xE8 the rate** (86400 / FullDayDuration + 0x18);
    - **+ 0xEC a time scale** (1.0);
    - + 0xF4 = -1;
    - **+ 0xF8 stopped** (data PausedOnLoad + 0x30).
  - Its update (slot 23, 0x143BC78E0) tests + 0xF8.
  - Its pace (0x143BC4CB0) = + 0xEC x + 0xE8 (x a curve when + 0xF4 > 0).
- **ServerTimeOfDayClockControllerEntity** (vtable 0x141CD8960) works on every ServerTimeOfDayClockEntity it
  finds (the class's instance list, entity = node - 0xD8):
  - its event handler 0x143BC4AA0:
    - event 0xA4259012 writes **TimeToSet to + 0x30** once;
    - event 0x0DD8DDF7 sets + 0xF8 = 1 (stopped);
    - event 0xC44B5C3C sets + 0xF8 = 0 (runs);
  - its property handler 0x143BC6520: property 0xAA3B68E3 (TimeScaleMultiplier) writes **+ 0xEC** when >= 0.
- **So in a mission the tools' time still applies.** The tools write the same + 0x30. A mission can only stop the
  clock or change its pace. Nothing in the controller keeps rewriting the time.
- **What didn't work: replays.** They never recorded the clock. A recording made in a mission's time played in
  whatever time it was at playback (often the free-roam time after the mission).

### 2. Weather

- The game has no weather system: rain is level-placed effects in a few zones, see Research_Weather_2026-10-25.md.
  The weather feature (VISUALS > Weather, `Visuals/Weather.cpp`) keeps the game's rain at the camera anywhere.
  Its `weather::GetState()` / `SetState()` are meant for replays.
- The other "weather" a mission has is its effects (smoke, dust, set pieces: FX/Ambient/...) and its visual
  environments.
- **The game's clouds and wind** come from the blended visual environment (ToD and cloud VEs such as
  `ve_tod_clouds_cirrus*` carry the sky's cloud fields and a WindComponentData). The replay records the blended
  state's **Clouds block (state + 0x390, 0x290 bytes)** and **Wind block (+ 0x6E0, 0x20)** 4 times a second, as
  the game shows them.
  - While playing, the known fields of the VISUALS components "Clouds" and "Wind" are written at each VE update
    (VisualsManager::WriteReplayLook): floats and colors blended between the two samples, anything else from
    the earlier one, and a component changed in the menu written on top.
  - When it stops nothing is written, and the game's blend puts its own back (as "Reset to game values" relies
    on).
- **Not done:** the other VE parts a mission changes (fog, grading). A replay can't make a VE entity that's gone,
  and writing a live one's visibility (+ 0xA0) was found risky before (MEC_Reverse_Notes: visibility 0 turned the
  grade blue).

### 3. Faith's look (verified in data; nothing changed)

- Faith's model comes from **7 story-stage customizations** in `characters/customizations/faith/`: `c_faith_prologue`,
  `c_faith_prologue_nogridlink`, `c_faith_notattoo`, `c_faith_notat_magrope1/2/3`, `c_faith_withtattoo`. There are
  also `_npc` variants.
- They're applied by the player spawner **`gameplay/spawners/pf_spspawn_01`**: seven CustomizeCharacterEntity
  (server realm), each with one customization, picked by story progression.
- No mission prefab imports them (importers of `c_faith_withtattoo`, `c_faith_prologue` and `c_faith_notat_magrope1`:
  only pf_spspawn_01). The default bag `unlock_faith_toolbag` comes from the customizations.
  `faith_pickupbag_basic` is only in the mesh variation database.
- **What this means for replays.** The replay poses the live Faith's body, so she wears what she wears at
  playback. Within one game session (replays aren't saved) that's the same look as when recording, unless a story
  beat changed her customization in between (e.g. the MagRope stages).
- Things a mission hands her (a delivery's package) are props, the mission items in
  Research_Missions_Replay_2026-10-25.md.
- **Not done:** giving the replayed Faith a recorded customization would mean running the customization on the
  live character (server component, mesh parts rebuilt). Whether that's safe is unknown, and like the spawning
  found unsafe earlier, it isn't attempted. Where the live character keeps its customization wasn't traced, so the
  replay can't yet tell you when the look differs.

### 4. What the tools do

- **Time of day in replays** (`Camera/FaithReplay.*`, `Visuals/VisualsManager.*`, config `[Replay] TimeOfDay`):
  - the clock is recorded with each sample (`m_Tods`);
  - while playing, `TimeOfDayAt` gives the recorded time: in a straight line the short way round midnight, but
    more than 120 s between two samples stays a jump. It's set through `VisualsManager::SetReplayTimeOfDay`
    (priority: camera track > replay > stopped clock > stuck-clock fix);
  - the time-jump catch-up (lighting reset, reflections) sees it like any jump;
  - at stop, `StopReplayTimeOfDay` gives back the clock's time from before (not while a track sets it).
- **Weather in replays:**
  - the weather menu's state (`weather::State`) is taken when recording starts;
  - while playing it's given (`ApplyRecordedWeather`);
  - at stop the earlier state comes back, only if the menu still holds the recorded state.
- **Mission and ambient effects** (`Util/Hooks.cpp` TakeInPlayingEffects, IsTakenInKind):
  - FX/UX and FX/Ambient effects are noted from their start (up to 32768, erased when stopped), with their
    parameters;
  - the ones within 80 m are taken in when recording starts;
  - each plays only while the game's own handle is gone;
  - **rain (FX/Ambient/Rain/) is left out**, because the weather menu moves the game's rain with the camera
    (`weather::FollowRows`).
- **TIME OF DAY menu:** a line when the game has stopped its clock or runs it at another pace (`ReadClockHold`
  reads + 0xF8 and + 0xEC, only on an entity whose vtable is 0x141CD8438).
- No new hooks. The reads are guarded and the class is checked by its vtable.

# 23. Delivery runs, dashes and missions in the replay (2026-10-25)

Offline research (game image and game data). What a run or mission puts in
the world, what the replay already records of it, what was added, and what can't be done safely.
Anything not checked in game is marked **[not verified]**.

### 1. What runs and missions are made of

#### The classes (reflection names in the game image)
- **Missions**: PamMissionEntity (client / server), PamMissionManagerEntity, PamMissionStatusEntity,
  PamMissionStartPointEntity, PamMissionDescription*, ObjectiveEntity / TacticalObjectiveEntity, and the UI
  providers PamClientUIMission* and PamClientUI*LeaderboardWidgetDataProvider.
  - PamMissionEntityData fields: Mission, FlagsSetWhenReplaying, the re-enable and stream-out delays, Enabled,
    StreamInOnAvailable, StreamOutOnCompleted / Fail / Abort, ReloadFromLastCheckpointOnFail,
    EnableCityAlertDuringMission, AllowStreamInWhenAlreadyInside.
  - Missions are in the main city's layers: layer26_sidecontentmanager, layer43_act1flow,
    layer59_securityhubs, layer64_deaddropdeliveryflow.
- **Checkpoints**: PamCheckpointEntity (client / server, only in gameplay/social/timetrial/pf_timetrialcheckpoint)
  and PamMissionCheckpointEntity (only in gameplay/mission/openworldsystems/pf_l_missioncheckpoint).
- **Countdowns**: PamCountdownEntityData (Timescale, AddValue, StartValue), in the city alert logic, three story
  layers, the auto-tutorial and the skip-video widget. The runs' timers are UI.
- **Runner Vision**: PamClientRunVisTrailRenderEntity. Its one instance is in
  levels/sp/sp_maincity/mainlogic/mainlogic/layer3_ingamemap_schematic, with these settings:
  - SplineTesselationFactor 25, TrailEntitiesSpeedMSec 20 (m/s), TrailEntitiesSpawnIntervalSec 5;
  - HeightEditorObjects 0.64, HeightNormalObjects 0.2, PlayerHeightSpawnOffset -1;
  - DrawPlayerToFirstNode and DrawLastNodeToDestination on;
  - TrailEntity = fx/ux/runnersvision/rvtrail_invisibletriangle_temp.

#### What they show in the world
- **Runner Vision's red trail.** The renderer spawns `RVTrail_InvisibleTriangle_TEMP` objects along the route,
  one every 5 s, each moving at 20 m/s. Each is a StaticModelEntity with an invisible mesh and an auto-started
  EffectComponent, **FX/UX/RunnersVision/FX_UX_RunnersVision_Trail_Main**. The red trail you see is that effect,
  started by the component (0x1432B8CD8 -> the effect play 0x14329B860) and moved with its object every frame
  (0x14329F9A0).
- **Time trial checkpoints** (pf_timetrialcheckpoint):
  - a PamCheckpointEntity with an area trigger and three UI sounds (ui_timetrial_checkpoints 1-3);
  - map markers;
  - **pf_s_checkpointbeacon**: the models ui/art/props/beacon/beacon and beacontip, plus a shader parameter;
  - **pf_s_timetrialcheckpointvisuals**:
    - the effects **FX/UX/Triggers/FX_UX_Triggers_Checkpoint_Place / _Pass / _Remove**;
    - the **checkpointcircle** model (objects/props/runnerobject/dasharrows), scaled by four timelines;
    - an AR widget, ui/widgets/ar/challenges/timetrialcheckpointwidget: the checkpoint's number or time in the
      world, drawn by the UI.
- **Time trial marker** (pf_timetrialmarker): UI sounds (start, complete, fail), the badge model, HUD visibility,
  and the **projection character** (characters/projection/projectioncharacter): the ghost runner.
- **Dashes**: the dash arrows (objects/props/runnerobject/dasharrows: arrows and the checkpoint circle), the dash
  UI sounds (ME_Sound/UI/...dash...) and the dash music (ME_Sound/Music/Districts/*_dash_*).
- **Deliveries** (covert and fragile opportunity missions, gameplay/logic/pf_deliverymission*):
  - the pickup and drop boxes and the delivery cabinet (objects/props/gameplay/deliverycabinet_01);
  - the delivery object (objects/props/missionitem/deliveryobject01);
  - the NPCs' end-of-delivery animations (gameplay/mission/opportunitymission/pf_opportunitymission_deliveryend_*).
- **Other FX/UX effects**: the collectibles' orbs (FX_UX_Triggers_CompulsionOrb, _MetaGridOrb and its init), the
  projection meshes (FX/UX/ProjectionMesh/..._Trail_M, ..._LocalCluster_M), and FX_UI_Hacked.

### 2. What the replay already had
- **Faith**: pose, sounds, MagRope line.
- **People within 40 m**: the delivery NPCs, and the ghost runner if it's a character the people scan finds
  **[not verified]**.
- **Moving models within 40 m**, found again by label after streaming. This should cover the checkpoint circle
  while its timeline scales it, and the delivery object while it moves with Faith, if they are models the scan
  lists **[not verified]**.
- **Gun, impact, combat and VTOL effects**. No FX/UX effects: **this is why Runner Vision's trail and the
  checkpoint effects were missing from replays.**

### 3. What was added
- FX/UX effects are recorded and played like the guns' effects:
  - started within 80 m of Faith, with every move and parameter set, and stopped when the game stopped them;
  - the trail effects keep moving along the route as they did.
- On a seek, the trail, the orbs and the projection meshes are restarted where they are (lasting kinds). The
  checkpoint place / pass / remove effects and the hack effect are one-offs: they play when the playback passes
  them.

### 4. Not done, and why
- **Checkpoint and beacon models after the run.** The game destroys a checkpoint's objects when it's passed or the
  run ends. The replay poses things that still exist and doesn't spawn game objects (spawning was found unsafe
  earlier, the KrugerSec spawn buttons). A finished run's checkpoints can't be shown again; they show only while
  they still exist.
- **AR widgets, the HUD timer, results screens**: drawn by the UI system, not the world. Not recorded.
- **UI sounds and the dash music**: HUD sounds are left out of replays on purpose (the MagRope tooltip). The music
  isn't recorded. Both could be added if wanted.
- **Mission state** (objectives, timers, success): the replay is a picture of what happened, not a rerun of the
  game's logic. Running the mission scripts again would change the live game's progress.
- **Runner Vision's highlight** of objects (red surfaces): a renderer state, not traced here.

### 6. Mission items shown and hidden (later on 2026-10-25, offline)

#### Why the delivery package was missing from replays
- The package is **objects/pf_deliveryobject01**: a prefab whose interface field **Visibility** goes to its one
  object's **Visible** (ObjectReference to objects/props/missionitem/deliveryobject01, a StaticModelEntityData;
  Visible at data + 0xDC, True by default).
- The delivery start and end timelines (pf_opportunitymission_delivery*_animations_*) switch that Visibility
  with an AndEntity (I2U -> Visibility), and attach the package to a character with an AttachTransformLayer.
- So the game shows and hides it rather than moving it away. The replay posed it where it was but left it as
  the game had it at playback time (hidden).

#### How the game shows and hides models in prefabs (verified in code)
- Models in a prefab are members of a **ClientStaticModelGroupEntity** (vtable 0x141AFBE90, getType 0x143187BD0,
  type info 0x1427ED720).
- Its property handler is vtable slot 2, **0x14318DC70**(group, event { u32 hash, value pointer }):
  - the plain hashes are the group's own: BlueprintTransform 0xE790F446 (moves the whole group) and
    ObjectVariation 0xD806FCC1 (ignored);
  - any other hash is a member's field: hash & 3 = the field (0 Enabled, 1 ObjectVariation, 2 Visible),
    (hash >> 2) & 0x7FF = the member + 1, (hash >> 13) & 0x7FF = which of the member's instances;
  - the members are at [group + 0xE0], 0x130 bytes each, [group + 0xE8] of them; 0x1431840F0 makes a member's
    record when first used (byte + 0x120);
  - Visible goes to **0x14318F730**(member, the value's byte, instance);
  - ObjectVariation goes to **0x14318FB30**(member, instance, value) -> **0x14376C4B0**, which reads only the
    variation's name hash (value + 0x18) and looks the variation's mesh up from it (0x14354FBF0);
  - Enabled goes to 0x143183290 / 0x143185940 / 0x143181590 (on) or 0x1431856E0 / 0x14317F340 (off).
- The group's destructor is **0x14317CE50**, called only from its deleting destructor (0x14317E15F).
- Not these: **0x14318DE90** handles Visible for **ClientTerrainEntity** (vtable 0x141AFB8D8), not static
  models (an earlier label was wrong). A single ClientStaticModelEntity (vtable 0x141AFB520) handles Transform,
  ObjectVariation, BlueprintTransform and TransformSpaceSimulationSetting (0x0608E888) in 0x14318DA10, and keeps
  a handle to its Visible value at entity + 0x148 (made by its slot 1, 0x14318E400, through 0x1446C07D0). What
  reads that handle wasn't found.
- Other Visible (0x35BC69AB) checks in the game, not traced: 0x14325A21D, 0x14325A377, 0x14376A4C1,
  0x14376A681, 0x14391997B, 0x14393564C, 0x14394E0A5, 0x14394E297, 0x143B08E68, 0x143B31B97.

#### What the replay does
- Hooks 0x14318DC70 and 0x14317CE50 after checking their code.
- While it records: each member Visible and ObjectVariation the game sets (group, hash, time, value).
- While it plays: each one as it was at that time, by giving the group's handler the same event (for a
  variation, a copy holding only its name hash). Before a member's first change: what the game had given it
  when the recording started, if known, otherwise left as the game has it.
- When it stops: each gets back what the game last gave it.
- A destroyed group's entries are dropped, so nothing is given to a group that's gone. Enabled isn't replayed.
- Under REPLAY > Doors, elevators, moving objects and mission items.

#### Not verified
- That the package and the cabinet really go through the group path (not a single static model's).
- The delivery cabinet: its ObjectVariationMultiSwitch sets the cabinet prefab reference's ObjectVariation. That
  reaches the members as member events only if the prefab system passes it on that way.
- Items the game destroys (a finished run's checkpoints) still can't be shown.

### 7. Why dialog, mission effects and collected items were still missing (2026-10-25)

Evidence: what was seen in game. Code: the decrypted game image (offline). Game data: the `fb\` parser.

#### 7.1 Dialog (voice lines): cause found in code, not fixed yet
- **What was recorded.** VO voices did reach the sound replay (NoteVoiceOverVoice). On playback the replay gave
  `ME_Sound/VO/TimeLineVO_Player_Faith` its start event (0x0DC0EFA5) and `.../TimeLineVO_Player_Cone_wLPF` its
  events, all on voices the replay made, with no known place (seen in game).
- **Why it's silent (verified in code).** The voice-over system's line update **0x14303C5E0** doesn't say a line
  through voice events:
  - it keeps a few voices per speaker, made once through the sound system's slot 8 (loop at 0x14303C6B0, the voice
    kept at entry + 8);
  - per line it gets a node of the voice's sound graph: voice slot 7 **0x14301A920** -> 0x143003340(graph, id),
    the id from [speaker + 0x48], called at 0x14303C925;
  - it queues the line's wave on that node: **0x143027E90**(node, wave, language, &slot), at 0x14303CA3F.
    - The language comes from 0x143035C90(channel, wave), which picks among the sound system's language data the
      wave has chunks for.
    - The wave's stream is looked up by the 16 bytes before the wave pointer (0x14302BE00).
    - 0x143027C80 fills one of the node's two wave slots (node + 0x88 bits 6..8 = count, 0x28 bytes a slot).
  - it starts the wave with **0x14302C110**(node, slot): slot flags |= 0x800, at 0x14303CBCC;
  - it clears the wave with **0x143023200**(node, slot) when done, at 0x14303CD93.
  - Each of 0x143027E90, 0x14302C110 and 0x143023200 has only that one caller.
  - So the replay's start event on a voice of its own reached no wave.
- **Also found:** the sound replay never recorded a VO voice's place. ReplaySoundsRecordFrame keeps a pose only
  while `IsSoundEntityLive(e.Entity, ...)` holds, and for a VO voice (Entity = the voice) that reads the voice as if
  it were a SoundEntity. Hence no known place.
- **A diagnostic:** it hooks voice slot 7 and 0x143027E90 after byte checks (both functions, the call site's bytes
  before the return address 0x14303C928, the voice vtable's slot 7 pointer, and the queue's only call). It logs
  each line queued while recording: time, the voice's sound name, node, node id, wave and its 16-byte stream id,
  and language.
- **Next:** find out whether mission dialog goes through there, and which voices carry it (VO_Narrative*,
  TimeLineVO_*?). Then replay lines on a voice the replay makes from the same sound: slot 7 with the recorded id,
  0x143027E90 with the recorded wave and language (only while the 16 stream bytes still match), 0x14302C110 at the
  recorded start, 0x143023200 at the end, and the voice's place recorded from the VO system's transform calls.
  **[not verified]**: whether a voice needs a start event besides this, and whether a mission's VO wave stays
  loaded after the mission.

#### 7.2 Mission effects: cause found, and a fix [not verified in game]
- **Seen in game:** the effects diagnostic (every effect through 0x14329B860 within 60 m of Faith, in 5 s windows)
  shows **no FX/UX effect at all**, and no other mission kind. Only FX/Movement, FX/Combat and world sounds appear.
- **Why:** mission and collectible effects start with their objects at stream-in, usually far away and long
  before a recording, and most never move. NoteReplayEffect takes only effects started while recording within
  80 m; TakeInEarlierEffect takes only one that moves.
- **The fix (TakeInPlayingEffects):**
  - every FX/ effect's start (blueprint, transform, second parameter) is kept until 0x1432A2080 stops it, in two
    generations of 16384;
  - an FX/UX effect's last parameter set is kept too (1024 at most);
  - when recording starts, the FX/UX ones within 80 m are taken in at 0 s, Static: played to the end unless the
    game stops them first, their moves and parameters recorded as usual;
  - every FX/ kind playing within 80 m is listed in the log ("playing as it started: ...");
  - while playing, a Static one that never moved is played only while the game's own handle is gone, and on a
    seek it's started again like a lasting kind.
- **[not verified]:** that the missing VFX are FX/UX effects, and that a collected item's effect is stopped
  through 0x1432A2080.

#### 7.3 Collected mission items: cause found (seen in game, game data, code), not fixed yet
- **Seen in game:** the game showed or hid no group models while recording and switched one look. The switch is the electric box's base: in `pf_collectable_electricbox`, an ObjectVariationSwitch goes to
  the base's ObjectVariation, on -> off. The collectables' moving parts were recorded and found again at playback,
  so they exist, but the taken ones stay hidden.
- **Game data** (`objects/props/missionitem/collectableobject01/pf_collectable_electricbox`):
  - the key is an ObjectReference (#8) whose **Visible** comes from a BoolEntity (#22, default True) by a
    property connection;
  - the take's timeline end (EventSync -> BoolEntity event 0x27D4023A) sets it false;
  - the key is moved by the prefab's AntAnimatable (BlueprintTransform) and linked by an EntityTrack.
  - It's built as a **single ClientStaticModelEntity**, not a group member, so the group hook never sees it.
- **Code:**
  - a single static model's property handler 0x14318DA10 takes Transform, ObjectVariation, BlueprintTransform and
    0x0608E888 only, not Visible;
  - its slot 1, **0x14318E400**(entity, hash), binds Visible (0x35BC69AB) to a reader at **entity + 0x148**
    through 0x1446C07D0 -> 0x142A46F80: + 0x148 = the connected value's cell (0 if none), + 0x150 = the data's
    default (data + 0xDC);
  - the game's reader **0x142A424B0** takes [cell] when byte cell + 0x1C has 0x40, else + 0x150.
  - Raw scans of the image found no code reading + 0x148 / + 0x150 as that reader (no `lea rcx, [r + 0x148]`
    into 0x142A424B0, and no inlined form) outside the light entities (0x14376xxxx). **What applies a single
    model's Visible is still unknown.**
  - The group path's render calls (show 0x1436C40B0, hide 0x1436D2EC0, instance id at mesh + 0x8C) are called
    from group code only.
- **Added:** ReadStaticModelVisible reads the reader the way 0x142A424B0 does (byte checks on 0x14318E400 and
  0x142A424B0; only for entities whose slot 1 is 0x14318E400). It logs each recorded model's Visible as it first
  moved and when the recording stops, and lists at playback start the recorded ones the game hides now.
- **Next:** if Visible goes 1 -> 0 for the taken items, find what applies it (a hook on the binder, or a live trace
  inside the DLL), then show them while the replay is before their hide time.

### 8. Voice lines played again; items researched further (2026-10-25)

#### 8.1 Which voices carry the lines (seen in game)
- Voice lines go through 0x143027E90 on these voices:
  - **VO_Narrative_Faith** (Faith's mission lines; node id 0x215D38800);
  - **VO_Narrative_RadioOnDistance** (the radio; id 0x1F8C53550);
  - VO_Ambient and VO_AI_DistantAmbient (people);
  - VO_Faith_Emotes_Quieter / _Louder (Faith's emotes; id 0x1F8D008E8).
  - Each narrative line was on a new voice. A pooled voice (VO_Ambient) carried many lines. All lines used one
    language pointer.
- **Game data** for `me_sound/vo/vo_narrative_faith`:
  - a SoundPatchAsset, IsPersistent, radius 0.5 m;
  - its graph plays through a **DialogSamplerNode** whose Triggered and Continue aren't connected. Its one
    public event (0x0DC0EFA5, Start) isn't wired to the sampler.
  - So the sampler plays what's queued on it without an event.

#### 8.2 Playing the voice lines again
- **Hooks** (each checked, along with its only call site):
  - the wave start 0x14302C110 (`8D 42 FF 48 8D 04 80 81 4C C1 24 00 08 00 00 C3`, called at 0x14303CBCC);
  - the wave clear 0x143023200 (`8D 42 FF 48 8D 04 80 81 64 C1 24 FF BF FF FF 8B 81 88 00 00 00`, called at
    0x14303CD93);
  - these sit next to the voice's slot 7 and the queue.
- **Recording.** Each line is kept with:
  - its queue, start and clear times;
  - its node id, wave, language and the wave's 16-byte stream id;
  - its voice among the recorded ones (ReplaySoundVoiceIndex), so the replay makes a voice of its own from the same
    sound at playback.
  - A voice-over voice's place is now recorded with the others once it has said a line
    (ReplaySoundsRecordFrame: IsRecordedSoundVoice).
- **Playing** (PlayVoiceLines, from ReplaySoundsPlay):
  - each line on the replay's voice for that sound, at its times: node = slot 7(voice, id), then 0x143027E90(node,
    wave, language, &slot), then 0x14302C110 at the start time and 0x143023200 at the clear time;
  - only while the 16 bytes before the wave still match;
  - a seek, a loop or the start clears what's queued; lines already under way aren't joined;
  - at stop, everything is cleared before the replay's voices are released.
- **[not verified]:** that a voice made by 0x143019860 runs its graph without an event (the data says the sampler
  needs none), and that a mission's VO stays loaded after the mission (otherwise the line is left out).

#### 8.3 Collected items: not physics objects; what hides them
- **The key isn't a physics object.** `collectable_electricbox_key` is an ObjectBlueprint with a
  **StaticModelEntityData**: PhysicsEntityData, StaticModelPhysicsComponentData with keyframed RigidBodies
  (RigidBodyType 5), and a StaticModelHealthComponent. The game builds it as a ClientStaticModelEntity, and the
  replay records it moving.
- **What the replay leaves out.** It records only ClientStaticModelEntity and PamClientStaticModelEntity. Physics
  classes (ClientBangerEntity, ClientDynamicModelEntity under ClientPhysicsEntity) aren't recorded. Game data has
  only 3 BangerEntityData and 35 DynamicModelEntityData files, none of them a mission item.
- **The missing items are the ones the game hides** (seen in game): beacon, beacontip, mstub,
  collectable_electricbox_key, collectable_kiosk_chip.
- **The readable Visible doesn't follow what's seen.** The keys read Visible 0 when they first moved and 1 at the
  recording's end. The beacons read 0 throughout, though a run's beacons are seen (the prefab
  `pf_s_checkpointbeacon` also has a shader parameter).
- **So the take is shown and hidden another way.** The key's take timeline in `pf_collectable_electricbox` has an
  EntityTrack on the key (EntityLink -> ObjectReference #8) with a **BoolTrack on its Visible**
  (TargetPinNameHash 0x35BC69AB): True at 0 s, False from 3 s.
- **Next:** find how a timeline's property track reaches a single static model's Visible. Candidates: the
  timeline hooks the tools already have (TimelineCtor 0x14368D590 / Dtor 0x14368DC60, from the world log), or
  the static model's binder 0x14318E400 being called again by the timeline (log its calls for the recorded
  models). Then record the Visible the timeline gives each recorded model and give it back while playing.

#### 8.4 Collected items: first try
- **No code was found that reads the reader.** Searched the image for readers of entity + 0x148 / + 0x150:
  `lea rcx, [r + 0x148]` into 0x142A424B0 (only light entities 0x14376xxxx and one int reader at 0x142D501EC),
  the inlined getter (none), and qword reads of + 0x148 with + 0x150 nearby (none in model code). The Visible
  handlers that write a byte at + 0x54 (0x14325A1F0 / 0x14325A360) belong to UI classes (DiceUIInputActionListener,
  PamUIPressStartWidget, PamUIElementStickyMapMarkerIcons).
- **Recording** (ReplayModels::RecordFrame): every candidate model within 40 m that is a single static model
  (slot 1 = binder 0x14318E400) has its reader's value kept at the start and at each change (up to 256).
- **Playing** (ReplayModels::GiveVisible):
  - when the reader now gives another value than at that time, its cell pointer (+ 0x148) is swapped for one of
    the replay's (+ 0x00 = a pointer to the value, byte + 0x1C = 0x40, the layout 0x142A424B0 reads);
  - the swap happens only while the entity's slot 1 is still the binder and the reader still holds the cell just
    read (SwapStaticModelVisibleCell);
  - the game's cell goes back at stop, or when the model is made again; if the game rebinds meanwhile, its new
    cell is taken as the game's;
  - the replay's cells are static (they live as long as the tools).
- **Log:**
  - the stop line lists, per moving model, "Visible N at the start, N as it first moved, N now, K changes: v at
    t s, ...";
  - playback start lists the models the game hides now;
  - the stop line counts how often a model was given its recorded value.
- **[not verified]:** whether the drawn model follows that reader. If the items still don't show, the next step is
  a live trace (a data watch on a collected key's + 0x148 / + 0x150 inside the DLL, to find the code that reads
  it), or the timeline's property track path.

### 9. Cutscene lines (2026-10-26)
- **Seen in game:**
  - most voice lines through the voice-over system (VO_Narrative_*, VO_Ambient, VO_Faith_Emotes_*) were said again
    on playback;
  - the cutscene's speakers weren't among them: **ME_Sound/VO/TimeLineVO_Player_Cone_wLPF** (the KrugerSec) and
    **TimeLineVO_Player_Faith**. Their voices are made by the timeline (0x143901D68 < 0x14368D282 <
    0x14369002A ...) and started through 0x14301C522 < 0x143902840 < 0x143904B0C.
- **How a cutscene says a line (verified in code and data):**
  - the timeline's keyframe loop 0x1439027D0 calls each keyframe's slot 2;
  - for a sound track's keyframe that's **0x14301C4E0**(keyframe, voice, patch, &id). It calls the voice's
    **slot 2, 0x14301DA80**(voice, id, the keyframe's asset + 0x18): [voice + 0x18], its graph, then
    0x143006180(graph, id, asset), then 0x143018BB0. Then, if keyframe + 0x24 (TriggerDefaultStartEvent), it fires
    patch + 0x68 (DefaultStartEvent), hash at + 0x14, through slot 0.
  - Game data, `me_sound/vo/timelinevo_player_cone_wlpf`: a SamplerNode whose **ExternalWave** is the patch's one
    public asset parameter. Its DefaultStartEvent is 0x0DC0EFA5.
- **The fix [not verified in game]:**
  - the voice's slot 2 is hooked: its bytes, its call 0x143006180, the voice vtable's slot 2 pointer and the trigger's
    bytes at 0x14301C4EF are checked;
  - while recording, each asset given to a recorded voice is kept: time, voice index, id, asset, its vtable and
    name;
  - while playing, it's given to the replay's voice for it through the original, before that frame's events, only
    while the asset still has the recorded vtable and name. After a seek, the last one per voice and id up to then.
  - A voice-over voice's place is recorded once it's among the recorded voices, which includes the timeline's
    voices now that they're noted by NoteVoiceOverVoice.
- **[not verified]:** whether a cutscene's line waves stay loaded after the cutscene (if not, they're left out and
  the log says how many).

# 24. The Shard drawn twice: its far-away model over the real tower (2026-10-25)

Sources: the game's data (`Data` / `Patch` under `<game folder>`, read only),
the decrypted game image (offline), and two small read-only reads of the running game (known pointers only, no
scan).

### 1. The cause (verified)

- **The far-away model** is a sub-level of its own: `Levels/SP/SP_MainCity/SkyCity_Backdrop/SkyCity_Backdrop`
  (release0.sb). Its StaticModelGroupEntity has 3 members: `skycity_backdrop_far_whole` and
  `skycity_backdrop_far_whole_lit` (both at 765.1, 26.7, -2962.6) and one city facade light
  (`dt_release_facadelights02`, at 136.9, 4.5, 437.9). Its layers add two fan prefabs
  (`pf_windfarm_propellerbackdrop_skycity`, a skycity_building_fan01 turning at 30 deg/s, at y 1356 and 3888) and a
  searchlight prefab.
  After the story the game uses `SkyCity_RuinBackdrop` instead: one member `skycity_backdrop_far_destroyed`, the two
  fans and a smoke effect (`fx_shard_backdrop_smoke`).
- **What streams it** (main level `levels/sp/sp_maincity/sp_maincity`, patched, rebuilt from base + delta, see §4):
  - SubWorldReferenceObjectData #84 = SkyCity_Backdrop, #83 = SkyCity_RuinBackdrop (BundleHeap 3, no AutoLoad).
  - `layer48_districtstreaming` #79 (a LogicPrefabReference, area-trigger prefab) **OnEnter -> #84.StreamIn,
    OnLeave -> #84.StreamOut**; #49 the same for #83. Both are bound to `layer1_streaming` **#22**
    (`0x31FB3B9F` link -> VolumeVectorShapeData).
  - Which of the two is enabled: progression flag #34 through MathEntity #83 (-> #79.Enabled) and #18 (-> #49.Enabled).
    `Installed` from #45 (NotEntity) too. (The flag's name isn't resolved; whole vs ruin is inferred from the names.)
  - Volume #22: points (1691.87, -1155.07), (1708.01, 1891.06), (-1278.21, 1590.95), (-1235.05, -1259.32), y -0.18,
    Height 2000: **the city's area**. The PamAreaTrigger counts the player's team (Include 2, TeamOfAllies 1), so the
    far-away model is loaded while **Faith** is in the city and unloaded when she leaves it.
  - Hash names (Frostbite string hash, h = h*33 ^ c from 5381): OnEnter 0xFB35AD6C, OnLeave 0xFBD34B3F,
    StreamIn 0xD27BC17E, StreamOut 0x21F3F677, OnLoaded 0x7589A363, IsLoaded 0x30A15EF8.
  - Volume #15 (around the Shard, x -872..2724, z -4850..-1162) streams `SkyCityTopOpenBlinds` / `TopClosedBlinds`
    (#139 / #188) the same way (not touched by the fix).
- **The real tower** is not in the mission sub-level `TheShard` (its 14 layers are logic, flow, sound, FX, train ride;
  no art layer). Every patched ebx was rebuilt and searched for skycity imports: the tower's geometry is
  **zone 55 of the city's buildings streamer** (`centralcitybuildings_zs_zs_55`, 360 skycity imports: the buildings,
  the atrium, the rip, the maintenance tunnels, the fans...). The props zones only have one skycity prop, in the
  city (zone 622, at 75, 62, 176).
- **Live read (read only, game running, the free camera at the Shard):**
  - Buildings streamer 0x1F955C7E0, path `Levels/SP/SP_MainCity/CentralCityBuildings_ZS_ZS_`, 95 bundles (83 zones +
    12 regions). Bundle 25 is named **"55"**: flags 8 (available), slot 4, refs 1 = **loaded**; its parent is bundle 87
    `Region_Building_Default` = the **Default** district. Zone "55":
    centre (828.6, -2615.4), box x -1513..3698, z -4745..-750.
  - ClientStaticModelGroupEntity instance lists: exactly one member mesh with "skycity_backdrop" in its
    name: group 0x3EC381190, `objects/architecture/unique/skycity/buildings/skycity_backdrop_far_destroyed_Mesh`
    (1 member, 1 instance). So the **ruin** backdrop was loaded, at the same time as zone 55.
- So: the game swaps the two by **Faith's** position (backdrop while she's in the city; the real tower only loads
  around her out there). The tools load zones by the **camera** (and Always districts with the camera on or off),
  so zone 55 loaded while Faith stayed in the city and both were drawn.

### 2. The game's code used by the fix (verified offline in the decrypted image)

- ClientStaticModelGroupEntity: vtable 0x141AFBE90, slot 0 0x143187BD0 = `lea rax, [0x1427ED720]` (its ClassInfo;
  name read "ClientStaticModelGroupEntity", super 0x1427EE290 = ClientPhysicsEntity). Instance lists at ClassInfo
  \+ 0x60 / 0x70 / 0x80 / 0x90, link at entity + 0x40 (as AttachTargets).
- 0x1431840F0 (member record): data = [group + 0x30]; member data = [data + 0x90] + k * **0x68**; record =
  [group + 0xE0] + k * 0x130, made flag + 0x120.
- 0x14317B310 (member set-up): record + 0x18 = member data; reads [md + 0x38] (an asset, type-checked twice: the
  MeshAsset; its name at + 0x10 read live), [md + 0x40] = instance count (allocates count * 8 at record + 0xC8),
  [md + 0x48]; [md + 0x64] the group mesh type. (The file layout is 0x50 bytes; in memory 0x68.)
- 0x14318DC70 (the group's property handler, vtable slot 2): hash & 3 = field (0 Enabled, 1 ObjectVariation
  0xD806FCC1, 2 **Visible 0x35BC69AB**), (hash >> 2) & 0x7FF = member + 1, (hash >> 13) & 0x7FF = instance; Visible
  -> 0x14318F730(record, byte, instance). Neither the member nor the instance is bounds-checked by the game.

### 3. The fix

`Camera/CameraManager.cpp` (section "The Shard", after the vistas), `Util/Hooks.cpp`
(`util::hooks::SetModelGroupMemberVisible`), `Util/Util.h`, `Camera/CameraManager.h` (`m_ShardSwap`).
At first: a menu tick (Vistas) and `[Misc] ShardSwapAtCamera`; both removed in the second round (§3b), it's always on.

1. **The view in the city keeps the real tower out.** In the zone streamer hook, the view = the free camera
   (g_SortView, published every frame) or, with it off, the streamer's own first focus (+0x2A8, the game's camera
   next to Faith). Inside volume #22's x/z outline (height left out) -> zone "55" of the streamer whose path has
   `CentralCityBuildings_ZS` gets `never` in `EnforceNeverDistricts`, the same path as a district set to Never
   (asked to unload, made unavailable once released, let back and asked to load when the view leaves). The zones the
   game's own foci are in, and their neighbours, stay (s_kept): Faith's and the missions' ZoneStreamerFocusEntity's.
   The view changes sides only 50 m past the edge. Paused while Faith isn't spawned (as the districts).
2. **The far-away model hidden while the real tower is loaded.** In the camera hook (the client's thread, where the
   replay already gives model groups their Visible), every 100 ms: zone "55" loaded = slot and not loading (the
   server streamer's table, as the vistas read it). While loaded: the model groups with a member mesh containing
   `skycity_backdrop_far_` (whole, lit, destroyed) get those members' Visible = 0 through the group's own handler
   (looked for at once, then every 2 s for groups streamed in again). When it isn't loaded, or the swap is off: each
   hidden group still there (vtable, data and members re-read) gets Visible = 1.
   Only those members: the facade light in the same group, the fans, the smoke and the searchlights stay as the game
   has them.

### 3b. Second round: the tower had no top; automatic, no menu tick

The swap itself works (seen in game): the far-away model is hidden once zone 55 loads, and shown again in the city.
Goal: the real tower streamed whole, as the mission has it, and the swap automatic, not a tick in Vistas.

- **The top isn't in zone 55** (verified in data). `SkyCityTopOpenBlinds` / `SkyCityTopClosedBlinds` (main level
  #139 / #188) each hold `pf_skycity_building_05` (`_opaque` in the closed one) at (870.1, 1569.6, -2982.9), the
  tower's top (Kruger's office), plus a StaticModelGroup (catwalk railings...), a DynamicEnlighten and, in one, three
  movement exclusion boxes. `layer48_districtstreaming` #25 -> #139, #80 -> #188 (OnEnter -> StreamIn, OnLeave ->
  StreamOut), both bound to `layer1_streaming` **#15**: the area around the Shard (8 corners, convex, no height:
  (2406.72, -1968.19) (2723.83, -3548.88) (1756.24, -4646.43) (326.239, -4850.4) (-872.062, -3680.05)
  (-781.582, -2490.59) (210.563, -1424.52) (1429.53, -1162.08)). Which of the two is enabled: progression flag #26
  (#80) and MathEntity #65 / the level's interface (#25) - not resolved further.
- **The triggers are camera triggers.** All of layer48's LogicPrefabReferences are `gameplay/logic/pf_cameraareatrigger`
  (file guid dafa2cd5..., patched): a client `CameraEnterAreaTriggerEntity` (UpdatePass 2, TimeTreshold 0.1,
  FireOnLeaveWhenDisable), its inside bool -> a PropertyGate closed while `ui/map/maptransform` is on (the map screen)
  -> EventSync to the server -> the interface's OnEnter / OnLeave. So the game streams these by the **game's camera**
  (next to Faith), not the free camera (the far-away model stayed loaded with the free camera at the Shard).
- **Code (offline):** CameraEnterAreaTriggerEntity: TypeInfo 0x1427F0D50 (name read), vtable **0x141B11290** (read live;
  the 0x141B11260 written here first is the vtable of the update object it registers, and the slot numbers below count
  from it: getType is the entity's slot 0, the handler its slot 4) (getType
  slot 6 0x143232D90, event handler slot 10 0x143232310: Enable 0x8BA423E4 registers the update (0x1432306F0),
  Disable 0xF90216B1 unregisters it). Update **0x143230DD0**: the camera = 0x143279950([0x142415E50 area], local player id
  [player + 0x78]) -> 0x143278E40(entry, transform at rbp - 0x19); then **0x14330D320(rsi + 0x30 links,
  &{data, 0x31FB3B9F}, [rsi + 0x20], &transform row 3 = rbp + 0x17)** -> al inside, at 0x143230EBE (return
  0x143230EC3) and 0x143231121 (return 0x143231126); per player record + 0x24 the state, + 0x28 the time; on a
  change it sends 0x1787CAB5 (in) / 0x16E7FAE6 (out) through 0x14314E8A0 (names not resolved). 0x14330D320 is a pure link-volume test (16-byte aligned
  float4 position, `movaps`), with 13 callers in all (other area triggers): the hook only acts for those two returns.
- Other users of camera area triggers (all ebx, patched ones rebuilt): lifts (pf_elevator_01 ...), the Shard's drone
  buddies, window cleaners, in-world markers (ui/singletons/pf_s_inworldmarker), character streaming (layers 56, 62),
  construction, mischiefmaker, ambient characters. So the free camera must not count for all of them.
- **Fix:** `Util/Hooks.cpp` "The Shard's top": MinHook on 0x14330D320 (code checked: its prologue, both call sites'
  16 bytes before the call, the call targets, `test al, al` after). From those two calls only, when the game's
  camera isn't inside and the tools say the free camera counts (camera on and out of the city's area, see §3), the
  free camera's position is tested too. Only for triggers on volume #15: told apart once per (links, data, owner) by
  the game's own test on 8 points 25 m inside its corners (all in) and 8 points 25 m outside (all out). So the game's
  own trigger fires OnEnter, and the top streams in exactly as for Faith; leaving (and Faith not there) OnLeave.
  `util::hooks::SetShardAreaCamera` (from the camera hook every frame).
- The menu tick and `[Misc] ShardSwapAtCamera` are gone: the swap is always on. Also fixed: at a level load the game's
  focus is at FLT_MAX (seen in game): such positions are now ignored.
- Not known: whether the top sub-level streams in fast enough that the moment the far-away model is hidden (zone 55
  loaded) the top is already there (they load independently; a short moment without the top is possible), and
  whether the mission's other sub-levels (TheShard's own props, its visual environment ve_skycity) matter for the look.

### 4. Tools written for this (read only on game files)

(They use the `fb\` parser; run with `-I`.)
- `patched.py <ebx name> <out.bin> <fb dir>`: **rebuilds a patched asset** from the patch catalogs' 60-byte records
  (result, base, delta) and Frostbite's delta blocks (0 copy base blocks, 1 big fixes, 2 small fixes, 3 copy delta
  blocks, 4 skip base blocks, then the rest of the base). The rebuilt sp_maincity (421792 bytes), theshard (77600)
  and layer0_default (840480) all match the index's originalSize, and parse. 502 of the index's ebx are patched; the
  old parser skipped them all (importers.py missed every placement in them).
- `wiring_file.py <bin> <out> <fb dir>`: wiring.py on a rebuilt file. `conn.py`: connections with imported instances
  resolved to `<file>#index(type)` (set FB_DIR). `patched_importers.py`: importers among the patched ebx.
  `layout.py`: a complex's field layout in the file. `fbhash.py`: Frostbite name hashes.
- `shard_live.py`, `shard_groups.py`: the two live read-only probes above.

### 5. Not known / not verified

- That Visible = 0 also takes the far-away model out of the shadow pass (Frostbite usually does; not read).
- Whether the ruin's two fans (or the whole backdrop's) also double up with zone 55's own fans (not checked).
- Whether a moment with neither model shows when zone 55 unloads (the far-away model comes back within 100 ms of the
  server table saying unloaded; the client may drop the tower's meshes a little earlier or later).
- Vista zone 25 (the vista copy of zone 55) is handled by the existing *Hide a vista where its buildings are loaded*.
- The progression flag's name (whole vs ruin) and the 2000 m height's base (assumed y of the points).

### 6. The Shard's tip for lightning (2026-10-26)

For the weather's lightning (weather::SetShardTop, Visuals/Weather.h): the top of whichever Shard is drawn, verified.

**Mesh data (offline, read-only):** a MeshSet res (type 0x49B156D4, res_index.tsv) starts with its bounding box (two
float4); LOD0 at [0x20]; in the LOD: + 8 section count, + 0xC the sections (0x130 apart: + 0x10 name, + 0x20 primitive
count, + 0x28 vertex offset in bytes, + 0x2C vertex count, + 0x4C 16 vertex elements (usage, format, offset, stream),
\+ 0x8C stride), + 0x58 index bytes, + 0x5C vertex bytes, + 0x64 the vertex/index chunk id (found with chunkfind.py;
vertices first, then indices). Position = usage 1; formats 3 Float3, 4 Float4, 7 Half3, 8 Half4 (7 and 8 seen). Every
decoded vertex of the 7 meshes checked lay inside its mesh's box. Scripts: mesh_vertices.py, roof_meshes.py.

**Far-away models** (sub-levels SkyCity_Backdrop / SkyCity_RuinBackdrop, one model group member each, InstanceCount 1):

**The real tower: not given.** Zone 55's model group has 591 members and 20652 instances, but only 4988 instances

### 7. The real tower's tip, measured (2026-10-26, the camera at the Shard)

- **Live, read-only:** with the top streamed in, its model group (vtable 0x141AFBE90; 115 members = SkyCityTopOpenBlinds)
  has antenna05 as member 10, antenna03 member 9, skycity_building_top_mesh member 50, each with an empty data

  30..30, antenna03 29..29, the top 283..285; data-placed members have FFFFFFFF.

  bits), position + 0x30, scale + 0x40, 0xFFFF0000 | physics part at + 0x54 (parts without collision have none: 399 of
  427 here); a second copy of the records later in the file. Checks: part 283 (the top's mesh) = 871.360 1616.353

  900.5045 1635.79 -2948.6228, rows (-0.29028 0 0.95694) (0 1 0) (-0.95694 0 -0.29028), the same in the closed-blinds

- **antenna05_mesh** (15885 vertices, all inside its box -1.24 -0.14 -1.57 .. 1.14 42.00 0.79): its top is a 16 cm cap at
  local y 41.938 around (0, 0) -> world **900.504 1677.728 -2948.621**; the physics box's top is 1677.734.
