# 30. A mission's world in its replay (2026-10-26)

Why a replay recorded in a mission had nothing to play, what bringing that world back would take, and what was built.
Sources: a game session's log, the decrypted game image, and the earlier notes
(`Addresses_2026-10-25.txt`, `MEC_Reverse_Notes.md`). **[not verified]** marks what wasn't checked in code or game.

### 1. What happens (seen in game)

- **A recording starts** in free roam.
- **A loading screen starts the Release mission.**
  - The game's clock jumps to 04:30.
  - The game dresses Faith in C_Faith_Prologue (Release).
  - After 15 s of loading screen, the replay lets its kept people go, as it does since the fast-travel hang
    (LoadScreenEvent hook 0x143B2E130), and holds again once it's gone.
- **The mission plays** at about 60 – 112, -17 – 25, 894 – 1194.
  - The replay keeps 12 KrugerSec the game asked to take out.
  - It keeps one server sub-level (id 0xB3FEAF3, container 0x69A06090) for 60 s; the game keeps asking.
- **The recording stops.**
- **The mission ends or is left.** A short pause or load, with Faith gone (dead or loading).
  - The game takes **whole containers** out: 0x68E05550 (4096 entities, 22 characters) and the kept sub-level's
    0x69A06090 (81 entities).
  - All 12 kept KrugerSec are destroyed another way.
  - The client copies go through **0x143469170 < 0x14323B3C0 < 0x143494360 < 0x14323B340 < the client update
    0x1431A2B50**. That's the network layer deleting the client copies of what the server destroyed
    (Addresses_2026-10-25.txt).
  - The game's clock is back at about its free-roam time: free roam again.
- **Playback.** No recorded person is posed (all are gone), none of the moving models is there, and only some of
  the recorded voices are.

So nothing was missing from the recording. The mission's world was unloaded when the mission was over, and the
replay only poses what still exists.

### 2. Ways to have that world back, and why they weren't done

1. **Keep the mission's world loaded after the mission ends.**
   - The server took the mission's containers down whole, together with the mission's end and Faith's re-spawn in
     free roam. That's not the sub-level unload (0x143340000) the replay already holds for a chase.
   - Holding it would mean holding a mission's whole server layer (4096 entities, its logic included) after the
     game says it's over, across a load. A hold across a load hung the game before (fast travel),
     and the mission's logic could run on with the mission gone. **Not done.**
2. **Load the mission again by its progress flags.**
   - Missions are streamed in by their progression (PamMissionEntity: StreamInOnAvailable, StreamOutOnCompleted /
     Fail / Abort; PamProgressionFlagEntity).
   - Setting those flags is setting the saved progress, and it would start the mission's scripts (its AI, its
     objectives, its time of day). **Not done:** the save isn't to be changed.
3. **Let the game load it: start the mission again from the game's own menus, then play the recording.**
   - The game then loads the mission's world properly.
   - What the replay can match again in it today:
     - moving models: re-found by label near the replayed Faith (`ReplayModels::Refind`);
     - sounds: by sound name;
     - effects: replayed by blueprint while it's loaded;
     - voice lines: when their dialog is loaded.
   - **What it can't:** the people. They're matched by entity pointer, and a restarted mission has new
     KrugerSec. Matching them again (by class and their place at the recording's time) is the next step for
     this route. **[not built]**

### 3. What was built

- When a playback starts and none of the recorded people are in the level, the REPLAY menu now says why: the
  mission or part of the city they were in was unloaded (a mission that's over, a fast travel), so a mission's
  recording is played before leaving the mission (`FaithReplay::PlayPeople`).
- Nothing else is changed: no flags, no holds across a mission's end.

### 4. Next, if wanted

- **Re-find people after a restart** (route 3): at playback, a recorded person whose entity is gone is matched
  to a live one of the same class (PamClientCharacterEntity, its weapon, drones) nearest its recorded place at
  that time, within a few metres, once each. That makes a recording from a mission play after the mission is
  started again from the game's menu.
- **Say which mission:** read the active PamMissionEntity while recording, to name it in the message. Where the
  game keeps the active mission wasn't traced. **[not verified]**

### 5. People found again after the mission is restarted [not verified in game]
- **FaithReplay::ClaimForGone**, called from ScanOthers before a live person near the replayed Faith is hidden as
  an "other". A recorded person takes over the live one when:
  - the recorded one is gone (StillCharacter fails) and the replay is within its recorded time (± 1 s);
  - the live one has the same vtable, bone count and body offset (a character, or a gun / drone);
  - its world bone 1 (from its pose slot's world pose, as recorded) is within **10 m** of the recorded one's bone 1
    at that time (RootWorld, the frame at or before the time). The nearest such recorded person is chosen.
- Its entity and animatable are replaced, and its per-playback state is reset (taken, frozen, drawn, held, gun,
  entity offset, culling box, actor). The rest goes on as for a person found while recording.
- **Log:** "Replay: X wasn't in the level any more: the X 0x... N m from where it was at T s plays it now", and at
  stop the count.
- **Limits:**
  - an "other" already hidden earlier in the playback isn't taken over (releasing a hidden one alone isn't
    supported);
  - a person whose world pose wasn't kept (RootWorldOk false) can't be matched;
  - matching is by place only: if the restarted mission stages its KrugerSec elsewhere, nothing matches.

### 6. Borrowed people after the mission is over (2026-10-27)
- **Why borrowing, not spawning.** Spawning recorded KrugerSec "the ghost way" was judged unsafe on 2026-10-24
  (MEC_Reverse_Notes, "Runner ghost spawn vs KSec"). It needs:
  - a live spawner to borrow;
  - a spawn template made in memory;
  - the network layer accepting made-up networked data;
  - and Unspawn removes all of a spawner's characters.
- **How borrowing works.** The replay already draws a taken person's body where it was recorded while the live
  entity stands elsewhere (its client entity and culling box follow the drawn body).
- **FaithReplay::BorrowForGone** runs from PlayPeople after ScanOthers, once a second, while any recorded person is
  gone. It scans:
  - characters within **3000 m** of the replayed Faith (attach::ScanNearby);
  - guns and drones (FindActors).

  It skips Faith, anyone in the recording, and anyone already hidden as an other. Each gone person, within its
  recorded time, takes a candidate with the same vtable, bone count and body offset: **the same entity data
  (entity + 0x30, recorded at ScanPeople) first**, then the nearest to its recorded bone 1. Then RetargetPerson.
  The log says "the live X ... (the same kind / the same class, N m away) plays it now".
- **Limits:**
  - the look is the live one's;
  - with no same-data KrugerSec loaded, one of the same class and skeleton is used;
  - with none of that class loaded, the person stays missing;
  - the borrowed one's own AI goes on server-side, while the real Faith takes no damage during playback.

### 7. The spawning system, decompiled (2026-10-27)
- **The KrugerSec spawner.** PamServerCharacterSpawnEntity, vtable 0x141C4B388, TypeInfo 0x1428577C0.
  - Bases: ServerCharacterSpawnEntity 0x141B4E0C8, ServerSpawnEntity 0x141B4DDB0.
  - Constructor **0x143953860**(memory, info, data), called only at 0x143957667; it installs the vtable at + 0x31.
  - Destructor body **0x1439548A0**, called only from the deleting destructor 0x143954F10.
  - Its slot 4 is 0x143958790 → 0x143382D20 → **0x143383D40** (ServerSpawnEntity's handler; event id at + 8).
- **The events in 0x143383D40:**
  - **0x0DC320DE = Spawn** (0x143383DB4):
    - only with byte spawner + 0x2A4 set;
    - unless the data's QueueSpawnEvent (+ 0x180), only when 0x1433804A0(spawner, 0) says it can spawn and
      0x143388DD0 says it isn't at its limit;
    - then it sets flags at + 0x108, checks the realm (0x14314C5E0) and that it isn't queued yet (0x143174F20 on
      the spawn manager), and **queues the spawn with 0x143174360(spawn manager, spawner)**.
  - Other ids, not identified yet: 0x2E52F119 (calls slot + 0xE8), 0xDC67A888 (slot + 0xF0), 0xCE486545
    (0x143383E76: the Unspawn loop per the 2026-10-23 notes), 0x448B6017 (clears + 0x108 bit 3, sets bit 4),
    0x5CF6281D / 0x772DEA1D / 0x772E3E05 and one more (on + 0xF8 + 0x530 through 0x1433013C0, or 0x1433862A0).
- **The data** (CharacterSpawnReferenceObjectData, 0x1D0 bytes):
  - ControllableTransform + 0xA0 (local to its blueprint);
  - Team + 0x138; MaxCount + 0x144; MaxCountSimultaneously + 0x148; Enabled + 0x17C; AutoSpawn + 0x17F;
    QueueSpawnEvent + 0x180; TryToSpawnOutOfSight + 0x186;
  - **Template + 0x198**, Template2 + 0x1A0, Template3 + 0x1A8, SpawnTemplateIndex + 0x1B0;
  - SpawnVisible + 0x1BD.
- **Stage 1 (read only):**
  - the constructor and destructor are hooked after byte checks (their prologues, their only call sites, and both
    installing vtable 0x141C4B388);
  - the live spawners are kept in a list;
  - when a playback finds none of its recorded people, the log lists each spawner: on / off (+ 0x2A4), template
    name, MaxCount, data place;
  - nothing is sent to a spawner.
- **Stage 2 (planned, once the list shows usable spawners):**
  - send Spawn (0x0DC320DE) to an enabled spawner of the right template, from the server's update thread (as the
    outfit module sends its Apply);
  - let the borrow pass take the new KrugerSec as the recorded one;
  - remove it at stop with the game's own destroy request 0x143167700(character, owner), one character only.
- **Risks to check in stage 2:**
  - a spawned KrugerSec has live AI: the coordinator counts it, it can hunt the real Faith (she takes no damage
    during playback), and city alert or combat music may react;
  - it appears at the spawner's place, not the recorded one: the replay draws its body where it was recorded
    (as with borrowing);
  - a spawner in an unloaded mission layer doesn't exist after the mission: only free-roam spawners can be used.

### 8. Stand-ins, stage 2 (2026-10-27)
- **What stage 1's spawner list showed (seen in game):**
  - a recording across the Release mission's loading screen, played after the mission was over: no recorded person
    was posed; borrowing gave a few of them bodies (the same class, 591 / 901 / 885 m away), the rest stayed gone;
  - 40 spawners were loaded, all on (+ 0x2A4), every data place 0, 0, 0 (ControllableTransform is local to its
    blueprint: where it spawns is the spawner's own place):
    - Enemy: AIRanged_Enforcer01 ×2, AIRanged_Enforcer02 ×2, AIMelee_Protector ×4 (MaxCount -1), AIMelee_Sentinel ×4
      (MaxCount 1), consecutive addresses 0x2D0C872B0 - 0x2D0C89960 (one free-roam group);
    - civilians: AIMale / AIFemale / AIFemale_Heels "ErrorTemplate" ×6 (MaxCount -1), and AIMale_Icarus_Collision,
      AIFemale_Black_November_02, AIMale_HighCaste02, AIMale_Black_November_02, AIFemale_MidCaste_02 (MaxCount 1);
    - SpawnTemplate_Faith_NoTattoo ×1 and SpawnTemplate_Projection_Replay ×16 (runner ghosts).
- **Spawn's path, checked byte for byte (decrypted image):**
  - PamServerCharacterSpawnEntity slot 4 = 0x143958790. On Spawn it calls 0x143386A40 (a property 0x84B9DE3F of the
    spawner's CharacterBlueprint, + 0xB8 of what 0x143115190 finds); when that's not 0, the AI coordinator
    ([0x142548710] − 0x30, + 0x608) must agree (0x14392D710, its pools), else nothing happens. Then
    ServerCharacterSpawnEntity's 0x143382D20.
  - 0x143382D20: only with + 0x2A4 set. On Spawn, when 0x143386A40 is 0 it asks the event's type (slot 0) for its class
    id (+ 0x28); a ServerPlayerEvent (ids [0x1427FF808] - [0x1427FF80A], 0x5DB - 0x5DD in the image) is a player's
    spawn (its + 0x20 read, kept at + 0x2B0). Any other event goes on (tail jump 0x143382EA1) to ServerSpawnEntity's
    0x143383D40.
  - 0x143383D40's Spawn branch (0x143383DB4) reads nothing of the event but its id: + 0x2A4; unless QueueSpawnEvent,
    0x1433804A0 / 0x143388DD0; it sets + 0x108; then the realm and "not queued" checks and the queue 0x143174360.
  - The spawner's characters: the vector at + 0x148 / + 0x150 of entity pointers (Unspawn copies it and gives each
    to 0x143167700 with [character + 0x28], 0x143383EB3 - 0x143383F4F).
- **What stage 2 does:**
  - the server's update (Server::update 0x1433446F0, hooked by the outfit module) calls the replay's
    ReplayServerUpdate at its start, on its thread; it does nothing unless the replay records or plays, or has
    stand-ins;
  - then, once a second (every update while a spawn is awaited), it reads each spawner's template and characters
    and where each character is (ServerCharacterPlace, the despawn check's way);
  - while recording, each character gets the template of the spawner character nearest its bone 1 within 2.5 m;
  - while playing, a gone person with a template takes only a live one of the same data or template; with none,
    it asks for a stand-in; the server's update picks an enabled spawner of that template (else of the same
    folder and kind word, never an ErrorTemplate), notes its characters, sends Spawn (the tools' event: id
    0x0DC320DE at + 8, a type whose class id is outside ServerPlayerEvent's) to 0x143958790, and waits up to 15 s for a
    new character in that spawner's list (3 spawners at most); one spawner is asked one stand-in at a time;
  - the live copy nearest the stand-in's server character (3 m) plays the person (retargeted like a borrowed one);
    ScanOthers leaves anything near a made stand-in alone;
  - while the replay holds people, destroy requests and despawn checks for stand-ins are held by who they are
    (KeepGuard, HoldsAIDespawn);
  - at stop: each made stand-in is dropped from the kept lists and destroyed with the original 0x143167700, on the
    server's thread; one asked but not made yet is destroyed when it appears (or forgotten after 15 s); the
    character destructor hook forgets one the game destroyed.
- **Not known:**
  - whether a Spawn sent at the start of Server::update makes a KrugerSec (the coordinator's pools may turn it
    down);
  - how long a spawn takes, and whether "TryToSpawnOutOfSight" spawners wait while Faith can see them;
  - where those 12 Enemy spawners stand (if farther than 3 km from the replayed Faith, the stand-in isn't found);
  - whether the city's alert, music or other KrugerSec react to a spawned one;
  - whether the mission used the same templates (if not, a same-kind spawner is asked).

### 9. Stand-ins seen in game, the spawner's limits, and changes (2026-10-27)
- **Seen in game:**
  - a recording across the Release mission's loading screen had 16 people with templates: AIMelee_Protector ×6,

### 10. A mission's own models drawn after it's over (2026-10-27)
- **The chain, read live (read only, game running; scripts mesh_record_probe.py, dump_classify.py, lod_buffers.py,
  lod_layout.py):**
  - static model entity + 0x30 → StaticModelEntityData + 0x98 → RigidMeshAsset (vtable 0x141BBDAB0; + 0x10 name,
    \+ 0x20 MeshSet, + 0x30 MeshLodGroup);
  - MeshSet (vtable 0x141BBF880, TypeInfo 0x142835050) + 0x20 → its data (the MeshSet res as loaded): + 0x00 / + 0x10 box,
    \+ 0x20 … + 0x50 level pointers (up to 7), + 0x58 full name, + 0x60 short name;
  - a level: + 0x08 section count, + 0x0C (unaligned) sections, + 0x54 index format (0x21 16-bit, 0x2E 32-bit; seen on
    the 14 vista meshes with 4-byte indices), + 0x58 index bytes, + 0x5C vertex bytes, + 0x64 chunk id;
  - a section (0x130 apart): + 0x00 a runtime block inside the MeshSet (+ 0x380 …; vertex declarations per pass,
    vtable 0x141BD3918), + 0x10 material name, + 0x20 triangles, + 0x24 first index, + 0x28 vertex start (bytes), + 0x2C
    vertex count, + 0x4C elements (usage, format, offset, stream; 0xFF ends), + 0x8C vertex size;
  - enums from their reflected member tables: VertexElementFormat at 0x1428E0CB0 (3 Float3, 4 Float4, 5 Half, 6 Half2,
    7 Half3, 8 Half4, 0xC UByte4, 0xD UByte4N …), VertexElementUsage at 0x1428E2040 (1 Pos, 6 Normal, 7 Tangent,
    9 BinormalSign, 0x21 TexCoord0 …); e.g. a fence: Pos Half3 @0, BinormalSign Half @6, BoneIndices UByte4 @8,
    Normal Half4 @0xC, Tangent Half4 @0x14, TexCoord0 Half2 @0x1C, stride 32;
  - the MeshSet + 0x50 + level × 0x50: + 8 vertex and + 0x10 index Dx11RenderBuffer (vtable 0x141BD6840, TypeInfo
    0x1428389C0: + 0x10 ID3D11Buffer, + 0x40 size, + 0x44 1 vertices / 2 indices, + 0x58 the bytes it was made from);
    only the loaded levels have them (a far fence: level 2 only);
  - over every mesh record: 2311 / 1187 / 864 / 108 / 4 loaded levels 0-4, all sizes equal to the level's, all bytes
    readable;
  - the mesh streaming manager's record (0x350): + 0x2A0 level count, + 0x2B4 … each level's vertex + index bytes.
- **What was built:** Camera/ReplayShapes.cpp (+ ReplayShapes.hlsl compiled with fxc into ReplayShapesVs.h / Ps.h):
  - capture (game thread) as a recorded model first moves (ReplayModels::RecordFrame): the most detailed loaded level,
    its bytes copied, its drawable sections (position format 3/4/7/8, sizes in range, every index below the section's
    vertex count), the buffers re-checked after the copy; one copy per MeshSet; 32 MB a mesh, 256 MB in all;
  - drawing (render thread, Present, before VISUALS > Images): the models ReplayModels::Play finds the game doesn't have
    (HasLive false), not hidden then, at their evaluated recorded transform; position only (a half3 read as half4,
    the shader keeps xyz), flat-shaded from screen derivatives, one colour, two-sided; tested against the game's
    depth copy (greenplane::TakeFrameDepth, new user bit WantReplayShapes) and a D32 depth target of its own.
- **Not done / open:** textures (the section's material → its textures not traced; the albedo could be kept alive by
  holding its D3D texture); solidity (no collision); the capture rules weren't checked on live meshes; mission models
  that aren't rigid meshes are skipped (logged).

### 13. Colour textures for the shapes (2026-10-27)
- **Materials in the data:** MeshAsset fields (reflected, tools\classfields.py): + 0x30 LodGroup, + 0x60 Materials
  (array), + 0x68 NameHash …; MeshMaterial (0x70): + 0x10 ShaderInstance, + 0x18 Shader (SurfaceShaderInstanceDataStruct,
  0x28: its shader and parameter arrays), + 0x58 DisplacementMap …; TextureBaseAsset + 0x18 Resource. The gate's and the
  bus's meshes (fb\dump.py, old parser: the struct's arrays misread) carry shader references and parameters
  (PatternTiling 25 25, DiffuseColor 1 1 1 1, NormalDetailTiling, EmissiveIntensity) but no texture names: textures come
  from elsewhere (shader instances / variations), not traced.
- **Taken from the drawing instead:** ID3D11DeviceContext slots 12 (DrawIndexed) and 20 (DrawIndexedInstanced) of the
  immediate context, and of a deferred context made for the purpose where its functions differ, hooked (MinHook through
  util::hooks::CreateGameHook) at the first shape a recording keeps. While recording: IAGetVertexBuffers slot 0 looked up
  in a map of the captured levels' vertex buffers (their addresses; the buffers held until the recording ends);
  IAGetIndexBuffer must be the level's; first index + offset / index size and the count must be a section's; then
  PSGetShaderResources(0, 16): the first TEXTURE2D view in BC1/BC2/BC3/BC7/R8G8B8A8/B8G8R8A8/B8G8R8X8 _SRGB is kept (one
  reference) for that section. Each section's texture coordinates: element usage 0x21 (TexCoord0), format 6 (Half2) or
  2 (Float2).
- **Drawing:** input layout POSITION + TEXCOORD per section; the colour texture at t1 with an anisotropic wrap sampler;
  pow(albedo · lit, 1/2.2) out. Holding the textures keeps mission textures in video memory until the recording is
  forgotten or a new one starts.
- **Open:** whether Frostbite draws these meshes with DrawIndexed(Instanced) on the hooked functions (an indirect draw
  or another call wouldn't be seen); whether its colour textures are sRGB views (if not, the diagnostic lines list the
  views seen); materials' tiling (PatternTiling) not applied.

### 14. Textured shapes, and the way to a 1:1 copy of a mission (2026-10-27; research, offline)
- **Seen in game:**
  - nearly all the models recorded within 60 m, moving or still, were drawn at playback from the kept shapes;
  - colour textures kept for most sections (the views seen: formats 72 BC1_SRGB / 99 BC7_SRGB picked at t2 or t5;
    t3/t6/t8 BC5 (83: normals), t4/t7 BC1/BC3 (71/77), R8 / BC4 masks); the textures show, but look wrong. The pick is
    the first sRGB colour view; the game's materials blend several layers (pattern /
    detail textures, tiling such as PatternTiling 25 25, masks), so one texture with the mesh's first UVs isn't its look;
  - the two runners (Runner_02) and Icarus (Icarus_Collision) weren't played, with no log line at all. No live one of
    their class with a template within 3000 m, and no spawner with room for their template or kind (551 spawners
    listed). That case is now logged ("isn't shown").
- **Why reconstruction can't be 1:1:** after a mission the game streams its world out: its models (only their shapes
  and one colour map can be copied), its people (only stand-ins from free-roam spawners or borrowed bodies of another
  kind), its sound banks, its materials and its lighting. Every piece rebuilt is an approximation.
- **What keeps the real world (decompiled):**
  - PamMissionEntityData (0x48): + 0x18 Mission, + 0x20 FlagsSetWhenReplaying, + 0x28 ReenableOnAbortDelay, + 0x2C
    ReenableOnCompletedDelay, + 0x30 StreamOutOnCompletedRadius, + 0x34 StreamOutOnCompletedDelay, + 0x38
    StreamOutOnAbortedDelay, + 0x40 Enabled, + 0x41 StreamInOnAvailable, + 0x42 StreamOutOnCompleted, + 0x43
    StreamOutOnFail, + 0x44 StreamOutOnAbort, + 0x45 ReloadFromLastCheckpointOnFail, + 0x46 EnableCityAlertDuringMission,
    \+ 0x47 AllowStreamInWhenAlreadyInside. Act 1's missions are in levels/sp/sp_maincity/sp_maincity/layer43_act1flow
    (PamMissionEntityData × 12 with StreamOutOnCompleted True, delays 15 - 23 s, radii -1 / 20 / 25 / 50 / 80 m; some
    with FlagsSetWhenReplaying lists of DebugFlagValue).
  - PamServerMissionEntity (vtable 0x141C7ACD8, TypeInfo 0x142864420; no event handler: slot 4 is the empty 0x142A1C590).
    Its completion step 0x143A76D60: [mission + 0x28] (its data) + 0x42 set → 0x143A7A200(mission, 1, 0) at 0x143A7736D
    (also when + 0x11D and not StreamInOnAvailable): the world's stream-out, scheduled by its delay / radius.
  - PamServerMissionManagerEntity (vtable 0x141C7ADD0, handler 0x143A74BF0; data PamMissionManagerEntityData: + 0x18
    MissionToReplay, + 0x1C AllMissionsDisabled): events 0x975A3FCA = AbortCurrentMission (hash checked), and 0xF258E0DB,
    0xC5B7322F, 0xAA99C8D7, 0xACC994DF, 0xC6551D27, 0xE868AB1C, 0x37BB9BFC, 0x41EE0DA7, 0x68FB16FC, 0x6A4E64CA, 0x7DD57BA0
    (names not found). The game has a mission replay path (MissionToReplay, FlagsSetWhenReplaying); whether the retail
    menus reach it isn't known, and it sets progression flags.
- **Recommended: hold the recorded mission's stream-out.**
  1. While recording, note the mission running (its PamServerMissionEntity, its data's Flags and Mission name).
  2. Hook 0x143A7A200 (after byte checks of it and of its call at 0x143A7736D): while a recording made in that mission
     is kept, a stream-out of that mission isn't passed on; noted, logged.
  3. The mission's world stays as it was when it ended: its own models, people (the same entities: the replay already
     plays them by pointer), materials, lighting, sound banks. Playback is then the real thing, not a reconstruction.
  4. Let go (the noted stream-out passed to the game) when the recording is forgotten, a new one starts, or before a
     loading screen (the earlier hang: a load waited on held sub-levels) and as a menu button.
  - Open: whether the mission's end itself (the respawn / move to free roam, with Faith gone for 11.8 s) loads
    something that waits on this stream-out; what of the mission's logic keeps running after it's over; the mission's
    copies of free-roam places drawn twice where both are loaded; memory.
- **Not recommended:** the game's mission replay (it sets progression flags and runs the mission again, with autosaves);
  holding the containers' destruction (0x143469170 …, a whole layer across a load).

### 15. The hold on the mission's stream-out, built (2026-10-27) [not verified in game]

- **0x143A7A200 alone isn't enough (decompiled):** called (mission, completed, aborted) from the completion step at
  0x143A7736D, it sends StreamOut at once only when nothing makes it wait. With StreamOutOnCompletedRadius (+ 0x30) it
  stores Faith's place (+ 0xE8 / + 0xEC) and sets + 0x120; with StreamOutOnCompletedDelay / StreamOutOnAbortedDelay
  (+ 0x34 / + 0x38) it stores the game's time to send it at (+ 0x118, a float: now from 0x1432F5540 + the delay) and
  returns. The mission's update sends it later, from elsewhere in its code. Every Act 1 mission waits (15 - 23 s), so a
  hold there would only have seen the note.
- **Where every send ends:** the mission's world is a ServerSubLevelEntity (vtable 0x141B47BC0) at
  [[mission + 0xD0]] - 8, with a second one at [[mission + 0xD8]] - 8 that some paths use. The mission calls its event
  handler (slot 4, 0x14335EFB0) directly, from 21 places in 0x143A76D60, 0x143A792D0, 0x143A79440, 0x143A79520,
  0x143A79FE0, 0x143A7A0A0, 0x143A7A200 and 0x143A7A380. Those are all of the handler's callers; the only other
  reference to it is the vtable. The calls send StreamOut 0x21F3F677, StreamIn 0xD27BC17E, and through the same
  handler Preload 0xCE6D3F44 (name checked by the hash).
  - The handler: StreamOut is ignored if + 0x58 is empty (nothing in). Otherwise the event is copied (slot 2) into a
    queue at + 0x90 and the queue is worked (0x143365B90).
  - StreamIn / Preload are ignored if + 0x58 is set and + 0x120 bit 4 is clear. Otherwise they're queued, bit 4 is set
    for Preload, and 0x143363C00 runs.
  - The event is a plain EntityEvent (vtable 0x141A4A8B0, 16 bytes; its copy 0x143144F90 takes + 8 and + 0xC). The
    mission builds it on its stack, and afterwards only its destructor 0x142D4E9A0 runs, which puts the base vtable
    back.
  - After its StreamOut, the mission re-reads its state (0x143A77640 → 0x143A76D60), which can send StreamIn for its
    next availability in the same frame.
- **Built:**
  - The handler is hooked. A world is noted when a stream event reaches it from one of the 21 calls (the return
    address), or when it's the world of the mission 0x143A7A200 is called for.
  - A StreamOut to a noted world that has something in is kept instead of passed on when the replay records, or keeps a
    recording and the world wasn't streamed in again after it stopped. Stream events sent to that world later in the
    same server frame are kept too, in order.
  - They go to the game as the mission made them (rebuilt EntityEvents, on the server's thread, from
    ReplayServerUpdate) when:
    - a loading screen shows;
    - the recording is forgotten, a new one starts, or the recording stopped with fewer than 2 frames;
    - the option is turned off;
    - the REPLAY button "Let the mission's world go" is pressed;
    - the game sends that world a stream event in a later frame (the kept ones go first, then that one).
  - The deleting destructor (slot 7, 0x14335D790, the only caller of the body 0x14335D360) forgets a kept world the
    game destroys.
  - 0x143A7A200 is hooked for the log: it says when the mission's world streams out (at once, by radius, or by time)
    and whether the replay will keep it.
  - Every byte relied on was checked against the game image before building: the handler's id tests and StreamOut
    branch, the vtable slots 4 and 7, the destructor and the vtable its body restores, the event's vtable and copy,
    0x143A7A200's prologue, its call, its StreamOut send, and all 21 calls.
  - No other hook in the tools is on these functions.
- **What isn't known:**
  - whether the mission's end (Faith moved back to free roam) waits on this stream-out;
  - what of the mission's logic runs on in a world it thinks is gone;
  - whether places drawn by both the mission's world and free roam look doubled;
  - the memory a kept world costs;
  - whether destruction of a kept world can come from another thread than the server's (the log names the thread).

### 16. Leaving the Release mission reloads the level (2026-10-27)

- **What happens (seen in game):** leaving the Release mission from the pause menu, the game tears down its whole
  server level, then makes it again: Faith respawns in her free-roam outfit, three physics worlds are made, the
  Vista's 83 far zones are made, and the streaming triggers are switched.
- **The hold never came into it:**
  - 0x143A7A200 was never called, and no StreamOut was kept.
  - The mission's 4096-entity container and an 81-entity one went in the server's level teardown, on this stack:
    0x14333D4D0 (Server, + 0x1B0: the level's sub-level tree) → 0x14311E940 → 0x14311EBA0 (each sub-level, children
    \+ 0x70, next + 0x78; slot 11 / 0x58) → 0x14348AFB0 (slot 25 / 29) → 0x1431744E0 (container slot 11) →
    0x14311E9B0.
  - Leaving this mission reloads the level. Nothing of the mission's world can be kept across that: the level that
    holds it is destroyed. The hold applies to missions that end in the loaded city with a stream-out (Act 1's in
    layer43_act1flow); this one doesn't.
- **So at playback:** none of the recorded models were there. Nearly all were drawn from the kept shapes, with the
  colour textures picked from the game's draws. That is why the textures look wrong: the first sRGB view the pixel
  shader had, drawn unlit, with no material layers.
- **Missing models:**
  - Some models had no shape kept. Two were named: door_glitchkey_oneway_right and door_breachsingle_01 (not rigid
    meshes the replay can read); the others had no reason given.
  - Nothing beyond 60 m of Faith is recorded.
  - The level's static model groups (most buildings) aren't single models and aren't recorded at all.
- **Runners:** the two AIMale_Runner_02 were played by city men 591 m and 905 m away (HighCaste02, Black_November_02).
  After the reload no runner exists and no spawner of a runner template is on. Icarus was played by the lair's Icarus
  (the same template). The KrugerSec had stand-ins: Protector and Enforcer01 of their own template; Sentinel,
  Enforcer02 and SubProtector of the same kind.
- **Ways on (not decided):**
  1. Play the recording before leaving the mission: its level is still loaded, so its models, textures and people are
     the real ones (the people already kept by the replay's hold on them).
  2. Record the game's own draws of the mission's models and people (its shaders, textures and constants, held on
     the GPU) and draw them again in its pass that draws the scene's surfaces, so it lights them. That's the only way
     found to a 1:1 look after a level reload, runners included. It's large and unresearched: how the game binds its
     constants (per view or per object, and on deferred contexts), where that pass is, and the memory the moving
     people's constants need.
  3. Improve the shapes: the colour texture by the material's own parameter name (the level's meshvariationdb), the
     static model groups' members, and the doors that aren't rigid meshes. Still unlit, and the runners stay borrowed.

### 17. Recording the game's own draws (2026-10-27; research, offline; nothing built)

The question: can a mission's models and people be recorded as the game draws them, then drawn again by the game's own
shaders after the mission's level is gone? That would give the real look (textures, layered materials, the game's
light), the models the shapes miss, and the runners' own bodies.

**What the game's shaders say:**
- Source: the city's shader database (levels/sp/sp_maincity/sp_maincity/shaderdb, 128 MB), read offline. It has
  5173 vertex and 4960 pixel shaders, with their reflection names kept. The 2637 distinct instanced vertex shaders
  were disassembled with fxc /dumpbin. Tools: rdef_stats.py, vs_kinds.py, vs_extract.py.
- Every mesh shader takes its data from three constant buffers at fixed slots, the same in vertex and pixel shaders:
  - b0 functionConstants: per draw (in 5014 vertex shaders);
  - b1 externalConstants: the material's parameters (953 vertex, 3917 pixel);
  - b2 viewConstants: the camera, 1120 bytes, in all of them. Inside it: viewMatrix @32, projMatrix @96,
    viewProjMatrix @160, crViewProjMatrix @224 (camera-relative), cameraPos @720, fog, exposure.
- 4718 of the 5173 vertex shaders take each draw's placement from one buffer of float4s, t0 instanceVectorBuffer.
  b0 holds dxVectorBufferOffsets: the draw's start and the stride per instance (index = instance x .y + .x).
  - A static model's instance: its world matrix as 3 rows of float4 (absolute world space), then a visibility
    float per part (> 0: drawn). Some shaders put the matrix further in (+ 9 .. 11, after their own data).
  - The shaders then subtract cameraPos and multiply by crViewProjMatrix.
- **Skinned meshes** are drawn the same way, with no compute skinning. About 360 vertex shaders read 2 or 4 bone
  indices from a vertex attribute (all attributes are named TEXCOORDn), multiply by 3, and fetch each bone's 3x4
  matrix (absolute world space) from the same buffer at instance start + 12 + 3 x bone. They blend the bones by the
  vertex's weights, then subtract cameraPos.
  - Another 288 with the same pattern are foliage sway: 3x3 branch rotations plus wind.
  - The program database's compute shaders skin only cloth and morph targets.
- 928 pixel shaders write 4 targets: the G-buffer, which the game's deferred lighting reads (as in
  Research_Weather).

**So a recorded draw can be drawn again:**
- What's held: the game's vertex and pixel shaders, input layout, vertex and index buffers, the material's textures
  and samplers, and its states. All of these are D3D objects; holding a reference keeps each valid after the game lets
  go (COM).
- Copied on the GPU when it's drawn while recording: b0 and b1's bytes, and the draw's slice of the instance buffer.
  They're read back later through staging buffers, so the tools know them: the stride, the matrix rows, the bones.
- Played back in the game's G-buffer pass, while its targets and its b2 (this frame's camera) are bound:
  - the tools' own b0 (start 0, the same stride) and t0 (the instance data: the recorded world matrix for a model,
    the bones for a person), and the copied b1;
  - the game's shaders, textures and states;
  - then DrawIndexed(Instanced) with the recorded counts.
  - The game then lights it, fogs it, reflects it and puts it through its post effects as its own.
- **People:** the bone matrices of a frame can be worked out from the replay's own recorded pose (it already records
  162 - 183 bones a person a frame). The skinning matrix for mesh bone i is that bone's world transform times a
  constant: worked out once, from one frame where both are known, matching each mesh bone to its skeleton bone. That
  way no extra data is kept per frame. Kept raw instead (about 3.5 KB a person a frame) it would be about 300 MB for
  a 135 s recording.

**Is it safe?**
- **It never writes to the game's memory or data.** Everything goes through D3D11 calls in draw hooks the tools
  already have (DrawIndexed / DrawIndexedInstanced on the immediate context and the game's deferred contexts), on
  the thread that owns each context, plus the tools' own GPU buffers.
- **D3D11 is forgiving here:** a read past a buffer's end gives 0, and a missing texture reads as black. A wrong
  draw shows as a wrong picture, not a crash, as long as every object passed is a live one (held references make sure
  of it).
- **The real risk is new:** these tools have never drawn inside the game's own command lists (only at Present, after
  the game). Every state changed there has to be put back exactly for the game's next draw. A mistake shows as
  broken or missing game objects in that frame. In the worst case the driver resets the device ("device removed"),
  which closes the game. Visuals/D3DStateBackup.h already saves and restores state, which helps.
- **Memory:** the held textures and buffers of what was recorded stay in video memory until the recording is
  forgotten. That could be hundreds of MB for a mission, so it needs a cap.
- **Not covered at first:** shadows (the replayed things wouldn't cast them unless also drawn in the shadow pass),
  and see-through materials (glass, decals; drawn in other passes).

**What can't be known offline (needs a log-only build first):**
1. How b0 / b1 are bound: whole buffers, or D3D11.1 offsets into one big buffer (VSGetConstantBuffers1). The game's
   code calls the context indirectly; counting its call sites was inconclusive.
2. The instance buffer: its size, kind and how it's refilled each frame (where a draw's slice is).
3. The G-buffer pass: its targets (count, formats), its depth test (an EQUAL test after a depth pre-pass would hide
   draws that weren't in the pre-pass: they'd need their own depth state), and which deferred contexts draw it.
4. Which shader is which: the D3D objects don't carry their reflection names. Hooking the device's
   CreateVertexShader / CreatePixelShader (the level's shaders are made at its load) would tie each object to its
   bytecode, and so to which of its slots are per draw, per material or per pass.
5. People: which draws are a character's (the mesh buffers of a character entity: the chain from the entity to its
   skinned mesh wasn't traced; rigid ones are matched today by their buffers), and the mesh-bone to skeleton-bone
   match.

**Recommended:**
- Stage 0, log only: for the recorded models' draws while recording, log (1) - (4), and tie shaders to their names.
  It draws nothing and changes nothing; it's safe to run.
- Stage 1: static and moving models drawn by the game in its G-buffer pass.
- Stage 2: people.
- Stage 3 (optional): shadows and see-through materials.

### 18. Stage 0, the draw log (2026-10-27)

- Built as recommended in section 17: Camera/ReplayDrawLog.*, log only. Its lines start "Draw log (diagnostic):".
- **Shader names:** the device's CreateVertexShader / CreatePixelShader are hooked at the first Present. Each shader
  made after that is noted by its object: code hash, bindings, constant buffer sizes, the dxVectorBufferOffsets
  offset, outputs, and the bone test. The bone test is the immediate l(3, 3, 3, 3) in its code; offline it matched all
  649 bone-reading vertex shaders of the city's 2637 instanced ones and no other (bones_pattern.py).
- **Sampled frames (1 in 60):** draws are counted per pass. The first draw of each (vertex shader, pixel shader,
  pass, model) that is a recorded model or bone-reading has its full state logged (at most 48): constant buffers with
  11.1 offsets, the instance view and buffer, pixel shader views, input, depth / stencil, blend, raster, viewport.
  The passes are listed every 10 s.
- **The snapshot:**
  - Once, 5 s in, on the first context with such a draw into 3 or more targets: up to 24 draws.
  - What's copied: their b0, the first's b2, and their instance buffer, by CopyResource into staging buffers in the
    game's command list.
  - Read back 3 frames later. Decoded: start / stride from b0 (at the vertex shader's dxVectorBufferOffsets), the
    instance's rows 0 - 3, bones 0 - 3 at start + 12 + 3 x bone, and the recorded person nearest bone 0.

### 19. What the draw log settled

Seen in game, in free roam with KrugerSec fighting (Enforcer_Lowsense, SubProtector):
- **Shaders:** 5300 vertex and 5059 pixel shaders noted from the first Present, none unread. Every shader the logged
  draws used was known.
- **All the logged draws are on the immediate context**, the G-buffer's included. The game didn't record them on
  deferred contexts; drawing into its pass is a render-thread matter.
- **The passes** (one sampled frame):

  | Pass | Targets | Depth | Draws | Notes |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | #1, the G-buffer | 4: RGB10A2, RGBA8_SRGB, RGBA8, R11G11B10F | D32FS8 | 1064 | recorded models' and bone-reading among them |
  | #2 | the first 3 of #1's | D32FS8 | 38 | |
  | #3, likely motion vectors | 1 RG16F | D32FS8 | 47 - 86 | bone-reading among them |
  | #4 / #30, shadow maps | none | D32F 1536x1536 | 58 - 87 | recorded models among them; no bone-reading |
  | #5, see-through / forward | 1 RGBA16F | D32FS8 | 93 - 169 | |
- **The G-buffer pass's states:**
  - Depth test on, write on, func 7 (GREATER_EQUAL: reversed depth). No EQUAL test, so draws need no depth pre-pass.
  - Stencil on, writing a material code: ref 2 (read mask 0x20, func 7) or ref 32 (func 8 ALWAYS), REPLACE.
  - Blend off; cull none or back; full-frame viewport.
- **Constants:** b0 (functionConstants, a 256 B window) and b1 (externalConstants, 256 - 512 B) are windows into one
  1 MB dynamic buffer, set with D3D 11.1 offsets (first / num in 16-byte units). b2 (viewConstants) is a 1136 B
  dynamic buffer of its own.
- **The instance buffer:** one 1 MB dynamic buffer (65536 float4s, RGBA32F, the whole range viewed). Each draw's
  vertex shader has dxVectorBufferOffsets at byte 0 of its b0.
- **Input:** a mesh's vertices are a range in a shared immutable vertex buffer (e.g. stride 64 at offset 590080 in a
  1.9 MB one); 16-bit indices; triangle lists.
- **The pixel shaders confirm the layered materials:** a character's has texture_Diffuse_AO, NormalRS,
  Opacity_SSS_Metal_Trans, Emissive, MaterialMask, then Material01 - 04 Diffuse / NormalMap / RSM. A building's
  has the level's lightmaps (lightMapIrradiance / Direction / SkyVisibility). That's why one picked texture can't look
  right, and why the game's own pixel shaders are the way.
- **The snapshot:** the camera position from b2 was right (by Faith). The b0 ring (1 MB) was over the copy limit
  (64 KB), so no draw's start was known and its instance data wasn't decoded: the people weren't matched.
- **Not seen:** the other passes' states. The 48 state logs went to the G-buffer pass in the first sampled frame.

**Fixed:**
- Constant buffers up to 2 MB are copied, so the ring is copied whole at each snapshot draw: about 48 MB of staging,
  freed after the read.
- State logs: one per (vertex shader, pixel shader, pass), up to 24 per pass and 120 in all.

### 20. Stage 0 answered

Seen in game, in free roam with KrugerSec.

**The instance data, decoded:**
- b0's first 16 bytes are dxVectorBufferOffsets: (start, stride, start, stride) in float4s. The second pair is the
  same here; likely the previous frame's, for motion.
- **People (bone-reading draws):** the bones sit at start + 12 + 3 x bone, 3 rows each, in absolute world space.
  - Draw #0 had stride 63 = 12 + 3 x 17 bones. Its bone 0 was **0.10 m** from where the replay recorded that
    KrugerSec (PamClientCharacterEntity 0x3FFCC43D0) at that moment. So a person's draws can be told by their bones'
    places.
  - Draws #1 - #10 (strides 30 - 252, up to 80 bones) had their bones about 1.5 m from the camera: Faith's own
    body.
  - The 12-row header differs: identity rows in #0, material-like values in Faith's.
- **Models (stride 5 for most):** the world matrix is **not** at the instance's start. For vertex shader
  AD4348C5DF535549 it's rows 2 - 4: rotation in xyz, translation in w (an aircon at x -94.11, y 57.93, about 5 m from
  the camera). Rows 0 - 1 hold per-instance values: a lightmap scale / offset by their look, and other constants.
  Other shaders (stride 12, light_ext_dt_wall) start with colour-like values. So the matrix's place is per shader.
  At capture it can be found as the rows equal to the entity's known transform.

**The passes, all on the immediate context:**

| Pass | Targets | Depth | States / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1, G-buffer | 4: RGB10A2, RGBA8_SRGB, RGBA8, R11G11B10F | D32FS8, frame size | depth GREATER_EQUAL, write on, stencil REPLACE ref 2 / 32 |
| #2, decals or overlays | the first 3 | same | depth write off, writes only RT1's RGB (mask 0 7 0 0), cull none |
| #3, motion vectors | 1 RG16F | same | moving things only (a revolving sign, people), depth write off |
| #4, see-through / forward | 1 RGBA16F | same | blend on, depth write off |
| #8 / #9 / #10, reflection capture | the same G-buffer formats | 512x512 | |
| #27 / #28, shadow maps | none | D32F 1536x1536 | a position-only stream (stride 8), its own vertex shader, depth bias -1000 |

**The buffers:** b0 / b1 windows and the instance data come from a pool of 1 MB dynamic buffers, several of them, in
rotation. b2 (viewConstants) is one 1136 B buffer.

**So stage 1 (models) is well-founded:**
- **While recording,** at a recorded model's G-buffer draw, keep the following, read back as the snapshot does:
  - the game's vertex shader, pixel shader, input layout, vertex and index buffers (with their offsets), its views,
    samplers and states (held);
  - copies of its b0 / b1 windows and its instance slice;
  - which rows are its world matrix.
- **While playing,** on the render thread, at the end of the game's G-buffer pass (its targets still bound), draw
  each recorded model the game doesn't have:
  - with the tools' own b0 (start 0, the same stride), b1 (the copy) and t0 (the slice, with the recorded transform
    written into the world rows), and the game's b2;
  - then put back every state.
- The game then lights it, fogs it and reflects it as its own.

**Still to come:**
- People (stage 2): the mesh-bone to skeleton-bone match needs a few frames of bones next to the recorded poses.
- Shadows: the shadow pass's own shader and stream.
- Motion vectors.

### 21. Stage 1 built: the models drawn with the game's own draws (2026-10-27)

- Camera/ReplayGameDraws.*; option REPLAY > ... > *With the game's own drawing of them*, `[Replay] GameDraws`.
- **The pass's end:** the immediate context's OMSetRenderTargets (vtable slot 33) and
  OMSetRenderTargetsAndUnorderedAccessViews (slot 34) are hooked. Leaving the main G-buffer is the end of its pass:
  its 4 targets R10G10B10A2 / R8G8B8A8_SRGB / R8G8B8A8 / R11G11B10F, and a depth target the swap chain's size.
- **Capture (recording):**
  - The first G-buffer draw of each shape section (found by the game's vertex and index buffers, first index and
    count) is kept as a recipe.
  - Held: its VS / PS / GS / HS / DS, input layout, topology, VB slots 0 - 3 with strides and offsets, IB, VS views
    0 - 7, PS views 0 - 31, samplers, depth (with stencil ref), blend and raster states. Slots holding the instance
    buffer are marked.
  - Pages copied at the pass's end (CopyResource into staging): its VS and PS b0 / b1 pages and its instance page.
    The camera's b2 is copied at the pass's first kept draw.
  - Read back 3 frames later:
    - the windows' bytes;
    - start / stride, from the vertex shader's dxVectorBufferOffsets offset (the draw log's shader registry,
      ReplayDrawLog's VectorOffsetsOf);
    - up to 256 instances;
    - the world rows: 3 rows whose xyz columns are at right angles (2 % of their lengths), with a finite translation
      within 600 m of the camera.
  - The tools' b0 (dynamic) and b1 copies (default) are made then.
- **Replay:**
  - At the pass's end, for SetDraws' models: each recipe of that shape gets the model's instance, the nearest
    recorded one within 2 m of the model's place (remembered per entity), with its transform written into every
    world-row block.
  - The tools' instance buffer (dynamic, RGBA32F) is filled, each recipe's b0 gets offsets (start, stride, start,
    stride), and the game's state is saved: shaders, 14 constant slots per stage with 11.1 first / num, views,
    samplers, input, depth, blend, raster.
  - Each recipe is drawn as one DrawIndexedInstanced, then everything is restored.
  - replay_shapes::Apply skips the sections drawn so (TakeDrawn).
- **Not covered:** shadows, motion vectors, see-through, decal-pass parts, b0-world-matrix shaders, people.

### 22. Stage 1 in game, the 1:1 people rule, and stage 2 (2026-10-27)

**Stage 1 in game:**
- Stage 1 works (seen in game): recipes kept while recording, and parts drawn with the game's own draws at playback;
  the G-buffer was bound at the end of its pass. The KrugerSec looked almost right.
- The runners were wrong because of the borrowing. The two Runner_02 runners were played by HighCaste02 (591 m away)
  and Black_November_02 (905 m away), taken as "a spawn template of the same kind". The stand-ins came from spawners
  "of the same kind": Sentinel for Protector, Enforcer02 for Enforcer01.

**The 1:1 people rule:** borrowing takes only the same data or the same spawn template. Stand-ins are
asked only of spawners of the exact template (StandInPossible gives 2 or 0). Anyone else isn't shown.

**Stage 2:**
- **The relation used:** a skinned draw's bone rows are the skeleton's matrices for the bones that mesh uses. The
  draw log saw bone 0 at 0.10 m from a KrugerSec's recorded place. The pose slot's matrices are the world pose times
  a fixed transform per bone, the same in every body of a skeleton (RawSlot notes, 2026-10-23, ReadUnbind).
- **Capture:**
  - replay_gamedraws::CaptureSkin every 30 frames: G-buffer draws whose vertex shader reads bones (the registry's
    l(3,3,3,3) test), up to 64. TakeState is shared with the models' CaptureDraw.
  - Read back like the models'. Each instance becomes a SkinCandidate {id, the recording's clock, vb, start index,
    count, stride, instance}.
- **Skeleton:** RecordPeople notes the pose manager, and reads the fixed transforms (FindRawSlot + ReadUnbind) until
  two frames agree within UnbindTolerance (at most 300 tries).
- **Matching (FaithReplay::AdoptGameDraws, game thread):**
  - The header is tried at 12 rows first, then 0 - 20, where every bone block is a transform.
  - Candidate people: those whose recorded bone 1 is within 3 m of the draw's first bone at its clock.
  - The time: clock - 0.20 to + 0.05 s in 1/120 s steps, chosen by the draw's first bone against every skeleton
    bone (within 4 cm, rotation within 0.05).
  - Then every bone is matched to its skeleton bone (all within 4 cm). The person with the smallest worst error
    wins.
  - Matrices come from the recording: bones 0 - 3 from RootWorld; the others composed from the packed local pose
    by the hierarchy's Order and Parent, as DrawBody does; times Unbind (MatricesOf, WriteBody's maths).
  - A person keeps one frame's set, the one with the most indices. Duplicates and Faith's draws are released.
- **Playback (DrawPeopleWithGameDraws):**
  - For each person with parts, within their window and not StillCharacter: the matrices at the replay's time.
  - Instance = the header rows as kept plus each bone's matrix (by Map), drawn with stage 1's injection.
  - BorrowForGone and AskStandInsAhead skip such people (DrawnByGameDraws).
- **Not known:**
  - whether the header rows hold per-frame values (e.g. a place for lighting) that should follow the person;
  - whether hair, eyes or cloth are drawn in the G-buffer pass;
  - how often the matching succeeds for fast movers;
  - the cost of the capture frames.

### 23. Stage 2 in game

**What worked:**
- The recorded people were matched to the game's own draws of them: 4 - 11 parts each, their bones within 0.0 - 2.2 cm,
  the frame drawn -200 to +33 ms from the recording's.
- Matched: Protectors, Enforcers, SubProtectors, the Runner_02 runners, Icarus (11 parts) and the Cutscene_Enforcer_Baton.
- At playback with the game's own draws, everything looked right except the items below (seen in game).

**Missing, and why (seen in game, and the game's data read offline):**
- **Icarus's hood / jacket:** characters/male/icarus/jacket_cloth/icarus_jacket_cloth_mesh is a RigidMeshAsset with a
  cloth asset (icarus_jacket_cloth_clothasset_win32): cloth simulated on the graphics card each frame (the program
  database's cloth compute shaders, clothBoneTransforms / renderVertexBuffer). Its draw isn't a bone-reading one, so
  stage 2 doesn't see it. Replaying it 1:1 would need its simulated vertices recorded every frame (large), or the
  game's cloth simulation run again.
- **KrugerSec weapons (batons, guns):** weapons/handheld/cpf_baton/cpf_baton_mesh and apr-11 are SkinnedMeshAssets.
  The recorded PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity (26 bones) all have a known hierarchy, yet none got parts. Which
  check failed (their fixed transforms not read, no capture of their draw, or no match) isn't known.
- **The hunter drone:** characters/enemy/drone_hunter/drone_hunter_mesh is a SkinnedMeshAsset. Its 49-bone skeleton's
  hierarchy was worked out with a loop, so its world pose can't be made from the recording:
  GameDrawable needs the hierarchy's Order.
- **The two doors:** door_glitchkey_oneway_right and door_breachsingle_01 aren't rigid meshes the replay can read, so
  neither stage 1 (shapes) nor stage 2 (people) covers them. ReplayModels records their entity's transform, not
  bones.

**Proposed (stage 2b, before stage 3):**
1. Guns, batons and drones (actors): record their whole world pose each frame (26 or 49 bones, about 5 MB a drone
   for 110 s), so their matrices don't depend on the hierarchy. Log per person why no parts were kept.
2. Doors: match a kept skinned draw no person fits to a recorded model of no shape near it, keep its bones relative to
   the model's transform at that time, and pose them with the model's recorded transform when it plays (exact for a
   door moved by its entity; its own bone animation, if any, isn't recorded).
3. Icarus's cloth: a later step of its own (record the simulated cloth on the graphics card, at a lower rate).

### 24. Stage 2b built (2026-10-27)

- **Actors (guns, batons, drones; PersonTrack BodyOffset ActorBodyOffset):** AppendMatrices copies the pose slot's
  RawMatrices (bones x 12 floats) with each stored frame. FlushPending repeats it, TrimPerson keeps it in step, and
  MatricesOk turns false (the copies let go) on a failed read. PersonMatricesAt uses them, interpolated per number,
  before the skeleton path (RecordedWorld x Unbind). PersonPlaceAt falls back to the first matrix's place.
- **Shapeless models (doors):**
  - ReplayModels gains ShapelessNear (recording: the nearest track with Shape < 0, by Last), GoneTransform (playback:
    !HasLive, keys, visible: Evaluate) and ShapelessMoved (for the log).
  - AdoptGameDraws gives unmatched candidates to the nearest shapeless model within 3 m: B_i = T^-1 S_i (the general
    3x4 inverse).
  - Each model keeps its most detailed set. DrawPeopleWithGameDraws poses them S_i = T(t) B_i.
- **Log:** LogGameDrawsMissing at StopRecording (after a last AdoptGameDraws), per person or model with no parts: the
  reason (matrices not recorded / fixed transforms not read / hierarchy unknown or a loop / world pose not recorded /
  no draw near / N near, the best miss), then a total.
- **Cloth (Icarus's jacket):** not covered; a step of its own.

### 25. Stage 2b in game, and the fix (2026-10-27)

**Seen in game:**
- People (stage 2) matched as before, within 0.0 - 2.9 cm.
- **Doors took people's bodies.** 'door_glitchkey_oneway_right' 0x4358E2730 took sets of 95217 - 132252 indices (10 -
  11 parts): Icarus's body (his set is 107556 indices, 11 parts). 0x2D45551A0, 0x3E7CF2F30 and three 0x65160Axxx
  models took 87594-index sets (4 parts). Matching by "the nearest shapeless model within 3 m" let any unmatched
  skinned draw near a door become the door, and the most detailed set (a body) won.
- **Guns:** no PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity matched. Three had their closest 1173 - 1189 m off (their slot
  matrices aren't where the game draws them); the rest 1e32 cm (their slot matrices couldn't be read, so MatricesOk
  went false and the skeleton path had nothing).
- **The drone:** no draw that reads bones was kept near it. Its vertex shader skins with one bone a vertex
  (`imad r.x, v.x, l(3)`), which the 4-bone byte test (`l(3, 3, 3, 3)`) never saw.
- **Icarus's hood / jacket:** GPU cloth, not covered (section 23).

**The fix (stage 2b):** [not verified in game]
- **Bone-reading shaders:** ReplayDrawLog's test is now instruction-level: an `imad` whose first source is a vertex
  input and whose second is an immediate 3 in every component. Checked offline over the city's 2637 instanced vertex
  shaders against fxc's disassembly: 912 of 912, nothing else (the byte test found 649).
- **Draws known by their mesh:** a gun's MeshSet is at its entity + 0x258 (MEC_Reverse_Notes 2026-10-23); a door's
  through its data + 0x98 asset + 0x20 (the same path as a rigid model's, the asset's vtable not checked; the MeshSet's
  and each RenderBuffer's are). replay_shapes::LevelVertexBuffers reads each loaded level's ID3D11Buffer.
  FaithReplay::BindOwners hands them to replay_gamedraws::SetWantedSkins; those draws are kept every 10 frames (up to
  32 a frame on top of the others' 64). A draw of one of those buffers goes to the nearest owner of that mesh within
  3 m (guns of a kind share a mesh), never to a person, and people's matching skips them.
- **Guns and drones recorded as world poses:** AppendWorld copies the pose slot's whole world pose (bones x 8 floats)
  with each stored frame (26 bones: 832 B a frame; 49: 1.6 KB), in place of the slot's matrices.
- **Posing by motion, not by a fixed transform read from the game:** a draw's bones S_i are a recorded bone's world
  matrix W_j (a door: its transform T) times a fixed K_i. From the first draw kept, K_i = W_1^-1 S_i (all following
  bone 1, where a gun is; a door's K = T^-1 S). When a later draw of the same part comes (0.15 s or more later, the
  owner having moved 5 cm or 0.05), FitPair finds for each bone the recorded bone that moved the same way: K from the
  first, checked at the second within 4 cm and 0.05, the two frame times searched as for people (the frame's people's
  fit preferred). A set a later draw doesn't fit is let go (the wrong gun of two of a kind), the owner given up on
  after 3.
- **The drone** (mesh place not known): a skinned draw near it that is no person's part waits in a pool (128, 5 s) for
  a later draw of the same part; taken if every bone of it moved and each fits one of the drone's recorded bones by
  the same pair fit.
- **Playback:** S_i(t) = W_j(t) K_i (a door: T(t) K_i), for a gun or drone the game doesn't have any more, and a door
  the game doesn't have (GoneTransform).
- **Log:** each owner's buffers read (or not, with tries), each set kept / checked / let go, and at the end of a
  recording who has parts and who hasn't and why (world pose not recorded, buffers not read, no draw of its mesh kept,
  sets that didn't fit, no draw near the drone that moved with it).
- **Not known:** whether a gun's world pose (the slot's world buffer) moves the way its draws do (the
  pair fit says so, or logs the miss); whether the doors' asset + 0x20 is a MeshSet for a skinned mesh (the vtable
  check says so in the log).

### 26. The asset log and how a mission loads (2026-10-27)

- **Asset log (Camera/ReplayAssetLog.*).** While the replay records or plays it notes, in Cinematic Tools\ReplayAssets.log:
  - the game's mesh table, once a second;
  - textures made (CreateTexture2D, device slot 5);
  - the main G-buffer pass's draws every 15th frame, the game's and the replay's own (vertex buffer → mesh name, the
    pixel shader's textures 0 - 7);
  - and the game's bundles (log-only hooks on the bundle manager).

  When playback stops it reports the meshes drawn while recording at the seconds played that weren't drawn (missing,
  partly) and those drawn with other texture sizes or formats. [not verified in game]
- **How a mission loads:** Research_Mission_Loading_2026-10-27.md (compartments, the sub-level bundle loader, the
  unload message, the replay options A / B / C).

# 31. Snow in Mirror's Edge Catalyst (2026-10-26, offline)

Offline research (game data, the mod file). Anything not checked in game is marked
**[not verified]**. The weather this builds on is in Research_Weather_2026-10-25.md.

### 1. The game has no snow
- No EBX or resource name in the game's catalogs has snow, blizzard or flake in it. The 8 names with "frost" are
  frosted glass (kingdomcell_01_frostedglass*, t_frostedglass_*) and Frostbite logos.
- So snow has to be made, either from other effects (what the mod does, section 3) or drawn (what the tools do,
  section 5).

### 2. The mod file
- `snowfall.fbmod`, "Snowfall" 1.0 by Toffiklubitoffi, category Graphic. FrostyMod format 5, profile
  MirrorsEdgeCatalyst, game version 175205. Read as data only; nothing in it was run.
- Its own description: the snow changes through the day. Known issues it lists: slight, distant snowfall in closed
  spaces; blizzard particles flicker near light sources; motes glint in the dark; untested in missions.
- 31 resources. The resource list ends at 0xE28, which is exactly the data offset, and the 27 data entries end at
  the file's end (0x174A1FE). So the parse is complete.
  - The icon (PNG) and 4 screenshots without data.
  - 25 EBX: 10 change the game's own assets, 15 are new (flag 8).
  - 1 chunk, b8b3c73f-e3d2-f536-e008-0da67b5664e4, 24191472 bytes. It's the game's own chunk for the wave
    ME_Wind_AltitudeQuadShorter_01, replaced (the game's is 2394544 bytes). It starts with an EA audio header
    block (0x48).
- How it was read:
  - The resources were parsed with tools\fbmod.py. Their data was undone from Frostbite's blocks with fb\cas.py
    (tools\decomp.py). The mod's data is kept in its own folder, snowdata\.
  - The EBX were parsed with fb\ebx2.py (Frosty's instance layout).
  - Each was diffed against the game's own copy, with instances matched by content, not order (tools\snowdiff.py,
    moddiff3's way). The new assets were diffed against the asset they copy.
  - Blueprint connections were printed with their hashed names resolved (tools\conn.py, fb\hashnames.tsv plus the
    names in each file's own type table).
  - The fog values by hour come from tools\vefog.py.

  of the Bauble cutscene (Patch\Win32\anchor.sb). Against the game's:
