### 4. What of this the tools can use
- **The emitters: not used.**
  - em_bauble_cameradebris_dust is in the Anchor bundle (anchor.sb). The tools only move effects the city has
    placed and loaded (Research_Weather sections 5 and 8), and nothing places this one in the free-roaming city.
  - Changing the rain's emitters into snow in memory would mean rewriting their templates' gravity, size and
    texture, and the texture is a loaded resource. None of that is decoded.
  - So the snow is drawn by the tools (section 5), the way the rain in the distance is.
- **The look: used.**
  - The fog fields the mod changes are in the mixed state at offsets that are already known: the fog block
    \+ 0x620, its HeightFogAltitude + 0x90, Depth + 0x94, VisibilityRange + 0x98; the sky block + 0x390, its
    HeightFogColorAdd + 0xD0, MinHeightFogTransmittance + 0x24C.
  - The sun: as the rainy look (OutdoorLightScale, the sun's final light, its disk and its flare).
  - Not used, because their state offsets aren't verified: RayleighScatteringCoefficientScale, the extinction
    relation, ScaleHeightRayleigh, the classic fog switches, Enlighten, the lens reflections and exposure.

### 5. What the tools do (2026-10-26)
**The menu:** VISUALS > Snow (weather::DrawSnowUI, its own header right after Weather, VisualsManager.cpp).
- Snow or rain: ticking Snow or Random snow clears Rain and Random rain, and the other way round.
- One intensity (g_Intensity) and one forecast serve either. The chance is the chosen one's.
- g_RainOn is now "falling and rain chosen" and g_SnowOn "falling and snow chosen". So with snow on, the game's
  rain isn't moved to the camera, EmitterParameter3 isn't given, and there's no rain sound, rain in the distance or
  rain zones loaded.
- Thunder stays the weather's. "Thunder and lightning with it" is Random rain's only.

**Falling snow** (WetLook.hlsl SnowAt, drawn at Present with the rest of the pass):
- Sheets of flakes fixed in the world, as RainAt's, in three families: vertical across x, vertical across z, and
  level, so it still snows looking straight up or down.
- The wind (an integrated offset, g_SnowDrift) carries each sheet across itself and its flakes along it.
- Bands out from the camera: 0.35 - 6 m a sheet every 0.75 m (cells 0.22 m), 6 - 20 m every 2 m (0.35 m, flakes
  x 1.6), 20 - 50 m every 5 m (0.7 m, x 3); 70 m when snow isn't kept out of buildings.
- Per cell a flake with probability Snow amount x the intensity (x 1.5 in a blizzard, at most 0.95).
  - On the vertical sheets each column falls at 0.75 - 1.35 m/s; the level sheets fall at 1 m/s.
  - Each flake sways ±0.15 of its cell.
- A flake is 6 - 14 mm across x Flake size. It's drawn round as seen: its distance from the pixel's ray, not on
  its sheet. Under a pixel it's spread over 0.7 px and made fainter by the area it lost.
- Faded into the game's fog (FogAt). With Keep snow out of buildings on, drawn only where KnownOpenAt > 0.5, the
  weather's squares (2 m, 50 m each way).
- Colour: the frame's average luminance x 1.3, plus what's round it x 0.2, plus 0.03, a cool white with 20 % of the
  light's colour.
- The pattern jumps once when the snow's clock wraps (2000 s of snow) or the drift passes 10 km.
- At sheets seen almost edge-on, a flake can be cut at its cell's edge (cells keep flakes 0.2 cell from their edge).
- The pixel shader went from about 3521 to 6315 instruction slots (the bands and families are unrolled). A pixel's
  ray crosses at most about 36 sheets: the sum over families of distance x |its axis| / spacing, at most √3 x
  (7.5 + 7 + 6). The cost wasn't measured.

**Snow on the ground** (PsMain, while snow is chosen; the wet look is off then):
- Where normal.y is smoothstep(0.35, 0.8) (up to about 55 degrees, more on what's flatter), away from depth edges,
  out to "On the ground up to", times the fog.
- Not under the squares' roofs, and not on Faith, people or vehicles (KeptDry, DryShapes.cpp). wetlook::Reach()
  now gives the snow's reach while snow is chosen, so dry::Update scans for them then.
- Inside the squares: only what KnownOpenAt knows is open. Past them: the open counts (it can't be told).
- Coverage: smoothstep(1 - c - 0.12, 1 - c + 0.12, noise x 0.85 + flatness x 0.15), all of it from c 0.85 up,
  with c = settled x "Snow on the ground".
- Settled (weather.cpp UpdateSnow): + dt / (Settles over) x the intensity while it snows, - dt / (3 x Settles over)
  when it doesn't, real time, steps of at most 0.25 s.
- Brightness: max(the pixel's luminance x 1.8, what's round it (the frame's copy at its level about 240 px wide),
  the frame's average x 0.6),
  capped at 1, cool white with 25 % of the light's colour.

**The snowy look** (GiveLook with RainyLook.Snowy, in the mixed state right after each mix, as the rainy look):
- The snow mod's four hours (section 3), linear between them round the clock (noon straight on to midnight):

  | | 0:00 | 6:00 | 7:00 | 12:00 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | visibility (m) | 250 | 6000 | 5000 | 500 |
  | altitude (m) | 30 | 50 | 0 | 350 |
  | depth (m) | 90 | 200 | 150 | 300 |
  | MinHeightFogTransmittance | 0 | 0.6 | 0.7 | 0 |
  | HeightFogColorAdd | 0.6 0.65 0.7 | 0.5 | 0.6 | 1 |

  - Where the mod left a field at one of these hours, the value is the game's own there.
- Visibility and MinHeightFogTransmittance only go down: never clearer than the game's. A blizzard halves the
  visibility. "Fog: seen through up to" caps it.
- The fog fields are blended by Snow fog x the look's amount x the indoor easing (as the rainy look's fog). The
  colour is blended by the look's amount.
- New field: HeightFogAltitude, fog block + 0x90. This is the offset FogParams already reads; the fog set-up uses
  it as A in its coefficients (Research_Weather section 23).
- Against the rainy look:
  - the sky's luminance isn't lowered;
  - the sky light x (1 + 0.5 less sun) instead of 0.3;
  - cloud sun colour x (1 - 0.15 grey), cloud colours x (1 - 0.1 grey);
  - bloom x (1 + grey) instead of 2 grey;
  - forward scattering and UseOzone left as the game's.
- Fix: the time of day is now read for the looks too, not only for the forecast. Before, the rainy look's by-hour
  values stayed at the last hour known (noon at first) unless Random rain was on.

**Not verified / not known:**
- All of section 5 in game: how the flakes look and move, their brightness by day and night, the cost.
- How the snow on the ground looks on the city's mostly white surfaces.
- How the snowy fog looks with the physical sky.
- The wind's way isn't the game's: WindDirection (+ 0x6E4) is known, but not which way 0 degrees points.
- A room seen through a window past 50 m can get snow on its floor.
- Not done: replays don't record snow. Their weather (REPLAY > Time of day and weather as recorded) is
  weather::State (Rain, Heavy, KeepOut, LoadZones), which is unchanged, so a replay leaves the snow as it is.

### 6. Flakes of their own, the game's interiors (2026-10-26)
Goal: make the snow less confusing and tiring to watch, keep it out of the Runners' lair, and check the snow on the
ground for puddle reflection faults.

**The roof sweeps in the lair (seen in game):** in the Runners' lair (-4 to -20, 69.3, 270 to 290) the camera was
found under a roof 3.7 / 7.4 / 1.8 m up and under the open sky by turns, every few seconds. So the roof sweeps (one
zero-radius ray straight up per 2 m square, collision filter 9, CameraCollision.cpp) found a roof over some of the
lair's squares and nothing over others.

**Why (offline):**
- objects/architecture/unique/trainstation/lair has collision (lair_physics_win32). lair_exterior and the windows
  (lairblindswindow_256 / _512) have none.
- **[not verified]** that the missing roof is lair_exterior's: the Havok collision data wasn't read.

**The game's interiors (verified in data):**
- In levels/sp/sp_maincity/visualenvironments each environment's Visibility is driven by an AreaProximityEntity's
  Out, in layer1_ve_volumes_schematic.
- Those entities are linked (field 0x31FB3B9F) to boxes (OBBData: a transform, half extents) and prisms
  (VolumeVectorShapeData: closed points and a height) in layer0_ve_volumes.
- The cross-layer connections were resolved with tools\xlayer2.py; the table is in vevolumes.txt.
- ve_runners_lair_interior is AreaProximity #41 (ProximityDistance 0.5). Its shape is the prism #97: floor y 63.37,
  16 m high, points (-14.02, 270.88), (-39.56, 287.95), (-36.72, 292.20), (-7.60, 326.63), (13.71, 312.39).
- Every lair position seen in game is inside it. The three at about (-16, 270.5) are outside, where the camera was
  under the open sky.
- Used: the environments whose names say they're inside: ve_runners_lair_interior, ve_plasticslair,
  ve_familymatters_krugersapartment_01, ve_generic_interiortheview (two proximities), ve_droneworks_interior (two),
  ve_benefactor_anansitower_interior_01, ve_kingdom_interior, ve_elysium_interior01 and ve_trainstation_rightwing.
  That's 59 boxes and 2 prisms, generated into Weather.cpp by tools\interiors_cpp.py.
- Not used: the districts' (ve_anchor, ve_theview), the Shard's fog and shadow distance, ve_dof_override, and the
  ones whose names don't say (ve_prisonerx_01 - 03, ve_generic_gridnode, ve_vlr_*, ve_omnistattunnels_transition,
  ve_skycity_atrium, and four proximities with no environment resolved).
- **[not verified]** that each volume matches its walls exactly. They were made for lighting.

**What the interiors do:**
- WetLook.hlsl InteriorAt(rel): the nearest 32 boxes and 2 prisms within 1100 m (WetLook.cpp, weather::GetInteriors,
  nearest first by the sphere round their corners).
- ShelterAt is max(the squares, inside); KnownOpenAt is min(the squares, 1 - inside).
- weather::ShelterAt does the same on the CPU (InsideInterior, the whole table).
- So inside them: no falling snow, no snow on the ground, no wet look or puddles (the rain's too), and the lightning
  only through openings.
- Not changed: the game's own rain particles (their exclusion boxes still come from the roof sweeps) and the rain drawn
  in the distance (the open-sky squares).

**Why the snow looked confusing and tiring (from the first build's design):**
- Every flake on a sheet was carried the same way, and the level sheets all fell at 1 m/s together. That's a wide
  field of points moving coherently, which induces vection, the feeling of moving yourself. Fine detail and high
  contrast strengthen it (LaValle, Virtual Reality, "Vection reduction strategies": a smaller field of optical flow,
  lower spatial frequency, lower contrast).
- Sheets every 0.75 - 5 m in world-aligned planes: rows and layers.
- Thousands of points under a pixel: shimmer.
- Flakes from 0.35 m: big points rushing past at the lens.
- No motion blur: every flake jumped several pixels a frame when the camera turned.
- Real snow (research): unrimed aggregates fall at 0.4 - 1.2 m/s, very differently even at the same size (Locatelli &
  Hobbs 1974, as cited by Copernicus ACP 25, 16729, 2025). In the atmospheric surface layer snowflakes respond to the
  turbulence (Stokes numbers 0.1 - 0.4, accelerations with wide exponential tails; Nemes et al., J. Fluid Mech. 2017),
  so no two move alike.

**The flakes now (SnowVsMain / SnowPsMain, a second draw after the pass, alpha blended):**
- 24000 flakes in a 16 m box and 10000 in a 48 m box round the camera, each at a random place, kept in the box as
  the camera moves (frac of the world position minus the camera, over the box): they stay put in the world.
- Snow amount x the intensity decides how many: each flake has its own share, faded in over 3 %.
- Each falls at 0.5 - 1.3 m/s. Its own wander: a loop of 0.15 - 0.5 m every 5 - 20 s. Its own flutter: 1.5 - 4 cm,
  0.6 - 1.4 times a second, with a little up and down. The wind's drift is added on top.
- Every speed is rounded so that it's whole cycles, or whole boxes, over the snow clock's 2000 s, and the drift wraps
  at 9600 m (600 near boxes, 200 far ones). No flake moves at either wrap (offline).
- Fades:
  - out between 0.30 and 0.47 of the box from the camera (a sphere, no cube corners);
  - the far box's flakes in from 4 - 6.4 m;
  - none nearer than 0.8 m, faded in to 2 m.
- Size: 6 - 14 mm across x Flake size, the far box's x 1.5. Under 0.7 px a flake is drawn at 0.7 px and made fainter
  by the area lost (8 m: x 0.36 at 1920 px wide; 16 m: x 0.09).
- Motion blur: the flake's place on the frame before, from the camera then (its view-projection and place, kept by
  WetLook.cpp; known when drawn within 0.2 s and moved less than 10 m). It's stretched along half that motion
  (at most 40 px), with its strength spread over the length (radius / (radius + length)).
- Hidden behind what the game drew (soft over 0.3 m, by view depth). With Keep snow out of buildings, not where
  KnownOpenAt (the squares and the interiors) is under 0.5. Faded by FogAt.
- Light: as before (the frame's average luminance x 1.3 + 0.2 x what's round it + 0.03, cool white).
- Visible at full amount, by the densities: about 800 near flakes and 500 far ones on screen. Counted with
  the 90 x 59 degree view, not measured.
- Shaders: vertex about 507 instruction slots, pixel 36. The full-screen pass went from 6315 (with the sheets) to 4696
  (the interiors in it). 204000 vertices a frame; the cost wasn't measured.

**Snow "puddles" (checked in the code):**
- While snow is chosen, WetLook.cpp's wet is false, so g_Rain.z is 0. The wet branch of PsMain (darkening, puddles,
  ripples, TraceReflection) doesn't run, and InPuddle sees g_DrawnWet.Rain.z 0.
- The snow on the ground is a blend toward its lit white, with no reflection. So no reflection faults can come from
  it.
- The snow on the ground now also stays out of the game's interiors.

**Sources:**
- Locatelli & Hobbs 1974, Fall speeds and masses of solid precipitation particles, via
  https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/25/16729/2025/
- Nemes et al. 2017: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-fluid-mechanics/article/abs/snowflakes-in-the-atmospheric-surface-layer-observation-of-particleturbulence-dynamics/FB25E913F649B01A487E527D7B4FE867
- LaValle, Vection reduction strategies: https://lavalle.pl/vr/node319.html
- Rasmussen et al. 1999, The estimation of snowfall rate using visibility:
  https://impacts.ucar.edu/en/publications/the-estimation-of-snowfall-rate-using-visibility/ (heavy snow ≤ 1/4
  mile; not used yet)

**[not verified in game]** all of this section.

### 7. Freezing water and waterfalls while it snows: is it possible? (research only, 2026-10-26, offline)
**The city's water (game data):** three kinds.
1. **Waterfalls and fountains are particle effects** (fx/ambient/water: 30 effects, 57 emitters). They're placed in
   the city's prop zones:
   - fx_waterfall in zone 1;
   - fx_waterfall_base_small in zones 61, 444, 448, 655, 659;
   - fx_waterfall_base_tiny in 118, 431, 446, 448;
   - fx_water_fountain_01 in 134, 444, 584, 704;
   - fx_pf_water_fountain_setup_01 in 447, 692, 704, 757;
   - inside the waterfeature_01 / 02 prefabs (zones 61, 417, 419, 446 - 448, 655, 658, 659).
   The water is sprites:
   - em_waterfall_water: EmittableType 100, ss_fx_distortion_color_atlas, waterfoam_01, 4.5 a second, 12 s life,
     10 s pre-roll;
   - em_waterfall_small_water: 15 a second, 1.3 s;
   - the splashes: 70 a second, 0.4 s;
   - the fountains' streams: watersplash_2x4, 35 a second, 2 s.
   None scrolls its texture (ModifierU / V 0). Each effect also has smoke or spray emitters. Cull distances 40 -
   350 m.
2. **Water surfaces are static models with water shaders:**
   - objects/props/waterplane_01 (ss_waterplane_01 and its interior / parallax / The View variants): in 36 prop zones
     and ground zone 11, as StaticModelGroup members (zone 134 has 4 of them), with no collision
     (PhysicsPartCountPerInstance 0);
   - the streams objects/props/waterstream_* (ss_waterstream_01): zones 394, 397, 401, 486, 708, 738;
   - ss_poolwater_01 and ss_anc_runningwaterwall_01.
3. **Puddle decals** (objects/decals/waterpuddle). The tools' own puddles are already off while it snows (section 6).

**How the waterfalls could freeze (verified in code):**
- EmitterTemplateData has TimeScale at + 0x44, from the game's type info (the same table gives DebugName + 0x158 and
  ExclusionVolumeCullEnable + 0x165, both verified earlier). It's 1 in every water emitter.
- The game multiplies each emitter's time step by it every update:
  - 0x1430F1930: rdi = [[emitter + 0x280] + 8], the template; `mulss xmm1, [rdi + 0x44]`; then x a per-quality
    global ([rax + quality x 4 + 0x14788]); then added to the emitter's clock as a double.
  - The particle update scales by it too (0x1430E2AC5, `mulss xmm1, [r11 + 0x44]` with r11 the template, next to
    its + 0x16B LocalSpace), as do 0x1430F0D8E and 0x1430F65BF.
- So TimeScale 0 stops an emitter: its particles stay where they are, stop aging, and no new ones spawn. A waterfall
  stops as a still sheet of foam: a frozen waterfall. A fountain stops as frozen spray.
- The tools already find placed effects by their emitters' DebugName in the effect manager's list (the rain,
  Research_Weather section 8): Em_Waterfall_Water, Em_Waterfall_Small_Water, Em_Waterfall_Base_*_Splash / _Smoke,
  Em_Water_Fountain_*.
- Writing the template's float is the DLL writing game data, as it does elsewhere. 1 goes back when the snow goes.
- **[not verified]**:
  - that [emitter + 0x280] + 8 is the same EmitterTemplateData the effect instance chain reaches (instance -> data
    \+ 0x60 -> EmitterEntityData + 0xA0 -> document + 0x28);
  - whether pre-roll is scaled too. A waterfall that streams in while frozen may start empty;
  - how frozen distortion sprites look;
  - the smoke and spray emitters would freeze as still puffs: they could be left out (hidden) instead.
- The waterfalls' and fountains' sounds keep playing. Muting them isn't researched.

**How the water surfaces could freeze:**
- No water-only switch was found. The water shaders animate on the frame's global time (viewConstants `time`, read
  by 9924 city shaders) times their material parameters.
- ss_waterstream_01 has `Speed` (2 on waterstream_straight_500_128, 5 on _800_128). The others are named generically:
  external_Speed in 99 city shaders, ScrollA / ScrollB, TimeScale (25), Scroll (9).
- The visual environment's shader-parameter list does reach shaders as `external_<name>` (ToD_EmissiveMultiplier,
  skyVis_addValue sit in the same externalConstants buffer). But "Speed" would hit 99 shaders, and whether an
  environment's value overrides a material's own wasn't traced (the list's reader wasn't found, section 15 of
  Research_Weather). Not usable.
- **An ice overlay drawn by the tools is possible.** The water planes' and streams' placements are readable offline
  (the zones' StaticModelGroup members: MemberType waterplane_01, InstanceCount, transforms). Their sizes would come
  from the meshes' MeshSet resources (not in the EBX; not read yet).
  - Passed to the pass like the interiors, pixels on those surfaces could be drawn as ice: frosted, pale, still
    (the frame blurred under it). The water's own motion would still show faintly under it unless the ice is opaque.
- Faith's steps: the water-footstep hook (Research_Weather section 21) could give frozen water a solid material
  (no splash or water sound on ice).

**Verdict:** waterfalls and fountains: yes, by holding their emitters' time (a modest change on the rain's effect
code; the live checks above first). Pools and streams: only by an ice overlay over their known places (a bigger
job: placements plus mesh sizes); not by stopping their shaders.

### 8. Waterfalls and fountains frozen while it snows (2026-10-26)
Goal: freeze the waterfalls and fountains while it snows (TimeScale 0 on their emitters, back to 1 when the snow
goes).

**Checked offline before writing it:**
- ScalableEmitterDocument's four templates: Low + 0x18, Medium + 0x20, High + 0x28, Ultra + 0x30 (type info). The
  rain code already reads + 0x28 for its names.
- EmitterEntityData.Emitter is + 0xA0.
- A live emitter's template holder [emitter + 0x280] is set from an argument when the emitter is set up
  (0x1430DAFBC). Every field the update reads through [holder + 8] fits EmitterTemplateData's layout: + 0x44, + 0x124
  / + 0x128, + 0x161 / + 0x162, + 0x16B. **[not verified]** that it's the same object the document points to, so all
  four quality templates are frozen.
- Code bytes checked before anything is written (IsTimeScaleCode):
  - 0x1430F1938 `mov rax, [rcx + 0x280]`;
  - 0x1430F1958 `mov rdi, [rax + 8]`;
  - 0x1430F1973 `mulss xmm1, [rdi + 0x44]`;
  - 0x1430E2AC5 `mulss xmm1, [r11 + 0x44]`.

**What it does (Weather.cpp UpdateFrozenWater, game thread, every update; the effect list scanned once a second):**
- While snow falls and the box is ticked:
  - every effect instance in the effect manager's list is read;
  - each of its components' emitter document gives four templates;
  - templates whose DebugName starts with Em_Waterfall or Em_Water_Fountain, without "OnScreen" in it, count;
  - the effect's place must be outside the game's interiors (InsideInterior: the Kingdom's waterfalls stay).
- A template is set to TimeScale 0 once every running (not culled) effect using it has run for 6 s.
  - An effect is "started" when first seen, and again when its + 0x1B8 bit 0x10 (culled) clears.
  - While one using it hasn't run 6 s, the template gets its own value back, so a newly loaded waterfall gets water
    first.
- The game's value is read before writing. It goes back when the snow stops, the box is unticked, the tools shut
  down, or the code check fails, and only where it's still 0 and the template still has the same DebugName.
- A template whose name no longer matches (its zone unloaded) is forgotten without a write.
- Limits: 256 effects, 256 templates.
- Menu: "N waterfalls and fountains near, M of their emitters frozen". Log: "Snow: waterfalls and fountains frozen
  (...)" and "... flowing again (...)".

**[not verified]:**
- that they freeze, and how frozen foam and distortion sprites look;
- whether pre-roll gives a newly started one its water in the 6 s;
- the fountains' frozen spray.
Their sounds keep playing.

### 9. Intensity, the blizzard, the freeze's fix, snow on the ground with depth (2026-10-26)
Goal: a snow intensity slider (the snow was too light), a working Blizzard tick, waterfalls that really freeze with an
icy look like real frozen water, and snow on the ground with depth instead of a bland look.

**Intensity (Weather.cpp SnowIntensityNow, GetSnow; WetLook.cpp):**
- *Snow intensity* 0.1 - 3 (1.5 by default) replaces *Snow amount*. The flakes' share drawn is intensity / 3 of the
  budget, times how far the snow has come on (the forecast's ramp).
- The budget went from 24,000 near + 10,000 far to 60,000 near (16 m box) + 24,000 far (48 m box). The old share was
  capped at 0.95.
- The snowy look's fog: seen through no farther than 1500 m / intensity. The NWS calls snow heavy at a quarter mile
  (about 400 m) or less, moderate up to half a mile, light past that. 1500 / 3 = 500 m, so at intensity 3 the fog
  alone stops short of "heavy" by day; the hour's own value can be lower (250 m at night), and the flakes cut the view
  further. **[not measured in game]**

**The blizzard (why the tick did nothing):** the old density was min(amount x 1.5, 0.95), so from amount 0.63 up the
tick added no flakes. Its fog thickening was inside the snowy look, which wasn't on unless that box (or Random snow's
look) was ticked. Now: intensity x 1.8 (capped at 3), the wind x 3 (as before), SnowLookWanted() true with Blizzard
on, and the fog seen through 250 m at most.

**Flake streaks:** the flake's position a frame earlier is now rel - (wind.x, -fall, wind.z) x frame time, projected
with the previous frame's view-projection (g_SnowWind: xy the wind in m/s, z the frame time). Before, only the camera's
motion smeared them.

**The freeze's fix (UpdateFrozenWater):**
- The first rule restarted an effect's 6 s "fill" whenever its culled bit cleared, and a restarting effect thawed its
  whole kind. Effects cull at their EffectEntityData CullDistance (+ 0x78 + quality x 4), so walking about kept
  culling and restarting them and the kinds kept thawing: few ever froze.
- Now, for every water effect's data, the four cull distances are read and raised to 3000 m while frozen (the game's
  values written back on thaw, only where 3000 is still there and an effect still uses that data).
- A template freezes once every running effect using it has run 6 s, or 20 s after it was first seen at most.
  Culled effects don't count. Only an effect not seen before (New) thaws its kind until it has run 6 s.
- **[unknown]** whether a raised cull distance takes effect on an instance already created, or only on new ones
  (the instance may copy it). Not checked in game.

**Not frozen by this: the waterfalls on the walls**, the `waterstream` ribbons on facades. They're static models
(MeshSets `waterstream`, `ss_waterstream_01`) whose water is scrolled by their shaders' external_* constants. Section 7:
those can't be safely overridden from here. An ice look drawn over their places by the tools (their placements from
the zones' StaticModelGroups, their shapes from the MeshSets) is the next step.

**Snow on the ground with depth (WetLook.hlsl SnowHeight, SnowGround):**
- Height: three octaves of value noise at 2.2 m, 0.75 m and 0.21 m, weighted 0.55 / 0.3 / 0.15.
- Parallax: the height is looked up displaced along the view by h x 0.06 / max(view.y, 0.25).
- Relief normal: the height's central difference over 4 cm, scaled as if the whole range were 0.25 m tall, added to
  the ground's own normal.
- Shading under an overcast sky (no sun in the snowy look): 0.72 at the steepest to 1.04 facing up (on facing
  squared); hollows to x 0.9; the shade tinted towards (0.80, 0.88, 1.0); a patch's edge darkened to x 0.78.
- Glints: one 3 cm cell in 12 holds a facet tilted at random; it glints as (facet . halfway)^80, where halfway is
  between the view and straight up (the sky's light). It's a dot 4 mm across, or one pixel when farther.
- Detail fades by the pixel's footprint on the ground: the relief gone at 8 cm a pixel, the glints at 3 cm. That keeps
  far snow from shimmering.
- **[not verified]:** how strong the relief reads at the 0.25 m scale, and whether the glints flicker as the
  camera moves (they're fixed to the world, but a pixel-sized dot can alias).

### 10. Snow footsteps (2026-10-26)
Goal: a snow walking sound for Faith's steps in the snow on the ground.

**The game's data (offline, from the CAS files: tools\dumpebx.py, waveids.py, gridsound.py):**
- No snow footstep sounds anywhere (the index has none; section 1).
- me_sound/character/faith/footsteps/faith_footplant: 20 WaveSwitcherNodeData, most with 62 waves indexed by the sound
  id. Index 5 is the gravel in the steps', landings', slides' and stops' ones: me_footsteps_gravel_walk (walk), _run,
  _sprint, _land_heavy (landings), _slide_into / _slide_loop, _sprint_release_faith (stops and turns). The wall runs'
  have concrete at 5; three short switchers (7 and 2 waves) aren't indexed by it.
- The city's grid (levels/sp/sp_maincity/sp_maincity/materialgrid_win32): MaterialPropertySoundData.MaterialSoundId
  5.0 on grid 8 (MaterialIndexMap 10) and grid 54 (map 75). Both play FX/Movement/FX_Foot_Gravel against the steps'
  foot material (grid 24). That effect is two emitters: pebbles and smoke.
- Other soft-sounding ids seen: 34 garbage bags, 40 / 41 a mattress. Gravel is the only crunch.

**How it works:**
- Util/Hooks.cpp WetStep: for Faith's own steps and landings within 3 m of her, on the sound handler's call only (no
  axes given), when wetlook::InSnow is true: byte 2 of the surface's MaterialDecl becomes 10 (an unset one becomes
  0x0A0A8000). Before the first swap per material manager, 0x143282B80 must say 10's MaterialSoundId is 5.0. If not,
  the log warns and nothing is swapped.
- The effect handler's call keeps the real surface, so FX_Foot_Gravel's pebbles and smoke never play on snow.
- wetlook::InSnow follows PsMain's snow block and SnowGround with the last drawn frame's camera and fog, each soft
  step at its middle:
  - snow chosen, Cover > 0.001, the pass drawn last frame;
  - flat = smoothstep(0.35, 0.8, |normal y|) >= 0.5;
  - open = min(outside, saturate((KnownOpenAt - 0.25) x 2)) >= 0.5. Past the squares it's not open here (the shader
    counts it as open there), so no snow steps when the camera is over ~50 m from her, rather than snow steps indoors;
  - settled = flat x open x distance fade x fog > 0.002;
  - the patch (the two noise octaves, without the parallax) >= 0.5.
- Not followed: the shader's 4-pixel flatness (needs the frame's depth), and KeptDry (Faith's box starts 0.12 m over
  her feet, so a step's contact is outside it).
- Log: "Snow: the level's material 10 is the gravel (sound id 5): Faith's steps in the snow crunch", then "Snow:
  Faith's step at x y z is in the snow ..." every 5 s at most while it happens.
- **[not verified]** all of it, including whether the slide loop keeps the last step's sound id. The
  footplant's MathEntity iff(ANT int == 3, 26, input) (Research_Weather section 21) still overrides it whenever
  that state is 3.

Goal: icier ice on every water surface, a stronger snow slider, snow that piles up, footprints in the snow like the
wet ones, a tick for the snow step sound, and a wind sound outside, muffled indoors and stronger in a blizzard.

**Why it wasn't icy (seen in game):** the ice ran. The game's water (material 16) under one of Faith's steps, at
562.21 59.68 89.31, is inside the zone 431 pool rectangle (u 0.12, v 0.71), 9 cm under its plane at 59.77. So the
ice was drawn there, but:
- the pool look let the frame show through (`behind` x a blue tint) over about half its area;
- its whites were the frame's light, dim at night;
- the snow block then laid snow over it, since the depth was the floor under the shallow water.
Fixed: the ice is opaque (0.97 - 0.98), mostly frosted, and the snow lies x 0.3 on pool ice (IceAt's onPool).

**Every water mesh (tools\importers.py, meshwater.py, waterparts.py, icewater.py, icetable2.py):**
- The water shaders, the importers of: ss_waterplane_01 (+ _interior / _parallax / _theview), ss_waterstream_01,
  ss_poolwater_01, ss_backdropwater_01, ss_water_calm, ss_anc_runningwaterwall_01, ss_waterfeature_01,
  ss_vw_watersplash_01 / _watersplashwall_01, ss_omnistatcomplex01_water, ss_waterleak01.
- Many are sections of bigger meshes: ground_anchor_02 / 04_a / 04_detail03 / 05 / 08, ground_bdstatue_05 / 06,
  ground_station_01, ground_marina_01, ground_water_01 (the far sea), anansitower_plaza, anc_area02_plaza01, the
  waterfeature_01 / 02 meshes, the train station's exterior water.
- MeshSet LOD0: LOD at [0x20], section count at LOD + 8, sections at [LOD + 0xC], 0x130 apart. A section has + 0x10
  its material name (e.g. "m_water_01", "M_Water", "m_Water1"), + 0x20 primitives, + 0x24 first index, + 0x28 vertex
  offset, + 0x2C vertex count, + 0x4C elements, + 0x8C stride. The LOD has + 0x58 index bytes, + 0x5C vertex
  bytes, + 0x64 the chunk id.
- The chunk: found in the superbundles' chunk lists (fb\chunkfind.py and dbobj.py; all 15 found). It holds the
  vertices, then 16-bit indices relative to the section's first vertex (checked: ground_bdstatue_06's indices 0 - 40
  for 41 vertices).
- Each water section's triangles are joined into pieces (shared vertices, or vertices at the same place) and
  fitted along their own long axes. A piece is split along its length while a rectangle would be under 60 % water
  (4 times at most, single triangles kept). Flat under 12 cm: a pool or a stream strip. Else a box, except a near
  flat sheet under 1 m thick (the far sea's waves), which becomes a pool with that tolerance.
- Placed: StaticModelGroup members by MeshAsset, objects in layers by Blueprint (its mesh is <name>_mesh), in 72
  zone files. 471 pieces: 345 pools, 85 stream strips, 33 boxes, 8 walls. Left out: waterplane_01's interior
  (437213773) and Kingdom (1961834087) variations, interior meshes (Kruger's office, the Kingdom: not in the city's
  zones), the puddle decals.
- **[not verified]**: the large pieces from single triangles (fill about 0.5) may cover a little ground next
  to the water where that ground is level with the water. Where the ground is higher or a wall, it hides them.
- GetIce: the nearest 48 by true distance to the piece; MostIcePlanes 48 (g_IcePlane[192]).

**Heavier snow:** SnowIntensity is 0.1 - 5 (MostSnowIntensity). Density is intensity / 5 of 150,000 near + 60,000
far. Flake size is x (1 + 0.5 x saturate((i - 2) / 3)). The fog is 1500 / i (300 m at 5).

**Piling:** g_SnowPile (0 - 1) grows once the cover is 1, at step / (3 x settle) x min(1, intensity ramp) x i / 1.5,
and melts at step / (3 x settle) when it doesn't snow. SnowFall.Pile = pile x SnowPileDepth x SnowCover. Shader
(g_SnowPile.x):
- flat's smooth goes to 1 by 8 cm;
- the patches go from 2 - 8 cm;
- relief is 0.25 + 1.5 x depth;
- SnowPileSide: for non-top pixels within reach, 4 samples down the frame up to the depth's height in pixels
  (1.5 - 64). A sample is a top when its 2 px neighbours make a normal with |y| >= 0.8, it's open (ShelterAt /
  KnownOpenAt) and it's not KeptDry. The ray's point at the top's distance is over the top by -2 cm .. depth x
  lump (0.75 - 1.25) and within depth + 0.4 m sideways. It's drawn as side-lit snow.
**[not verified]**: its cost (up to 4 x 3 depth taps a pixel); seeing a ledge from below shows no lip
(its top isn't on the frame).

**Footprints:** wetlook::InSnow records a print when true, one per step:
- the same StepSameMs (250 ms) / StepSameMetres (0.25 m) as the wet steps;
- the direction comes from the last snow step, 0.2 - 3 m away within 2 s.
64 kept. They fill at seconds x Amount x Intensity / 300 on the play clock (g_PlayMs), and are gone when no snow
lies. The shader's SnowPrintsAt draws a 30 x 12 cm sole: the floor is where the sole shape, moved back along the
view by the print's depth (3 cm + 0.6 x pile, up to 20 cm), is under the ray, else the far wall. The floor is x
(0.80, 0.86, 0.95), the wall x (0.60, 0.68, 0.82).

**Footstep tick:** Settings::SnowStepSound and weather::SnowStepSound(). Hooks.cpp swaps to the gravel only when it's
ticked; InSnow (the prints) runs either way.

**Wind:** weather::Update, under the weather's lock (the camera known):
- strength = min(1, 0.15 + 0.45 x i/5 + speed/30 + 0.3 in a blizzard);
- volume = 0.12 x ramp x (0.35 + 0.45 x i/5 + 0.25 x min(speed/8, 1.5)) x (1.6 in a blizzard) x WindVolume;
- inside = max(roof squares' g_Inside, a named interior at the camera);
- speed is the snow's wind now (its gusts at 11.3 s and 4.7 s periods, x 3 in a blizzard).
thunder::SetWind(volume, strength, inside) drives a WindVoice in Thunder.cpp: a 24 s stereo loop, the volume
following over 0.8 s, a low pass of 700 - 6000 Hz by strength, and inside down to 260 Hz and x 0.35.
**One wind voice:** a second WindSynth.h loop (brown-noise body, pink hiss, a wandering whistle), with SetWind(float
level) in Thunder.h, was made for a wind with the rain and replaced this one for a while. The snow's WindSynth.h is
the one kept, and its one wind voice, thunder::SetWind(volume, strength, inside), is driven for the rain too (the
rain's branch in the same block of weather::Update).
**[not verified in game]** all of section 12.

### 13. Turbulence, exact water triangles, slide trails, jump prints, depth by place (2026-10-26)
**Flakes:** SnowVsMain, per flake:
- a slow eddy: amplitude (0.4 - 1.2 m) x turbulence, at 0.04 - 0.10 Hz;
- a quick eddy: (0.1 - 0.35 m) x turbulence, at 0.2 - 0.45 Hz;
- each eddy an ellipse (squashed 0.3 - 1) turned to a random way, the slow one tipped up and down 0.2 - 0.5 of its
  size;
- the flutter as before;
- all frequencies whole cycles over the clock (WholeOverPeriod);
- the streak velocity = wind + fall + the eddies' derivative.
Turbulence (g_SnowWind.w, SnowFall.Turbulence) = min(3, 0.6 + 0.4 x mean wind (m/s, x 3 in a blizzard) + 0.5 in a
blizzard), followed over 4 s. Gusts: angle += 0.45 sin(2 pi t / 9) + 0.25 sin(2 pi t / 3.7 + 1.3) (up to 0.7 rad);
speed x (1 + 0.35 sin(2 pi t / 8) + 0.2 sin(2 pi t / 3.3 + 1.3)). SnowWind's default is 0.5 m/s.

**Ice triangles:** waterparts.py writes every water section's triangles (waterparts.tsv.tris), and the Anchor's
triangular pool's section "lambert2" too (its chunk f60bc7b70e13...). icewater.py places them: 1,078 triangles,
tolerance 0.3 m on the far sea. The rest stay planes: waterplane_01, vw_watersplash, the streams and walls, and the
fountain features' boxes (272). IceTable.h has IcePlanes and IceTriangles. weather::GetIceTriangles takes the nearest
96 by true point-to-triangle distance (Ericson 5.1.5), with the named interiors left out by each triangle's middle.
The shader's g_IceTri[384] (at 29200) holds the corner, the duals of the sides (u = p.g1, v = p.g2), and the normal.
A hit uses the pool look on world metres.

**Pool look:** the clear patches are smoothstep(0.34, 0.2, 0.7 Noise(p / 7) + 0.3 Noise(p / 2.5)). The frost is
brightness x (0.95 + 0.1 frost), its metre-scale octaves faded by the footprint.

**Slide trail:** NoteSlide (the FX/Movement/FX_Slide* effect near Faith) calls NoteSnowSlide.
That marks the slide when the snow lies there (SnowLiesAt, InSnow's test without the print) and extends the trail.
Each frame, while a slide was seen within 0.7 s and the snow lies at her feet (dry::FaithFeet), the trail extends
to her feet. It's stretches every 0.35 m (48 kept), 0.22 m each side. The shader's SnowTrailAt draws the floor and
wall with the prints' parallax, and the berm brighter (x 1.06). It fills as the prints do. (g_SnowTrailCount /
g_SnowTrail / g_SnowTrailEnd at 35344 / 35360 / 36128; the end is 36896.)
**[not known]** how often FX_Slide plays during a slide; the per-frame feet extension covers the gaps up to 0.7 s.

**Jumps:** Characters/FaithCharacter's impacts, named by FNV-1 of their names (checked: FootPlantLeft = -313593505):
- steps (FootPlantLeft / Right);
- landings FootPlantLandSoft (+ the effect's FootPlantLandingSoft) and FootPlantLandHard, the right foot only;
- Slide (right foot, the effect only);
- SkillrollForward;
- FootPlantWallLeft / Right (material 0x59598000);
- FootClimbScuff / Release Left / Right;
- FootSpringboardLaunchLeft / Right;
- hands (HandLand*, HandClimb*, HandRelease*, HandScuff*, and 3 not named).
There's no take-off. So in Apply each frame her feet's vertical speed is measured:
- rising faster than 2.5 m/s within 0.4 s of a snow step adds that step's other foot, 0.24 m to the side away from
  the step before, x 1.15 deep;
- falling faster than 3 m/s marks a landing, and the next snow step within 0.35 s presses both feet +-0.12 m
  sideways, x 1.4 deep.

**Depth by place:** SnowDepthAt(xz) = pile x (0.45 + 1.1 Noise(xz / 6 + 101)), mirrored in C++ (SnowLiesAt). It's
used by SnowGround's patches and relief, the prints' and trails' depth (depthScale), and SnowPileSide (searched up
to 1.55 x the pile, tested with the top's own depth).

**Ceilings:** SnowPileSide's top must face up with the camera above it (its normal turned towards the camera,
y >= 0.8). It was abs(y).

**After dying [not found]:** after a respawn, with the snow switched off and on and the look given again, the game's
fog was seen to go from (floor 0.84, height fog 57 m, seen 1650 m) to (floor 0.00, 200 m, 5000 m), and the snowy fog
to 2664 m (seen in game). That points at the game's visual environment changing after the respawn. What looks wrong
after dying isn't known.
**[not verified in game]** all of section 13.

### 14. The snow on the ground rebuilt, one slide groove (2026-10-26)
Goal: snow on the ground that looks better (it was mottled blue-grey every few decimetres), and slides back to back
that join smoothly instead of repeating a pattern.
**Causes [code]:**
- SnowHeight was value noise (2.2 / 0.75 / 0.21 m). Its relief was min(0.25 + 1.5 x depth, 1), so up to a metre of
  height over a 4 cm difference, which is very steep. Shade ran 0.72 - 1.04 on facing squared, with a blue tint.
- lit used Luma(color) x 1.8: the pixel itself, so the ground's texture and reflections showed through.
- The prints were x (0.80, 0.86, 0.95) and x (0.60, 0.68, 0.82), with hard edges (x 5).
- SnowTrailAt took the max over stretches of each one's capsule, so each joint's rounded ends showed.
**Now [code]:**
- GradientAt / GNoise: Perlin's 2D with the quintic fade, 0.5 + 0.75 x the value.
- SnowHeight: 0.65 GNoise(p / 5.5) + 0.27 GNoise(rot(p) / 1.9) + 0.08 GNoise(rot2(p) / 0.65).
- height = 0.05 + 0.25 saturate(depthHere / 0.6) m. The slope is taken over 15 cm. Parallax = (h - 0.5) x height.
- shade = 1 + 1.4 (dot(surface, sky) - dot(normal, sky)), with sky (0.29, 0.92, 0.26); x lerp(0.95, 1.02) by height;
  the patch edge x 0.93; a grain of +-2.5 % at 3.5 cm (fading with the footprint, 2 cm).
- lit = min(max(Luma(around) x 1.9, Luma(average) x 0.85), 1). White (0.95, 0.97, 1.0), down to (0.84, 0.90, 1.0)
  in shadow (lit under twice the scene's).
- Prints: the floor x (0.90, 0.93, 0.97), the wall x (0.78, 0.83, 0.90), the rim x 1.04 (SoleShape at 1.25 x minus
  the sole); the edges are softer (x 2.5).
- Trails: the nearest distance over all stretches (and for the floor seen through), with "left" weighted by
  nearness. The floor is rounded (x 1 - 0.5 (d / w)^2). Colours as the prints', berm x 1.05.
**[not verified in game]**

### 15. Edges, noise, the ice pass, hands, body, rolls, fog, blizzards (2026-10-26)
Goal: snow on the ground with no pixelation and no bleed over edges, smoother at its edges and in its noise; no blur
hiding UI elements; no water flicker; model-accurate handprints; indoor waterfalls stopped and frozen water without
alpha faults; fog and snowfall sliders that go further; Faith's body outline in slides and rolls instead of circles;
objects under the snow not greyed; blizzards as foggy as real ones; the rain prints' ShoeSole for the snow prints.

**Bleed / pixels [code]:**
- flat was relaxed by the pile (`max(flat, pile...)`), so deep snow reached the pixels FrameNormal's `smooth` cuts
  (a depth jump). Now `flat = smoothstep(0.35, 0.8, normal.y) * smooth`, always.
- SnowPileSide took any snowed top 1 - 4 steps down the frame, also one far behind a ledge's edge. Now only a top
  whose distance is within -0.6 / +0.3 m of the pixel's own.
- Glints: shown only while the footprint is under 1.2 cm, one 3 cm cell in 16.
- Soft edges: `SnowEdgeAt` = smoothstep(0.35, 0.95, the share of 12 points (6 at 1.5 px, 6 at 3.5 px) within 4 % of
  the pixel's plane). It multiplies `settled` only, so it never adds snow.

**Noise [code]:**
- `around` (the scene copy, level round(g_Frame.z) - 2, about 240 px across: 16 px a texel at 4K) was SampleLevel
  bilinear, so its texels showed. `SceneAround` reads it as a cubic B-spline (4 bilinear reads at the weights' centres).
  The level is rounded, not trilinear any more.
- Patches: `SnowPatchNoise` = 0.7 GNoise(p / 2.2) + 0.3 GNoise(rot(p) / 0.9 + 23), band +-0.16 (was value noise
  1.7 / 0.43 m, +-0.12). WetLook.cpp's SnowLiesAt has a C++ GNoise with the same Hash and the same sum.
- SnowHeight's weights 0.67 / 0.29 / 0.04 (was 0.65 / 0.27 / 0.08). shade x 1.1 (was 1.4). Parallax: view.y clamped
  at 0.5 (was 0.25). Grain: GNoise at 3.5 cm turned 53 degrees, +-2 %, gone by a 1.2 cm footprint (was 2 cm).

**The ice pass [code]:** IceTable.h now has IcePlaneData { Centre, A, B, Tolerance, Type } (239) and
IceTriangleData { A, B, C, Foot, Tolerance } (4,462, the waterfeature falls included, Foot = that placement's lowest
water y). WetLook.cpp's Make() makes an immutable vertex buffer of them (POSITION world xyz + tolerance; TEXCOORD0
local x, y, kind, foot; TEXCOORD1 half sides), drawn after PsMain with g_SnowBlend by IceVsMain / IcePsMain. The pixel
shader tests the scene depth itself, keeps to ShelterAt's open sky, and fades by OverTheGround. weather::GetIce /
GetIceTriangles are gone (weather::IceAmount instead).

**Over the ground:** `OverTheGround(color, around)` = max(smoothstep(0.12, 0.3, Luma(color) - 1.3 Luma(around)),
smoothstep(0.6, 1.2, |chroma(color) - chroma(around)|) x smoothstep(0.04, 0.12, Luma(color))). It scales the snow's,
the side's and the ice's alpha. The HUD's alpha in the frame copy wasn't looked at (an idea: one histogram, logged).

**Hands [data, code]:** Characters/FaithCharacter (steps/faithcharacter.txt):
- PamMovementImpactSoundEntityData's SoundDatas: HandClimbLeft -792823598, HandLand 481714765, HandReleaseLeft
  1884008210, HandScuffLeft -1872667002 (ClosestBone LeftHand 15); HandClimbRight -1011724695, HandLandRight
  -938062431 ... (RightHand 123).
- The effect data has HandLandLeft 86534698 and HandLandRight -938062431 (ComputeVelocityForBone 15 / 123).

  wetlook::NoteHand(contact, normal y, side).
- HandShape: palm 7 x 5 cm + 1.5 cm round; fingers index 7.0, middle 7.8, ring 7.3, little 5.8 cm (1.6 - 1.8 cm wide,

**Body slide:** SnowTrailAt's signed distance, half width |w| (0.19); a trail's newest stretch has w < 0. That stretch's

### 16. Edges at a glancing angle; Faith's real hand (2026-10-26)
**Edges [code]:** Goal: no snow bleeding round edges seen from an angle.
- The depth isn't the cause: the depth target is the frame's size (seen in game).
- FrameNormal takes the nearer neighbour each way (its dx and dy). Seen at a glancing angle, a ledge's front face has
  its pixels far apart in 3D. So for the face's row at the corner, the nearer pixel up is on the top, across the
  corner: that row's normal faces up, its `smooth` stays 1, and it took the top's snow.
- The fix (ice\edit_snow_normal.py): SnowNormal for the snow alone. Each way it takes the side whose
  pixels 1 and 2 off are in line with this one (OffLine: the distance off the line through them; a plane's are exactly
  in line). clean = saturate(2 - that distance / a pixel's width at its distance) multiplies flat. SnowEdgeAt and
  SnowGround take the same normal.
**Her hand [data]:** Goal: hand prints that match Faith's hands.
- **Skeleton:** characters/skeletons/skeleton_faith (SkeletonAsset, 182 bones). LeftHand 15, then each finger's
  bones 0 - 4 (Ring 16 - 20, Pinky 21 - 25, Index 26 - 30, Middle 35 - 39) and Thumb1 - 4 (31 - 34), plus ThumbBase /
  IndexBase / PinkyBase. RightHand 123 is the mirror image (z negated in the hand's frame).
- **Joints in LeftHand's frame** (ModelPose: x along the hand, y the palm's side (the fingers curl that way), z across,
  the thumb at -z; tools hand\handbones.py):
  - knuckle joints (1): index (74.0, -28.7), middle (75.1, -9.6), ring (71.0, 8.8), little (64.6, 24.6) mm (x, z);
  - knuckle to tip joint (the segments summed): index 81.6, middle 91.6, ring 86.0, little 68.4 mm;
  - Thumb1 at (12.6, 15.0, -16.1) mm, its segments 44.2, 28.6, 25.1 mm. Its bind way is out of the palm (y 0.039 of
    0.098); laid flat (its y turned to -z) it's 29.9 degrees from the hand's axis.
- **Mesh:** characters/faith/arms/faith_arms_mesh LOD0, chunk 14b8808cb2bd822be3a48b76923d928b.
  - Sections: SkinUpper (6,280 vertices) and Glove_M (3,459), both stride 60, position float3 at 0. A third, unnamed
    one has stride 28.
  - Its vertices are in the skeleton's model space: the hand's vertices sit round LeftHand (0.472, 1.039, 0.153).
- **The outline (hand\handmesh.py):**
  - the vertices within 3.5 cm of a bone (palm: wrist to each knuckle; fingers; thumb), each taken to its nearest;
  - a finger's straightened along its in-palm way from its knuckle joint, its offset across kept;
  - the mesh's triangles filled on a 1 mm grid (none bridging two fingers); the forearm cut at x -5 mm.
- **Her measures (hand\measure.py)**, widths across each straightened finger:
  - index 17 - 15.5 mm near its base, 14 - 13.5 in the middle, 12.5 near the tip; it ends 83.0 mm from its knuckle joint;
  - middle 17.5 - 16 / 14 - 13 / 13, 91.5 mm;
  - ring 16 - 15 / 13.5 - 12.5 / 12, 86.5 mm;
  - little 15 - 12.5 / 10.5 - 9.5, 67.5 mm;

  - the palm 72 mm across the knuckles; the heel 49 mm across at the wrist joint;
  - the hand 17 cm from the heel to the middle fingertip.
- **The fit (hand\fit.py, verify.py):**

  - four tapered capsules (the shader's TaperedCapsule) from the knuckle joints to the tip rounds: index 8.5 -> 6.25 mm,
    middle 8.75 -> 6.5, ring 8 -> 6, little 7.25 -> 5;
  - the thumb's pad, 12.5 -> 9.5 mm over its first 45 mm;
  - the thumb, 8 -> 5.25 mm from 50 mm to its tip, 1 mm towards the index;

### 17. Far snow, the pile, the haze over interiors, the snowy look's brightness
Goal: far snow that stays when looking straight ahead, a better-looking snow pile, a better snow haze, a snowy city
look that isn't too bright, a better snow shader and no water flicker.

**Far snow [code]:** SnowNormal's clean (section 16) was the off-line distance over a pixel's width at its distance.
Looking straight ahead, the ground's neighbouring pixels are 0.2 - 1 m apart (at 30 m from 1.7 m up the ground is seen
at 3 degrees: 1.3 cm a pixel across, 23 cm along), so a bend of 1 - 2 degrees failed it. Now clean =
1 - smoothstep(0.3, 0.6, the bend's sine), the off-line distance over the step to that side's neighbour.

**The pile [code, research]:**
- What's seen over the foot of a wall or a curb with snow lying there is the snow's own top surface in front of it:
  the ground's snow going on up to the wall.
- It was drawn as a band of its own:
  - lit by the wall pixel's own luminance x 1.8, so the wall's texture showed through;
  - with a pattern of value noise on world.xz / 0.2 + world.y / 0.1, diagonal stripes up the wall;
  - faded over its top quarter, see-through;
  - its edge value noise 0.35 m across, x 0.75 - 1.25.
- And SnowEdgeAt (section 15) faded the ground's snow before every wall: points off its plane either way counted,
  4 %, so a bare strip lay between the ground's snow and the band.
- Now:
  - SnowPileSide gives where the ray meets the snow (snowAt: the ray's point at the top's distance, at the top's
    height) and how far up the layer (wallward). PsMain draws it with SnowGround at snowAt (normal up, flat 1), x
    (1 - 0.08 smoothstep(0.5, 1, wallward)) in the corner, solid, soft over 1.5 px.
  - Its edge against the wall is depth x (0.85 + 0.3 GNoise(xz / 0.9)).
  - SnowEdgeAt counts only points under the plane (dropping away), by 10 % of their distance.
- Sources:
  - shadowed snow is lit by the sky, so it's bluish under a clear sky and grey under an overcast one:
    water.washtenawcd.gov "Why is the snow blue?", discuss.pixls.us "why do winter landscapes look blue";
  - games' accumulation is an up-facing mask with soft edges and a fake thickness: the Unity 2018 Shaders cookbook,
    the V-Ray distance-mask tip, Foldes and Benes 2007;
  - snow sticks and rounds over at edges: the cornice study, egusphere-2024-2458.

**The haze over interiors [code]:**
- The haze took hazeOutside = the point's own outside amount, ShelterWith(world, InteriorHere(world)). InteriorAt's
  sides count from 0.3 - 0.7 m outside each box. So a building with an interior volume had its walls counted as inside
  and got no haze.
- Seen in game: a tall blue tower crisp in a thick haze while nearer buildings were fogged. The Anansi tower's
  ve_benefactor_anansitower_interior_01 is 75 x 491 x 77 m. Which tower that was isn't confirmed.
- Now hazeOutside = max(that, g_HazeView.x). g_HazeView.x = Haze.Outside = 1 - g_LookIndoors, the camera's eased
  outside amount. g_HazeView is at 37984, the size 38000.

**The snowy look's brightness [data, code]:**
- The Snowfall mod's HeightFogColorAdd against the game's own (section 3's table):
  - 0:00: 0.05 0.08 0.31 -> 0.6 0.65 0.7 (luminance 0.08 -> 0.64);
  - 6:00: 0.17 0.08 0.03 -> 0.5 (0.10 -> 0.5);
  - 7:00: 0 -> 0.6;
  - 12:00: 0.66 2.42 5 -> 1 (2.23 -> 1).
- The mod also lowers the night's exposure compensation 1.5 -> 0.5 and raises dawn and dusk MinEV 0.4 -> 1.2. The
  tools don't give those (their state offsets aren't verified), so with the game's exposure its night and dawn fog
  was 5 - 8 x as bright.
- Given at amount a, whatever Snow fog said.
- Now the colour is the mod's hue / its luminance x the game's own luminance at the hour x 1.15, by snowFog (Snow
  fog, eased indoors). The sky light's boost is 1 + 0.3 less sun, as the rainy look's; the 0.5 was for the snow's
  bounce, which the game's lighting doesn't see.

**Not done:**
- The haze's colour is from the frame's average (x 1.9, greyer). It changes as the camera turns (darker towards dark
  things), but the haze's real light is the sky's. A steadier source would be the sky's pixels, or the game's fog
  colour in the frame's units (needs the exposure and tonemap).
- The water flicker: not handled here (the weather's).

**[not verified in game]**

### 18. Bodies pressed in by their own meshes, KrugerSec boots, no crunch on glass or metal (2026-10-27)
Goal: no snow step sound on glass and metal; the snow slide in Faith's exact shape; KrugerSec leaving snow footprints
and, when they die and ragdoll, their outline in the snow; Faith's snow handprints when she jump rolls or lands.

**Glass and metal [data, seen in game]:**
- Her snow steps were given the gravel crunch on sound ids 11, 13 (glass) and 24, 26, 27, 29 (metal).
- The footplant's wave switchers (every one of them): 10 - 19 are the glass waves
  (me_footstep_glasspane*, me_footsteps_glass_*), 20 - 29 the metal ones (me_footstep_metal*, me_footsteps_metal*,
  ductwork, poles, gantries).
- Hooks.cpp's SnowStep now leaves sound ids 10 - 29 as they are. The print in the snow there stays.

**Her hands when she lands [seen in game]:** every pair of FX/Movement/FX_Hand_* effects came
with an FX_FootLandHard_* effect about 0.3 m away: a hard landing puts both hands down, through HandLandLeft /
HandLandRight (86534698 / -938062431, in HandImpactIds). Whether those reach NoteHand isn't known: its log
line shared the steps' 30 s limit, so it was hidden behind the landing's own line. It has its own now. The game has
no hand impact for a roll (section 15), so a roll's hands come from her body (below).

**Her body, and theirs [data, code]:**
- The meshes (read offline):
  - A MeshSet LOD section record (0x130 bytes): + 0x40 bones per vertex (u8), + 0x41 bone count (u8), + 0x44 the bone
    list's offset (u16 skeleton bones).
  - The vertex elements are Frostbite's usages: Pos 1, BlendIndices 2 / 3, BlendWeights 4 / 5 (UByte4 / UByte4N).
  - Each LOD's last section is the whole mesh merged, positions and skin only.
  - Every vertex's weights sum to 255; its heaviest bone is 1 - 11 cm from it (median) in the bind pose.
  - Faith: faith_lowerbody_mesh and faith_upperbody_mesh LOD1, faith_arms_mesh LOD2: 5,299 vertices, 10,057
    triangles, 1.50 m to her neck.
  - An Enforcer: enforcer_fullbody_mesh LOD2: 5,951 vertices, 10,759 triangles, 1.93 m.
  - SnowBodyMesh.h keeps their vertices in mm with 4 bones each, and which part each is (feet, legs, the rest).
- The pose (FaithReplay.cpp's findings, read only):
  - A body (soldier / character + 0x248) has its pose manager at [[+ 0x158] + 0x1B8]. Its page holds the world pose
    (+ 0x08) and the 3x4 skinning matrices (+ 0x10, when manager + 0x2B9 is set: the world pose times the inverse bind
    pose).
  - Checked at run time, once per kind: each bone's bind place through its matrix must land within 1 cm of its world
    place for 90 % of its bones, rows or columns. Else that kind presses nothing, and the log says so.
- Skinned each frame only when a gate bone (hips, hands, knees, head, chest, forearms) is within the snow's depth +
  35 cm of the ground.
- Each triangle down in the snow is pressed into a stamp: 128 x 256 texels, 2 cm each, 16 slices, R8, in a
  Texture2DArray at t4. A texel's value is how far down the body went there: (ground + depth + 3 cm - height) / (depth
  \+ 3 cm), only from 15 cm under the ground up. The most so far is kept.
- Faith:
  - Her ground is her transform's height, with the ground's rise along her motion.
  - Her legs and shoes press only while her hips are within 0.55 m of the ground (her steps have their own prints,
    and her ankles go into deep snow at every step).
  - A stamp runs the way she moves, her hips 1.2 m along it; when off it, a new one.
- KrugerSec:
  - Every PamClientCharacterEntity within 40 m whose pose has 163 bones (Skeleton_Enemy), 12 at most, found every
    0.5 s.
  - They press while they lie (hips within 0.35 m of their lower foot), with the Enforcer's mesh, on their last
    step's ground, else their body's lowest point.
- The pass (SnowStampsAt) draws a stamp like a print: the floor through the parallax, the inner wall, a rim within
  6 cm. It fills as the prints do.
- Her slide's trail and her roll's print give way to her body's stamp where it pressed within 0.3 s, and stay as
  they were where it didn't.

**Their boots [data, code]:**
- An Enforcer's sole (LOD0 triangles within 1.5 cm of the foot's lowest point, 2 mm grid): 28.4 cm long, a
  heel block 7.2 cm across, a shank 4.2 cm, the ball 9.4 cm, 1.7 cm outward. Faith's by the same measure is 24.6 x 8.8 cm
  (the rain's ShoeSole is 27 x 10).
- BootSole has that shape. Its tread isn't in the mesh, so it has none.
- OtherSnowStep (from Hooks.cpp's other feet, the sound's call) presses one per step, the last 48 kept
  (g_OtherSnowPrint). The toe's way comes from their foot bone to their toe base now, else from their step before.

**A pose not where it's drawn:** a gun's pose slot was found 1.2 km from where the game drew it
(CHANGELOG). The check above only shows that the matrices agree with the world pose. So a frame is also

place (a ragdoll thrown by a kick is left a few metres behind it).

g_OtherSnowPrintDir[48] 42704. The size is 43472 (fxc's listing matches the static_asserts).

### 19. Smoothed body outlines, stamps only when pressed, her slide's wake in her shape (2026-10-27)
Goal: smoothed body outlines in the snow; Faith's outline, smoothed, for water slides too; the 'shadow' square in the
snow that goes away when the camera comes close; the snow's flicker found and fixed.

**SnowBodies.cpp [code]:**
- Each slice keeps its mask as pressed and a smoothed copy that's sent: a Gaussian with sigma 1.5 texels (3 cm),
  separable, 4 texels each side, over the changed rows and 4 round them.
- A triangle counts only when its corners reach into the band over the ground under each of them, with the stamp's
  rise. PressTriangle tells whether any texel went in. A stamp taken that nothing went into goes back.
- The gate: her knees only while her hips are low.
- A KrugerSec lying again takes back the stamp they pressed last (LastOwner), so the same body isn't stamped twice.
- Modes: snow, or the wet look's water (her body only, hips low, layer 3 cm), or none. Take frees a stamp of another
  mode. In the water a stamp lasts WaterStampSeconds (7 s, past SlideTrailSeconds).

**SlideWake [code]:** WaterStampAt gives her stamps' value where one is (g_SnowStampCount.z 2). There, pushed is
saturate(stamp x 1.5) x the path's age fade instead of the 30 cm band. The waves and the churn stay the path's.

**The shadow square [code, not confirmed]:**
- ShelterInSquare's under = saturate(square.y - 2 - y). square.y is the first surface UpdateRoofs' down sweep finds
  from the camera's height, at the square's middle only.
- A square whose middle is on a ledge, a roof edge or an awning, seen from above, has its street half counted as under
  (no snow, bare ground).
- A closer re-sweep (3 m of height, or 2 s within 10 squares, 5 s farther) can find the street.
- The same could flip squares back and forth: a flicker.

**The flicker [not found]:**
- The camera at the depth's frame is never off (the diagnostic, seen in game: 0 of ~1000 frames).
- The sky light never falls back once seen (NoteHazeSky smooths and keeps it).
- Candidates: the squares (above); stamps given up by the bug above (fixed).

### 20. Snow in shadows, by edges, on concrete and gravel (2026-10-27)
Goal: no grey snow by edges and when not looked at directly, no trouble in shadows, and a right look on concrete and
gravel.

**Causes [code]:**
- OverTheGround's bright was smoothstep(0.12, 0.3, Luma(c) - 1.3 Luma(around 16 px)). The sunlit side of a shadow's
  edge is up to 2 / (1 + s) times its 16 px surroundings, s being the shadow's light over the sun's. At L 0.9 and s
  0.1 that's 0.26 over, so bright was 0.82 and the snow kept 18 %: a grey strip along every shadow and every lit edge
  with something darker beyond. On gravel and concrete, a bright stone or stain did the same.
- SnowLit took 0.75 - 1 by shaded = smoothstep(0.4, 1, around / SceneAround(uv, 0)), about 128 px of everything.
  - A shadow wider than that came out lit inside, with a dark, bluer band along its edge.
  - By an edge, or towards the horizon, the 128 px took in the sky or the bright distance, so the snow went grey.
  - Looking straight down at the snow, none of that is in it.
- The sunlight term (ground x 1.9) was the ground 6 px round, so in sun concrete's stains and seams and gravel's light
  and dark stones showed in the snow. Deep snow's light was SceneAround(uv, 1), 32 px of everything (walls, sky past
  an edge).

**Now [code]:**
- OverTheGround's bright also needs smoothstep(1.8, 2.4, Luma(c) / Luma(around)). A shadow's edge is 1.3 - 1.6 there
  (under 1.9 unless the shadow is nearly black); a glow, a spark or the HUD's text is over 2.
  - Lost: white HUD text over ground brighter than about 0.45 (it's then under 2 x its 16 px surroundings). The old
    test missed it over ground above about 0.6 anyway.
- SnowLit, once the sky is known: max(sky x 0.9, ground x 1.9). It is cool white (0.89, 0.93, 1) up to white (0.95,
  0.97, 1) by smoothstep(1, 1.3, ground x 1.9 / sky x 0.9). No neighbourhood comparison; until the sky is seen it is as
  before.
- SnowLightAround (the light given to SnowGround in PsMain and for the pile): SnowAroundAt's 6 px (x 2) plus 8 points
  20 px round (PixelScale) on the scene copy's level 2. Each counts as far as it's within 5 cm + 2 % of the distance
  \+ half the snow's depth of the plane; not the sky. A shadow on the snow is about 20 px soft (it was 6).
- Cost: +8 depth reads and +4 samples per snow pixel (the pass was 5 - 6.5 ms in the rain at 4K, seen in game).

**Not done / not known:**
- Gravel's own shape (thin snow on its stones' facets, per pixel) is unchanged. Whether what's left on gravel is
  that isn't known.
- The fog fades the snow's cover (FogAt x settled) rather than fogging its colour. At middle distances that lets
  T (1 - T)(ground - fog) of the ground through: greyer than right where the ground is darker than the fog. Not
  changed: the fog's own colour isn't known in the shader.

**[not verified in game]**

### 21. Gravel whole under the snow once it covers the ground (2026-10-28)
Seen in game: a roof's gravel bed under the snow, grey and speckled stone by stone (white in a few patches by the
units), the concrete ledge and walkway round it white.

**Cause [code]:**
- Until 3 cm had piled (buried = smoothstep(0.03, 0.12, depth) = 0), the snow's facing and its bend test (SnowNormal,
  clean) came from the pixels 1 and 2 off. On gravel those are a stone's own facets, so flat (normal.y and clean) went
  stone by stone.
- The concrete is flat, so its cover was whole.
- The wide normal (when buried) was 4 px: at 4K and 3 m that's under a centimetre, smaller than a stone.

**Now [code]:**
- buried = max(smoothstep(0.03, 0.12, depth), smoothstep(0.6, 1, cover)): once the snow covers the ground, relief of a
  few cm counts as buried however little has piled.
- The wide SnowNormal's step is 12 cm on the ground (round(0.12 / (distance x pixel angle)), between 4 px x PixelScale
  and 48). It's taken as far as it's in line (buried x cleanWide), so never across an edge.
- SnowEdgeAt's tolerance is at least 4 cm at full cover.
- Cost: the wide SnowNormal now runs wherever the cover is complete (8 more depth reads a pixel).

### 22. Her handprints from her own posed hand; lying KrugerSec in the rain (2026-10-28)
Goal: handprints in snow and rain in the shape of Faith's hand; dying and ragdolled KrugerSec leaving their shape's
ripples (the wet look's part, it needs SnowBodies).

**Her hand [data, code]:**
- SnowHandMesh.h: faith_arms_mesh LOD0's merged section, the vertices whose heaviest bone
  is LeftHand / RightHand or under them, and the triangles all of whose corners are. Left 2,178 vertices and 4,327
  triangles; right 3,637 and 6,955 (the right has more detail; why isn't known). Positions in 0.1 mm.

  within 300 ms and 15 cm is the same one.
- For 400 ms its hand is skinned each frame (her body's checked matrices).
  - The first frame frames it: the normal turned towards her hand; its middle her hand's vertices' centroid on the
    plane; U = LeftHand to LeftHandMiddle1 laid in the plane; V = normal x U.

    within 6 cm of the plane either way): (nearest + 1.5 cm - its distance) / 1.5 cm.
  - The stamp is 64 x 64 texels of 4 mm, R8, a Texture2DArray of 32 (t5), smoothed 1 2 1 each way.
- A print's state: 1 pressed (drawn from the stamp), 0 still being pressed (drawn neither way), -1 nothing went in, or
  its slot was given to another touch (drawn as HandShape).
- WetLook.cpp's snow and rain hand prints carry the stamp; the pressed ones go to g_HandStampAt / U / V (43472 /
  43488 / 44000 / 44512, size 45024).

  rim). HandPrintsAt draws the wet ones within 3 cm of the plane.

**KrugerSec lying [code, for the wet look]:**

- snowbody::LyingBodies: each lying one's 15 capsules between bones in world space, with DownAt and KnockAt

- The radii are from enforcer_fullbody_mesh LOD0: each vertex goes to its nearest segment, and the radius
  holds 85 % of them, left and right averaged:
  - head 0.152, lower torso 0.217, upper torso 0.211;
  - upper arms 0.151, forearms 0.060, hands 0.057;
  - thighs 0.155, shins 0.085, feet 0.089.

### 23. The game's own G-buffer for the snow; its shaders made ahead; the scene's depth from the G-buffer pass (2026-11-01)

Goal: snow kept through drone takedowns; not blurry when not looked at directly or in bright places; not lit by
reflections; no lag the first time rain or snow comes on; a better snow layer on models and meshes.

**Was the snow's light reflection based? In effect, yes [code].**
- SnowLit took its light from the frame's own picture of the ground: SnowLightAround, the same surface 6 + 20 px round on
  the scene copy's level 2, x 1.9, never below the sky's x 0.9.
- The picture holds the ground's reflections (SSR and cube maps on the city's glossy surfaces). They grow towards a
  glancing view (Fresnel) and are brightest in bright places, so the snow took a blurred copy of them.
- x 1.9 took bright places over white (min(..., 1)), so no shading was left there.

**The game's G-buffer [code: offline, the game's own shaders, fxc /dumpbin]:**
- A city material shader that writes all four targets (sp_maincity shaderdb, offset 93384056):
  - the normal's basis = round(texture_normalBasisCubemapTexture(n).a x 255.49), its colour target's alpha = basis / 6;
  - target 0 xy = (n.x R0 + n.y R1 + n.z R2).xy x 0.5 + 0.5, with R_c = viewConstants register 26 + 3 x basis + c;
    target 0 z = a texture's y (the smoothness), w = 0;
  - target 1 rgb = the base colour (sRGB target);
  - target 2: x 0, y and z textures (the metal mask, the reflectance), w = saturate(light map sky visibility x 3.5 +
    the material's own);
  - target 3 = the light map's irradiance x exposureMultipliers.x.
- The sun's light pass (systems shaderprogramdb, offset 2210594, cbuffer OutdoorlightConstant):
  - reads t0 - t2 (the G-buffer), t6 (depth), t7 g_shadowAccumTexture (.x the sun's visibility, x the cloud shadow t9);
  - the normal back: local = (2 xy - 1, sqrt(1 - |xy|^2)), world c = local . g_normalBasisTransforms[basis] row c;
  - diffuse = base x (1 - metal); f0 = lerp(0.16 r^2, base, metal), r = target 2's z; roughness = 1 - target 0's z;
  - g_lightDir and g_lightIlluminance are the sun's.
- The screen-space sun shadow pass (offset 546399): the depth back to the world (g_invViewProjMatrix), x
  g_shadowmapTransform, one compare sample into o0.x. So g_shadowAccumTexture is a screen-sized mask of the sun's
  shadow. **Not used yet:** how to find that texture at run time isn't known.
- viewConstants (the shaders' b2, 1120 bytes): normalBasisTransforms[6] at 416 (3 float4s each), exposureMultipliers at
  784, light0Dir at 1008, the fog's values from 800.
- The 6 bases aren't in the game image as plain floats (a scan for runs of 0 / +-1 floats: none orthonormal): set
  at run time, so they're copied with viewConstants.

**Drone takedowns [data; not seen live].**
- A disrupted drone plays FX/Weapons/Drone/FX_Drone_Disrupted with Em_Drone_Disrupted_Distortion, and
  FX/Weapons/Hacking/FX_Disrupted_Drone with a disruptor-volume mesh particle and its own shader.
- A distortion can draw passes of its own. The depth copy took the biggest depth target shaped like the frame that got
  cleared, so one as big, cleared for another pass, took the scene's place: no snow, wet look or green screen, or the
  sky everywhere.
- **Not confirmed:** a takedown with snow hasn't been seen in game.

**The first-time lag [code].**
- The pass's shader is 738,584 bytes of bytecode (about 24,130 instruction slots); PsQuery is 91,276 and IcePs 64,912.
- Make() created all 7 in the frame any of the weather first came on, and the graphics driver's compile of them held
  that frame.

**Changes [code]:**
- GameFrame.cpp / .h (new):
  - through the replay's render target hook (ReplayGameDraws' Targets, installed by gameframe::Want while any weather is
    on), the G-buffer pass's depth targets, the last 4 seen;
  - while snow lies, copies of targets 0 - 2 and of viewConstants where the G-buffer and decal passes end;
  - after 30 frames with no G-buffer pass, the depth targets are forgotten (the old rule until one is seen again);
  - GreenPlane: when none of them is cleared for 30 frames while another one shaped like the frame is, they are given
    up on (gameframe::ForgetSceneDepths: not learned again; a new one is). The reason: the wet
    look, haze, puddles and snow all read that depth copy, so a stale target must never stop them.
- GreenPlane OnDepthClear: once a G-buffer pass has been seen, only its depth targets are the scene's. Any other one
  shaped like the frame is left alone and logged once ("another depth target shaped like the frame was cleared").
- ReplayGameDraws: g_PassKinds is also cleared on a frame size change.
- WetLook.cpp:
  - StartMaking: Make() on a worker thread from the first frame (in that frame if the device is single-threaded),
    logged with its ms;
  - Apply draws nothing until it's made, and the frame isn't held up;
  - "Weather (diagnostic): the rain, snow and wet look not drawn: ..." and "drawn again after ..." (at most 12 a
    minute);
  - t6 - t8 and b1 bound for PsMain (the game's b1 put back); g_GameFrame at 46672 (size 46688).
- WetLook.hlsl:
  - GameSurfaceAt decodes the normal as the game does. Rejected: a basis off 0 - 5 by over 0.1, |xy|^2 > 1.05, or a
    length under 0.5.
  - The snow's facing is the game's where the depth surface isn't clean (byGame = 1 - clean, within SnowDrift.w), and
    flat doesn't need clean there. So snow lies on rails, pipes, small and far models and stops at a model's own
    edge. Clean surfaces keep the depth's facing (the game's has the texture's bumps).
  - The snow's light (GameLightAt / SnowLitByGame) is the picture (^2.2) at 2 x 2 pixels over what the surface gives
    back: base x (1 - metal) x (1 - mirror) + mirror, with mirror = f0 + (max(smoothness, f0) - f0)(1 - n.v)^5. Then
    x 0.85, the colour 70 % of the light's, back ^ 1/2.2, rolled off from 0.8 to at most 0.97.
  - trust = enough given back (smoothstep 0.04 - 0.1) x not a mirror (0.25 - 0.6) x not a metal x the fog
    transmittance^2. Where it's low, the sky's light (g_HazeView), never the ground's picture. SnowLit is only used
    without a G-buffer copy; the pile's side is lit the same way at its foot.

**[not verified in game]**

**Not known:**
- Whether the copy point (leaving the G-buffer / decal passes) has the decals.
- The copies' cost: 3 full-frame targets a frame while snow lies, 4 bytes a pixel each.
- How the division looks on every surface. The picture is tone mapped, so ^2.2 is only near; under TAA and motion blur,
  the picture and the G-buffer differ by a pixel at sharp colour edges.
- Whether the takedown's trouble was the depth target (the depth target lines and the diagnostic lines above
  would say).
- What else is slow the first time rain or snow comes on (the weather's own start: effects, sounds). The make line
  gives the shaders' ms.

### 24. Snow brightness; Faith's shoes; the shaders drawn ahead (2026-11-01)

Goal: the snow more apparent.
- **Why it was dimmer [code, reasoning; not measured]:** SnowLitByGame gave back 0.85 of the light reaching the ground
  (linear), fresh snow's own. The old light, the ground's picture x 1.9 in the picture's values, is about x 4.1 in
  linear light. For a mid-grey ground (0.45 in the picture, base colour 0.5) that's 0.57 of white now against 0.86
  before.
- The glints took part of their light from `around`, which isn't worked out when the game's light is used (0 then),
  so they were dimmer too. They use the game's light now.
- **Change [code]:**
  - weather::Settings.SnowBrightness and SnowFall::Brightness (SnowBrightnessDefault 1.75), with the slider "Snow
    brightness" (0.5 - 4) under "Snow on the ground";
  - g_GameFrame.y = it, and .z = (it / 1.75)^(1/2.2) for SnowLit's light without the G-buffer (unchanged at the
    default);
  - SnowLitByGame: 0.85 x brightness x the light, rolled off (RollOffWhite, 0.8 -> 0.97); the sky fallback x
    brightness^(1/2.2), rolled off the same way.
- The six other shader headers came out byte-identical; only PsMain changed. (Then g_SnowShoe changed all 7.)
- **The first-time lag, measured [seen in game]:**
  - The shaders and states are made in 10 ms, on a worker thread: making them was never the slow part, so section 23's
    "the driver's compile of them held that frame" was wrong in its detail.
  - The first 10 s of snow: the wet look's render-thread work 0.189 ms a frame, most 154.10; later 10 s spans 0.1 ms,
    most under 2. The driver compiles at a shader's first draw.
  - Now WarmUp draws each shader pair once (a 1 x 1 target in the frame's format, the query's own target, the pass's
    states, constants all 0) once they're made. Every loop in WetLook.hlsl counts by one to a fixed bound, a count
    from the constants (0 then) or a clamped one (2 - 8, 8 - 48), so none runs long.
- Seen in game: the G-buffer copied (formats 24 / 29 / 28) and used; the G-buffer pass's depth learned; a half-size
  depth target the game also clears left alone; a second G-buffer pass in a frame seen; the pass never "not drawn".
- **Faith's shoes blue on snow** (cyan snow on her red shoe tops, seen in game) [code, reasoning]:
  - GameLightAt's light was picture / given channel by channel. On a saturated base colour, a low channel's
    "given" is small, so anything else in it (the sky mirrored, a TAA pixel) came out the complement: cyan on red.
  - Now the brightness is Luma(picture) / Luma(given), and the colour is the channel ratio over it (clamped 0.6 -
    1.5), used only as far as the diffuse colour is grey (saturation 0.15 - 0.4).
  - FeetKeptAt kept her shoes only within 0.43 m of dry::FaithFeet (her transform). Now ShoesKeptAt adds a capsule per
    foot on her bones (snowbody::FaithShoes: LeftFoot / LeftToeBase / RightFoot / RightToeBase from her body read,
    250 ms, g_SnowShoe at 46688, size 46752).
  - Her shoe in LOD0's bind pose (577 vertices whose heaviest bone is the foot, toe base or toe):
    - the foot bone to the toe base is 14.6 cm;
    - the vertices run from 2.6 cm behind the foot bone to 5.9 cm past the toe base (2 - 98 %), all within 9.9 cm
      of that line;
    - the sole is 9.1 cm under the foot bone and 2.1 cm under the toe base.
  - The capsule: from 3 cm behind to 6.5 cm past, radius 10 cm (soft to 13), over min(ankle - 9.1 cm, toe base -
    2.1 cm) by 1 - 2.5 cm.

### 25. The ground snow stronger; the forecast's share of the day (2026-11-01)

Goal: a stronger snow-on-the-ground effect.
- **Its opacity [code]:** settled (flat x open x SnowReach x FogAt x ice x SnowEdgeAt x not kept) x snow.a (patch x not
  over VFX x not on a glowing panel).
- **What held it back, by default [code, reasoning]:**
  - **patch:** with "Snow on the ground" 0.85, c = 0.85 once settled. patch = smoothstep(-0.01, 0.31, noise x 0.85 +
    flat x 0.15) is down to 0.5, and smoothstep(0.85, 1, c) is 0, so the patches stay half see-through until the snow
    depth (SnowDepthAt) passes 2 - 8 cm. The pile reaches 0.12 x 0.85 = 10 cm over 3 x the settle time (12 min).
  - **FogAt:** the fog's transmittance faded the snow's alpha. In a blizzard's 120 m, T(30 m) = exp(-3 x 30 / 120) =
    0.47.
  - **Brightness:** 1.75 gave 0.73 of white for a mid-grey ground's light.
- **Changes [code]:**
  - SnowCover default 1.0; SnowBrightnessDefault 2.5 (the tooltip says so);
  - WetLook.hlsl: where g_HazeView.y >= 0, settled and the pile's side no longer take FogAt; the snow's colour is
    lerp(g_HazeView.yzw, snow, FogAt). HazeSkyAt's sky is averaged over the upper two-thirds of the frame, held steady
    on the CPU.
- Only PsMain's bytecode changed.

**Not known:** whether the sky's colour matches the fog's in the snowy look, at dusk and at night.

**"How much of the day it snows" [code, offline]:**
- Random snow uses the rain's forecast (Weather.cpp MakeForecast / ForecastAt) with SnowChance.
- The old plan: the first spell at 0 - 6 h; each 40 - 150 game minutes; each gap -ln(1 - 0.999u) x length x
  (1 - c) / c, at least 15 min. That's c of the day only on average over many days, and one day's forecast repeats.
- Worked out exactly (offline: float32, the same draws, storm's extra draw included), the first seed
  0x2F6E2B1 gives these shares of the day falling:
  - 0.05: 24.6 %;
  - 0.1, 0.2, 0.3: 33.2 % each;
  - 0.5: 53.1 %;
  - 0.7: 65.0 %;
  - 0.9: 74.3 %.
- **The new plan:**
  - the lengths are drawn until they add up to c x 86400 (the last one is what's left, at least 40 min);
  - each spell's weather is drawn as before;
  - the gaps are max(15 min, dry / n) + the rest x exponential weights, placed from a random start of day (Start in
    0 - 86400, End past midnight allowed: ForecastAt and ForecastStatus check +-1 day).
- Over 5 seeds x 7 settings it's within 0.03 % (the 10 s sampling step), with no overlaps (offline).
- The game's clock: about 20 game s a real s (MEC_Reverse_Notes, MEC-TC), so a game day is about 72 real minutes.
  The forecast reads GetCurrentTimeOfDay, so a stopped clock holds it.

  - groundmarks::ProbeTraffic, the motorcycle diagnostic.

  - groundmarks::Update before the constants (red written where snowed, green where the wet look is);
