### 27. Wet tyre tracks after a puddle; marks only at their own height (2026-11-01)

Goal: the wet tyre tracks from the open question at the end of section 26.

**The height problem in section 26's map [code, not seen in game]:** its map (R16G16) had no height, so a mark showed at
any height over or under where it was made: a step under an awning on the awning's top, a car's track on a bridge
over it.

**Built [code]:**
- **The tracks (DryShapes):** each back wheel carries water (0 - 1). Every 0.5 m it drives, wetlook::PuddleUnder(the
  wheel) looks for a puddle there: PsMain's own test with the last frame's values (PuddleAt: the wet look drawn, the
  ground wet, open to the sky, within the fade distance, inside a puddle's edge). In one it's 1. It wears off
  linearly over 12 m. Called in the motion loop with no lock held, then groundmarks::Wheel queues (PuddleAt takes
  wetlook's g_Mutex, then weather's ShelterAt lock, one after the other).
- **The map (GroundMarks):** R16G16B16A16_UNORM, 2048 x 2048 x 4 cm (82 m). Red: in the snow how far it's pressed, in
  the rain the wet track (a wheel's carried water, a step none). Green: the water stirred. Alpha: the ground's height.
  - Red dries over 30 s in the rain (WetTrackSeconds) and fills at the prints' rate in the snow. The map is cleared on
    a snow/rain switch.
  - **Height:** alpha x 1200 m + HeightLow: 1.8 cm steps. HeightLow is the camera's height less 600 m when the map was
    cleared; it's cleared again when the camera is 300 m from that middle. Stamps outside the range are dropped.
    (Not a 16-bit float: it was already UNORM; the base is per map anyway.)
  - **Only where a mark is left:** StampPs does clip(max(red, green) - 0.02), so a quad's faint fringe doesn't move the
    height (else a step on a bridge would move a track from the road below).
- **WetLook.hlsl:**
  - MarksAt: rg bilinear; the height from the nearest texel (Load at floor(uv x 2048) & 2047; bilinear at a mark's
    edge blends with the cleared texels' 0). The mark counts within 0.4 - 0.8 m of that height.
  - The tracks: wet = max(wet, track x ground x max(g_Wet.x, g_Wet.y) x the wet ground's fade (distance, FogAt) x
    (1 - kept)). They're as wet as the puddles they came from. In Weather.cpp the puddles dry over 1200 s and the
    ground over 600 s (GroundDrySeconds, PuddleDrySeconds), so after the rain they show across a drier road. In a
    downpour they're no wetter than the road. Under a roof too, as her prints are.
  - g_MarksOn.z: the tracks on (the wet look drawn, no snow); g_MarksOn.w: HeightLow.

**[not verified in game]**

**Known limits [reasoning]:**
- A step on a bridge right over a fresh track still moves that sole-sized bit of the track to the bridge: a rain step
  writes green, so it sets the height where its sole is.
- PuddleAt finds no puddle where the ground's wetness is 0, as PsMain draws none there. Once the ground has dried, the
  puddles left over (fill > 0) aren't drawn and leave no tracks.
- Motorcycles still make two car tracks (section 26).

Goal: a faster snow pass; and no ice fighting the water on a pool seen partly ice and partly water.

**The snow's cost [data, seen in game]:**

- The breakdown (7 parts then): the whole pass 3.64 ms, "the rest" 4.51, the rain's five parts -2.23 to
  1.70. While snow is chosen the wet look is off (WetLook.cpp: wet = s.On && s.Wetness > 0 && !snow.Chosen, so
  g_Rain.z is 0 and every wet pixel's `wet` is 0): those five did nothing, their numbers are frame-to-frame noise of
  about 2 ms (3 frames 0.3 s apart). So nearly all of the pass in the snow is the snow block and what every pixel does.
- CPU: the camera hook 5.80 ms a frame with the tools' drawing on, 3.28 paused. Of that, the weather's game-thread
  work is 0.45 - 0.82 ms and the people kept dry 0.09 - 0.19 ms, the street level's planning 0.19 - 0.22 ms. The rest
  of the camera hook isn't timed apart; what it is isn't known.

**fxc's counts (ps_4_1, /O3) [data]:** the whole PsMain 43 temps, 31,079 instruction slots; the rain's copy
(RAIN_ONLY) 40 / 18,406, unchanged by this change; the snow's copy (SNOW_ONLY) 28 / 15,838
(15,760 before the pile's search and the breakdown's switches went in). The ice's 17 / 1,733.

**The snow's copy [code]:**
- WetLook.hlsl's WetDrawn (false under SNOW_ONLY) is ANDed into the rain's own gates: wetFade's g_Rain.z, PrintsAt,
  MarksAt for the water and the tracks (g_MarksOn.y / z), her splash (g_OtherCounts.y), her wet handprints, the drips,
  the drainpipes, the splashes (g_OtherCounts.y), the distant rain (RainAt).
- WetLook.cpp draws it (g_SnowGroundPs, WetLookSnowGroundPs.h) only when snow lies and Rain.z <= 0.5, DripCount.x <= 0.5,
  PipeCount.x <= 0.5, OtherCounts.y <= 0.5, DistantRain.x <= 0, read from the constants just written (before Unmap). Under
  those the full shader's gated parts are all off too: `wet` stays 0 (wetFade 0; prints gated by g_Rain.z; the
  tracks x wetFade), marksHere is read only inside the wet block, keptHere and bodyWet stay 0. So the picture is the
  same by construction. Otherwise the whole one.
- WarmUp draws it once; the breakdown times it and the whole one, and its line says which copy it drew.

**The breakdown's snow parts [code]:** 5 more bits, left out in this order before the rest of the snow (32768):
65536 the piled side, 131072 what's pressed in (SnowGround's prints, trails, rolls, stamps, the ground's marks),
262144 the snow's light (SnowLitByGame, SnowLightAround), 524288 its edges and what's kept out (SnowEdgeAt, KeptDry,
her hands and shoes), 1048576 its facing (both SnowNormals, the G-buffer's). 20 parts, 22 draws of the pass in each of
the 3 frames after a measurement.

**The pile's search [code]:** SnowPileSide read the depth one row after another: up to 5 steps (each stopping the
loop at the first top), 3 halvings, then the 2 rows under the top: up to 9 rounds of reads, each waiting for the one
before. Now: the 5 steps at once (the first top among them taken), the first two halvings' 3 rows at once, the third
on its own, then the top's point with the 2 rows under it: 4 rounds, the same rows and the same result (the halvings'
rows are the same sums in the same order). Up to 34 depth reads instead of 30.

### 29. The pile against walls without stripes (2026-11-03)
Goal: no stripes or bands in the piled snow at the foot of walls, boxes or curbs.

**What was seen [data]:** at a roof's parapet, from inside (seen in game): along its foot, the band where the pile is
drawn is dark grey-purple, in columns a pixel or two wide crossed by fine near-horizontal lines, its top a smooth
swell, its lower edge ragged where it meets the white ground snow. That was before section 26's change moved the
pile's light onto 3 taps 8 px out on the ground; the pile hasn't been seen since.

**What made stripes in the code [code, reasoning]:**
- Its look: PsMain drew SnowGround at snowAt, the foot point SnowPileSide found under the pixel. Every pixel up a column
  of the wall has the same foot, so the grain (3.5 cm), the glints (one 3 cm cell in 12, a dot 4 mm across), the
  ripples (0.28 m crests) and the prints at that one point were drawn up the whole pile: vertical streaks, a glint a
  bright line.
- Its foot's row: 5 steps of tall / 5 rows (up to 12.8 at 4K) and 3 halvings, in fractions of a row: the row found was
  within tall / 40 (1.6 px) of where the top begins, and as the steps are counted from each pixel, the next pixel up
  often got the row above or below. The foot point, its light's taps (8 px out from it) and its swell height moved
  with it: lines across the columns.
- Its light: SnowLitByGame's 3 taps were taken only when all 3 had the G-buffer (else SnowLightAround, a different
  light), so where a tap fell on something else (a person, the sky, a face turned away) the pixel took the other
  light.
- Close by: the search went 64 px at 4K at most. The pile is g_SnowPile.x x 0.45 - 1.55 x 0.85 - 1.15 tall; at the
  most piled (0.12 m average) that's 64 px at 4K about 3.6 m off. Nearer, the pixels over 64 px found no foot, so the
  pile's top was a hard straight line 64 px over its foot.

**Changed [code]:**
- The search in whole rows: the 5 steps at rows round(reach x (s + 1) / 5), the halvings on whole rows until the
  top's first row is found (3 batched rows, then up to 4 single ones; 3 at 4K). With the depth's own texels (frame
  and depth the same size) every pixel over a foot finds the same row, whichever steps it took. 128 px at 4K
  (x PixelScale) at most; where the pile is taller on the frame than that, faded out over the search's last 30 %.
  The continuation below the top is as before (half the reach, 32 px at most).
- Its look where the pixel sees it: seenAt, where the ray meets a 45 degree drift from the pile's height at the wall
  down to the ground's snow (here - dir x (height - over) / max(across + down, 0.25)). Lower pixels see it further
  out, so the grain, glints and ripples lie on it as on the ground. SnowGround's footprint there is as the ground's
  (its normal up), so seen from the side its fine details fade as the ground's do at a glancing angle.
- Its light: the taps the G-buffer has averaged, however many (1 - 3); none, SnowLightAround as before.
- Not changed: where it lies (the tops, the foot's checks, its height and swells, open, kept dry), its soft top edge.

**Cost [data, fxc /O3]:** the snow's copy (SNOW_ONLY) 28 temps both, 15,900 -> 16,285 instruction slots; the whole
PsMain 43 temps both, 33,272 -> 33,668 (its two indexable temps were there before). The other 14 shaders built from
WetLook.hlsl (GbufferWet.hlsl includes it) and GroundMarks.hlsl are byte-identical before and after (the rain's copy,
PsQuery, NodesPs, GbufferWetInfoPs / GbufferWetPs, the flakes', the ice's, the marks').

### 31. The pile's light from a lattice fixed on the frame (2026-11-03)
Goal: no stretched snow on walls on a gravel roof, with section 29's pile fix in.

**What was seen [data]:** along a box's foot on gravel under snow, the pile's side is a band of vertical
streaks a pixel to three wide, light and dark like the gravel's speckle beside it. Along one row of the band the red
channel goes 100 - 219 from column to column.

**Which path drew it [data]:** the game's G-buffer was copied and used for the snow when it was seen. So it was the
G-buffer path.

**Why [code]:** every pixel of a column takes its light from the same foot (footUv). Its light was 3 SnowLitByGame taps
of 2 x 2 pixels, 8 px out from that column's own foot and 6 px apart. GameLightAt is the picture over what the surface
gives back, pixel by pixel, and on gravel each stone is lit its own way. So each column took other stones' light and
drew it up its whole height. The fallback without the G-buffer (SnowLightAround at footUv) was each column's own too.
SnowGround doesn't read its `color`, and its other inputs for the pile (seenAt, SceneAround's B-spline) go smoothly
from column to column.

**Changed [code]:**
- PileLight: the game's light on a lattice fixed on the frame, nodes 16 px apart (at 4K, x PixelScale).
  - Each node is GameLightAt over 2 x 2 pixels 4 px apart (its new spread), through SnowFromGameLight (SnowLitByGame's
    own sums, moved out).
  - Only nodes on the ground count: facing up in the G-buffer (n.y >= 0.7), not the sky, and within 0.2 m + 1 % of
    the distance of the foot's height.
  - The 4 nodes round the point 8 px out from the foot are blended bilinearly over the ones that count. Where their
    share is under 0.15 it fades to SnowLit(SceneAround at the foot) x Snow brightness against its default; without
    the G-buffer, that's all.
- PsMain's pile passes footLit = PileLight (a = 1), so SnowGround's around isn't read.
- GameLightAt(..., spread, trust): SnowLitByGame passes 1, the same pixels and sums.

**Offline [data]:** a random per-pixel light standing in for gravel (blobs 3 px, plus noise per pixel). The
light along a foot line slanting 1 row in 3 columns changed from one column to the next by:
- old taps: 0.053 on average, 0.231 at most;
- the lattice: 0.008 on average, 0.029 at most;
- with the nodes above the foot line left out (the wall), by their own place, for slants of 1/3, 1, 3 and -1 rows a
  column: 0.006 - 0.009 on average, 0.021 - 0.052 at most;
- for scale, the ground's own light pixel to pixel along a row: 0.178.
This is a stand-in, not the game's gravel.

**Cost [data, fxc ps_4_1 /O3, with and without the edit]:**
- WetLookPs: 43 temps both, 35,779 -> 35,490 slots.
- WetLookSnowGroundPs: 28 temps both, 17,803 -> 17,531 slots.
- The other 14 headers are byte-identical between the two compiles.
- Reads per pile pixel: 4 nodes x (2 G-buffer + 1 depth + 12) = 60, against 3 x 14 = 42 before, plus SnowLightAround
  where a tap was missing.

**What it gives up [reasoning]:** the pile's light follows the ground in front of it over 16 - 32 px, not pixel by
pixel. Light and shade there sharper than that (a shadow's edge across the foot) are soft on the pile. The lattice is
fixed on the frame, so as the camera moves its nodes go over other stones and the pile's light changes slowly over
16 px stretches.

**The walls [data, code]:** a gravel roof's parapet and a skylight's frame: along their foot the pile's side

at its foot. The bands are PileLight's (section 31): the 4 lattice nodes 16 px apart on the gravel in front, each the

row by row is the likeliest [reasoning]). Since there should be no snow on walls at all, the pile isn't drawn:
`static const bool SnowOnWalls = false` in front of PsMain gates its block (its code kept). The snow lies on what
faces up (up to 55 degrees), up to the wall's foot.

such a line moves with the frame, on all the water (section 30). Section 30's light change didn't
touch it, so that wasn't its cause.

  thing here drawn from the world's own shapes (IceTable.h's triangles) and tested against the game's depth. It was
  drawn with g_ViewProjection, the camera hook's camera as it was at the frame's depth clear (GreenPlane.cpp
  SetView / FrameViewLocked, from the render view), and its depth test put the frame's point (RelativeAt, the same
  camera) against the ice's.

  camera) the frame's point is off the water by about h (1 - y_ours / y_game), y a ray's up part: linear across the
  frame, so past a straight line on it more than IceOnWater (0.15 m + 0.1 % of the distance; a pitch error gives a
  line along the horizon, a roll one a slanted line). A shift of the camera's place only moves the point along the
  water (no line). **How far off that camera is in first person hasn't been measured** (the diagnostic of "the
  frame's camera taken at its depth clear" only says it didn't change between the clear and Present).

  viewConstants, at least 1120 bytes, first 0, as its G-buffer and decal passes end; g_Copied needs that copy, both
  reset each frame), IceVsMain draws the ice with the game's own camera of the frame: (place - cameraPos, register 45)

  quad 1.80 x as wide and 1.28 x as long. So the rectangle is the car's shadow plane.
- Not read: whether that shader writes the depth. If it does, its edge is a drop of about 3.7 cm (its height over
  the car's lowest point), and SnowEdgeAt's buried (half the snow's depth, at least 3 cm, 4 cm once it covers)
  counted it with under 7.4 cm lying: the plane's outer 1 - 2.5 pixels lost snow (on 12 points, 1 and 2.5 px round).
  That is the 1 px + fainter pixel seen. No other part of the snow's pass was found that draws a line on a shape's
  edge when the depth has none there [code].
- Section 32's rectangles round "parked cars" were these planes too (the same proportions), not the parking
  bays' paint: section 32's cause was wrong. Its change (OwnColourAt) stays: paint brighter than the road round it
  is laid on as the surface's own colour; whether paint ever showed through isn't known.

**The railings [data, code]:** a metal staircase: the handrail's top, the steps' perforated tops' front lips and the
stringers' edges with snow in jagged blocks and blobs, some on their sides. They're a few centimetres across: where
the depth's facing isn't clean there (an edge, a thin part) the snow takes the game's own facing (GameSurfaceAt,
PsMain's byGame), up on a rounded or bevelled top; its patches (SnowPatchNoise) and the edge fade cut it up.

**Changed [code]:**
- SnowEdgeAt's buried: at least 6 cm (was 3): a car's shadow plane, a lip or a seam under 6 cm is buried.
- SnowWideAt: 8 points 5 cm round (RingDirections; at least 2, at most 48 of 4K's pixels, x PixelScale), counted as
  SnowEdgeAt counts them, with the same buried; none from 2.5 of them on (a rail: the 2 along it), all from 5 (a wide
  top's straight edge: 3 drop). Nothing under about 7 cm across holds snow; a top's corner fades over its last 5 cm.
  Run after SnowEdgeAt, in the same SkipSnowEdges branch, where some snow is left.

**Compiled [data, fxc /O3]:** with and without: code changed only in WetLookPs (42 temps as before, 28,612 -> 28,918
slots) and WetLookSnowGroundPs (26 as before, 10,713 -> 11,016); the other 14 byte-identical.

**Not known:** whether the planes write depth (if not, the rectangle's cause is elsewhere); how the snow looks on
steps, curbs and ledges near their edges with the width test.

### 35. The depth's texel clamped; the camera drawn with checked against the game's own (2026-11-04)
Goal: find and fix anything wrong with the game's depth as read and with the snow's depth on the ground.

**Gone through [code]:** GreenPlane.cpp's depth copy (which target, at which clear, the reversed depth and the sky's
depth from the projection), the frame's camera (the camera hook's at the frame's first depth clear), WetLook.hlsl's
DepthAt / RelativeAtTexel / WetInfoAt / RelativeAt / RelativeAtViewZ / IsSky (the depth terms worked back from the
projection's rows: right), the reflections' march (its reads stay on the frame), the G-buffer pass's PlaceAt;
SnowDepthAt and its three C++ copies (WetLook.cpp's prints, steps, stamps: the same Hash / Noise step for step),
Weather.cpp's snow pile (grows once the cover is whole, goes over 3 x the settle time once it stops).

**Wrong, fixed [code]:** DepthAt, RelativeAtTexel and WetInfoAt took the texel as int(saturate(uv) x the copy's size):
a point at or past the frame's right or bottom edge was texel W or H, outside the copy, which reads 0, the sky
where the depth runs reversed (it does: GreenPlane's z1 > z100); one past the left or top edge was the edge's own
texel. So every ring that looks past the frame (SnowEdgeAt, SnowWideAt, DropAt, KeptDryAt's, SnowAroundAt, the
G-buffer pass's) saw the sky along the right and bottom edges only: the snow (and the wet look's edges) thinned
there, and with SnowWideAt (section 34, 5 cm, up to 48 px) the snow went in the bottom right corner. Now DepthTexel:
int(min(saturate(uv), 0.99999) x size), the same texels inside the frame (for frames up to 100,000 px across), the
edge's own past it. (A clamp() to the copy's size cost one more register in WetLookPs, RainPs and QueryPs; this
doesn't.)

**Not known, measured from now on [code]:** whether the camera the tools draw with (the camera hook's at the frame's
first depth clear; the G-buffer pass's turn too) is the game's own for the frame. If the game thread runs the next
frame's camera hook before the render thread clears this frame's depth, it's a frame ahead: still, nothing shows;
turning, what the tools place by the depth's points (the snow's and the puddles' patterns, prints, the kept-dry
boxes, the ice before section 33) is off by a frame's turn. The existing diagnostic ("in 0 of them the game's camera
had already moved on by Present") can't tell. New gameframe::CheckCamera (diagnostic, called from WetLook.cpp's pass
where the G-buffer copy is there): twice a second the copy of the game's viewConstants (its first 736 bytes) into a
read-back buffer, read 3+ frames later without waiting; 9 points 20 m ahead of the tools' camera (ndc +-0.8, 0) put
through the game's crViewProjMatrix (registers 14 - 17) less its cameraPos (45): how many pixels off they land, for
the frame's camera, the frame before's and the frame after's (the next one the pass is drawn with). Every 10 s: "Wet
surfaces (diagnostic): the tools' camera against the game's own of the frame (its viewConstants), N checks in 10 s: a
point 20 m ahead drawn x px off on average (most) with the frame's camera, ... the frame before's, ... the frame
after's; the closest: ...; the camera's place m off". The game's TAA jitter alone is under a pixel.

**The snow's depth on the ground [code]:** nothing wrong found: SnowDepthAt is the pile x 0.45 - 1.55 by value noise
6 m across, the same on the CPU and the GPU.

**Compiled [data, fxc /O3]:** with and without: temps the same in all; slots WetLookPs 28,918 -> 29,161, RainPs
22,441 -> 22,604, SnowGroundPs 11,016 -> 11,107, GbufferWetPs 11,059 -> 11,154, QueryPs 7,429 -> 7,537, IcePs
1,881 -> 1,926, NodesPs 671 -> 682, GbufferWetInfoPs 711 -> 712, SnowPs 36 -> 38; the other 7 byte-identical.

**[not verified in game]**

# 32. VISUALS tab audit (2026-10-26)

Goal: find the VISUALS tab's bugs, starting with the blur not following the lens distortion, and why DoF method 2
crashed the game.

All addresses are in the game image (PE timestamp 0x5762E3B7).
"State" is the visual environment state, `[[[[*OFFSET_MAIN + 0x50] + 0x90] + 0x1C0] + 0x30] + 0x85470`. In the
renderer's per-view object the same state starts at `+ 0x84970` (film grain `+ 0x85470` = state `+ 0xB00`).

### 1. The blur doesn't follow the lens distortion

#### How the game draws it

- The post-process is `0x1435BE3A0`. It's called from the world renderer at `0x14374689B` with a parameter block at
  `rbp + 0xD70`:
  - `+ 0x90` tonemap (state `+ 0x1D0`)
  - `+ 0x98` depth of field (state `+ 0xA50`)
  - `+ 0xA0` vignette (`+ 0xAC0`)
  - `+ 0xA8` film grain (`+ 0xB00`)
  - `+ 0xB0` filmic effects (`+ 0x9B0`)
  - `+ 0x28` "DofMethod is Gaussian" (`sete` of frame flags `+ 0x38`, `0x143746624`)
  - `+ 0x29` "BlurMethod is Gaussian"
- Order inside `0x1435BE3A0`:
  1. The ironsights DoF (`0x1435BEC5F` – `0x1435BF026`, only with IronsightsDofEnable).
  2. The tonemap pass: struct at `rbp + 0x100`, built `0x1435BF129` – `0x1435BF8F8`, drawn by `0x1435C9A70`.
     - Filmic effects are read at `0x1435BF526`: `+ 0x80` Enable, `+ 0x81` / `+ 0x14` / `+ 0x18` chromatic aberration,
       `+ 0x83` / `+ 0x24` / `+ 0x28` lens distortion. They go to struct `+ 0xF8` … `+ 0x10C`.
  3. **Then** the Simple (Gaussian) depth of field, `0x1435BFB7B` on, when `[rbp - 0x70]` is set:
     - `0x1435B42A0`: a blurred copy of the tonemapped output.
     - Then one of three: `0x1435C8DA0` (blur add ≥ 1: all blurred), `0x1435C9150` (a flat amount), or `0x1435BC810`
       (by depth: focus `+ 0x4`, Simple near/far `+ 0x18` – `+ 0x24`, near/far planes from the view).
     - The depth is read at the output pixel, the colour is the bent picture: **so the blur is beside what it blurs.**
- The tools' own passes are all at Present (`Main::OnPresent`): `wetlook::Apply`, `greenplane::Apply`,
  `panini::Apply`. They use the game's undistorted depth and camera, so they didn't follow the bend either.
- The Sprite DoF (`0x1435C6810`, world renderer `0x14374578C`) runs before the post-process, so it would follow the
  bend. The game never runs it (section 2).

#### The game's formula

- Shader: `systems/shaderprogramdb` (res `953bdb67341f77db9c1e0286c241d1ed069d2b8a`, only as a patch delta: rebuilt
  with `py/patched.py`, 66 MB, 7402 DXBC blobs).
  - 1792 distinct blobs mark `filmicLensDistortParams` as used (parsed from RDEF: the variable flags bit 2; for SM5
    the variable records are 40 bytes, target `(t >> 8) & 0xFF`).
  - Smallest one, `fxc /dumpbin`:
    ```
    t = v2.xy - 0.5;  r2 = dot(t, t)
    if |p.y| < 0.0001:  f = (1 + r2 p.x) p.z
    else:               f = (1 + r2 (p.x + p.y sqrt(r2))) p.w
    uv = t f + 0.5;  sample mainTexture, tonemapBloomTexture there
    ```
    with `p = cb0[11]`. No aspect correction. Vignette uses the unbent `t`.
- CPU (`0x1435CA05D` in `0x1435C9A70`, xmm6 = 1.0, xmm7 = 0, xmm8 = 0.5):
  `p = (gain, cubic, 1 / (1 + 0.5 max(gain, 0)), 1 / (1 + 0.5 max(gain + cubic sqrt(0.5), 0)))`.
  So for a positive gain the corners (r2 = 0.5) stay in the corners.

#### The fix

- `Visuals/LensDistortion.{h,cpp,hlsl}`, headers `LensDistortionVs.h` / `LensDistortionPs.h` (fxc vs_4_0 / ps_4_0,
  the commands are in the .hlsl). It's built like Panini: a copy of the back buffer, one triangle, linear clamp
  sampler. Its maths is the shader's above; the ps disassembly matches.
- `Main::OnPresent`: after the green screen, before Panini, under `!perf::DrawingPaused()`.
- `VisualsManager::ApplyLensDistortion` (each visual environment update, after the components are written):
  - With Filmic effects changed and both Enable and Lens distortion ticked: the state's `+ 0x9B0 + 0x83` is written 0
    and `lensdistortion::Set(true, gain, cubic)`.
  - Otherwise (and with no level / no state manager): `Set(false)`.
  - `CheckStillApplied` skips that field while it's redirected.
- Known differences from the game:
  - The game's vignette and film grain (same tonemap pass) and its HUD now bend too.
  - With a negative gain the corners sample further in, so vignette corners are lighter than the game's.
  - The game's sampler mode is unknown (only matters for uv outside 0 – 1: odd gain/cubic combinations).
  - If the game doesn't fill the back buffer with its 3D view (a viewport), the centre would differ. Not seen.
  - During a load with the change on, the pass keeps the last values until the next update says no level.
- The game's own lens distortion with no change made here (a game VE that sets it) is left alone: its DoF still
  wouldn't follow it. Not seen in MEC's data; not searched.

### 2. "DoF method 2" crash

- The crash: an access violation (`0xC0000005`) at `MirrorsEdgeCatalyst.exe+0x35C72EE` (reading 0x8), `rax 0`, stack
  `+0x3745791` (after the world renderer's `call 0x1435C6810` at `0x14374578C`).
- `0x1435C72E4 lea rbx, [rdi + 0x3B8]; mov rax, [rbx]; mov rcx, [rax + 8]`. This is the Sprite pass's "unchanged?"
  check on its first render target. It compares the size with `rsi + 0x160 / 0x164` and others, and skips the rebuild
  when they're unchanged.
  - The targets (6 pointers at `+ 0x3B8`) are zeroed by the post-process object's constructor (`0x1435AF760`, eh
    vector ctor `0x142E41D80` = store 0).
  - The only writer in the image is the rebuild path `0x1435C755F` (`0x1435C736C` on), after the check (whole-image
    scan for qword stores to `+ 0x3B8`). The flow from the `+ 0x288` rebuild falls into the check too
    (`0x1435C71C1` → `0x1435C72E4`), so **the first frame always crashes**.
- OFFSET_DOFFIX is exactly `0x1435C72EE`. The original tools' *Sprite DoF fix* is `jmp +0x7E` → `0x1435C736C`.
- When the pass runs (frame flags `+ 0x16`, `0x14375AF81` – `0x14375B00F`, r14 = the PostProcess settings):
  - DofMethod (`+ 0x154`) == 1 and DoF Enable (state `+ 0xAA8`); or
  - BlurMethod (`+ 0x158`) == 1 and `0x1435CE330`: DoF enabled with BlurAdd > 1e-6 (and BlurEnable `+ 0x228`), or the
    forced settings, or filmic Edge blur (`+ 0x87`, gain `+ 0x3C` > 0) or Distance blur (`+ 0x86`, `+ 0x34`).
- The game never runs it:
  - `0x143759409`: `if (!SpriteDofEnable) *(qword*)(settings + 0x154) = 0` (DofMethod and BlurMethod).
  - initfs: High / Ultra / Hyper set DofMethod_Sprite + BlurMethod_Sprite, then the PAMPLONA block
    "Disable sprite dof on high and ultra but expose it to console instead" sets SpriteDofEnable 0. Low / Medium are
    Gaussian.
- Enums from type info (enum info: `+ 0x1A` count, `+ 0x20` entries of 0x18 bytes: name, ?, value):
  - DofMethod: Gaussian 0, Sprite 1.
  - BlurMethod: Gaussian 0, Sprite 1.
  - The settings class has DofMethod `+ 0x154`, BlurMethod `+ 0x158`, SpriteDofEnable `+ 0x247`.
  - So the menu's "Method 2" was not a game value.
- **Not known:** how value 2 reached the pass. With it, the tools wrote SpriteDofEnable 0, which makes the game zero
  BlurMethod. "Sprite (bokeh)", the second entry, reaches it directly. The crash site proves the pass ran.
- Fix:
  - `VisualsManager::InstallSpriteDofGuard`, from the constructor. It checks 20 bytes at `0x1435C72E4` and
    `B8 06 00 00 00` at `0x1435C736C`, then writes `FF 25 0 <page>` over `0x1435C72E4` – `0x1435C72F1`.
    - No rel32 call/jmp/jcc lands inside those bytes (whole-image scan); the only jump in is `0x1435C7204 → 0x1435C72E4`
      itself. No short jump within 130 bytes lands inside them.
  - The page:
    ```
    lea rbx, [rdi + 0x3B8]; mov rax, [rbx]; test rax, rax; je none
    cmp byte [flag], 0; jne rebuild
    mov rcx, [rax + 8]; jmp 0x1435C72F2
    none:    inc dword [count]
    rebuild: jmp 0x1435C736C
    ```
  - It's the same register state as the old fix's jump. After the rebuild, the two values the skipped code would have
    set (`[rbp - 0x58]`, `[rsp + 0x54]`) are only compared at `0x1435C7A30` / `0x1435C7A3B` (the second group's
    rebuild check), never used as sizes.
  - *Sprite DoF fix* sets the flag when the guard is in; otherwise the old 2-byte patch.
  - The log: "Sprite depth of field: crash guard in at …" and "… the guard had the game make them (N times so far)".
  - The menu: DoF method has 2 entries. The game's SpriteDofEnable is saved in ReadFromGame and put back.
- **Not known:** whether the Sprite DoF then draws correctly (DICE turned it off on PC).

### 3. Everything else checked

#### Bugs found and fixed

- **Enum Int fields typed freely.** Type info: SimpleDofBlurFilter is BlurFilter (BfNone 0 … BfGaussian31Pixels 6),
  TonemapMethod (Linear 0, Filmic 1, FilmicNeutral 2, LinearApproxGamma 3, Parametric 4, FilmicAD 5, FilmicADDebug 6,
  None 7), BloomMethod (GaussianSimple 0, GaussianCustom 1, FFT 2), BloomDirection (None 0, Horizontal 1,
  Vertical 2). Now combos (`Field::Items`). The effect of out-of-range values in the game: not checked.
- **Filmic fields with no reader.** The only `lea` of the view's `+ 0x85320` are `0x14374669F` (post-process params),
  `0x14375AFE3` (`0x1435CE330`) and `0x143757E8E` (the Sprite pass's `+ 0x38`).
  - Reads: `0x80`, `0x81`, `0x83`, `0x14`, `0x18`, `0x24`, `0x28` (tonemap); `0x86`, `0x87`, `0x34`, `0x3C` (check);
    `0x87`, `0x3C`, `0x44`, `0x48`, `0x86`, `0x34`, `0x38` (`0x1435C6DA7` – `0x1435C6E06`).
  - No direct displacement for the other fields, relative to the view or the state manager.
  - No system shader name with flash / heat / ripple. The `g_EdgeBlur*` / `g_DistanceBlur*` are in the 12 Sprite DoF
    CoC shaders.
  - Removed: Vignetting, falloff, luminance percent; Frame flash, gain; Depth flash, colour, half distance; Edge blur
    depth target scale, matte dilate size, matte blur kernel size; Heat ripple and its 8 values.
  - The post-process params' callees `0x143547B10`, `0x143546610`, `0x1435D6980` showed no `[params + 0xB0]` load, but
    were only skimmed.
- **SpriteDofEnable restore** wrote `(original method == 1)` instead of the game's own byte.
- **Stop all changes** during a pending *Reset to game values* (0.3 s): the reset turned the change back on.

#### Checked and fine

- Component offsets vs reflected `*ComponentData` (data − 0x80 = state):
  - ColorCorrection, Dof (all 21 menu fields), FilmGrain, OutdoorLight (all 31), Tonemap (all 40), Vignette, and
    FilmicEffects (the remaining ones).
  - Sizes match: DoF 0x60, Tonemap 0x150, Filmic 0x90, …
- ImGui IDs: components under `PushID(Name)` + `###Header`; field names unique within each component. Lights are
  under `PushID("Lights")`, the green screen uses `##GreenPlane`, weather `##Weather`, snow `##Snow`.
- Locks: DrawUI and the visual environment update both under `m_Mutex`. Lights take their own lock after.
- DoF method restore runs on the path where no component is changed (`anyOverride` includes `m_DofMethodApplied`).
- Weather / Snow typed-in extremes: the code clamps rain strength, distant rain, wind amounts, volumes, intensity,
  flake size, snow cover / pile / settle, strike distances (min/max swapped is handled), fog thickness and seen
  distance.
- Green screen: distance / size clamped after the sliders.

#### Not verified

- Outdoor light: the menu writes *Final sun luminance / illuminance* and *Outer space* values with the rest. If the
  game works them out from Sun colour × intensity during its update, our after-update write would keep the old ones
  and a changed *Sun intensity* might show less than expected. Not traced.
- Weather / Snow / wet look render paths beyond the UI and clamps (thousands of lines): not audited line by line.
- Lights: inner angle > outer angle isn't stopped; what the game does then is unknown. Changing lights after a level
  change is warned about in the UI (could crash) [not verified in game].
- *Lightning brightness* goes to 4, but the bolts cap it at 2 (`GetBolts`); the flash uses the full value. It looks
  deliberate; left.
- Everything new is untested in game.

### 4. Depth of field: does it work, and the focus distance (2026-11-04)

Goal: check that the depth of field works, fix its bugs, and make the focus distance work.

#### The chain (offline + live, read-only)

- The tools write view 0's state: the world renderer calls `0x143742BD0` with `r8 = wr + i * 0x89400 + 0xB00`
  (`0x14373EAA1`). So view 0's `+ 0x84970` is the state manager's `+ 0x85470`. Live: 1 view.
- The settings at `[mgr + 0x138]` are **GlobalPostProcessSettings** (class info `0x142837118`, 179 fields):
  - `ForceDofEnable` `+ 0xBC` (int, −1 unset); floats, −1 unset:
    - `ForceDofBlurFactor` `+ 0xC0`, `ForceDofBlurAdd` `+ 0xC4`, `ForceDofFocusDistance` `+ 0xC8`
    - `ForceSimpleDof*` `+ 0xCC` – `+ 0xDC`, `ForceSpriteDof*` `+ 0xE0` – `+ 0xF0`
    - `ForceVignetteScale` `+ 0xF4`, `ForceVignetteExponent` `+ 0xFC`
  - `BlurEnable` `+ 0x228`. Live: every Force −1, BlurEnable 1, DofMethod 0, BlurMethod 0, SpriteDofEnable 0,
    IronsightsDofEnable 1.
- **Live, the game's own DoF block:** Enable 0, focus 1.5, BlurFactor 0, BlurAdd 0, filter 4, Simple max 1.5,
  Simple near 5 / 8, far 30 / 7, Sprite near 5 / 7, far 8 / 30, max 1.5, UseCameraSettings 0.
  - A game visual environment fading in briefly gave Enable 1, focus 5 → 2, factor 0.3 → 0.6, near 2/7 → 1/3,
    far 30/55 → 15/30.

#### Simple (Gaussian), in the post-process after the tonemap

- Depth blur on (`[rbp − 0x6F]`, `0x1435BE7C6`) when all of these hold:
  - params `+ 0x28` (DofMethod 0)
  - Enable, or ForceDofEnable ≠ −1
  - ForceDofEnable ≠ 0
  - blur add < 1
- Then `0x1435BFD03`:
  - Each value is Force*, else the DoF's: focus `+ 0x4`, near `+ 0x18 / + 0x1C`, far `+ 0x20 / + 0x24`.
  - Starts are kept ≥ 0. Ends are kept ≥ start + 0.01 (`0x141A11984` = 0.01).
  - The struct for `0x1435BC810`:
    - `+ 0x40` focus
    - `+ 0x44` focus − ns
    - `+ 0x48` ne − ns
    - `+ 0x4C` focus + fs
    - `+ 0x50` fe − fs
    - `+ 0x54` blur add
- `0x1435BC810`, with the depth texture (params `+ 0x38`) and not physical-camera mode (params `+ 0xB8`):
  - `dofParams = (f − ns, f + fs, 1 / (ne − ns), 1 / (fe − fs))`
  - Shader (systems DB, 3 blobs use `dofParams`): `alpha = 1 − (sat((d − x) z) − sat((d − y) w))`.
  - So it's fully blurred at `f − ns` and sharp from `f − 2 ns + ne`. The far side: sharp to `f + fs`, full at
    `f + fe`. `dofParams2` (blur add) isn't used by that shader.
- Blur size (`0x1435BFB94`): `max(BlurFactor × SimpleMaxBlur, 1)` (each Force-able), with the filter `+ 0x10`, into
  `0x1435B42A0` (its `[rbp + 0xA0]` goes to the two separable passes `0x1435C01F0`). Its exact width in pixels was
  not traced.
- Physical-camera mode: params `+ 0xB8` = view `+ 0xCDC` && DoF UseCameraSettings (view `+ 0x85419`, `0x1437466AD`).
  It uses the view's camera values (`+ 0xC8C` …) and the lens-CoC shader. The focus distance is not used then.

#### Sprite, in the world renderer (`0x1435C6810`)

- View data from `0x143757E50`:
  - `+ 0x30` DoF, `+ 0x38` filmic
  - `+ 0x48` = (DofMethod == 1), `+ 0x49` = (BlurMethod == 1)
  - `+ 0x4B` = UseCameraSettings && view `+ 0xCDC`
- Constants (`0x1435C69C0` – `0x1435C6BBA`):
  - Near / far starts are kept ≥ 0; ends ≥ start + 0.01.
  - `g_OutFocusNearStart = f − ns`, `NearEnd = f − ne`, `FarStart = f + fs`, `FarEnd = f + fe`.
  - `g_MaxFarCoCSize = height × clamp(SpriteMaxBlur × (Enable && +0x48) × BlurFactor × 0.01, 0, 1)` (k at
    `0x141A11984` = 0.01).
  - `g_AddBlur` = Enable ? BlurAdd : 0 (or Force), × BlurEnable, ≤ 1.
- CoC shader (4 blobs use `g_OutFocusNearStart`):
  - Far `sat((d − FarStart) / (FarEnd − FarStart))`; near `−sat((d − NearStart) / (NearEnd − NearStart))`.
  - Both are × MaxFarCoC, plus a vignette / add term, × 0.5.
  - So: sharp from `f − ns` to `f + fs`, full at `f − ne` / `f + fe`.
- **At BlurFactor 0 the Sprite method blurs nothing** (only Blur add).
- DebugDrawFocusPlane (`+ 0x5A`): no code addresses it (view or state manager displacement). Not implemented.

#### Fixes

- `VisualsManager::DrawDofUI` (the DoF menu): Enable, method, focus, and *Set up around this focus distance*.
  - The button writes both methods' fields:
    - f (≥ 0.1, else 5)
    - Simple: ns 0.5 f, ne 0.9 f, fs 0.2 f, fe 1.5 f, max 2, filter kept (4 if 0 or out of range)
    - Sprite: 0.1 f / 0.5 f / 0.2 f / 1.5 f, max 2
    - factor 1, add 0, Enable 1
    - It also ticks the override.
  - The distances are shown in the Sprite semantics. The Simple near pair is converted: shown sharp = 2 ns − ne,
    full = ns; written ns = full, ne = 2 full − sharp. The values are only written back when edited, with the game's
    clamps.
  - Effective blur: Sprite `% of height`, Simple width.
  - *More settings*: the other method, ironsights, UseCameraSettings (`+ 0x59`, new field, so the override pins it),
    Sprite DoF fix.
- `AutoFocusReference(base, sprite)`: with focus ≤ 0.05, it uses the middle of the method's sharp range in game
  terms: Simple `(ne − 2 ns + fs) / 2`, Sprite `(fs − ns) / 2`. Before, it used `(ne + fs) / 2` from the raw values.
- CameraManager's Auto-focus help: the "(and for Sprite, its Sprite DoF fix)" is gone.
  - The Sprite pass memsets and fills its constant block every call (`0x1435C6B46` on). Its rebuild check (sizes,
    `+ 0x421`, `+ 0x424`, `+ 0x428`) only covers its buffers.

#### Not verified

- How the button's set-up looks in game, and the Sprite method's look on PC.
- The Simple blur's width in pixels for a given factor × max.
- Whether any game camera sets view `+ 0xCDC` (physical camera) where a player could be.

### 5. Depth of field checked in game (2026-11-04)

Pictures of the frame: `frameshot` (Visuals/FrameShot.*), the back buffer at Present before the menu, a PNG via WIC
on a worker thread. Seen with a free camera looking at Faith, focus 1.21 m (the camera's focus):

- **Game values, Enable on:**
  - Sprite changes nothing (Blur factor 0, as worked out).
  - Simple only softens the far city (focus 1.5 + far start 30 → blur past 31.5 m, σ = 1).
- **Set-up:**
  - The focused face is exactly as sharp as without the DoF.
  - The background and the floor near the camera are strongly blurred in both methods.
  - But the sharp zone at 1.21 m (12 cm in front, 24 cm behind) also softened her shoulder strap (−30 %) and, with
    Sprite, her legs (−37 %) (sharpness = mean |gradient| of the luminance).
- **Look (full-size crops):**
  - Simple: a dark halo round her hair. The blurred half-size copy holds her own dark pixels, laid over by depth.
  - Sprite: no halo, a rounder and stronger blur, but a hard, slightly jagged outline round her hair.
- **The guard** (`0x1435C72E4`) caught the Sprite pass on first use, and again after the method was Simple in
  between. So the game frees the Sprite buffers when Sprite isn't used, and each switch back would have crashed
  without it.

#### The Simple blur's width (code + live, read-only, + pictures)

- Blur buffers: post-process object (`[view + 0x72940]`) `+ 0x1B0` / `+ 0x1F8`.
  - Texture `+ 0x44` / `+ 0x48`, the getters at vtable `+ 0x58` / `+ 0x60` are `0x14362CAE0` / `0x14423F450`.
  - Live: **half the frame's width and height**. GlobalPostProcessSettings: DownsampleBeforeBlurEnable (`+ 0x238`) 1,
    QuarterDownsamplingEnable 0, BlurPyramidEnable 1.
- `0x1435B42A0`:
  - Filter 0 = copy only.
  - It asks `[0x142563300]` vtable `+ 8` (`0x1434986C0` = `mov eax, 1`) and limits the filter to 3 only for 3 or 6:
    never on PC.
  - Downsample into `+ 0x1B0`, horizontal pass into `+ 0x1F8`, vertical pass back into `+ 0x1B0`
    (`0x1435C01F0` × 2).
- `0x1435C01F0`:
  - Taps per filter: 1 → 3, 2 → 5, 3 → 7, 4 → 9, 5 → 15, 6 → 31 (`0x1435C02A5` on).
  - Weights from `0x1435B5FF0(N, σ)`: `exp(−i² / 2σ²) / (√(2π) σ)`, σ = max(BlurFactor × SimpleMaxBlur, 1).
  - Merged in pairs into bilinear fetches one texel apart (`0x1435C0382` loop, offsets × the texel size).
- So the window is N texels of the half-size copy, about 2N screen pixels. σ is in those texels; above about N / 3 it
  only flattens the kernel.
- Pictures: a background edge 12 – 16 px wide (10 – 90 %) became 24 – 26 px with Simple at σ 5 (expected 2.56 σ =
  25.6 px for σ = 10 screen px) and 36 – 45 px with Sprite at max blur 3 (CoC 3 % of the frame's height, about 62 px, a disc
  about that across).

#### Fix after the pictures

- *Set up around this focus distance*: sharp at least 0.25 m in front and 0.5 m behind (still 10 % / 20 % of the focus
  when more); fully blurred at least 0.5 m / 1 m past those (still half / 1.5 × the focus when more).
- Help texts: Simple's halo, Sprite's hard edge, measured edge widths; the Simple line now shows spread / taps /
  screen pixels.
- Not re-checked in game after that change (it only moves the four distances).

### 6. Every effect checked, Outdoor light's sun (2026-11-04 / 05)

Goal: fix the VISUALS tab's bugs and make sure every effect actually works.

#### Outdoor light's derived sun (offline + live, read-only)

- The "VisualEnvironmentUpdate" hook (`0x1436ED460`) is a state copy (dst `rcx`, src `rdx`). Callers:
  - the VE mix `0x143703D60` at `0x143703EEE` (into the manager's own copy);

    physical sky); else solid = (1 − cos(radius · π / 180)) · 2π, illuminance = max(0, color · I), luminance =
    illuminance / solid, into + 0x10 / + 0x20 / + 0x30 / + 0x40, + 0x50 = 0;

- Fix: `RecomputeSun` after Outdoor light's write calls the direction and the physical sky (or the
  formula) again on the view state. Byte checks at the three RVAs, `__try` in two static helpers; a failure turns it
  off with a warning. The physical call takes a 16-byte-aligned zero vector.
- The five Final / Outer space fields left the menu (the recompute overwrites them).

#### The city's sky has its own sun

- Live, at a spot in the city: Sky Enable 1, SkyType 2, Light1TakesColorFromOutdoorLight (+ 0x606) 0,

- Fix, `ScaleSkySun`: with the physical sky and that flag 0, Light 1's color / intensity = the game's ×

#### Every effect in game

Each effect seen in game, outside in the city, with every other override off and the game's values plus one change:

wrong value for it (see below).

Sun intensity works (×4 gives the final illuminance ×4, the picture, the sky and bloom brighter), a red sun turns
the light, the sky and the sun's disc red, and the rotation works; Sky color ×4 brightens nothing (**the game zeroes

**Sky color / Ground color** (offline + live, read-only):

- `0x143736038`: state + 0x60 / + 0x70 → view + 0x845C0 / + 0x845D0. Then
  `mov rcx, [0x14256AF40]; call 0x143791B80; test al; je; both = 0`.

- The only other reader, `0x143734D33` in `0x143733C80` (rsi = rdx, r15 = 0 from `0x143733D12`, neither changed

- The lightning's sky-light part (`ApplyWeatherLook`, Outdoor light + 0x60) does nothing where this holds.

**The sun read at the hook:** read at the hook's start, before the tools write, it is the game's sun about one time
in three. The hook runs at each of the game's three state copies a frame (`0x143703EEE`, `0x14372E27D` into the view

**Chromatic aberration** (the shader calls it chromostereopsis; `chromostereopsisParams`, cb0[27] in the tonemap PS):

- CPU `0x1435C9E63` (s = + 0x14 scale, a = + 0x18 aspect, d = s − 1):
  `cb27 = (0.5 / (1 + a d), 0.5 / s, 0.5 / (1 + 0.5 a d), 0.5 / (1 + 0.5 d))`.
- PS: red at `2 t cb27.xy + 0.5`, green at `2 t cb27.zw + 0.5`, blue at uv (t = uv − 0.5).
- So the red is drawn (1 + a d)× sideways and s× up and down, the green half that. 1 = none.
- Live in the city: Enable 0, CA 1, scale 1.005, aspect 0.5. A value of 0.1 draws the red at a tenth of its size.

  - the help explains both values.

# 33. The game not closing after quitting (2026-10-27)

Goal: find why MirrorsEdgeCatalyst.exe keeps running after quitting; fix it if it's the tools. Result: **cause not
found yet** (no record of what the game did while it hung); the tools now record it next time, and three exit hazards
in the tools are fixed.

**A frozen close:** exit code 1 with hang event 1002 a few seconds before. config.ini was not saved: the tools save
config.ini whenever the window gets WM_DESTROY (Main::Run's exit, logging an error if it can't), so the tools' exit
path never ran. The window froze before it was destroyed and Windows ended the process. The freeze is in the game's
window thread or something it waits on (the tools' hooks not ruled out). Not known: whether Quit had been chosen when
it froze.

### What the records show (read only)

- **Steam's `logs\gameprocess_log(.previous).txt`** has every game process's start, end and exit code. Exit codes:
  - 0: normal end. 1: Windows closed it (each one has an "Application Hang" event 1002 four to five seconds before:
    "stopped interacting with Windows and was closed", i.e. the window was frozen and was closed).
    42: the game's own (seen before the tools existed too). -1073741819 = 0xC0000005 crash,
    -1073740791 = 0xC0000409.
  - Exit code 1 is seen before the tools existed too, though less often.
  - An infinite load (the Prison Yard one, see the loading notes) also ends in exit code 1.
- **A clean quit**: the last log lines are the level being taken out (the game takes all entities out of the level,
  the positioned model instance list goes 524288 -> 0), and the process is gone a few seconds later.
- **A frozen session leaves no record**: CT.log keeps only one previous session, so older ones are overwritten.
  No dump (WER's report queue holds only empty placeholders; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps` has crash dumps only). And
  the tools wrote nothing at a session's end anyway, so even a kept log couldn't have said where it stopped.
- Other mods in the game folder: `dinput8.dll` = Catalyst Clarity 0.2.2 (DLSS, own Present hook),
  `CryptBase.dll` (2023-01-06, not identified), `usp10.dll` = the tools' loader.
- A crash dump (0xC0000409 at CT_MirrorsEdge.dll+0x1AA430, FAST_FAIL_INVALID_ARG) had 153 threads:
  mid-game, not at exit. Not looked at further (no PDB for that build).
- With the game still running at its menu: read-only stack walk (Hang_2026-10-25_stacks\stackwalk.py) showed the
  window thread in GetMessageA (through Origin's overlay hook) from the game's pump 0x142A2FEF1, the game's main
  thread 0x142A6342B in a frame, and the tools' four threads idle (Main::Run sleeping, controller thread, wheel hook
  thread in GetMessageW, thunder thread in its condition variable). Nothing stuck then.

### The tools' end, as it was

- `WM_DESTROY` on the game's window -> `g_shutdown`; `Main::Run` saves the config and turns hooks off one by one
  (`MH_DisableHook` each, each freezing every thread); then `RunCT` deleted Main, which ran the destructors on that
  thread while the game was still closing: FaithReplay (AI despawn hold off, Faith unprotected, animation culling,
  StopPeople), VisualsManager (bounce light and exposure put back), UI (ImGui DX11 objects released), and Main freed
  while game threads could still be in a hook or the window procedure (`g_mainHandle` was never cleared).
- At the process's end (DllMain detach, other threads already stopped by Windows) the static objects go:
  `replay_audio`'s `g_CaptureThread` / `g_PlayThread` are std::thread objects; still joinable (quitting while a
  recording records or a replay plays, nothing joins them then), their destructor calls std::terminate: a crash
  at exit. Also many file-scope `ComPtr<ID3D11...>` are released there (not changed; not shown to cause anything).
- The thunder thread releases its XAudio2 engine when `g_shutdown` is set (not changed).
- None of this is shown to be what froze the window in the frozen closes: a frozen *window* means the game's window
  thread stopped pumping, before `WM_DESTROY`; the tools' code on that thread is the window procedure and the hooks
  the game calls from it.

### Changed (Main.cpp, DllMain.cpp, Util/Log.cpp + Util.h, Camera/ReplayAudio.cpp/.h)

- `Exit:` lines in CT.log: WM_CLOSE ("asked to close"), WM_DESTROY ("is closing"), "the tools stop ...", "stopped in
  N ms", DllMain process detach ("the game process is ending ..."), and the last static object's destructor
  (`#pragma init_seg(lib)`, "the tools' objects are gone"). The detach lines use `log::ExitNote` (no locks at all).
- Hang watch (Main.cpp `HangWatch`, own thread from `Main::Initialize`): `IsHungAppWindow` each second; at about 15 s
  frozen and again at 45 s, and 20 s after `WM_DESTROY` if the process still runs, it writes
  `Cinematic Tools\Hang_*.txt` / `ExitHang_*.txt` (each thread: CPU ms, start address, RIP, code addresses on the
  stack as module+offset; modules list) and a `[WARNING]` in CT.log via `log::TryWarning` (skipped if another thread
  holds the log). Read only: GetThreadContext without suspending, PSAPI module list, SEH-guarded stack reads. At most
  4 reports a session. Resolve CT_MirrorsEdge.dll offsets with the build's PDB.
- `RunCT` no longer deletes Main after `Run` (only when `Initialize` fails, and clears `g_mainHandle` then).
- `replay_audio::OnProcessExit()` from DllMain's process detach detaches the two threads.
- Offline: in a plain process (no game) both detach lines are written at exit and it exits at once. The hang watch's
  code reports a frozen window at about 15 s with the frozen thread's stack (in Sleep) and notes when it answers again;
  with the window destroyed and the process kept running, the ExitHang report comes at 20 s [not verified in game].

### Running the game without the tools

Rename `usp10.dll` in the game folder to `usp10.dll.off` (the tools' loader; with it renamed the game uses Windows'
own usp10.dll and the tools don't load); rename it back afterwards. To leave out Catalyst Clarity too, also rename
`dinput8.dll`.

### What a stuck quit is

- In a stuck quit the log has the camera off, the pause (the menu), the level taken out ("Faith gone", containers
  destroyed, the positioned model instance list 524288 -> 0), then nothing until the window was asked to close
  (WM_CLOSE, the window's X). No "is closing" (WM_DESTROY) line. Hang event 1002 and exit code 1 follow a few seconds
  later. config.ini not saved.
- Live during a stuck quit (read-only stack walk of all 153 threads): the window thread in GetMessageA
  (Origin's overlay hook) from the game's pump 0x142A2FEF1, Responding; the game's main thread in its frame loop
  0x142A6342B < 0x142A2923C < 0x142A315B5 < 0x142A2D700 < 0x1432F5C0F < 0x1432EEBC9, the frame limiter (it sleeps the
  rest of a frame through 0x142A4F8C0 -> 0x142C79070), the same place as in the infinite loading screen; no
  tools code on either; the tools' threads idle (Main::Run, hang watch, controller, wheel hook, thunder). Disk reads
  not measured.
- **A quit that works (exit code 42)**: the level taken out, then "Exit: the game process is ending" (DllMain) and
  "the tools' objects are gone", with no WM_CLOSE / WM_DESTROY: the game's quit ends the process itself about 5 s
  after the level goes, without closing its window. So the tools' WM_DESTROY exit path never runs in a working quit,
  and in a stuck one the game never gets to ending the process.
- Both the working and the stuck quit had Unbroken Shard and Bauble on and the replay keeping a sub-level for a while;
  no replay refusal of a sub-level unload was logged at the stuck quit.
- Exit code 42: the game image has two `mov ecx, 2Ah; call [0x1448158A8]` sites, 0x142ADD3C7 (after a failed check in
  what looks like an allocator) and 0x14344B6E6 (after a size check). Which import [0x1448158A8] is isn't known, nor
  whether the working quit took either.
- **Cause still not known.** Candidates: something the quit waits for after the level goes (a sub-level, bundle or
  entity the tools keep, or the game's own); whether it happens without the tools is not known.

### Capture for the stuck quit

- Hang watch also writes, with the level streaming's state in CT.log (`Exit (diagnostic):` lines, both managers' counts
  per state and the sub-levels not in, the WatchLoadScreen layout):
  - `LevelGone_*.txt` 20 s after Faith went (util::hooks::FaithGoneSince, from NoteFaithSoldier) with no loading screen
    (LoadScreenShown / gamestate::Loading), once per time she goes;
  - `Close_*.txt` 2 s after WM_CLOSE if the window hasn't closed (the window thread's stack is where it blocks).
  - At most 6 reports a session.
- Hooks.cpp: LogStreaming takes a prefix (default unchanged); util::hooks::LogLevelStreaming(prefix); g_FaithGoneSince.

### A quit that worked

- Exit code 0: level taken out, then "the game process is ending" a few seconds later. No LevelGone / Close report
  (none due).
- The free camera, a replay played, thunder, spot sounds and loading screens were all in a stuck session and in one
  that quit fine, so none of them is shown to matter.

### A stuck quit with the LevelGone/Close capture

- **Level streaming at the LevelGone and Close reports: both managers 0 sub-levels in every state.** The quit isn't
  waiting on sub-levels.
- Threads (reports in the game's `Cinematic Tools` folder): the game's main thread used 47 s of CPU in the 55 s
  between the reports, in its frame loop (frame limiter 0x1432EEBC9 then a frame's job wait); the window thread in
  GetMessageA (through Steam's and Origin's overlays) both times: not frozen when the Close report was written.
  Caveat: the reports' frames are a stack scan (stale return addresses included), not a call chain.
- Pattern in the stuck quits: the free camera was turned off shortly before (seconds to about a minute); in quits
  that worked it had been off for minutes or never on. Not proven to matter.
- Ruled out from the game's code: the zone pass batching (RunZonePassInBatches, Hooks.cpp) putting the request bits
  back. All three callers of the release / load passes (0x143C81732, 0x143C81A12, 0x143C81CD8) clear every zone's
  and region's bits 0-1 (`and byte [table + k * 8], 0xFC`) right after both passes.

### What the game's quit waits for (offline, game_image.bin)

- Main loop 0x142A29220: `while (0x142A315A0(this))`; that calls [[this + 8]] slot 0xB8 = the frame function
  0x142A2D470 and stops when it returns false; then 0x142A4F3C0, the engine's slot 0xB0, and a tail call with
  edx = 0x12 (WM_QUIT; the import isn't named in the image).
- Frame function end (0x142A2E102...): r15 = 0x142A31670([Main + 0x288]) = "keep going": 1 while
  [[Main + 0x288] + 8] is 0 (no quit), 0 once it's 1 (asked; then set to 2) or 2. When 0, the frame still returns 1
  unless ALL of: [Main + 0x48] == 0, ([Main + 0x50] ? 0x14319C9A0 : true) — `[client + 0x318] == 0x10` —, and every
  object in [Main + 0x160 .. + 0x168) answers true to its vtable slot 0x60. (Main assumed = [0x142142A48]; the new
  log checks its slot 0xB8 is 0x142A2D470.)
- `Exit (diagnostic): what the game's quit waits for (...)` gives those values and each list object's vtable / slot
  0x60 RVA, in the LevelGone and Close reports and once 120 s after the window is known (in play, for comparison).
  Read only, inside __try.

### A stuck quit: the chain, read live (read only)

- In the stuck quit: quit state 2, client state 16 (both done), [Main + 0x48] = 0x13F459030 (the same as in play),
  level streaming empty. The check's "frame function NOT as known" was a false alarm: Main's slot 0xB8 is 0x142A31650
  `jmp 0x142A2D470` (a thunk, no `this` change), so Main is the frame's object and the values hold.
- [Main + 0x48] = the server (vtable 0x141B42EE0). The frame (0x142A2DAA0...) runs the server's update as a job
  (0x142A30540, data Main + 0xD0: + 0x30 server, + 0x40 info, + 0x48 = Main + 0x118 the result) each frame; the job
  writes "finished" when the server is idle (0x1433433F0) or its update (0x1433446F0) returns false. That update
  always returns true, so only idle ends it. When [Main + 0x118] is set the frame calls 0x142A2D300, which destroys
  the server (0x142A31110, directly or as a job) and clears [Main + 0x48].
- Idle (0x1433433F0) = +0xB2 && ![[+0x70] + 0x46D0] && +0xB4 && !+0xB1 && !+0x60 && !+0x61. Live: +0xB1 = 1 (the rest
  pass). +0xB1 is cleared only at 0x14334505A (shutdown step 0x143344D90), after 0x1431515C0 (no node of a tree with
  a count left) and 0x1432EFD20 return true.
- 0x1432EFD20 waits on a resource manager ticket at [server + 0x10] = 0x0100031C (state [+0x18] = 2), made by
  0x142ABA6B0(..., 3, 0), polled by 0x142ABB590 -> 0x142AC2C50 (manager [0x1423A4228] = 0x78807EE0) -> 0x142AC4FE0:
  done when the queue's counter (manager + 0x4400 + 0 * 0xA80, word + 0x170 + gen 0 * 2) passes 0x31C. **The counter
  is 0x31B: every operation before the server's is done, the server's never is** (unchanged over minutes). The
  operation (map node + 8 = 0x724B0910) carries "carusRunnersLair" at + 0x30 (the IcarusRunnersLair bundle; full
  name not read).
- Ruled out: the replay's bundle loader +1s (the loader [manager + 0x7330] = 0x78F2FD20, shared by both managers, has
  0 entries); the zone pass batching (the game clears the bits itself).
- The replay held sub-level 0xD70ADC33 (4 recorded people) loaded through the quit (the 30 s "Faith may come back"
  wait), refusing the game's unload ~30 times a second. Other quits stuck after the replay's holds had ended, and a
  session that quit fine had a hold too. A quit also stuck with no replay bundle request. Neither shown to be the
  cause.
- **What the server's resource operation waits for is not known.**
- The quit-wait line accepts the thunk, and a second line gives the server's ticket, its state, how far its queue got
  and the operation's name.

### The Game compartment unload (a second reading, not checked)

- 0x142ABA6B0(int* handle, u16 compartment, int flag) unloads a compartment asynchronously (wraps 0x142AC3320 on the
  resource system [0x1423A4228]); compartment 3 = "Game" (0x142ABE490: 0 Static, 1 Frontend, 2 LoadingScreen, 3 Game,
  4-2003 sub-levels). So **the server's shutdown waits for the unload of the whole Game compartment**, and that unload
  never completes. IcarusRunnersLair is a sub-level whose bundle heap is its parent's (heap type 3), parent chain
  Icarus -> Game; its name on the stuck operation is why the operation shows "...carusRunnersLair" (what that name
  field means is not verified).
- What the replay keeps that touches a level's resources: ReplayGameDraws ComPtr references to the game's D3D buffers,
  views, samplers and states (freed only on a new recording or Forget, not at quit); ReplayShapes' game VB/IB ComPtrs
  and own copies; the mission-world hold and the sub-level unload hold (game objects kept alive).
- Against the D3D references being the cause: in one stuck quit "recording forgotten" (frees them) came 4 s BEFORE
  the quit, and it still stuck; in another a forget during the stuck quit didn't unstick it (ticket still not done
  minutes later). Not ruled out: an unload that can't recover once stuck.

### 2026-10-28: why some quits "close" (exit 42) and others freeze (exit 1); the DLLs

- The stuck quits seen with the ticket line were all stuck the same way: the server's shutdown waiting on the Game
  compartment's unload, queue one short (0x010003C4 / done 0x3C3; 0x0100027B / done 0x27A), operation
  'carusRunnersLair'. In play the line reads ticket 0, as expected.
- **A stuck quit "closed" (exit code 42) only because of the game's own watchdog**: after the X, the Close report
  still stuck, then DllMain "process is ending", exit code 42. Exit 42 comes from 0x14344B589 (a chunk of a timed job
  wait): it runs jobs while waiting for one (0x143447520) and, once 0x142A9FCD0's time minus the start passes its
  limit (0x142AA0050 x 4), calls the import [0x1448158A8] with ecx = 42 (0x14344B67E -> 0x14344B6E6). Inference, not
  traced: after WM_CLOSE the main thread ends up in such a wait for the stuck shutdown, and when nobody ends the frozen
  window first the watchdog does (9 s after the X there). In the exit-1 cases Windows' "not responding" close came
  first (8-17 s after X). The other exit-42 ends were probably the same watchdog (not checked).
- The Close reports of the stuck quits look alike 2 s after X: window thread in GetMessage (through the Steam
  overlay's and the EA overlay's hooks), main thread in its frame loop.
- **DLLs**: the same modules in every report (one of a session that quit fine included), except, only in the stuck
  ones: audioeng.dll, avrt.dll (Windows' audio engine, loaded with the replay's sound track), xaudio2_9.dll (the tools'
  thunder/wind), coreuicomponents.dll and two OneCore proxy stubs: loaded later in a session; the working session's
  report was written early in it, so this isn't evidence. Third-party code in the process every time: the tools
  (CT_MirrorsEdge.dll + the usp10.dll loader), Catalyst Clarity (dinput8.dll), Frosty Mod Manager's CryptBase.dll
  (game folder, 2023-01-06, PDB FrostyModSupport\ThirdParty\CryptBase.pdb), the Steam overlay (gameoverlayrenderer64),
  the EA overlay (igo64, Activation64), a graphics driver DLL, a peripheral maker's SDK, Defender's amsi/MpOav. No DLL
  stands out.

### Stuck quits ended

- Main.cpp HangWatch, each second: ReadQuitWait; stuck = Main's frame thunk as known, quit state 2, server present,
  a ticket at [server + 0x10] whose queue counter is behind it ((done - index) & 0xFFFF >= 0x8000), Faith gone
  (FaithGoneSince), no loading screen (LoadScreenShown, gamestate::Loading). The same ticket stuck for 15 s
  (StuckQuitSeconds) -> `[WARNING] Exit: the game's quit has been stuck ...`, the level streaming lines, then
  ExitProcess(42) (the game's watchdog's exit code; its own call at 0x14344B6E6 ran DllMain's detach (seen in game),
  so it goes through ExitProcess or exit too). In play the ticket is 0, so it can't fire.
- Not tried in the game. The cause of the stuck unload is still unknown; this only ends the game when it happens.

### 2026-11-01: MECMP blocked by the tools; usp10.dll checked; why the 15 s end didn't fire

- **MECMP** (0.9.0-beta.3.1: mecmp.dll, mecmp_inject.exe, its own version.dll loader). It checks game code
  before doing anything; one mismatch and it "stays inactive". With the tools in the game its build check found
  SpatialEntity::setTransform starting with E9 E0 5A C8 FC 41 18 45 0F B6 C8, expected 48 83 EC 38 8B 41 18 45 0F B6
  C8 -> inactive. Another time, with the tools in too: "15 functions and vtable slots match", all hooks installed,
  worked.
- MECMP's table (read from mecmp.dll's data, nothing run): bytes at ServerEntityCreationInfo ctor 0x14335CAB0,
  ServerEntityInitInfo ctor 0x14335CB50, Entity init 0x1431661C0, NetState::setDirty 0x14347E420,
  SpatialEntity::setTransform 0x1432EB1F0, Arena::allocFromMember 0x142A647D0, "XInput pointer store" 0x1437BA76F;
  vtable slots: PamServerCharacterEntity (0x141C3FCB0) + 0x340 applyCustomization 0x14336CF00, + 0x108
  getComponent 0x1431C6EB0; PamClientCharacterEntity (0x141C3C760) + 0x3D8 setVisible 0x143229480, + 0x108
  0x1431C6EB0; Pam/ServerCharacterSpawnEntity (0x141C4B388 / 0x141B4E0C8) + 0xD0 spawn 0x143390830, + 0x108 unspawn
  0x14338E4C0. Its own hooks are vtable slots (spawners, characters, UI system, map markers, replay updaters).
- Of the tools' 102 hooks only **ModelSetTransformBody at 0x1432EB1F0** (the replay's vehicles, Util/Hooks.cpp) lands
  on any of these; the tools write no vtable slot (CreateVTableHook unused).
- **usp10.dll** (the tools' loader in the game folder): its 44 exports are exactly the system usp10.dll's (all
  GDI32.<same name> forwards, checked); its only other act is a thread that loads CT_MirrorsEdge.dll. So it isn't buggy as a usp10 stand-in; "usp10.dll in the folder" = "the tools in the game".
- Other DLL seen: NoclipInjectedDLL.dll (CatalystNoclip) crashed the game (event 1000).
- Why the 15 s end didn't fire: in a stuck quit (frame loop + server tick job) X can be pressed before 15 s, and then
  Windows closes the frozen window first. A hang with two job waits is the job-queue help hang, not the stuck quit.
  A game start once had two
  game processes (the first exit -6, the second with "/dbrv=1" exit 0); the first held CT.log, so the second's tools
  couldn't log.
- Changes [not verified in game]:
  - Hooks.cpp: CreateHook(..., enable = true); ModelSetTransformBody created OFF; SetBodyHook(on) turns it on only
    while the replay holds actors (HoldActor 0 -> 1, ReleaseActors / last one let go -> off) and never while
    mecmp.dll is loaded; util::hooks::KeepBodyHookOffForMecmp() (the hang watch, each second) turns it off when
    MECMP comes in. The replay's own vehicle moves use the trampoline, which works either way.
  - Main.cpp hang watch: no Faith / loading screen conditions any more; ends the game (ExitProcess 42) when the
    server's shutdown waits 8 s on the same unload ticket, 1 s once the window was asked to close, or the quit
    (state not 0) is 30 s old; the quit-wait line at the quit's start and every 5 s.
