# 39. Ground level: why the streets aren't solid, and what the tools could do (2026-11-01)

Offline research from the game's data (CAS, base and patched ebx and res) and the decrypted image (BASE 0x140000000).
Nothing was read from or written to the running game. Anything not checked in the game is
marked **[not verified in game]**; things not found are said plainly.

Goal (also): check whether interiors that are drawn but not solid (e.g. the train station underneath the lair) can be
made solid. Section 5 answers that.

### 0. Short answer

Three separate things stop Faith on the streets. All three are needed before she could walk there:

1. **The streets have no collision at all.** The road surfaces are a handful of huge render-only meshes
   (`objects/architecture/roads/streamingground/ground_*`). None has a collision asset, and every placement in the city
   has 0 physics parts. She would fall straight through them (section 1).
2. **Street "kill floors".** Designers put `PamKillVolumeEntityData` volumes over the street level of each district:
   closed polygons at y ≈ 0 (−30.7 … 10.8), 4 – 61 m tall. Inside one, the server kills her (DamageType 104). The
   train station's floor reaches y = 19 (section 2.1).
3. **The fall check.** Her animation system (Ant's `RayCastCollisionProcessorAsset`) adds up how far she has dropped
   since she last touched the ground. Past `FallThreshold` (10 m in the asset's constructor; the data's value isn't
   known) it sets `HasFallenPastThreshold`. Falling from a roof to the street trips it however solid the street is
   (section 2.2).

**Can the tools fix it?** Yes in principle. Every piece is in the image and decoded below: the kill volumes' runtime
switch, the fall check, Havok's box and convex shape builders, and `hknpWorld::createBody`. But there is no ready-made
collision to switch on. Collision has to be **made**, from boxes or from the road meshes' own triangles. The ranked
options are in section 6. The train station under the lair is the same case: its meshes have no collision asset
(section 5).

### 1. Does street level have collision? (data, verified offline)

#### 1.1 The road surfaces

- The streets are drawn by about 40 meshes in `objects/architecture/roads/streamingground/`. They are placed in the
  `ground_zs` zone streamer's 16 zones (`levels/sp/sp_maincity/ground_zs/ground_zs_zs_1..16`), plus a few in
  `backdrops` and `benefactor`.
- **No road mesh has a collision asset.** A mesh with collision has a `<name>_physics_win32` res (HavokAsset type
  0x91043F65, e.g. `decal_waterpuddle_01_a_physics_win32`). None of the `streamingground/*_mesh` has one.
- **Every placement of them in every zone of the city has `PhysicsPartCountPerInstance = 0`** (script `roads.py`,
  all `levels/sp/sp_maincity` zone files).

Their MeshSet bounding boxes (local) and placements:

| Mesh | Placed at (zone) | Local box (m) |
|---|---|---|
| ground_downtown_01 | (−315.9, 67.2, −399.9) zs_16 | x −724.5…241.7, y −67.8…−56.5, z 483…1065 |
| ground_downtown_02 | same | x −131.6…597.3, y −70.3…−57.9, z −126.6…706.9 |
| ground_area_01 | (−630.0, −0.4, −405.3) zs_16 | 811 × 1.2 × 1428 |
| ground_station_01 (the train station's) | (−47.5, 0.8, 211.2) zs_1 | x −151.3…202, y −1.4…0, z −51.1…309.5 |
| ground_anchor_01 / 02 / 03 | zs_8 / zs_11 / zs_7 | 424 × 0.5 × 674 / 1292 × 10 × 764 / 858 × 0.8 × 573 |
| ground_anchor_04_a..d, 05..08, details | zs_9, zs_16 | several, some sloped (y −40…40) |
| ground_marina_01, marinaart_01 | zs_13, zs_14 | 752 × 4.8 × 744 |
| ground_release_01 / 02 | zs_5 / zs_15 | 876 × 0.2 × 614 / 507 × 11 × 977 |

- Downtown's road surface is at about y = 0. The ground traffic swarm sits at y = 0.1 – 0.3 (earlier live read,
  MEC_Reverse_Notes "Swarms"), and the kill floors' bases are at y = 0.0. **[road height per place: not decoded
  from the triangles]**.

#### 1.2 What *does* have collision down there

Every collision instance of every city zone was decoded: 307 zones, 216,082 instances, 0 failures. They come from the
zones' `staticmodelgroup_physics_win32` (hknpStaticCompoundShape instances), with each instance's world box from
its shape's Aabb. Script `zonecoll.py`, out `zc_all.tsv`.

- 22,817 instances sit low (bottom < 3 m, top < 12 m). Most are street props: bus stops, parasols, trees, canopies,
  bollards, the parked city bus, catwalks.
- **Building bases and storefront walls are solid.** For example `csg_dt_area06_cityblock02..06_storefronts`,
  `dt_area07_building09_storefront`, `anc_area02_building56`, and the train station's `trainstation_support`
  (y 0.2 – 10.9).
- **A few ground patches are solid:**
  - `area05_ground_01` (y −1.8…0.2, x −298…−205, z 18…102);
  - `csg_foundation_01` (zone 172);
  - Release's `area00_releaseexit_tunnelbusareaground`, `csg_area00_release_base_02`, `csg_rz_area01_releasegroundfiller_01/02`;
  - Anchor's `csg_anc_ground_01`, `csg_anc01_backdrop02b`, `anc_bd_detail_101`;
  - `rezoningground`.

  These are places a mission takes her to the ground (Release, the Anchor plazas).
- So the streets are **walls and props on nothing**. Between the buildings, the road itself has no collision.

#### 1.3 Live check

Not done; the data answers it. A read-only probe would ray-test down
at a street spot with the tools' `collision::Sweep` (filter 9, client world). It would only confirm "no hit until the
broadphase edge" (section 7).

### 2. What kills or respawns Faith down there

#### 2.1 The street kill floors (PamKillVolume)

**Data.**
- `PamKillVolumeEntityData` (info 0x14287FA18, size 0x20, base EntityData, no transform of its own):

  | Offset | Field |
  |---|---|
  | +0x18 | DamageType: 104 in all the city's data; 103 in one mission |
  | +0x1C | Enabled |
  | +0x1D | KillEnemies |
  | +0x1E | KillPlayer |

- Its volume is linked in: `LinkConnections` with SourceFieldId 838548383 (0x31FB3B9F), to `OBBData`
  (+0x20 Transform, +0x60 HalfExtents) or `VolumeVectorShapeData` (Points, +0x28 Height). The link usually goes across
  layers, through the SubWorldData.
- 66 base ebx and 8 patched ebx place them. Most are fans, the monorail train, and mission spots. **The ones at street
  level, all `VolumeVectorShapeData`, closed, Height as given** (script `killvols.py`):

| Sub-level (layer with the entity → layer with the shape) | Points | x range | z range | base y | Height |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| downtownarea1 (layer1_gameplay → layer0_logic) | 5 | −338…16 | 184…502 | 0.0 | 5 |
| downtownarea2 | 8 | −692…−269 | 167…463 | 0.0 | 5 |
| downtownarea3 | 11 | −580…−256 | 79…248 | 0.0 | 5 |
| downtownarea6 | 8 | −197…60 | −58…218 | 0.0 | 5 |
| downtownarea7 | 14 | −104…261 | −196…327 | 0.0 | 5 |
| downtownarea8 | 13 | −299…−14 | −445…28 | 0.0 | 5 |
| anchorarea1 | 6 | 69…528 | 321…678 | 0.0 | 20 |
| anchorarea2 | 8 | 66…481 | 40…437 | 0.0 | 27 |
| anchorarea3 | 10 | 228…742 | −251…364 | −10.6 | 20 |
| anchorarea3 (second) | 8 | 573…693 | 180…307 | 0.7 | **61** |
| theviewarea1 / 2 / 3 / 4 (streamed_areaNN_logic → _props) | 5 / 5 / 5 / 7 | 849…1200 / 661…1329 / 559…1185 / 1033…1355 | −61…273 / −767…−175 / −468…111 / −489…50 | 10.8 / −3.8 / 2.4 / −30.7 | 5 |
| trainstation (layer9_trainstation_gameplay → layer7_tr_policeoutpost_volumes) | 16 | −217…148 | 160…662 | 0.0 | **19** |
| release (layer3_release_flow → layer1_release_logic) | 41 | −81…161 | 579…1197 | −0.9 | 4 |
| construction (layer6_ct_streamed_logic → layer7_ct_streamed_gameplay) | 8 | −529…−430 | 469…562 | 9.3 | 4 |

The patched files' kill volumes were checked too (familymatters escape, savant allcom, theshard, vivelaresistance,
theview gridnode, skycity trainstation, elevators, the monorail train). All are mission spots or moving objects. None
is at street level.

**Runtime (server), decoded:**
- **Class.** `PamServerKillVolumeEntity`: type info 0x1428594A0, vtable **0x141C50698**, size 0x68. The constructor
  is in 0x14396AA40, called from the factory create 0x14396A4B0 (vtable slot 24 jumps there).
- **Fields:**

  | Offset | Content |
  |---|---|
  | +0x28 | the data |
  | +0x38 | its linked volumes (built by 0x143304CC0) |
  | **+0x60** | **KillPlayer** (copied from data +0x1E) |
  | +0x61 | KillEnemies (from +0x1D) |
  | +0x62 | the "Enabled" state now (0 at construction) |

- **On / off.** Slot 2 (0x1439726C0) is the property handler (field 0x28A000). On, it puts the entity into the update
  group (0x14396CC00 → 0x143174420); off, it takes it out (0x143174D30). Slot 15 (0x143971260) reads the initial value;
  slot 17 (0x143971050) takes it out when it goes.
- **The update group.** A global object at **[0x14257A8A0]** (vtable 0x141C50668, named "PamServerKillVolumeEntity",
  made by 0x14396CC00). Its live entities are a vector at **+0x28 / +0x30**: 0x10-byte entries {entity, u16 period
  +8, u16 counter +0xA}.
- **Each frame**, 0x143972370 (the group's vtable slot 2) runs, for every entity with bit 3 of [entity+0x18], once per
  period:
  - **if +0x60 (KillPlayer):** the player character (0x1439656C0); her alive check ([character+0x1F0] vtable slot 0);
    **inside = 0x143970D30(entity, character)**; then character vtable +0x370 (DamageType = [data+0x18]): the kill.
  - **if +0x61 (KillEnemies):** the same for every character (list from 0x143164D50, type 0x1428544B0).
- **The inside test.** 0x143970D30 takes the character's bounding-box centre (character vtable +0xB8). It tests it with
  0x14330D320(volumes at +0x38, link id 0x31FB3B9F, point). That function switches on the volume kind ([+0x20],
  1 – 6) after an XZ bounding-circle reject (+0 x, +4 z, +0x18 radius²). **[the prism's vertical test isn't decoded;
  "base y up to base y + Height" is assumed from the data]**

#### 2.2 The fall check (Ant `RayCastCollisionProcessorAsset`)

The only fall-death metric in the image. Strings and fields: `IsFalling`, `DistanceFromLastGroundHeight`,
`HasFallenPastThreshold`, `FallThreshold`.

- **The asset.**
  - Type registered by 0x142CF28A0 (its property names).
  - Made by 0x142CD15F0: 0x50 bytes, vtable **0x141A62EE0**.
  - Loaded by 0x142CCA910 (property index → offset):

  | Offset | Property | Default |
  |---|---|---|
  | +0x10 | EnablePlanting (game-state binding) | |
  | +0x18 | GroundTolerance | 1.0 |
  | +0x1C | GroundJumpTolerance | 0.2 |
  | +0x20 | IsGroundContact (binding) | |
  | +0x28 | IsFalling (binding) | |
  | +0x30 | DistanceFromLastGroundHeight (binding) | |
  | +0x38 | HasFallenPastThreshold (binding) | |
  | **+0x40** | **FallThreshold** | **10.0** |
  | +0x44 | ConstraintAxes (bits 1 / 2 / 4) | |
  | +0x48 | RayCastBus (binding) | |

- **Each update**: **0x142CE8200** (vtable slot 4).
  1. Ground contact comes from the RayCastBus hits, within GroundTolerance / GroundJumpTolerance of her height.
  2. IsGroundContact and IsFalling are written.
  3. **On contact, DistanceFromLastGroundHeight = 0.** Otherwise it adds dt ([+0x54] of the update info) × the
     vertical speed, downward only.
  4. **HasFallenPastThreshold = (−FallThreshold > distance)**, written through the binding's vtable +8 at
     0x142CE864C.
- **What it means:**
  - Walking or running on a surface the rays hit keeps resetting it. So **on solid ground the fall check never fires**.
  - A drop of more than FallThreshold metres trips it before she lands.
  - The animation graph (antstate data) does the actual death fall when this flag is set. **[the graph's use of the
    flag isn't decoded; FallThreshold's value in the data isn't known (constructor default 10 m)]**
  - **[not known]** whether AI characters use the same asset.

| Candidate | What was found |
|---|---|
| `DeathAreaTriggerEntityData` (Damage, TimeToReturn), `DamageAreaTriggerEntityData` | Not placed in any ebx (0 files). Runtime `ServerDeathAreaTriggerEntity` exists but is unused. |
| `KillAllEntityData` | 5 files, all skycity (falling blocks, maintenance tunnels). |
| `PamStaticModelEntityData.EnableOutOfBoundsCheck` (+0xE5, next to RunnersVisionVariation +0xE0, CantClimb +0xE7, CantStand +0xE8, CantVault +0xE9, CantWallrun +0xEA) | **Its reader isn't found offline.** Not in the client / server static model entity vtables (0x141C4DAD0 / 0x141C6D0C0) or the functions they call. What it does is unknown. |
| `PamMovementExclusionEntityData` (+0xA0..0xA4 ExcludeVault / HeaveUp / Hang / Wallrun / Magrope), `PamUncontrollableSlideEntityData` | Placed in the ground zones' layers (e.g. ground_zs_zs_1 layer0: 2 + 4). They block moves or force a slide; they don't kill. |
| Havok broadphase edge | The world's "body left the broadphase" handler 0x1434F35F0 hands the body's entity to the game (Research_Havok §4). Falling forever would end there. **[what the game then does to Faith: not traced]** |

#### 2.4 After death: respawn and checkpoints

- **Free roam.** `gameplay/spawners/pf_spspawn_01` spawns Faith (`CharacterSpawnReferenceObjectData`, template
  faith_notattoo). It holds `PamSafeSpawnTrackerEntityData` (info 0x14287FE40):

  | Field | Value |
  |---|---|
  | SafetyMargin | 15 |
  | PlayerTransform +0x20, OverrideTransform +0x60 | |
  | SafeMoves +0xA0 | two Ant enumeration values, 1 and 15 [their names aren't decoded] |
  | MaxSpeedForOnDistanceEvent | 1 |
  | TriggerEventOnDistance | 15 |

  It also holds `PamSafeSpawnLockerEntityData` (BlockReturnTeleport +0x18; also in `pf_unsafearea` and the security
  hubs). Runtime classes: `PamServerSafeSpawnTrackerEntity`, `PamServerSafeSpawnLockerEntity`.
- **What this implies [not traced in code]:** she comes back at the last place where she was in a "safe move". If the
  streets are made solid, a respawn could put her on the street. That works only while the tools' ground exists.
- **Missions.** `PamMissionEntityData` (info 0x142871940) has ReloadFromLastCheckpointOnFail at +0x45, among others.
  Also `PamMissionCheckpointEntityData` (`pf_l_missioncheckpoint`), `PamCheckpointEntityData` (time trials), and the
  runtime `PamServerCheckpointEntity` (type info 0x142864B80, vtable 0x141C7E750) / `PamServerMissionCheckpointEntity`
  / `PamClientCheckpointEntity`.
- **`PamplonaRestartGameMessage`** (info 0x142870CA8, 0x38 bytes, no fields): its sender isn't traced (messages are
  posted by a numeric id).
- None of this has to change to make the ground solid.

### 3. Streaming, LOD, traffic and pedestrians

- **The ground meshes are the real thing, not far LODs.**
  - One mesh per district (400 – 1400 m across), placed in the `ground_zs` zone streamer (16 zones plus the region
    sub-levels `region_ground_all / _default / _release`).
  - They stream with their zone, like the buildings, and are drawn from the roofs. **[their own LOD count: not
    decoded]**
  - Collision made for them by the tools would have to follow their zones in and out, or cover only a radius around
    Faith.
- **Traffic and crowds have no physics.**
  - Cars, flying traffic and pedestrians are members of a `SwarmEntity` (MEC_Reverse_Notes "Swarms"), moved by its
    `CrowdBoidsComponent`. Cars drive the `BoidsNetworkNodeEntityData` road network (Position, Connections,
    IsTrafficSignal).
  - Ground cars hold y = 0.1 – 0.3; only x and z change.
  - They aren't on the road meshes' collision (there is none) and have no Havok bodies. **On a tools-made ground, Faith
    would walk through the cars and the people.**
  - The parked `nonpamp_citybus_01` and bus stops are static models with collision.

### 4. Havok (hknp): adding a body, decoded

Research_Havok_2026-10-25 has the worlds:
- the client world, at `[[[[[0x142401CA0]+0x50]+0xF0]]+0x18]`, hknpWorld at +0x10;
- the server world and the client effect world.

The lair windows proved that Faith moves by the client's physics.

#### 4.1 Making a static body

| What | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `hknpBodyCinfo` constructor | **0x143F38A70** | 0x60 bytes: +0 shape, +8 reservedBodyId (0x7FFFFFFF), +0xC motionId (ctor 0x7FFFFFFF; **0 = static**), +0x10 qualityId (0xFF), +0x12 materialId, +0x14 collisionFilterInfo, +0x18 flags, +0x1C lookahead, +0x20 name, +0x30 position, +0x40 orientation (quaternion, identity), +0x50 spu flags, +0x58 local frame |
| `hknpWorld::createBody` | **0x143F41880**(world, &outId, cinfo, u8 flags) | Allocates an id (0x143F5E380; "Body buffer is full." path). A static body (motionId 0) is set up by 0x143F5E4F0 → 0x143F38340. Raises the body-created signal (world+0x3E8). **Unless flags bit 0, adds it at once**: 0x143F41A80 (addBodies, timer "LtAddBodies"; signal world+0x3F0) |
| hknpBody (0x90 bytes) | (from 0x143F38340) | +0x00 rows (translation.w = lookahead), +0x40 aabb, **+0x50 shape**, +0x58 flags, **+0x5C collisionFilterInfo**, +0x60 id, +0x68 motionId, **+0x6C materialId**, +0x6E qualityId, +0x6F shape size / 16, +0x88 userData. Bodies at [hknpWorld+0x20] |
| Moving a body | `hknpWorld::setBodyTransform` **0x143F3A6B0** | Already used by the tools (CameraManager.cpp MoveModelBodies) |
| Freeing ids | 0x143F5E830 frees marked bodies (called by createBody when no id is free) | **`hknpWorld::destroyBodies` itself isn't located yet** |

#### 4.2 Making a shape

| Shape | Function | Who uses it |
|---|---|---|
| **Box from half extents** | **0x143F2F140**(&halfExtents, convexRadius, BuildConfig*) → box polytope from an AABB 0x143F2F190 | The game's own box colliders (4.3), radius 0.01 |
| BuildConfig | constructor 0x143F2E490 | |
| **Convex from points** | **0x143F2E510**(hkStridedVertices {ptr, count, stride 0x10}, radius, BuildConfig*) | Faith's pose shapes (0x14351C970) |
| Capsule | 0x143F6B310(a, b, radius) | Character poses, physics bodies |
| `hknpExternMeshShape` (triangles of your own) | constructor **0x143F8A3E0**(this, geometry, u8, float): builds its tree with 0x144258500, then 0x143F8A9D0 | **Nothing in the game calls it.** Only Havok's class registry and loader reach the extern mesh classes. Linked but unused; would be a first use |
| `hknpDefaultExternMeshShapeGeometry` | constructor 0x143F65D10 | Registered at 0x1429D4020 |
| Vtables | ConvexPolytope 0x141D4F248, Capsule 0x141D4F448, ExternMesh 0x141D5F7E8, CompressedHeightField 0x141D5F8E8, ScaledConvex 0x141D52B68, StaticCompound 0x141D52760 | |

#### 4.3 The game's own invisible colliders: `OBBCollisionEntity`

Designers place invisible boxes with `OBBCollisionEntityData` / `PamOBBCollisionEntityData`. The train station prefab
has 11 of them.

- **Data:**
  - `OBBCollisionEntityData` (info 0x1428144B8, 0x90): +0x20 Transform, +0x60 HalfExtents, +0x70 PhysicsBodies
    (RigidBodyData), +0x78 CollisionLayer, +0x7C Material, +0x80 Enabled.
  - `PamOBBCollisionEntityData` (0xA0) adds +0x90 CantStand, +0x91 CantClimb, +0x92 CantVault, +0x93 CantWallrun.
  - The train station's use CollisionLayer 14 (**Character**: only characters collide). Most allow standing.
- **Runtime:** `OBBCollisionEntity` vtable 0x141B41918 (type info 0x1427FC690); `PamOBBCollisionEntity` vtable
  0x141C4E1A0 (0x142858650).
- **Body chain:** slot 15 (0x143335BC0) → 0x143333310 (reads HalfExtents) → 0x1435169E0 → **0x143516450**, Frostbite's
  "body from a shape description":
  - kind 1 box via 0x143F2F140; kind 2 sphere 0x143F6C460; capsule 0x143F6B310;
  - filter info = desc +0x1C (else 2), material from the RigidBodyData's;
  - createBody at 0x143516788;
  - then the game's own records (0x1434EFCA0, 0x1434EE790).
- **Filter info.** One other caller of Frostbite's body helper 0x1434EA9E0 passes filter info **0x17** (= layer 23,
  KeyframedCollisionBody). So the filter info's low bits carry `RigidBodyCollisionLayer` (table in Research_Havok §7).
  **[the other bits: not decoded]**

#### 4.4 The open risk with raw Havok bodies

- The game keeps its own record per body: `[[manager+0xF0][(id>>16)&0xFF]+0x130][id&0xFFFF]`, 0x1434EE790 /
  0x1434EE750, 283 call sites.
- Its queries return hits that other systems turn into materials, sounds, effects and entities. The sweep's result
  holds "the body's id" at +0x20.
- **How a hit on a body that has no game record is handled is not decoded.** If some caller doesn't check, a raw body
  could crash it.
- So does adding bodies from outside the game's entity system work at all. Only a guarded live test can tell (section 7).
- **Mitigation ideas [not verified in game]:**
  - copy a real static body's filter info, material and userData;
  - or make the colliders through the game's own entity (4.3), which registers them properly.

### 5. Interiors that are drawn but not solid (the train station under the lair)

- **The station under the lair.** In zone `centralcitybuildings_zs_zs_8`, the static group places, **with no
  collision**:
  - `objects/props/monorail/monorailground_trainstation_01_mesh` and `_02_mesh`, both at (19.16, 21.25, 328.94);
  - `monorailground_trainstation_barriers_mesh`, at (−75.73, 25.43, 309.09) and (29.35, 25.50, 347.69).

  Their local boxes: _01 x −18.9…60.1, y −29.3…4.5, z −391.9…379.5 (the station and track, 771 m long); _02
  x 6.9…17.3, y 4.0…4.5, z −17.1…95.9 (a 10 × 113 m slab, likely the platform, top near y = 25.8). **None of the three
  has a collision asset** (`monorailground_01_4096` elsewhere has one).
- **For comparison:**
  - The lair itself is solid: `lair_physics_win32`, the blinds, `trainstation_support`.
  - The station's skybridges are solid: `skybridge04_a/b/glass`, y 30 – 39, z 436 – 637.
  - The lair's outer shell, `lair_exterior_mesh`, has no collision asset either.
- **Kill floor below it.** The train station's kill floor (2.1) goes from y 0 to 19. A platform top near y = 25.8
  would be above it **[the prism test and the platform's real top: not verified]**.
- **City-wide** (the 307 zones that have a group collision file): 1,590 meshes are placed without collision, in
  99,462 placements. **Not one of them has a collision asset of its own.** So "drawn but not solid" is always "made
  without collision", never "collision switched off".
- 803 of them are architecture. Among them:
  - Anansi tower floors and interior facades (`anansitower_floor_a1 / b1 / b2 / c / e`, `facade_c_interior_*`);
  - storefront rows (`anc_storefronts01_*`);
  - backdrop buildings (`bd_buildingnear_*`, `bd_far_skyscraper_*`, `cornerbuilding_*`);
  - the road meshes.

  Full list: `nocoll_class.txt`; the placements are in `zc_all.tsv` (section 8).
- **What this means for making the interiors solid:** the same as the streets. No switch exists; collision has to be
  built from boxes, or from the meshes' triangles, by the tools (section 6). Mesh vertex decoding exists already:
  `mesh_vertices.py` and `meshset_head.py` read MeshSet LOD0 sections and positions.

**Suggested order:**

   Are the street floors among them?

### 9. Options A and B (2026-11-01)

Code: `Camera/GroundLevel.cpp` / `.h`; the road data in
`Resources/GroundRoads.bin` (an RCDATA resource in the DLL).

**Menu: GAME > Street level, two ticks** (config `[Misc] SolidStreet`, `NoFallDeath`; both off by default), plus a
status line.

**New findings this needed (offline, verified in code):**
- **How a Havok hit becomes the game's ids: 0x1435177B0**(physics world, flags, hit, out). The three hit collectors
  call it.
  - The hit's body is at hit +0x40. The body's **user data (+0x88)** is the game's physics id: its low 32 bits; the
    low 16 bits index the records at world +0x130.
  - With flags bit 0 it calls the record's slot 89 (+0x2C8) **with no null check**. For body records (vtable
    0x141BAC160) that's 0x1434F0D00, `[[[record+0xD0]+0x18]+0x2C][index]`, the index being the high 16 bits of the
    shape's user data (0x1434D28B0 returns shape +0x18 unless shape flag bit 2).
  - So **a body the tools make must carry a live record's user data.** The floor takes it from a real static body
    near Faith.
- **Havok body functions:**
  - `hknpWorld::addBodies` 0x143F41A80(world, ids, count, flags); createBody calls it at 0x143F41A38 unless its flags'
    bit 0 is set;
  - `removeBodies` 0x143F420B0 (timer "TtFireBodyRemoved");
  - `destroyBodies` 0x143F423E0(world, ids, count, 1) (removes first; "TtFireBodyDestroyed"). The game calls it with 1.
- **Where the game changes its physics world: 0x1434F4C80**(physics world). It does the records' deferred work, then
  destroys its put-off bodies (destroyBodies at 0x1434F4E91).
- **The street floors' identity:** the data's DataBusPeer Flags (+0x10). Each of the 18 street floors' values is
  unique among the 90 kill volumes in the game's data.
- **Road surface:** the 24 road placements are all unrotated. LOD0 sections were decoded (16-bit indices after the
  vertex data; float3 or half3 positions), leaving out water, railing and glass sections and the unnamed
  position-only copy.
  - That gives 86,402 triangles, of which 72,257 floor-like are kept (48,070 vertices, 1.44 MB, rounding under 0.5 mm).
  - Heights checked: downtown streets 0.11 – 0.16 m (the cars drive at 0.1 – 0.3 m), the station road 0.85 m.
  - **No road mesh in The View, at area05's own solid ground, or the construction spot sampled.**

**What the build does:**

| Part | How |
|---|---|
| **A1, kill floors** | A hook on the inside test 0x143970D30 says "not inside" for the 17 street floors (Release's third warehouse is left out) while Solid street is ticked **and** the floor is in the game's physics. Any other kill volume Faith is in is logged once by its Flags, so a missed floor would show. |
| **A2, fall death** | A hook on the fall check's run 0x142CE8200. For an asset with vtable 0x141A62EE0 it raises FallThreshold (+0x40) to 1e9 while ticked, and puts the original back on the first run after unticking. The original value is logged (the data's real value, not known offline). All characters using that asset are affected. |
| **B, the floor** | A static box, 16 × 2 × 16 m, top at the road height under Faith (the highest road surface no more than 0.6 m above her feet), tilted to the road up to 35°. It is moved when she is more than 1 m from its middle or the road under her differs by more than 3 cm. No floor where there is no road data, or when she is more than 0.5 m below the road. |

**How the floor is made:**
- It is made, moved and destroyed only inside a hook on 0x1434F4C80, before the game's own deferred work, for the
  client world.
- Shape: BuildConfig, then `createFromHalfExtents` (convex radius 0.01, as the game uses), shape user data 0.
- Body: hknpBodyCinfo, then createBody with "don't add". Its user data is set before it is added, so nothing can hit it
  with user data 0. Then addBodies, then setBodyTransform. Removed with destroyBodies(…, 1).

**Where the borrowed ids come from:**
- The camera hook sweeps round Faith (18 sweeps: down, two rings of 8 at +1.2 m and +6 m out to 80 m, up). It does
  this every 2 s, or at once when the current body's record goes.
- The hit hook gives each sweep's body ids.
- A body is taken only if it is static (motion 0), collision layer 1, its record is a body record pointing back at it
  in this world, and the record's material table can be read.
- Its filter, material, quality and user data go to the box. The first 12 bodies turned down are logged with the
  reason.

**Safety rules:**
- Every function's bytes are checked before anything is hooked.
- Every read of game memory is guarded.
- A fault in a Havok call turns the floor off until the game restarts.
- Before any operation, the floor's body must still have the tools' shape. A world not flushed for 3 s while another
  is wanted is taken as gone.

**Not known [not verified in game]:**
1. Whether 0x1434F4C80 runs for the client world every frame. If not, the status stays at "hasn't taken it yet".
2. Whether creating a body there is safe; the game destroys bodies there.
3. Whether layer 1's filter really has the layer in its low 5 bits.
4. Whether Faith's movement stands on it; the lair windows showed she moves by the client world.
5. The street floors' runtime Flags (logged when spared).
6. What the death fall does with the flag off.
7. Footstep sounds on the floor (the borrowed record's first material).

### 10. The crash, the stairs, water (2026-11-01)

#### 10.1 The crash
- **What:** 0xC0000005 at +0x351784F, reading 0x1B9, inside the hit-to-ids function 0x1435177B0, through the tools' hit
  hook (seen in game).
- **What it read:** `edi = 0x010001B8` was the floor's borrowed user data. The record slot 0x1B8 held
  0x1B9: a free-list link, so the record had been freed.
- **Where the game frees records:** only in the physics world's flush 0x1434F4C80. It writes `records[idx] = 0`, then
  the free head (u16 at world +0x150), then the head = idx; the live count is at +0x152. It's the only writer of
  +0x150 / +0x152 in the physics code.
- **Why the floor still had the dead ids:** the tools did their floor work *before* the game's part of that flush.
  Once Faith was far from the body the ids came from (e.g. in The View), the sweeps found no body record to
  lend ids, so the old ids stayed, the area unloaded, and the next hit on the floor
  crashed.
- **Fix:**
  - **Right after** the game's part of each flush, the floor's ids are checked. If their record is gone, the floor takes
    the wanted body's ids, or any live static body record found by going through the world's records. If there is
    none, the floor is destroyed. Records only die in that flush, so nothing can hit the floor in between.
  - Ids that died are never written onto the floor.
  - The camera side falls back to any live static body record when the sweeps near her find none.
  - **Safety net:** a hit on the floor whose record isn't a live body record is left unconverted (the collectors'
    default "no object", −1) and logged once. It isn't expected to happen.

#### 10.2 The stairs
- **The bug:** the box could be made with its top up to 0.5 m over her feet (`BelowLimit` 0.5, and surfaces up to
  0.6 m over her feet). Coming up stairs from under the street, it appeared round her feet and didn't hold her
  (seen in game).
- **Fix:**
  - The box is made only on a surface no more than 0.15 m over her feet.
  - Standing on it, a rise up to 0.45 m (a kerb) lifts it, with 1 s to be lifted onto it.
  - Her feet 0.25 m under its top otherwise means she's in or under it, and it's let go.
  - Surfaces only above her: "below the street", no box.

#### 10.3 Water
- **The problem:** the road meshes' water sections (`M_Water` of the marina, `m_water_01` of the station and Anchor)
  had been left out, so over the marina there was no floor. By the marina in The View (x ≈ 1000, z ≈ −53) she
  went from the floor at y 0.78 to no street under her, and died (seen in game).
- **Fix:** the water is in the data now. That's 72,432 triangles (+175), water at y ≈ 0.1 by the marina's quay at 0.78,
  checked on a 5 m grid there.
- **What it doesn't cover:**
  - the rooftop water (`waterplane_01`, 146, at y 38 – 79);
  - The View's water colliders (`vw_waterplane_collider_*`, which already have collision).

  - anc_street_platformx3 (4, an 81 m long flat platform);
  - highway_elevated_* (backdrop highway pieces, 80 – 230 m long);
  - highway_pillar_01.

**Can the tools make them solid? Yes, with the same parts as the floor (sections 4 and 9), no new game code:**
1. **Furniture as boxes near Faith.**
   - Offline: each mesh type's box or boxes, from its LOD0 vertices.
     - One box for compact props: bench, bollard, bin, pillar, parked car, kerb plants, divider.
     - A box per height band for props with overhangs: a lamp's pole and arm, a parasol's pole and top, a sign's post
       and plate. One box of a lamp's whole size would block 4 m of pavement.
   - With every placement's rows, they go into a small data file in the DLL like GroundRoads.bin.
   - At run time: static box bodies for the placements within about 40 m of her (shape per box size, made once),
     made and destroyed as she moves, in the flush, with the same borrowed ids. Each one's ids are checked after
     every flush (10.1).
2. **Bridge decks and platforms:** their floor-like triangles join the floor's surface data. The floor then holds her on
   a deck and picks the road under it when she's below (it takes the highest surface no more than 0.15 m over her
   feet). Their railings would be boxes as in 1.

**Not known [not verified in game]:**
- how many bodies the game takes comfortably (the tools gave it room for 65,536);
- the cost of making and destroying them as she runs;
- whether she vaults or climbs these boxes like real props: the moves come from the surface's flags (CantClimb …),
  which a borrowed record only partly gives.

Hits on them report the borrowed body's material (footsteps, bullet marks).

### 12. Random deaths and the death loop (2026-11-01)

- **Cause:** the street kill floors spared her only while the floor box was in the game's physics. Where the road
  data has a gap, or at a respawn at street level before the box was made, the kill floor killed her. That gave a
  death loop (seen in game).
- **Fix:**
  - the kill floors spare her whenever Solid street is ticked;
  - the void: when she falls below y −100, the game's fall check works even with No death from long falls ticked,
    so a fall through a gap ends.

### 13. Fixed ground tiles, solid props, bridge decks (2026-11-01)

Goal: make the props and bridge decks solid too, and stop Faith falling into the void going down a slope and then up a
slope.

#### 13.1 Why one box under her fails on slopes
- The old floor was one 16 m box that followed her. It was made again under her whenever the road under her was 3 cm
  off its top.
- A box made or moved round her feet doesn't hold her (seen in game, coming up stairs). On a slope after a slope it was
  raised into her.
- That's the reasoning from the code and the logs; the fall wasn't reproduced in the game. A second cause on steep
  streets was found offline, which the tiles had too until it was fixed.

#### 13.2 The ground now (GAME > Street level > Solid street)

**Tiles**
- Box tiles whose tops lie on the road, on a world grid of 2 m squares within 8 m of her (kept to 10 m).
- A square is split into 1 m and then 0.5 m squares where the road at its middle and its four corners doesn't lie on
  one plane within 6 cm (kerbs, holes, stairwell openings). Overhang past a hole is at most 0.25 m.
- 1 m thick. A tile tilts with the road up to 35° (steeper: level), and its sides are lengthened by 1 / cos so tilted
  tiles meet.
- **A tile never moves.** Its key is its square plus the road triangle under its middle.

**Which road a point takes**
- The highest road no higher than her feet + 0.5 m + 0.8 m per metre from her, at most + 2.5 m.
- So she gets the street under a bridge when she's under it, and the deck when she's on it.
- 0.35 m per metre (the first try) left the squares just uphill of her untiled on streets steeper than 19°: the slope
  fall (found offline).

**Near her (0.75 m)**
- A new tile is made only if its top stays at or under her feet + 3 cm everywhere within 0.3 m of her: where she can
  be by the time the flush makes it.
- A near tile that's too high is kept if it's there, but never made ("keep only"). So the plan never takes away a
  tile for being near her.
- A tile she's 0.25 m under (in it or below it) is let go.

**The rescue**
- When nothing holds her and the road is up to 0.4 m over her feet (the top of stairs short of the street, or real
  ground under the drawn road), a level tile is put at her feet. It goes in that square or one up to 0.25 m beside her.
- It's placed under her feet by twice her drop since the last frame.
- It stays asked for until it's made.

**Faith missing for under 1.5 s** (her transform unreadable for a frame) leaves the ground as it is.

**Props**
- `Resources\GroundProps.bin`: 3,243 boxes of 109 sizes, from 34 street prop meshes (section 11), at every placement.
  7 mirrored placements have their forward axis turned round.
- Made within 40 m of her, kept to 50 m, never round her (her feet to her head).

**Bridge decks**
- The floor-like triangles of `anc_streetbridge01`, `anc_street_platformx3` and 5 `highway_elevated_*` pieces were
  added to `GroundRoads.bin`: 74,178 triangles.
- Dense 16 m cells (more than 48 triangles; 750 of them) get a 2 m grid of their own.

**Havok**
- All bodies are made in the physics flush, 32 per flush, nearest first, and destroyed in one batch.
- They all carry one donor's ids, checked right after each flush: rebound to another donor, or destroyed (10.1).
- The hit safety net looks bodies up in a bit set by id.

**The body buffer**
- When the body buffer is full, Havok's createBody writes past it (Research_Havok_2026-10-25 section 4).
- So nothing is made while fewer than 4,096 of the world's places are free.
- The count is at hknpWorld + 0x68 (the body manager is at + 0x10, its count at + 0x58), checked in the id allocator
  0x143F5E380: `inc dword [rcx + 0x58]`. The free list head is at + 0x24, and 0 means full.
- The client world wasn't seen past a tenth of its 65,536 (seen in game).

#### 13.3 Found offline

- With the changes below, the planning code makes no tile into her (within her capsule with its top 5 cm or more over
  her feet), never takes the tile she stands on with nothing else under her feet, and doesn't let her fall through (a
  drop of more than 0.5 m with a road just over her, within 1 m). Offline, with a simulated Faith walking on the bodies
  the plan makes (a 0.35 m capsule, 0.45 m steps, gravity; the flush taking the plan two frames late); not counted:
  steep places (the road within 0.6 m spans more than a step: embankments, kerb faces, deck edges), spots with another
  road under 2.2 m over her (she can't stand there), and the data's edges.
- The dense cells' grids matched the 16 m cells on 400,000 points (offline).
- Tile keys round-tripped 100,000 times (offline).
- Up to 1,052 bodies near her (a dense plaza), usually 300 – 800 (offline).
- Planning takes 0.15 ms a frame on average, 6 – 10 ms at most (offline).

**What was found and what was changed**
1. The reach per metre (0.35 → 0.8, per point): squares uphill of her had no tile on steep streets.
2. Tiles kept only because they existed could be made again near her, and a plan made in a dip of her feet dropped
   the tile under her. Now: the Make flag (keep only), and blocked tiles stay in the plan.
3. The rescue tile changed key every frame until made, so the next plan took it away. Now it's carried over.
4. "Held" counted tiles that weren't there.
5. Up a slope at a sprint, a tile was made 5 – 9 cm over her feet. Now the 0.3 m lead.
6. Falling fast downhill, the rescue tile was made over her feet. Now it's lowered by her drop.
7. At ragged road edges, the square under her has no road at its middle. Now the rescue and "held" reach 0.25 m.

**Not covered offline [not verified in game]**
- Havok's real character (stepping, sliding, push-out from a box);
- the game's own collision;
- real stairs;
- the game's thread timing;
- walking into props;
- whether she vaults or climbs the boxes;
- the cost in the game.

This ground was then seen working in game.

#### 14.3 Steps that sound like the surface (2026-11-02)
- **Before:** every tile and prop carried the one borrowed body's ids, so a hit on them reported that body's
  material. Every step on the street sounded like whatever that body was.
- **How the game picks a step's sound** (Research_Weather_2026-10-25 section 21):
  - the foot impact's surface lookup 0x1439AE870 takes the contact's MaterialDecl;
  - byte 2 indexes the city material grid's MaterialIndexMap, which gives the MaterialSoundId;
  - Faith_Footplant's wave switchers play by that id.
- **The sound ids** (Faith_Footplant's waves, read again):

  | Ids | Surface |
  |---|---|
  | 0 – 3, 9, 30 – 35 | concrete (3: gritty) |
  | 4 | marble |
  | 5 | gravel |
  | **6** | **tarmac** |
  | 10 – 19 | glass |
  | 20 – 29 | metal |
  | 32 | tarp |
  | 40, 41 | mattress |
  | 50 – 59 | wood |
  | 60 | shallow water |
  | 61 | concrete with a water layer |
- **Where the decl comes from:**
  - The hit conversion 0x1435177B0 (the hit hook's function) copies the body record's material into `out + 8` when the
    query's flags byte has bit 0. Its default is used when that isn't set.
  - Its three callers are the game's three hit collectors (0x143512F5D, 0x143513151, 0x143513333).
  - The foot lookup's contacts carry the decl at + 8 too.
  - **[not verified in game]** that the foot contacts come only through it.
- **The change:**
  - Every road triangle and prop box has a surface (data version 2; `groundgen2.py`, otherwise byte-identical to
    version 1).
  - Each body's id carries its surface (a byte per id), and after the conversion a hit on one of the tools' bodies
    gets that surface's decl at `out + 8`.
  - The weather's puddle swap (byte 2 → 16 in the foot lookup) still works on top.
- **The decls:** each one is used by the city's own collision (`matdecls.py` counted every zone's
  MaterialDecls by part).

  | Surface | Decl | Map | Sound id | The game uses it for | Given to |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | tarmac | 0x12608000 | 96 | 6 | (1 part) | roads, markings, the far ground: 13,223 triangles |
  | concrete | 0x12078000 | 7 | 1 | its street set's kerbs | pavements, plazas, kerbs, decks: 60,780 |
  | water | 0x12108000 | 16 | 60 | The View's water colliders | water: 175 |
  | metal | 0x12028000 | 2 | 20 | signs, lights, construction fences | signs, lamps, cars, bollards, benches |
  | tarp | 0x123F8000 | 63 | 32 | tarps | parasol tops, site fences |
  | vegetation | 0x5E118001 | 17 | 0 | shrubs, trees | kerb plants |
  | bin | 0x12278000 | 39 | 27 | trashcan_01 | bins |
  | pillar | 0x12328000 | 50 | 3 | concpillar01 | highway pillars |

  - The benches' metal is a guess from their look (light grey slats); the game has no solid bench to compare with.
- **Offline:** on the version 2 data nothing is made into her, pulls her, or lets her fall through; tile keys with
  surfaces round-trip.
- **[not verified in game]:** the sounds themselves.

  - decals and flat dressing, trims and edgings;
  - cables, wires, ropes;
  - flat panels under 6 cm, and thin panels over 4 m under 15 cm thick (facade layers, sign plates: a box would stand
    off the wall);
  - things smaller than 30 cm, and floor litter (under 15 cm tall, lying flat);
  - grass, leaves, flowers;
  - effects, light beams, holograms, screens;
  - gameplay helpers (runner's vision arrows, triggers);
  - runner helpers: swing poles, climb pipes, ladders. Their moves need them as the game has them;

  (121 MB): the 17,361 from before, 2,243,500 new, and 10,687 roof boxes.

#### 16.4 How the boxes follow the drawn shape (hybridboxes.py, leftgen.py)

- **Small props** (≤ 5 m, or pole-like ≤ 1.5 m across): propsgen's band boxes, as before.
- **Trees, bamboo:** band boxes of the sections that aren't leaves.
- **Barriers, fences, thin long things:** thin columns (below).
- **Everything bigger** (buildings, roofs, plazas, walkways, the station, boats, highway decks, cranes): **hybrid**.
  - **Columns** of 0.25 m (meshes up to 200 m across) or 0.5 m. In each, the crossings of the faces that face up
    (tops) and down (undersides) give runs: from a top down to the next underside under it.
  - A top with nothing under it goes down to the mesh's lowest point if the mesh is closed (its undersides' area at
    least 0.6 of its tops'). Otherwise it's a 0.3 m slab, so single-sided canopies, sails and eaves stay open under them.
  - A double-faced plane (its underside on its top) is a 0.1 m slab.
  - Tops and bottoms are kept to 0.1 m. Equal runs are merged into rectangles (sparse, both ways round, the fewer kept).
  - **Thin columns** are for the near-vertical triangles a column doesn't hold within 0.3 m: poles, walls under a slab,
    lattices, railings. Points every 0.125 m, in 0.25 m cells, each cell solid from its lowest point to its highest
    (± 0.05 m). So they never stand over what's drawn. An earlier voxel version could stand up to a voxel (1 m) over a
    floor and was dropped.
- **Budget:** a hybrid mesh may come to 120,000 boxes a placement (240,000 over all its placements). Over that, the
  **envelope**: each column from its highest drawn top down to the mesh's lowest point (tops as drawn, what's under
  an overhang filled), its cell doubled until it fits. Far skyline backdrops (bd_far_*, backdrop_buildingsfar /
  central, backdrop_mountain, the far ground) get 3,000 a placement. The KrugerSec backdrop cluster (59 × 167 m,
  fully detailed) came to 1,000,907 full column boxes; its envelope is 23,061 at 0.25 m, tops within 0.1 m at 97 %
  of spots, 0.3 m at 99.9 %.
- **Coverage test fixed:** a near-vertical triangle counted as held when any run within the 3 × 3 neighbouring
  columns (± 0.375 m) reached its height ± 0.3 m. A thin rail beside a post was then left with no box of its own: the
  station's railings had 20 – 30 % of their top rail spots more than 0.3 m under the drawn rail. Now a neighbour's run
  counts only for a point within 0.1 m of their shared side, and ± 0.15 m in height: 97.7 % / 100 % within 0.1 m.
- **Meshes with no vertex chunk** (the yacht, airduct cloths, a banner, a mountain) keep their LOD data inline in the
  MeshSet. It starts at the LOD's +0x78 (the block) plus +0x74 (the LOD's offset). Checked: the only offset whose
  indices fit was 0xE30 for the yacht = its +0x78.
- **Box tops against the drawn tops (topcheck.py, 20,000 random spots a mesh, box top − drawn top):**

  | Mesh | Within 0.1 m | Within 0.3 m | Edge spots (box only / drawn only) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Anansi plaza | 99.2 % | 99.4 % | 55 / 10 |
  | station track and hall (`_01`) | 99.5 % | 100 % | 157 / 77 |

#### 16.6 The tools' side (GroundLevel.cpp)

- **Props loader:** up to 4 M shapes and 64 M boxes (was 4,096 shapes).
- **A grid over x / z** (32 m cells, or coarser so it's at most 4,096 a side) of the box indexes. Boxes over 8 cells
  across sit in a list looked at every time. For section 16's data (2,271,548 boxes, 48,872 sizes) the grid should
  come to 435 x 448 cells of 32 m, with 626 wide boxes.
- **PlanProps searches ring by ring** out from her cell, to 50 m. It stops once more than 3,000 are found and 3,000 are
  no further from her than the next ring can be (a box only in further cells is at least the gap to the side of the square done). Only a
  distance and an index are kept per box until the 3,000 nearest are picked.
- **Height:** boxes are made within 40 m over or under her feet, and kept within 50 m.
- **At most 3,000 prop boxes**, the nearest, where they're dense (the menu line says "(the nearest)").
- **A box whose top is at or under her feet is made even when she's at it** (a floor she stands on can't hold her
  inside it). Before, a respawn onto a plaza box not yet made would have dropped her through it.
- **Wood:** surface 9 = 0x120B8000 (map 11 → MaterialSoundId 50, wood; 5,207 of the city's own parts use it).
  Checked in the material grid (mg_sound.py on mg_full.txt).
- Help text and GroundLevel.h updated.

The full generation came to 2,533,434 boxes (135 MB). Checking it found three things:

   | Mesh | Block | What it is | Judged |

The deck has its own boxes in full (0 of 3,000 deck points over a street: it is over the water) |

### 17. Places still not solid, indoor spaces, the Bauble's ruins, and the frame time (2026-11-02)

Goal: fix the places still wrong after section 16 (the station hall, the Bauble plaza and the other plazas, the street
barriers, the walkway hall by Everdyne, the Ocean Pier buildings, the parasols at The View's marina, the underpass and
its walkway, an invisible wall before a bridge that isn't solid, an arch by a transit hub, the Bauble mall whole or
broken), find what costs frame time, and find solid blocks inside indoor playable areas (one in the lair).

#### 17.1 A roof over a floor was filled down to the floor

- **The cause.** hybridboxes' columns go from a top down to the next underside under it. A roof or canopy drawn
  single-sided (no underside) over a floor went down to the floor's underside. The Everdyne walkway (`bd_walkway_01_
  emocustom_08`) was one box from 6.18 to 9.28 m: Faith walked on its roof and its hall was a wall (seen in game).
- **The fix.** Another top 1.5 m or more under a top, before any underside: the upper one is a 0.3 m slab and the
  solid starts again at the lower one (column_runs' open_gap).
- **Tops held within 0.1 m** (topcover.py, before / after): walkway `_08` 62.9 / 97.9 %, `_04` 74.4 / 97.7 %, the
  Bauble plateau `bd_krugersec_building_06` 94.5 / 98.8 %, the Anansi plaza 93.5 / 99.1 %, familymatters_building01c
  96.2 / 99.3 %. Meshes with no roof over a floor are the same (station platform, monorail station, museum02).
- The walkway's stairs had 3.1 m blocks under each step; now 0.5 m steps.

#### 17.2 Band boxes and canopies

- **The parasols** (`vw_parasol_bd`, placed 2.6 times its size): its pole band's box took its 0.8 m base plate's width
  up to the canopy, a 2.1 m block from the ground to 4.79 m. Its hub has no underside, so the hybrid's closed fill made
  a 2.6 m column down to the ground too.
- **The fixes.** Band boxes only for meshes up to 2.5 m tall (BAND_MAX); taller ones hybrid. Canopies (parasol,
  umbrella, canopy, awning, tarp) never filled under them. The parasol is now a base slab, a 0.25 m pole (0.65 m at its
  scale) and the canopy from 5.5 m.
- **The first props set and the solid set** (groundgen2.py, solidgen.py: band boxes and voxels) are now made by
  leftgen.py from their own placements, like the rest (its 'base' source; GroundProps starts empty).

#### 17.3 The road meshes' walls

- GroundRoads.bin has the road meshes' faces that face up only, and none of their railing / glass sections; the ground
  tiles are floors, never made over her feet near her. So street barriers, planters, the Ocean Pier's buildings
  (part of `ground_anchor_05`; their roof at 4.9 m was road data) and the walkways' railings had no walls.
- roadwalls.py: their near-vertical faces (|ny| <= 0.3) and all of their railing / glass sections, water left out;
  points every 0.1 m along each triangle's longest side and up its height (the thin-column sampler's grid by the longest
  edge would put millions on a long kerb), in 0.25 m cells, each cell's runs as hybridboxes.sample_columns; kept 0.4 m
  tall or more (drawn 0.3 m or more: kerbs and steps stay floors). 180,805 boxes (50 % up to 1.45 m, 90 % 10.85 m).

#### 17.4 Indoor spaces (indoorcheck.py)

- **The test.** The game's own collision parts (zc_all.tsv, 20 m across or less) whose middle lies inside one of the
  props' boxes: a box filling a space the game furnished, so a space someone walks in.
- **Found:** 2,433. `lair_exterior_mesh` held 1,521 of them (the lair's pipes and ducts): the shell's roof top and
  its floor's underside were taken as one solid round the room. Also both Family Matters buildings, the Rezoning
  warehouse interior, the KrugerSec train tunnel, the Anansi tower's interior facades and floors, grid-node details and
  more (42 meshes, indoor_open.txt).
- **The fix: shells.** For those, every top is a 0.3 m slab and nothing goes down to an underside; the walls are thin
  columns. Band-box ones among them are hybrid, unless they have over 2,000 placements (gridnode_b_384x256_detail's
  2,927 went to the envelope and dropgen left its turned ones out: it keeps its band boxes).
- **After:** 508; the lair 14 (beams and pipe joints in its own roof slabs and walls). The rest: the Shard top's
  inner walkway on its own beams (y 1,388), wall-mounted parts in walls, shelves round their books.

#### 17.5 The Bauble's ruins

- The Bauble is streamed by camera triggers (Hooks.cpp, Unbroken Shard and Bauble): BaubleMall (the whole mall:
  `bauble_mesh`, the game's own collision; Faith can stand on its top at y 125.9, seen in game), BaubleDestruction (its
  collapse, the mission) and BaubleRuins: `bauble_02_rubble` and `_rubbleb`, no collision.
- gatedgen.py: their boxes (103,734) in group 1, the surface byte's high 4 bits. GroundLevel.cpp makes a group's boxes
  only while it's on: util::hooks::BaubleRuinsTrigger() (the BaubleRuins trigger's registered flag), read once a
  second; not set up counts as off. So the ruins' boxes never stand inside the whole mall.
- Offline: none of them planned at the ruins with the group off, 3,000 with it on.

#### 17.6 The frame time

- **The biggest, from the weather's own diagnostic** (seen in game): the wet look's GPU pass 5.5 - 8.1 ms a frame
  (most 14.9), its game-thread work 0.76 - 1.01 ms (roofs 0.70 - 0.92, most 6.2; people kept dry spikes to 7.7 ms).
  Not Street level's files (Weather.*, WetLook.*).
- **Street level's planning** looked at every box within 50 m each frame. Now a cache (PlanProps): the boxes within
  PropKeepRadius / PropKeepY + 2 m of where she was, or the nearest 8,000 of them. A frame's come from it only when
  that's exactly what the whole search gives: she's within 2 m of where it was gathered, and either every box in reach
  is in it or the nearest 3,000 wanted are nearer than the furthest gathered less how far she's moved (a box's distance
  changes no more than she moves). Else it's gathered again, and failing that the whole search runs.
  - Offline, on the final data: no frame differs from the whole search (ties at the cut aside); 0.156 ms a frame
    against 0.370 (most 5.7 against 8.8); gathered on 6 % of frames.
- **Its timing in the game:** "Street level (performance, diagnostic)" every 10 s while Solid street is on: planning a
  frame (most), gathers, the physics flush's part (most, flushes), bodies made and destroyed.
- **The log:** the replay's diagnostics write the most lines; each line is a mutex, a write and a flush (with the
  console off), so only bursts of hundreds cost a frame.

#### 17.7 Meshes with 4-byte indices (the DICE roof)

- Goal: make the DICE building's gravel roof solid (Faith could stand on its railings but not on the roof, seen in
  game).
- **The cause.** leftgen.sections read every index buffer as 2-byte. `bd_krugersec_building_04_clustered` has
  121,600 vertices in its first section, so 4-byte indices (1,946,508 bytes for 486,627). Read as 2-byte, its first
  section was wrong triangles (the full columns came to 1,000,907, so it went to the envelope), and its `Roof`,
  `lambert1` and `DICE` sections failed the index check and were left out: the gravel roof was never read.
- **The fix.** 4 bytes when the sections' indices fill the index block at 3 bytes or more each (2-byte meshes are 2.0 -
  2.7: padding between sections). Of 694 meshes (made, roofs, roads), 3 are 4-byte: the DICE cluster, and the roof step's
  `con_dreams_building_01_edited` and `bd_krugerseccompound_holeintheground`; the roads are all 2-byte.
- **After:** the DICE cluster is 6,677 hybrid boxes (no envelope); its roof held within 0.3 m in 98.2 % of 0.5 m cells
  (17,252), round where she stood all of it but the roof's diagonal edge. The dreams roof 232 boxes, the pit 2,864.

#### 17.8 Other changes

- roofgen.py: only the triangles reaching the collision's top less 1.5 m (upright placements), cached (the dreams
  building took over 29 minutes whole, 20 s clipped).
- leftpar.py: leftgen's and roofgen's meshes in parallel (5 - 6 workers), each with its own full-count file, merged.
- **The final data:** 2,909,707 boxes of 64,753 sizes (155 MB); 247 MB in the game; loads in about 0.2 s. Offline:
  nothing made into her, pulled, fallen through or blocked; the cache never differs from the whole search.
- **Not found yet:** the station hall's hole (from its platform at 34.8 m, off its west end onto the escalator's foot
  and down); the arch by the transit hub (nothing arch-like without collision near the spot; likely `ground_release_02`,
  a road mesh: its posts now walls, its beams road floors).

### 19. The game's own collision read, and every roof it doesn't hold (2026-11-03)

Goal: make solid every roof in Anchor, The View and the other zones that isn't. Comparing drawn roofs
with the collision parts' boxes isn't enough (the station hall: one box as big as the station, its floor not in it), so
the collision itself was read.

#### 19.1 The zones' collision, decoded (hkshapes.py, hkworld.py)

- Each zone's `staticmodelgroup_physics_win32` holds two Havok packfiles (the same layout; the first is read). hkpack's
  fixup tables don't read right here (its "global fixups" are floats), so the shapes are found by their order:
  - the root `hknpStaticCompoundShape`: its instances, 0x80 bytes each from +0xB0: rotation columns (3 x 16 bytes),
    translation (16), scale (16); the physics part number is the u16 at +0x54 (not the instance's place in the list:
    the first survey used the place and matched models to the wrong collision); the shape is the Frostbite header's
    `shapeOf[i]` (u16s; count at +0x34, offset at +0x38);
  - the shapes follow the root in index order; a compound's children right after it, one object an instance, nested;
  - checked by the instances' shape size (third rotation column's w, int24): equal to the object for every convex
    shape, city-wide; compounds say 208 and compressed meshes 160 (their class size) everywhere;
  - `hknpConvexPolytopeShape`: convex radius +0x14; vertices (relative array: u16 count, u16 offset from the field) at
    +0x30, 16 bytes each; planes at +0x40 (n, d; padded with n = 0, d = -FLT_MAX); faces and indices after;
  - also `hknpTriangleShape` / `hknpConvexShape` / `hknpSphereShape` objects in the sequence (leaving them out broke
    40 zones' order);

  edges. Of 59 highway meshes, most are straight diagonals (11 - 30 degrees or 60 - 72, 80 - 98 % of their long edges
  within a degree); a few curve (04e's long edges spread over 12 - 14 degrees).

### 21. Street level's own time: where it goes, and exact cuts (2026-11-03)

- **Goal:** find where the planning's and the flush's time go, and cuts that leave the same bodies made at the same
  places at the same times. In the game (~3,080 bodies, on a roof at 957 98 169): planning 1.0 - 1.3 ms a
  frame; the flush's part 0.20 - 0.30 ms a flush at 180 flushes a second (not one a frame), one flush of 34.7 ms.
- **Where it went** (the original, offline, the roof with ~3,080 bodies; the game's numbers are about 1.5 - 2 x):
  planning 0.66 - 0.85 ms a frame: the props 0.25 - 0.34 (8,000 cached boxes looked at, each a binary search of the
  made keys, each read from a different place in the 224 MB of boxes), nearest first 0.14 - 0.17 (std::stable_sort of
  ~3,100 88-byte items), the keys sorted 0.10 - 0.12 (std::sort), compared 0.11 - 0.13 (a binary search of the made
  keys for each of ~3,100 items), the tiles 0.05 - 0.08. The flush of the bodies' world 0.29 ms (0.37 - 0.47 in the
  ten-second lines): checking they're still the tools' 0.04 - 0.08, destroying 0.14 - 0.19 (a binary search of the
  plan's keys for each body, every flush, though almost none go), making 0.05 - 0.10 (a hash lookup for each of the
  plan's items, every flush, though almost all are made). The other two worlds' flushes ~0.001 ms: the game's figure of
  0.2 - 0.3 ms a flush is the bodies' world's (~0.6 - 0.9 ms) averaged over three.
- **Cuts** (GroundLevel.cpp; each one gives what the code before gave, checked offline):
  - the plan's items nearest first by a stable radix sort of the distances' bits (as unsigned integers they're in the
    floats' order, all being +0 or more; a NaN or a sign bit: std::stable_sort as before) (NearestFirst);
  - the keys sorted by a radix sort (the props' box indexes as 32-bit numbers, three passes, then the tiles') with
    each key's item index (Plan::SortedItems) (KeyOrder, RadixOrder); the made keys the same (PublishMade);
  - "one to make that isn't made" by going through the plan's sorted keys alongside the made ones;
  - a prop box's made key looked up only when its distance doesn't decide it (Wanted);
  - the cache's boxes copied side by side (CachedBox: extents, index, group) instead of read from the 2.8 million;
    the next boxes' rows prefetched while the items are made;
  - the flush: the set's sorted keys kept (Bodies::Sorted, handed over each time the set changes) and gone through
    alongside the plan's: those the plan doesn't want found that way, and the set gone through for their ids (in its
    own order, as before) only when there are some; the items not made yet found that way too (SortedItems gives their
    places), and only those gone through, in the plan's order (the others would be passed over as made). Where the
    set's sorted keys might not be all of it (some let go as not the tools' any more, all destroyed, the set renewed)
    the flush goes through everything as before.
- **Timers kept** (in "Street level (performance, diagnostic)"): the planning's parts (the tiles, the props, nearest
  first, the keys sorted, compared and handed over) and, in the flushes of the bodies' world (how many of them now
  said), checking the bodies, destroying, making, after the game's work.
- **Before / after** (offline, the roof, ~3,080 bodies, the thread's CPU): Update 0.687 -> 0.377 ms a frame (-45 %);
  the bodies' world's flush 0.289 -> 0.090 ms (-69 %); the game's figure (all three worlds' flushes) 0.100 -> 0.035
  ms. Planning's parts: the props 0.25 -> 0.19, nearest first 0.14 -> 0.065, the keys 0.10 -> 0.05, compared 0.115 ->
  0.007; the flush's: checking 0.04 -> 0.035, destroying 0.14 -> 0.02, making 0.05 -> 0.01. Over a 120 s walk across
  the city (offline): Update 0.382 -> 0.204 ms a frame, the bodies' world's flush 0.157 -> 0.050 ms. [not verified in
  game]
- **Left:** checking each body is still the tools' (~0.035 ms offline, every flush: reads every body's slot in Havok;
  can't be left out without the same answer), the props' look at 8,000 cached boxes (~0.09) and their nearest
  cuts, the tiles (~0.05).

### 22. The fence gate in downtown area 5's passage, taken away while Solid street is on (2026-11-09)

- **Goal:** while Solid street is on, take away the 3.2 m mesh fence gate across a tiled passage in downtown area 5
  (by (-268.8, 0.0, 39.4), street level).
- **What it is** (offline: hkworld.npz owners, the zones' groups, staticmodelgroup_physics_win32): five static model
  group members' instances, each placed by its physics with 2 collision parts, all turned the same way (right 0.274,
  0, -0.962):
  - zone centralcityprops_zs_zs_210, member 6 fence_01_128_electric_mesh (2 instances, parts 9 - 12): instances 0
    (-269.05, -0.12, 37.50) and 1 (-268.89, -0.12, 36.94);
  - zone centralcityprops_zs_zs_211, member 295 fence_01_256_electric_mesh (1, parts 1943 - 1944): instance 0
    (-269.75, -0.12, 39.97); member 6 fence_01_128_electric_mesh (4, parts 30 - 37): instances 1 (-270.11, -0.12,
    41.22) and 2 (-270.27, -0.12, 41.77); its 0 and 3 are 52 and 44 m away and stay.
  - Each (mesh, instance count, first part) is unique in sp_maincity's 2,392 files. The same electric fence meshes are
    used in 546 places, so hiding by mesh name was ruled out.
  - Behind it: a 3.86 m wide passage (building09's north wall and building20's south wall) running about 15 m to the open
    street, with nothing else blocking at body height. Its west part and the street are inside downtownarea5's street
    kill floor (0x61B863F1), which Solid street spares her in. No kill or damage volume at the fence.
- **How** (GroundLevel.cpp, namespace gates; DogenDoor.cpp's door machinery copied and generalised; ground::UpdateGates
  called from the camera hook right after ground::Update with Faith's feet whether Solid street is on or not):
  - each piece's member found by its mesh, instance count and first part (one walk of the model groups' instance lists
    every 2 s while some piece isn't found, Solid street is on and she's within 60 m); its draw object checked to be
    where the data puts it (2 mm in the axes, 2 cm in place) or the piece is left alone;
  - taken away: its collision parts off on the group's physics component's bodies (slot 60; their part bits, more than
    64 parts behind a pointer), then hidden
    (util::hooks::SetModelGroupMemberVisible; the renderer's handle -1). A try that doesn't take is undone in the same
    frame, so it's never drawn with no collision or hidden and solid; tried again after 500 ms, given up after 3. Drawn
    again by the game: hidden again at once;
  - back once Solid street is off (or Street level broken) and Faith is clear of it (0.6 m across from its box, or over
    or under it): only what the tools did undone (its collision on if they took it off, drawn if they hid it);
  - a zone streamed out and in again comes as its file has it: found again and taken away again;
  - CodeKnown: DogenDoor.cpp's bytes, checked once Solid street is first on.
- **Checked offline:** gates::CodeKnown is true on the game's own image (the decrypted one, loaded at 0x140000000),
  false with one byte of the part switch or of the Visible handler changed.
- **Review** (offline): four low findings, fixed: a failed hide left a piece drawn with no collision until the third
  try; one failure counter shared by taking away and putting back; log lines' flags; and the put-back now undoes only
  what the tools did.
- **Not known:** whether the game's server-side physics (AI, navigation) still sees the fence (Faith moves by the
  client's, as through Dogen's door); whether the fence's wind-rattle sound stays. The fence's removal is [not verified
  in game].

  base block's member) come down to h 102.29 - 103.07 over the hall's east 7 - 11 m: 1.6 - 2.5 m over its floor (h 100.62).
  Everything drawn there is higher: the lowest drawn surface over the hall's east end is the 45-degree ceiling at h 104.75
  (4.15 m over the floor).
- **The cut** (offline, read-only): each leaf cut at the base block's top,
  local y 102.57965088 (f32 0x42CD28C8, bytes c828cd42; block h 107.28835; the leaves' local frame is the block's).
  - What they lose outside the hall lies inside the block's old box: in its kept part (east of u -73.54) or in Street
    level's fill for its removed part (DataBit 1: the leaves are reshaped only when the props data has the block's
    stand-ins). Two slivers past that: 72679 at most 1.23 mm on building_01's south face, 72656 at most 11.8 mm (5.7 mm where
    no other leaf backs it) on its outer east face above street level; both under the shapes' 1 cm convex radius.
  - **72678** (400 bytes): its bottom vertices slid up their edges, plane 3's d; no header, face or index change.
  - **72679** (400 bytes): vertices moved inward, plane 3's d and one refit plane (0.072 degrees); no header change.
  - **72657** (880 bytes): the exact cut, 19 vertices (10 kept in their slots), a 9-gon cap as face 0, 18 faces; the face
    count 20 -> 18 (u32 + 0x44 0x028C0014 -> 0x028C0012); plane count stays 20 = ceil4(18).
  - **72656** (960 bytes): the exact cut with two vertex merges (the least loss of 91 sequences tried, one refit plane),
    20 vertices, a 10-gon cap as face 2; plane count 24 -> 20 and face count 21 -> 19 (one 8-byte store at + 0x40). Its
    arrays' offsets stay (4 padding planes left in the gap before the faces; indices at + 0x370): every reader reaches an
    array through its header offset (V3), so the gap is never read.
  - Made twice, independently (C and G: each its own decoder, clipper, encoder): byte for byte the same
    structure; only last-bit float choices differ, and C's are the ones inside the old planes to each leaf's own tolerance.
- **Havok's polytope rules** (V2, over zone 55's 2,213 hknpConvexPolytopeShape objects, both packfiles): face record
  = byte 0 minHalfAngle, byte 1 index count, u16 first index (running sums); minHalfAngle = min(round(theta_min * 255 / pi),
  128) over a face's edge neighbours (theta between the float32 normals; ties 128 for flags 0x0103 / 0x0143, 127 for
  0x0183, the box builder's); vertex count = ceil4(real), padding = copies of the last real vertex, real vertex i's w =
  0x3F000000 + i; plane count = ceil4(faces), padding planes 0, 0, 0, 0xFF7FFFEE (-HK_REAL_MAX); face k <-> plane k;
  counter-clockwise; d = f32(-max n . v); flag 0x40 where every face has 4 indices or fewer; at most 16 indices a face.
- **The game's readers** (V3, the decrypted image disassembled): hknpConvexPolytopeShape's vtable 0x141D4F248 (31
  slots). Every reader takes the counts from the header on each call (vertex count + 0x30: calcAabb, getSupportingVertex;
  plane count + 0x40: getSupportingFace and the manifold's inline searches; face count + 0x44: getNumberOfFaces,
  calcMinAngleBetweenFaces, and as the number of planes to scan in getSignedDistances, the polytope castRay and
  0x1442997C0); nothing caches a count, and none needs plane count = ceil4(faces). What is cached: the pair collision
  caches' face ids (a u16 at cache + 0x86 with two 8-bit ids when both shapes have flag 0x100, which all 2,213 have;
  else u32s at + 0x90 / + 0x94) and an angle budget (+ 0x8D, from minHalfAngle), reused with no bounds check: after a
  renumbering they must be renewed (0x143F3CD00). Static leaves' mass properties aren't read (+ 0x20 is 0 in the file;
  the 0xF100 lookups are in motion code).
  - **Write order** (simulated offline): made = the vertices, the planes in ascending slots (one aligned 16-byte
    store each), the faces and indices, the counts last: a reader in between is never more than 0.16 mm outside the old
    shape; back = the counts first, the planes descending, the faces and indices, the vertices. The other way round the
    space reaches 1.92 m (72657) / 1.77 m (72656) outside it. No order keeps a relisted leaf's planes, faces and indices
    consistent with each other mid-write, so the write is done where no physics step runs.
- **The change** (GroundLevel.cpp, namespace skycity):
  - six shapes, two members: the block and the four leaves in member 167 (skycity_building_01_mesh), the wedge in member
    161; each member searched once (FindPieces with 2 pieces), its group, physics and bodies shared by its shapes.
  - each shape's object compared whole (+ 0x10 to its end) against the file's image and the tools' (images.py;
    replaced in section 27: the game fills + 0x20 at load, so this compare failed in the game);
    Init checks every image pair (CheckImages: the same offsets, arrays in order and in their rooms, only the four counts
    differing in the header); a shape whose images fail isn't changed.
  - **the camera hook only decides** (each 250 ms, at once on a toggle: in / on top / boxes made, as section 24) and asks;
    **the physics flush writes** (hPhysicsFlush, after Street level's bodies are made and before the game's own flush):
    the write in the order above (Write: Put16 / Put8 / Put4, one store each, a compiler fence between), the object
    compared again. The two hand over under an SRW lock (the flush only tries it: it never waits); a flush that makes a
    change sets g_SkyHolding at once; a change is made only if Solid street is still on in that flush.
  - **two worlds:** a zone's static group component has 2 bodies, world index (game id >> 16) & 0xFF 0 the client world
    (Faith's) and 1 the effects world, each its own hknpWorld, both on the same root (the
    lair sashes' live ids 0x01000175 / 0x010100FD, Research_Unbroken_Shard_Bauble section 15). The write is done in the
    client world's flush (its body; a component without one: its first readable body's; its client body not readable
    now: nothing written, nothing taken as seen). Each body on a written root is renewed (0x143F3CD00) only in its own
    world's flush: the client's at once and at its next flush, the effects world's at its next two (it may be stepping
    while the client world flushes: never called for it from there). A body in another world on a root of its own is
    only looked at, in its own __try, and logged (not part of what's held). Renewals check the body's id and shape (a
    reused slot has another shape); one left for a world that never flushes again is dropped after 2,000 other flushes.
  - a fault in the flush keeps what's held (logged once, looked at again each check; given up 10 s after Solid street is
    off, or when the zone's group goes).
  - g_SkyHolding is now "something is changed" (with Solid street on too); StreetOn() is unchanged in effect.
  - the leaves have no top to stand on (their rest is over the space they open): they come back only once Faith is out
    of that space (Tops false).
  - a change asked for while Solid street was on and not made by a flush before it went off isn't made.
  - bodies whose shapes can't be read keep what they were last seen as (Street level stays on) until the member is given
    up after 10 s with Solid street off; a member whose world hasn't flushed in 2 s is logged.

### 27. The Sky City reshape didn't apply in the release build: the game's own bytes in the shapes (2026-11-10)

- **Found** (seen in game): the build with section 26's data finds both members (167 and 161 of the group's 591) but
  leaves all six shapes as they are: both of each one's zone bodies aren't as the tools know them. No change, wait or
  fault is logged at the station.
- **The cause** (offline, read-only):
  - The only paths that give Unknown 2 for every shape with nothing else logged: ObjectAt 0 on the root both bodies
    share, or the bodies unreadable. BodyOf, its offsets, Members[], the gates code and the FromRoot distances are
    unchanged since section 24's version, which changed the block and the wedge in the game. What changed in section 25
    is ObjectAt: the whole object from + 0x10 to its end against the image, where section 24's version compared only the
    four header (count, offset) pairs and the arrays by their counts.
  - zone 55's physics file has its pointer fixups in two 477,152-byte blobs after
    the packfiles (file 12,102,824 and 12,579,976; in each, 22,016 bytes of 2,751 local (src, dst) pairs, then 37,927
    global (src, section, dst) triples). Each of the six objects, in both packfiles, has exactly one fixup from inside
    it: a global one at + 0x20 to obj + Size, its hkRefCountedProperties (one entry, key 0xF100: an
    hknpShapeMassProperties 32 bytes after it). The block's in the second packfile: src 2408800 -> section 2, 2409168.
    Every pointer is stored as 0 in the file, and the images hold 0 there.
  - The game's own hkClass for hknpShape (0x1425C94B0, 0x30 bytes): + 0x10 flags, + 0x12 numShapeKeyBits, + 0x13
    dispatchType, + 0x14 convexRadius, + 0x18 userData, + 0x20 properties (a saved pointer); + 0x28 .. + 0x2F padding.
    hknpConvexShape (0x40): vertices at + 0x30, + 0x34 .. + 0x3F padding. hknpConvexPolytopeShape (0x50): planes, faces,
    indices at + 0x40 / + 0x44 / + 0x48, + 0x4C .. + 0x4F padding. The finish-loaded-object constructors OR the flags with
    1 (0x143F2FA95) and 2 (0x143F35335), bits all six already have.
  - So in the game + 0x20 is very likely obj + Size (not read in the game), and the whole-object compare failed for all
    six at both packfile places. Section 25's "+ 0x20 is 0 in the file" is true of the file only, and V3's "no fixup
    touches the leaves" came from reading the object data as fixups (hkpack). The mass properties the pointer leads to
    are the old geometry's; they're reached only through a body's root shape for bodies that move (0x143F3C390 reads
    [[body + 0x50] + 0x20]; 0x1434CE900 is called only from 0x1434FC860, which returns early when [body + 0x58] & 5,
    static or keyframed), not for these static leaves.
  - In one run seen in game, each "no flush of its bodies' world in 2 s" line came 2 s into a game pause of over 2 s
    ("paused or loading"; the map among them); in that run the 1.3 s and 1.5 s pauses gave none. Answers came between
    the lines (each line needs g_LateLogged cleared), so FlushMember didn't return -1 throughout that run (that answers
    come all through play is the likely reading, not shown). Harmless; left as they are.
- **The change** (GroundLevel.cpp, namespace skycity; no other file):
  - Counted (+ 0x30 .. + 0x33, + 0x40 .. + 0x4B) and Differs (the first byte of those and of + 0x50 .. Size not as an
    image has it); ObjectAt, the recheck after the write and LookOnly go by them. Nothing before + 0x30 and none of the
    header's other bytes is compared.
  - PutHeader: the counts one store each, + 0x40 8 bytes (72656's plane and face counts together, as section 25
    wants), + 0x30 and + 0x48 4 bytes (the same in both images for all six, so they change nothing); the + 0x38 word
    isn't written. No byte the tools don't go by is ever stored.
  - The "aren't as the tools know them" line: "; N couldn't be read" (with "(the client world's among them: none looked
    at)" when the client world's body couldn't be read), "; the first byte not as its file has it: + 0x.. / + 0x.." (or
    "not 16-byte aligned") at the first and second packfile's place; logged once, and once more if a later answer
    first gives the byte (DiffLogged). With diagnostics on, once per zone load: "Street level (diagnostic): <shape>: the
    game has bytes of it the tools don't go by that aren't as its file has them (left as they are): +0x.. ...".
  - Whether the six shapes now change in the game is [not verified in game]: at the station with Solid street on,
    CT.log should say "... changed in the game's collision (2 of its zone's bodies; ...)" for each of them.
- **Review** (offline: the code, the write's safety on a live object): no bug in the fix. Fixed from it: the diagnostic
  byte list was cut at 26 of 48; "couldn't be read" counted a readable effects body; an unaligned place printed
  as + 0xFFFFFFFF; the byte was never logged if the first look had the bodies unreadable; PutHeader read and wrote
  back the + 0x34 .. + 0x37 and + 0x4C .. + 0x4F bytes. Left: a body found as neither image right after its write gets
  no byte in the line (its "changed now ... neither" line shows it); Put16's _mm_store_si128 compiles to movdqu (one
  instruction per slot, but Intel promises 16-byte atomicity only for the aligned forms; matters only if a reader runs
  during the client world's flush, unknown, as in section 25).
- **Cost** (offline, a 120 s walk, measured under other load): Street level's bodies as before; Update 0.211 ms a frame.
- **Not known:** the live bytes (no game memory read): that + 0x20 is obj + Size, and whether the game also sets user
  data (+ 0x18) or anything in + 0x50 .. Size (the leaves' arrays have never been compared in the game; a byte off there
  would be named by the new line); whether the effects world's body shares the client's root.
