### 10. What the order check found (2026-11-02) (seen in game)

- The same order in every frame read: G-buffer, G-buffer, 1 dispatch, decals, decals, **G-buffer, G-buffer** (two more after
  the decals), the first lit pass (one draw run), 5 dispatches, **the SSR driver** (10 dispatches, 7 indirect), 14
  dispatches (8 indirect), then many lit passes, the half-size passes, 24 dispatches.
- The driver runs after the decals end, on the pass changes' thread, all its dispatches on the immediate
  context, no command lists. It ran throughout.
- So 7.A's precondition holds: what's written into targets 0 - 1 before the frame's first lit pass begins is in the
  G-buffer when the SSR traces. That the lights read it there too is **[inferred]** (the 14 dispatches after the
  driver and the lit passes come later; which of them is the light combine wasn't logged).
- **A bug found on the way:** gameframe copied the G-buffer as the frame's *first* G-buffer pass ended, before the
  decals and the two G-buffer passes after them; the snow's and the wet look's copy had no decals, and whatever those
  later passes draw showed what was under it. What they draw is **[unknown]** (characters or dynamic objects are
  likely: decals are drawn before what they mustn't land on).
- GlobalPostProcessSettings wasn't found in the settings registry: its live SSR values are still unknown.

### 11. 7.A as built (2026-11-02) [code]

VISUALS > Weather > Wet surfaces > **In the game's own lighting**
(on by default; off = the tools' own reflection at Present, as before).
- **Where:** gameframe::OnPass, as the frame's first lit pass begins (the replay's OMSetRenderTargets hook, called
  before the game's call goes through). gameframe now copies targets 0 - 2 *there* (the whole G-buffer: decals and the
  later passes in); Visuals/GbufferWet.cpp draws right after, with those copies as its input.
- **The pass** (GbufferWet.hlsl, ps_4_1, about 11,200 instruction slots, 34 temps; it #includes WetLook.hlsl and calls
  its own functions): binds the game's RTVs 0 and 1 (no depth), one full-screen triangle; reads the game's depth
  (an SRV of the G-buffer pass's depth texture, R32_FLOAT_X8X24), the copies (t6, t7), the game's viewConstants copy
  (b1, the 6 bases), the wet look's constants (b0) and squares / stamps / marks (t2 - t4, t9). Writes, only where wet:
  - smoothness: max(game's, lerp toward 0.5 - 0.75 by Reflections x wetness x facing), puddles 0.85 - 0.98 by
    Reflections x puddle, the slopes' sheet 0.9;
  - base colour x lerp(1, 0.55, wet x facing) x lerp(1, 0.7, wet puddle) x lerp(1, 0.82, sheet);
  - the facing (puddles flattened, rain ripples, step / drip / pipe rings, slide and body waves, rivulet tilt) encoded
    in the pixel's own basis (or the best of the 6), written only if it decodes back within 2.5 degrees (offline:
    with axis-aligned bases all are written, worst 0.19 degrees; with random turns 2.5 % are left as drawn).
  - Not ported (not needed in the G-buffer): NearerAround, RisesAround, KeptDryAt's edge softening (KeptDryKind is
    used), the puddle blur, the sheen and ring shading from the frame's light, the drops' specks, the trace.
- **Camera:** the wet look's constants are filled at Present, a frame before. The pass copies them with this frame's
  turn and projection (greenplane::FrameCamera: the camera taken at this frame's first scene depth clear) and keeps
  their camera position; positions for the lists are this frame's camera + offset - that position. Left: RingReaches'
  edge points are projected with this frame's camera though relative to the last one (off by one frame's camera
  motion, cm at running speed).
- **At Present:** wetlook::Apply sets g_Options.y when the pass drew this frame; PsMain then skips its whole wet
  ground block (darkening, puddle blur, sheen, rings' shading, the trace). Body wetness, handprints, print marks,
  lightning, distant rain, haze, drips, pipes and splashes stay at Present.
- **Not drawn** (logged once a reason): the wet look off or not drawn the frame before, snow lying, no G-buffer pass / copy / camera, the scene depth cleared twice before the lights, a viewport
  not at the corner, the depth not readable.
- **Log:** "Wet surfaces in the game's lighting: ..." (first draw, skips) and every 10 s "(performance, diagnostic)"
  with its GPU ms; "Snow: the game's G-buffer copied for the snow and the wet look as its first lit pass began".
- **Not known:** how it looks (the game's SSR is half-res and temporal, has the mirror fade, no SSR past
  150 m; the wet ground's reflection strength now follows the game's Fresnel, F0 0.04, so puddles seen from above
  reflect less than the tools' 0.3 floor), the GPU cost, a first-draw hitch (the shader isn't warmed up), whether the
  lights read the G-buffer after this point (inferred), and what the two G-buffer passes after the decals draw.

### 12. Cost in game (2026-11-02) (seen in game)

- Drawn in nearly every frame; now and then a single frame is skipped because the game's G-buffer wasn't copied that
  frame. Its shader is made in 2 ms on a worker thread.
- GPU, 10 s means: the G-buffer pass 1.76 - 7.23 ms (most often 3 - 5; worst frame 11.7); the pass at
  Present 1.76 - 3.65 ms. Together about 6 - 8 ms, against about 5.9 ms for the Present pass alone
  before.
- A breakdown of the Present pass (3.14 ms) puts 1.15 ms in the kept-dry boxes and 0.76 in the shelter and
  interiors, which both passes now work out; the G-buffer pass's own parts aren't broken down yet.

### 13. The vents / boxes / planks fix and the shared info (2026-11-02) [code]

- **The problem:** on a roof box's top looked down on, hard-edged darker rectangles stacked over it and straight
  lines from corner to corner. **What the code did there** [code]: smoothness = max(game's, lerp(game's, 0.5 - 0.75, wet
  x facing)), so with Wetness under 1 a decal's or stain's smoothness (different from the surface's) kept part of its
  difference, and the city's SSR switches on between roughness 0.4 and 0.3 (section 4.3): patches. The facing the game
  lights by stayed its own (vertex normals turning across triangles, decals' normals): lines and patches once glossy.
  That these are the rectangles and lines seen is **[inferred]** from their shape (decal rectangles, triangle
  diagonals) [not verified in game].
- **Now:** film = smoothstep(0, 0.3, wet); smoothness weight film x facing; on level clean depth surfaces (lean 0, no
  jump: plane) the facing is the depth's plane, weighted by film; facing for the darkening and gloss from the game's
  normal off the level (no depth-jump factor: the thin things' stripes). The basis alpha is always written with a new
  facing (a decal's blend of two bases decodes to nothing).
- **Shared info:** GbufferWetInfoPs (476 instruction slots) writes R8G8B8A8 (outside, kept, kept by a body, interiors)
  at the depth's texels; GbufferWetPs (about 10,800) and PsMain (g_Options.z, t10; the rain copy 18,676 slots) read
  it. PsMain also skips GameSurfaceAt while the wet ground is in the G-buffer.

### 14. The fix's result and the G-buffer dump (2026-11-03)

- The rectangles and lines on the box's top stayed with section 13's fix (seen in game), so section 13's reading of
  them (smoothness patches, the game's facing) was wrong or not the whole of it. Also ruled out by the code: the game's
  interiors and the weather's squares (their edges fade over 0.3 - 0.7 m; the ones seen are hard).
- Cost with that fix (seen in game): Present pass 0.84 - 0.96 ms (was about 3), G-buffer pass 4.2 - 5.4 ms (info
  1.36 - 1.49, wet ground 2.8 - 3.9).
- The diagnostic for it: *Save the G-buffer (diagnostic)*, decoded with dump_decode.py (PNGs of
  smoothness, decoded normals, basis, colour, metal / reflectance / sky visibility, info, depth, before and after).

### 15. The dump at the box and the fix (2026-11-03)

- **The dump** (camera about 2 m above a roof box looking down): the game's own colour
  on the box's top is plain (217); after the pass it's 156 where wet and 145 in a puddle, and the smoothness 0.86 /
  0.95. The rectangles and lines are in the pass's output only, in the puddle factor. The box's top is four faces
  leaning 1.6 and 4 degrees (FrameNormal y 0.9996 / 0.9975), meeting in an X.
- **The cause**, from a numpy model of PuddleSurface and FlatAround on the dump's depth (puddle_model.py): at a
  column through the top, the saved smoothness jumps 0.860 -> 0.956 in one pixel exactly where
  the 1 m test's count of drops goes 3 -> 2, and dips to 0.784 exactly where FlatAround's 3-pixel ring meets the fold
  (its points 2 - 7 % under the plane, about a millimetre). Of the 16,559 hard steps in the saved smoothness (over
  0.03 a pixel, not at the game's own), 99.9 % are at a step of these tests (the 1 m count 41 %, FlatAround 71 %, the
  holes 11 %, stairs 9 %; some at several).
- **Why any per-pixel point test steps:** each point's place moves with the pixel; when it goes over a cliff its
  answer flips at once, at a copy of the cliff moved by the offset. Tried and measured in the model, not used:
  - a search for the distance to the edge along 8 ways (bisection): this box has a 12 cm gap 0.59 m off, then another
    top 6 - 14 cm lower (right at the drop threshold), then the floor at 1.21 m; the search found a different one
    from pixel to pixel (jumps of 0.2 - 1);
  - lattice nodes lifted with the pixel's own plane: smooth on each face, but at a fold the plane changes, a node's
    probe crosses a cliff, and it jumps (0.06 at 0.5 m spacing, 0.53 at 0.75 m, 0.94 at 1 m);
  - lifting the node twice: a node past the edge then lands behind the box (taken for "something in front").
- **The fix:** the nodes are worked out without any pixel (NodesPs: per node of a 0.5 m world lattice, the first of 10
  probes down its vertical line seen behind the surface, then twice onto it; its broadness from 8 points 1 m round,
  level with it). Each pixel: 4 x 4 nodes, cubic B-spline weights; a node higher than the pixel counts whole (walls,
  Faith: no ring round her), one level with it (10 cm + 0.4 % of the distance, soft to 2.5 x) its broadness, one lower
  none. Plus the hole test by opposite pairs, the stairs test bounded to step heights, FlatAround's 1 cm least drop.
  In the model with the shader's exact steps: no step of the broadness beyond 0.023 over its ramp on either box; the
  puddle factor's hard steps on the lower box 42,242 -> 274 pixels (the rest at the crop's edge and real geometry).
- Not in the model, so unknown: the game's frames elsewhere (stairs, grates, kerbs, far ground), and the
  cost (expected about the same: 16 small texture reads replace 8 depth reads with projections; the node pass is
  65,536 pixels).

### 16. Does the snow step the same way? (2026-11-03)

- The snow has none of the tests that stepped: no 1 m broadness count, no FlatAround (DropAt), no hole or stairs test.

### 17. The gravel laid flat, and a dry patch at a wall's foot (2026-11-05) [dumps + model; not verified in game]

Goal: fix the rain's issue seen in saved G-buffer dumps. Three dumps, all taken
with the rain on: A and B (2 s apart, the same view down at a gravel roof with a concrete path)
and C (a roof of vent boxes by a tall wall). Read with dump_decode.py,
dump_compare.py, dump_region.py, dump_world.py and flatten_model.py.

**The gravel (A, B): fixed.**
- In a 600 x 500 px box of gravel, every pixel's facing after the pass is exactly up (normal y 1.000 at the 1st
  percentile), against the game's 0.83 median (34 degrees off level at the median, 59 at the 90th percentile). Its
  smoothness rose from 0.50 to at least 0.70. Over the whole frame, 54 % of the pixels were turned more than
  20 degrees.
- Why: GbufferWetPs's film (section 13) lays the facing on the depth's plane wherever that plane is level
  and clean (`flatten = plane * film`). A gravel roof is one flat plane in the depth, with its stones only in the
  game's normal map. So the stones went, and the game's reflections (from 0.6 smoothness) showed a smooth sheet.
  Water drains between stones; it doesn't film over them.
- Fix: `flatten = plane * film * fine`, `fine = smoothstep(cos 25, cos 12, dot(gameFacing, depthPlane))` where the
  game's facing was read (else 1, as before). Fully flat within 12 degrees, the game's own facing past 25. Puddles are
  unchanged (they still lie flat). So are the darkening and the smoothness.
- The limits came from the model (flatten_model.py: the depth's facing from the dump's depth, plane as the shader's
  lean, film 1). The model checked how far the new rule's facing turns from the current one:
  - The gravel keeps the game's facing (0 degrees from it at the median; now 34).
  - Unchanged within 1 degree on 99.4 % of the concrete path, 99.4 % of C's box tops and 98.7 % of its vents.
  - The 11-03 roof box (section 15's dump) is what the flattening was added for: its top's triangles turn up to about
    11 degrees, 10.5 - 11.5 at the 90th percentile on its X. Its diagonal bands don't move at 12/25. At 8/20 they
    would have (13.7 % of one band moved more than 1 degree). The level pixels that do move (1.1 % of its frame) are
    the box's edges, a lip across it and the vent grilles, which are real relief.
- GbufferWetInfoPs is unchanged. GbufferWetPs: temps 35, slots 11,154 -> 11,162, with
  `add -0.906308` and `mul_sat 13.919824` (the smoothstep).
- Not changed: WetLook.hlsl's PsMain (the wet look at Present). It draws the ground only when the G-buffer pass
  didn't run. It uses the depth's facing on the level, so it would show the same mirror on gravel there.

**The dry patch at the wall's foot (C): found, not fixed.**
- The open box tops at the foot of the tall wall behind them (world about -165.1..-164.3, 60.1, -35.6..-34.2,
  1.7 m under the camera) have the info pass's open-sky share 0. The patch's edge is blurred over about a 2 m
  square, and the frame shows nothing over it. The camera is too close above to see higher, so a real roof up
  there isn't ruled out.
- That share is the weather's 2 m squares (Weather.cpp UpdateRoofs: median sweeps up and down from the camera's
  height; ShelterInSquare: under a roof, or more than 2 m under the first surface found looking down), blended
  between the squares' middles.
- A possible cause: a square half on the wall's building found its top as "the first surface down". The box top in
  that square, and through the blend its neighbours' near edges, then counts as under it.
- The dump doesn't hold the squares, so this is unconfirmed. Next step: save the shelter grid (t3) and its corner
  and size with each dump.

**The squares in the dump (2026-11-05) [code; not verified in game].**
- GbufferWet.cpp stages two more parts in the dump's first block, after TakeGbufferPass. These are what the info pass
  reads that frame:
  - `shelter`: inputs.Views[1], the wet look's t3. Its texture is count x count, R32G32B32A32_FLOAT; texel (x, z) =
    (looked, first surface down, first roof up, from y). TexelBytes now gives 16 for that format; it had been skipped.
  - `wetparams`: inputs.Constants, b0.
- `_info.txt` adds a line for each. The squares' line gives g_ShelterGrid's byte offset, from
  `wetlook::ShelterGridOffset()` (offsetof the C++ Constants; 304, as the shader's reflection has it).
- The text goes into WriteDump's std::string, not the fixed 1 KB g_DumpNote, so sprintf_s can't overflow.
- Decoder: dump_shelter.py. For a pixel box it works out the info pass's open-sky share again

# 44. Dogen's place: the door and the inside (2026-11-03)

Goal: make Dogen's apartment (looked for in The View) reachable, with a door that opens (swings, doesn't vanish) and a walkable interior free of
its barrier blocks, with no menu entry (an easter egg).

Each claim is labelled by how it's known:
- **[data]** read from the game's files (ebx, res, Havok packfiles, mesh vertex data);
- **[code]** read from the decrypted game image (`game_image.bin`);
- **[inferred]** follows from the above but wasn't seen directly;
- **[unknown]** not found out.

Scripts of this analysis: `fbl.py`, `pos.py`, `areascan.py`, `zphys.py`, `blocks.py`,
`meshtris.py`, `cover.py`, `roominst.py`, `audit.py`, `uncovered.py`, `plan.py`. They use the shared fb tools and the
ground-level research's `zc_all.tsv`.

### 1. Where it is

**It's in Anchor, not The View [data].**
- Every Dogen briefing has its mission interaction (`gameplay/logic/pf_missioninteraction`) at one door:
  - `benefactordogenbriefing` at (186.09, 67.79, 305.21);
  - `familymattersbriefing` at (186.15, 67.79, 305.15);
  - `kingdombriefing` at (186.21, 68.08, 305.22).
- Their start markers are in `sp_maincity/layer11_missionmarkers_anchor`.
- The free-roam checkpoint `pf_l_missioncheckpoint` is at (185.71, 66.56, 304.07), in `layer16_anc_startpoints`. So
  is the briefing's `pf_teleportplayer`, which puts Faith back outside the door after the cutscene.
- The rooms are placed by `levels/sp/sp_maincity/centralcityprops_zs_zs_397`, a city props zone in the `anchor`
  superbundle (plain, not patched). The zone's x / z lie inside Anchor's area 2 (x 66 … 481, z 40 … 437; the
  ground-level research's district table). The View's areas are at x 559 … 1355.
- The "Dogen's" sign `anc_dogen_sign_bg` is over it, at (171 … 184, 84 … 87, 288 … 297), in
  `centralcitybuildings_zs_zs_5`.
- No asset with "dogen" in its name is placed in The View [data: ebx index search].
- The only apartment named in The View's data is **Kruger's** (`ve_familymatters_krugersapartment_01`, a volume at
  879, 223, −454). Dogen gives that mission (Family Matters) [data: `vo_family_getmission_l01_dogen`]. That apartment

**What's inside [data].** The cutscene set of `cs_05_benefactor_dogen` (`objects/cutscene/05_benefactor_dogen/
architecture/kitchen/`) is placed in the city by zone 397, all with collision, and comes with the zone in free roam:
- `kitchen01`: the kitchen, 10.2 × 7.7 m, 3.5 m high;
- `kitchen01_corridor01`: a 2.6 m wide corridor beside it, plus the entrance vestibule;
- `kitchen01_counter01`: the island counter, with a panelled partition up to the ceiling;
- `kitchen01_backroom01`: a back room behind a serving hatch.

The zone also places kitchen props there:

- drawn only: pots, knives, microwaves, cutting boards, towels, the chalkboard.

All four room pieces share one frame [data, the zone's physics compound]: origin (183.398, 66.5, 306.512), right
(−0.8315, 0, −0.5556), forward (0.5556, 0, −0.8315). In that frame:
- the kitchen is x 0 … 10.2, z −7.7 … 0;
- the corridor is x −2.6 … 0, z −10.3 … 1.2;
- the door is at z = 2.5;
- outside is +z.

### 2. The door

**What it is [data].** A plain member of zone 397's static model group:
- mesh `objects/props/door/door_oneway_01/door_oneway_right_01_mesh`, 1 instance;
- physics parts 290 – 292 (`PhysicsPartRange.First` 290, 3 per instance);
- placed by the zone's physics: compound instance 268 at (186.608, 66.5, 305.598), right (0.83147, 0, 0.55557);
- its frame `doorframe_oneway_right_16_01` sits around it.

It is no game door:
- The game's openable one-way doors are prefabs (`objects/props/door/pf_door_oneway_*`). Each holds the same
  door object, `pf_doorlogic` (two `PamSpatialEntryInputTrigger`s: press to open), and a
  `PamAntDrivenMeshPartsEntity`, so their opening is an Ant animation.
- Zone 397 uses those prefabs for other doors nearby (at 181.49, 66.51, 296.12 and 185.31, 64.0, 290.40), but not
  for this one.

**What turns it on or off: nothing found [data].**
- Zone 397's file holds no logic: only its sub-world, the static group with its physics and health components, the
  Havok asset, an Enlighten entity, the interface and a streamer notification.
- `areascan.py` read all 2,392 `sp_maincity` level files, plain and patched, for anything placed round the kitchen.
  None of them has a door, trigger or switch for it.
- The briefings only put a mission interaction and a teleport at it.
- A switch reaching the group from elsewhere (by property connection) wasn't searched for [unknown].
- Its collision: 3 convex blocks.
  - The door slab: 1.12 × 2.46 × 0.02 m.
  - A handle on the outside.
  - A push bar on the inside.
- So it's a one-way door that would open from the inside, shut for good [inferred from the handle and push bar].

**Streaming [data].** Zone 397 is an ordinary city props zone, so the inside streams with Anchor in free roam.
`layer37_mainmissionstreamingspheres` has a 30 m mission sphere centred at (163.7, 68.7, 303.2) beside it. What that
sphere streams wasn't followed [unknown].

### 3. The barrier blocks

**Correction.** The first version of this section said the game puts no invisible blocks inside. That was wrong
(there is collision inside, seen in game): it checked only the kitchen's own zone (397).
The building the kitchen is in, in another zone, fills the rooms with two invisible blocks (below,
"The building's fill blocks"). What follows is still right for zone 397's own collision.

**Zone 397's own collision has no invisible blocks inside [data].**
- `audit.py` decoded the Havok collision of every model with collision in the rooms, from each mesh's own
  `_physics_win32` (all are `hknpStaticCompoundShape`s of `hknpConvexPolytopeShape` blocks, their instances identity):
  - 41 blocks for the room pieces and the door;
  - the props' blocks too.
- The zone's own physics file holds the same blocks (each block's first vertex is found in it).
- `audit.py` then placed each block where the zone's compound puts it and measured how much of each face has drawn
  triangles on it, within 4 cm. The drawn triangles came from the meshes' LOD0 vertex chunks, found with
  `chunkfind.py`.
- **Every block that reaches into the walkable space has drawn faces**:
  - walls, floor, ceiling;
  - the island counter and its partition;
  - the hatch sill;
  - the door frame posts;
  - cabinets, radiators, coat rails, ladles, trays, rocks, wall light.
- No block stands where nothing is drawn.
- `uncovered.py`, the other way round: inside the walkable space (0.1 – 2 m up), the only drawn things without
  collision are:
  - pots, towels and the chalkboard;
  - a shelf along the kitchen's wall at 1.0 m (its triangles' middles 0.1 – 0.2 m from the wall);
  - a shelf on the partition at 1.45 – 1.95 m (its triangles' middles up to 0.4 m from it).

**The building's fill blocks: the barrier [data].**
- Every zone's collision whose box reaches into the rooms (`zc_all.tsv`) shows two buildings of zone
  `centralcitybuildings_zs_zs_5`: `anc_area02_building02` and `anc_area02_building03_edited`.
- The kitchen set stands inside `anc_area02_building03_edited`:
  - one instance in the city, compound instance 577, part 610;
  - one part a instance, so its whole collision is that one part;
  - 137 convex blocks and one compressed mesh;
  - its frame has the kitchen frame's axes.
- Two of its blocks reach into the rooms (`zone5.py`). Both are boxes with identity instances:
  - **block 0:** frame x −2.87 … −0.97, y 0.02 … 2.56, z −12.30 … 1.33. It fills most of the corridor.
  - **block 37:** x −0.95 … 12.47, y 0.02 … 4.85, z −12.30 … 2.61. It fills the kitchen, the back room and the
    space round them.
- Faith inside the rooms is inside these blocks: that's the collision met inside.
- Their faces against what's drawn (`bfaces.py`, the building's own triangles included):
  - block 0: no face drawn but its floor side (the corridor's floor). It's pure fill.
  - block 37 is also the building's outside: its street front (z+, 98 % drawn by the building), its side (x+,
    73 %) and part of its back (z−, 40 %).
  - No other convex block covers those faces. The compressed mesh wasn't decoded [unknown].
- Both blocks are in zone 5's physics file twice, once in each of its two packfiles, with the same bytes. Their
  distances from each packfile's root shape:
  - pf0: block 0 at 1,232,384, block 37 at 1,250,144;
  - pf1: block 0 at 1,233,792, block 37 at 1,251,552.

**Everything else near the rooms, checked to the end [data].**
- **The packfiles:** every physics file holds two packfiles, the first with 4-byte pointers, the second with 8-byte.
  The 64-bit game loads the second, so the live fill blocks are at pf1's places. The build tries both, and pf1's
  copies have the same bytes and the same internal layout.
- **Both buildings' triangle collision (`hknpCompressedMeshShape`) decoded** (`cmesh3.py`), from its Havok
  static-mesh-tree data: sections (box, dequantization origin and scale, first packed vertex, shared vertices,
  primitives), 11/11/10-bit packed vertices per section, 21/21/22-bit shared vertices over the mesh's box, and
  primitives of 4 u8 indices (a triangle when the last two are the same).
  - **The decode fits:** the primitive array fits at exactly one place; every vertex lands inside its own section's
    box; the triangle count equals the header's key count.
  - **`anc_area02_building03_edited`:** 979 triangles, 0 reaching the walkable rooms (0.05 – 3.4 m up).
  - **`anc_area02_building02`:** 105 triangles, 0.
- **The room members with a triangle mesh in their own physics:** only `anc_csgshape_03` (a wall detail): its
  20 triangles reach none of the rooms, at any of its 5 placements (`check_member.py`).
- **The three other models whose collision box (`zc_all.tsv`) took in the rooms:**
  - `trainstation_exterior` (zone 8, at the lair, 195 m away): 0 of its 77 blocks;
  - `elysiumglasswall_02`: 556 m away, its box made huge by its scale; 0 of its 21 blocks;
  - `elysium_curvedwall_03`: 610 m away, the same; 0 of its 21 blocks.
- **So** once the two fill blocks are reshaped, everything solid in the rooms is drawn. The ground-level boxes are
  the one exception, below.

**What can still feel like barrier blocks [data].** GAME > Street level (the ground-level research) makes every
drawn-only city model solid. Its data (`GroundProps.bin`, 3,173,746 boxes) has 21 boxes inside the
kitchen, made only while "Solid street" is on, within 40 m of Faith:
- 6 for the microwaves, by the wall, 1.03 – 1.81 m up (world boxes about 1.0 × 0.7 m across);
- 8 small ones for the pots, 1.0 – 1.7 m up;
- 6 for the ceiling lights, 3.0 – 3.5 m up (over her head);
- 1 for a toolbox, outside the door.

They stand where those models are drawn. They weren't changed: they're Street level's, and it makes drawn
things solid on purpose.

**Kill zones, out-of-bounds [data].**
- No kill volume, out-of-bounds volume or other trigger volume is placed in the rooms. The scan found only:
  - light probes, reflection volumes and effects;
  - a `kingdomexecutionsceneapproach` volume and the fast-travel box, both outside the door (frame z 2.7 and 5.0).
- Anchor area 2's street kill floor reaches y 27 only; the floor here is at y 66.5.

**Other limits of the place [data].**
- The back room can't be walked into. Walls are all round it; from the kitchen there's only the serving hatch,
  1.01 – 1.91 m up, 0.9 m tall.
- The corridor's side door and the back room's end door are `door_closedoff_01`, fake doors with a wall right
  behind them.

### 4. How the door is opened (the build)

**The game's own way to take one member's collision away [code].** It's how the group's `Enabled` event does it:
- The group's property handler is 0x14318DC70. Its `Enabled` false calls 0x1431856E0.
- For a member placed by its physics, 0x1431856E0 gives each of the instance's parts (first + per instance ×
  instance) to the group's physics component, `ClientStaticModelGroupPhysicsComponent` (vtable 0x141B1CE08,
  member record + 0x20), slot 60, 0x1434DB840.
- For each of the component's bodies (ids [+ 0x30], their count + 0x60, manager + 0x58), that slot calls the body
  record's slot 82, 0x1434EFFA0. The record is found through 0x1434EE790 and 0x1434EC740.
- Slot 82 clears the part's bit at record + 0xB8. The bits are inline when there are 64 or fewer, else behind a
  pointer there; their count is at + 0xC0.
- It then calls hknpWorld 0x143F3CD00 for the body, and 0x1434FC860.
- Slot 59 (0x1434DB9D0 → the record's slot 81, 0x1434F0100) sets the bit again, with the same follow-ups.
- The rest of the `Enabled` event is left out: work queued through 0x14317F340, the parts' components through
  0x14330F060.
- How the game's collision skips a cleared part wasn't traced [unknown]. That it does is [inferred]: it's what the
  bits are cleared for.

**Its drawing** goes with the member's `Visible`, through the same handler: field 2, 0x14318F730. The tools already
do this: `util::hooks::SetModelGroupMemberVisible`, used by the Shard swap and the replay.

**Faith moves by the client's physics [inferred, from the lair windows, seen in game].** The server's copy of
the door stays, as the server's copy of the sofa window did.

**Moving the door's collision isn't possible [code + data].** It's one instance inside the zone's single static
Havok body (1,433 instances), so setBodyTransform would move the whole zone. So it's taken out while the door is open
(above). It isn't needed then [data, `blocks.py`]:
- The entrance is a vestibule 1.12 m deep beside the hinge. The door is 1.14 m wide.
- Open at 88 degrees, the door lies along the vestibule's side wall (corridor block 1, face at frame x −2.25):
  - the push bar 4 mm off it;
  - the far edge 5 cm off the inner wall (frame z 1.35);
  - the hinge corner in the frame's jamb.
- That wall's own collision is behind it. At 90 degrees the push bar would touch the wall's face.

**Moving its drawing [code].**
- What draws a member placed by its physics is one object per instance: the physics component's object for the
  instance's first part (slot 66, 0x1434DC6D0, `[component + 0x68][part]`).
- The Visible handler (0x14318F730) takes that object, reads its renderer handle at + 0x8C (−1 while not shown),
  and builds a description with 0x143769330: the object's own rows at + 0x10 … + 0x50 (right, up, forward,
  position), the mesh's bounds through + 0x60, a LOD scale.
- Shown, it hands the description to the renderer (0x1436C40B0) and keeps the handle. Hidden, 0x1436D2EC0 takes it
  away and the handle becomes −1.
- So writing the object's rows while it's hidden, then showing it again, has the renderer draw it at the new rows.
- That the renderer doesn't read the rows again later (from the object) wasn't traced [unknown]. It doesn't matter
  here: the rows stay as written until the tools change them back.

**The hinge and the side it opens to [data + inferred].**
- The hinge is the door's origin:
  - the game's one-way door prefab (`pf_door_oneway_right_16_01`) puts the same door 0.56 m off its frame's
    middle, at the frame's edge;
  - here the origin is at the frame's left post (frame x −2.16);
  - the handle is 1 m from the origin, at the far edge.
- It opens to its forward, the inside:
  - the vestibule is the door's size on that side;
  - the game's own one-way doors are opened from their −forward side (`pf_doorlogic`'s triggers at z −0.4 / −0.8).
    Here that's the street.

**The build (Camera/DogenDoor.cpp, no menu entry, no config key).**
- Each frame in the camera hook, beside the lair windows. That's the game's thread, where those windows' Havok moves
  and the groups' `Visible` already run.
- While Faith is within 60 m it looks for the group by the model groups' instance lists. The group must hold:
  - `kitchen01_mesh` (1 instance, part 597);
  - `door_oneway_right_01_mesh` with 1 instance, parts 290 + 3, placed by physics.
  - Neither file name exists for any other mesh in the game [data].
- Its draw object's rows must be the data's placement (within 0.002 and 2 cm) before anything is done. If they
  aren't, it logs them and leaves the door as the game has it.
- **Opens** while her feet are within 1.5 m along the door, from 3 m outside to 3.5 m inside it, at the floor's
  height (−0.8 … +1.8 m). That's early enough for it to be open by the time she reaches it, running too.
  - First its collision goes (the component's parts off, read back on every body).
  - Then it swings to 88 degrees over 0.6 s, eased.
  - Each frame of the swing: `Visible` false, the rows turned round its up axis through its origin, `Visible` true.
- **Shuts** once she's been more than 5 m from it, or off that height band, for 1.5 s.
  - It swings back over 0.8 s.
  - The game's own rows are written back exactly.
  - Then the collision comes back.
- If the collision doesn't go, it doesn't swing (it stays shut and solid). If it can't be drawn swung, its rows go
  back and it stays shut and solid.
- A collision switch that doesn't take is retried every 0.5 s, 3 times at most.
- Every address it uses is byte-checked once, with the record functions' bit layout, the part-object getter, the
  description's rows and the Visible handler's steps. With a different game build it does nothing.
- It logs to CT.log as "Dogen's door: …".
- A first version made the door vanish (hidden); it was replaced by this one, which swings it.
- The byte checks match the decrypted image (offline).

**The body records seen in game, and what changed [live reads + code].**
- Seen in game: the door's group and member are found (member 32, collision parts 290 - 292), so the in-memory
  member fields + 0x48 / + 0x50 hold 290 / 3, as the decompile read them. A body of its collision wasn't as the
  tools knew it, so nothing was changed.
- Targeted read-only reads of the live game (`probe_door.py`, about 30 reads along the door's own pointers) found:
  - the door's draw object at exactly the data's rows and shown;
  - the zone's 2 body records of another class, the static one: vtable 0x141BABBA0, not 0x141BAC160.
- Its part switches [code]:
  - slots 81 / 82: `jmp 0x1434EC800` / `jmp 0x1434EC670`;
  - each tests the part's bit, then sets or clears it;
  - the bits are at record + 0x68 (inline when 64 or fewer, else a pointer there), how many at + 0x70;
  - then 0x143F3CD00 is called with [record + 0x30] + 0xE0 and the Havok id at + 0x50;
  - live: 1,566 parts, 290 – 292 on, on both bodies.
- **What changed:**
  - The door's collision reader takes both record classes.
  - The building's fill blocks are reshaped, while Faith is within 60 m of the door, checked every 3 s:
    - find the group whose member is `anc_area02_building03_edited_mesh` (1 instance, part 610);
    - each of its component's bodies gives its Havok body: [world + 0x20] + id × 0x90, its shape at + 0x50, its id
      at + 0x60 checked;
    - from that root shape, by pf0's places or pf1's, both blocks' headers (8 vertices / 8 planes) and all
      2 × 256 bytes of their vertices and planes must be exactly the file's;
    - then block 37 becomes the street front's slab: its inner side (frame z −12.30) moved to 1.35, the
      vestibule's wall, its other sides as they are;
    - block 0 becomes a 5 cm cube inside the corridor's outer wall;
    - then 0x143F3CD00 for the body, as the game does after its collision changes.
  - **What's lost [inferred]:** block 37's side (x+) and back (z−) faces below 4.85 m. They lie behind the kitchen
    set's own walls (0.9 m and 2.2 m in), and the roof parapet outside is at their top. If Faith can reach either
    from outside, she could step into the wall's hollow there, up to those walls.
  - Every address and byte it uses matches the decrypted image and zone 5's file (offline).

**Seen in game.**
- The building's fill blocks are taken out of the rooms, on both of its bodies.
- The lamps: 6 of 6 given their own look, 6 fixed lights made.
- The door's draw object is as the data has it.

**The lamps' light as downward spots.**
Goal: dimmer lamps, as spotlights facing down at the ground, 1,000 lm, with a smooth edge.
- **The fixed lights [code, `Lights/LightManager.cpp`]:**
  - `AddFixedLight` takes no cone; it uses `BuildLight`'s: the data zeroed (`new BYTE[DataSize]()`), the outer
    angle (+ 0xF8) 80°, the inner angle (+ 0xF4) left 0;
  - its own comment calls both angles the whole cone's, and a Look's softness sets inner = cone × (1 − softness).
    So inner 0 is softness 1: the light fades out all the way from the cone's middle, the smoothest edge the tools
    make;
  - the rows are right, up, backward, position, and a spot shines along −backward. Down: backward (0, 1, 0), up
    (0, 0, −1), right (1, 0, 0). The game's own strip lamp spot (`pf_light_int_surface_04`'s PbrSpotLight) has the
    same rows.
- **The spots:**
  - all 6 at 1,000 lm, 15 cm under each strip, 7,000 K as before;
  - reach 6 m in the kitchen (the strips 3.3 m up: the cone's edge meets the floor 4.3 m away), 4.8 m in the back
    room (3.0 m up: 3.9 m);
  - kept inside the building [data + arithmetic]: a ray 40° off straight down gets h sideways only after
    h / sin 40° = 1.56 h. The nearest outside planes (the kitchen frame's street front z 2.61, side x 12.47, back
    z −12.30, corridor wall x −2.87) are 4.09 m from the two kitchen lamps by the street front (largest reach 6.36 m)
    and 3.14 m from the back room's two (4.88 m).
- **Not known:** how bright 1,000 lm looks there, and whether the fixed lights cast shadows (if not, the
  cone also lights what's under the floor within its reach).
- **1,350 lm:** all 6 spots at
  1,350 lm; the cone, reach, place and 7,000 K colour as before. The reach doesn't follow the lumens
  (`AddFixedLight` writes them into two separate fields, the intensity and the attenuation radius [code]), so the
  cone's edge on the floor and the gap to the building's outside are as above. The panels' glow (DogenGlow.cpp, 100 × white) is its own value and isn't changed.

**The lamps glowing the game's way.**
Goal: make the lamps look like they emit light, as the game's other lamps do.
- **How the game's own lamps glow [data + shaders]:**
  - their meshes have an emissive material: `light_int_surface_01_mesh` uses `ss_object_emissive` with
    EmissiveIntensity 100; `_04` uses EmissiveIntensity 300 and EmissiveColor (0.72, 0.94, 0.98); `_08` 50 (its folder
    has `t_light_int_surface_08_e`). Their `_off` looks set EmissiveIntensity 0;
  - their light is a separate entity: `pfl_light_int_surface_01` is a `PbrRectangularLight` 0.15 × 1.4 m at 7,000 K,
    Color (0.9102, 0.9, 1), the same as the Lights tab's 7,000 K;
  - **no game light draws a visible shape:** of 168 lights in 1,520 light, lamp, neon and sign files, none sets
    `EmissiveShapeEnable`.
- **Dogen's lamp has nothing to glow with:** `light_int_surface_05_mesh` has one material, `ss_object` (no
  emissive), and its only other look is `_dark`. Its mesh: a 0.32 × 2.5605 m plate, 8 mm thick, 8 cm under its
  origin, hung on a 2.3 cm bar 1.28 m long; the plate's lower face (local z 0.08, facing straight down) is what's
  seen.
- **Where the game's emissive goes [shaders, sp_maincity shaderdb]:**
  - its G-buffer shaders with an emissive write four targets. Target 3 (R11G11B10_FLOAT) = (the light map's
    irradiance + EmissiveColor × EmissiveIntensity × its switch) × exposureMultipliers.x (offset 42633456: `mul o3.xyz,
    r0.xyz, cb2[49].xxxx`, r0 = irradiance + emissive);
  - other emissive shaders (a forward-shaded one, offset 42608368; a two-target one, 42618780) write their colour ×
    exposureMultipliers.z into their first target;
  - its vertex shaders place a model at world − cameraPos (viewConstants register 45) through crViewProjMatrix
    (registers 14 – 17, one row each; offset 6247752).
- **How it's done (Camera/DogenGlow.cpp, .h, .hlsl, the shaders' headers):** the same thing done for Dogen's six panels.
  - As the frame's first lit pass begins (the G-buffer whole, before its lights read it: where the wet ground goes
    into targets 0 and 1, GbufferWet.cpp), each panel's face, 3 mm under the plate, is added into target 3, only
    where the G-buffer's depth shows it (the pixel shader compares; which way the game's depth runs is worked out
    from the projection itself).
  - Placed with the frame's own camera: a copy of the view constants the G-buffer pass drew with, taken as it ends
    (as GameFrame.cpp does), through the game's own crViewProjMatrix and cameraPos.
  - **How bright:** what the lamps' light gives (1,000 lm each) from the panel's face as a flat emitter:
    1000 / (π × 0.32 × 2.5605) = 388 cd/m², × the 7,000 K colour (0.9102, 0.9, 1), × the frame's
    exposureMultipliers.x as the game's do. For scale, the game's own strips use EmissiveIntensity 100 – 300 [the
    units being cd/m² is inferred].
  - Only while the lamps' lights are wanted (Faith within 40 m, 60 m to take them away, the lamps found). The game's
    render target changes are watched from the first time it's wanted (replay_gamedraws::Hook, put in once).
  - Two calls in `Visuals/GameFrame.cpp`: `dogenglow::OnPass` right
    after `gbufferwet::OnPass` (after the snow's copies, which are targets 0 – 2 only), `dogenglow::FrameEnd` at the
    top of `gameframe::FrameEnd`.
  - It logs "Dogen's kitchen: the lamps' glow added into the
    game's G-buffer target 3 ..." once it's drawn, or "the lamps' glow not drawn this frame: <why>".
- **White and less strong:** the glow shows (seen in game). It's now white (1, 1, 1) at the game's own
  ceiling strip's EmissiveIntensity, 100 (it was 388 × the 7,000 K colour), about a quarter as bright.

**The low ceiling [data].**
- The audit above (`audit.py`) only looked 0 – 2.2 m up. Looked at again 2.0 – 3.7 m up (`ceil.py`, `faces36.py`):
  - **the kitchen:** its collision ceiling (`kitchen01_mesh` block 3) is at 3.53 m, where it's drawn. Over it the

    2.97 – 3.21 m in the back room: 0.5 × 2.7 m, 24 cm deep, 17 cm under the lamps' faces;
  - **the corridor:** the building's **block 36** (x −2.87 … −0.97, y 2.58 … 15.41, z −12.30 … 2.61, the mass over
    the corridor up to the roof) begins at 2.58 m, **0.95 m under the corridor's drawn ceiling and its own collision

- **The fix:** block 36's bottom raised to 3.53 (its local y 69.077 → 70.03), its other sides as they

### 5. Plan: a real game door

**Goal.** Faith opens Dogen's door the way she opens the game's own doors: the game's prompt, her own animation,
the door moved by the game's animation. Right now the tools swing it themselves.

**What the game has (data).**
- A game door is a prefab:
  - the door object, `door_oneway_right_01` (a `PamStaticModelEntity` whose 3 parts the animation moves:
    `PamAntDrivenMeshPartsEntity`);
  - `gameplay/interactive/door/pf_doorlogic`:
    - two `PamSpatialEntryInputTrigger`s (the press-to-open spots, 0.4 / 0.8 m in front);
    - `CharacterLookAtTrigger`s and UI input entities;
    - an `AntAnimatable` (the prop skeleton `masterpropscommon_ske`);
    - Ant game state reads and writes;
  - a path link for the AI.
- **It runs on both sides:** 29 client-only logic entities, 5 server-only, 4 on both (realm fields of the logic's
  entities; the triggers and sync entities have none). A `SyncedBool` and 3
  `EventSync`s pass state between server and client.
- **Which door prefabs are loaded with Dogen's zone (397, its layer0 and network registry):**
  - the glass one-way door `pf_door_oneway_right_16_glass_opaque_01` (at 181.49, 66.51, 296.12 and 185.31,
    64.0, 290.40);
  - the **breach door `pf_door_breachsingle_16_01`**, the kind Faith kicks open;
  - the zone also has its own animation state file.
- The non-glass one-way door (the same model as Dogen's) is only in zones 613, 731 (and 170's registry) and in
  Release, so it may not be loaded at Dogen's.
- **The zone's network registry** (`centralcityprops_zs_zs_397_networkregistry_win32`, 74 objects) lists the data
  the networked entities come from: the door prefabs among them.

**How it could be done.**
- The game builds a prefab's entities through the reference factories' create (0x1431C3F40). Its creation
  structure (`info`) holds:
  - the entity bus at + 0x10;
  - the realm at + 0x20;
  - the world transform at + 0x40;
  - the data at + 0xD0;
  - the blueprint at + 0x100;
  - (Research_Mission_Prefabs_2026-10-28 section 7: logged read-only, never used to make anything.)
- **The way with the fewest unknowns:** when zone 397's layer0 streams in, the game creates its own breach door
  (or glass door) reference, on the server and on the client.
  - Right after each, the tools create one more of the same, with a copy of that reference's data. The copy's
    transform is Dogen's door's, its blueprint the same, and the copy is made under the same bus.
  - So the new door is built from data that is loaded and in the zone's network registry, and lives and dies with
    the zone's own layer.
- The static door is then kept hidden with no collision (the way the swing does it now).

**The steps (nothing past step 1 until its log is read).**
1. **Read-only log (no change to the game).**
   - For zone 397's door prefab references, on the server and the client:
     - when each is created: the whole `info` (0x130 bytes, pointers marked), its bus, the data and blueprint, the
       entities made and their classes;
     - when each is destroyed (the zone streaming out), and by what.
   - The same for the network ids those doors' `SyncedBool` / `EventSync` get (how many, from where).
   - The creation hook is the replay's (`Camera/ReplayAssetLog.cpp`, only while a replay records). It
     would need a call added that tells other code about creations.
2. **Offline:**
   - from that log, the bus's life and the network id handling;
   - decompiled, what an extra instance needs that the game's own got, and the realms' order;
   - which door fits Dogen's frame (`doorframe_oneway_right_16_01`, 1.28 m): the breach door's own frame and
     size, or the glass one-way door.
3. **One door, with an off switch** (a hidden ini setting, so the easter egg keeps no menu entry):
   - made right after the game's own, both realms;
   - the static door hidden and solid-free while it exists;
   - every step logged.
4. **If anything fails** (a crash, the door not reacting, server and client out of step): the off switch, and the
   swing door stays as it is now.

**The risks (unknown until steps 1 – 3).**
- A wrong creation structure or bus crashes the game, which is why step 1 is read-only.
- Networked entities outside the registry's own count may not sync: the door could open on the server but not be
  drawn opening, or the reverse.
- Teardown: if the bus frees our copied data or doesn't destroy our entities, there's a crash or a leftover door
  after the zone streams out.
- Dogen's briefings put their own interaction prompt at this door.

**What stays as it is meanwhile:** the swing door and the kitchen's collision and lights.

**The door decompile.**

*How a game door works [data: the wiring of `pf_doorlogic` and the three door prefabs, `w_*.txt`].*
- Names: field and event ids are Frostbite's name hash (h = 5381; h = h × 33 xor c), checked on Visible, OnTrue,
  OnFalse, SetTrue, SetFalse. The shared `hashnames.tsv` gives some of them wrong names from collisions (its "I2U" is
  Out, "NI1" In1, "Ilp" In2, "Ilq" In3).
- **The logic doesn't move the door.** Nothing in `pf_doorlogic` outputs a transform or plays a timeline on the
  door. It:
  - shows the prompts: two `PamSpatialEntryInputTrigger`s 1.5 m up, one each side of the door's plane (the second
    with two input actions), each with a `CharacterLookAtTrigger` facing its way, and two tutorial input icons;
  - enables the prompts from server-realm logic (`And` / `Not` entities of realm 1): the door on (interface
    0x62FCA856) and not barred from that side (interface 0xBDB57BC3 / 0x2B2530B8);
  - writes the door's Ant game states once it spawns (realm 0, the client: 2044302041 from 0xBDB57BC3, 995534050
    from 0x2B2530B8), and 1064941186 = true on the interface event 0xC3BD37D8;
  - reads two Ant game states (1064941186, 206388097) and, through `EventSync`s, sends the interface's events
    0xBAA76900 / 0xD4ABF287, which the door prefabs send to their AI path link's Disable / Enable.
- **What opens it [inferred from the wiring]:** the `AntAnimatableEntity` (realm 2, both sides; prop skeleton
  `masterpropscommon_ske`, its own actor and collision world assets), linked to the door's
  `PamAntDrivenMeshPartsEntity`, which moves the door object's parts. So the door is opened by Ant, the animation
  system, with Faith's own animation: the game states tell Faith's side which ways it opens.
- **The prefabs:** the plain and glass one-way doors are the same prefab but for the door object
  (`door_oneway_right_01` vs `door_oneway_right_glass_opaque_01`): the logic at (−0.04, 0.03, 0.66), the door
  object at x 0.56, the same path link. The breach door adds a game spline (1.28 m, exit angles ±2.356) and has its
  own door object.
- **Zone 397's four game doors** (layer0 [24], [36] glass right; [93] glass left; [89] breach) each stand in their
  own `doorframe_breachsingle_16_01`, among crates, a mop cart, catwalks (`neardoors.py`). All are real doorways, so
  taking one to Dogen's would leave a doorway open somewhere else.
- **Networking [data + inferred]:** zone 397's network registry names objects by partition and instance: 16 of
  layer0's own (19), and two objects inside each of its three door prefabs (breach: 0028db42…, d548df00…; glass
  right: 0e3c9d40…, 42798eda…; glass left: 3e74c684…, e0b2918d…). Many placed doors share those objects, so what tells their instances apart while the game runs must
  be their entity buses.

*The creation code [code, the decrypted image].*
- **0x143167120(info, …): one object of a blueprint.** The data's slot 5 gives the factory for `info`'s realm
  (+ 0x20). For a spatial one (category 2 at factory + 0x28) it writes parent × the object's own transform into
  `info` + 0x40 – + 0x7F, calls the factory's create (slot 1) and then writes the parent's transform back. **So a
  create takes its place from `info` + 0x40, not from the data:** a second door from the same reference needs no
  copied data, only another transform there.
- **A prefab's loop keeps nothing:** 0x1431C6280's loop over a prefab blueprint's Objects (the call at 0x1431C6586)
  drops each result; the entities belong to the bus in `info` + 0x10. (For an object blueprint, its one object's
  entity is returned, 0x1431C647D.)
- **0x1431C6280, a prefab's instance:**
  - builds a child `info` on its stack (base constructor 0x14317BA20), copying + 0x88, + 0x90, + 0xF0, + 0x108,
    \+ 0x110, + 0x120, + 0x128 from the parent's, with the new bus at + 0x10 and the blueprint at + 0x100;
  - makes each of the blueprint's Objects (+ 0x40, count at − 4) through 0x143167120, skipping those whose slot 4
    gives 1 or 3;
  - then, when the bus's + 0x30 hasn't changed and bit 2 of the blueprint's word at + 0x30 is set, makes a 0x28-byte
    object for the bus (0x14315FE50, flag 0x800), registered by 0x143166EA0 and handed to the object at [bus]
    (its slot 1).
- **0x143146140 → 0x1431404A0, the new bus:** for blueprint types in a range it checks first (else the parent's bus
  is used), 0x78 bytes from the context's allocator ([[context + 0x38] + 0x58]), made with the parent bus, the
  reference's data and the blueprint. The constructor registers it with other objects
  (0x143154110, 0x143154400, 0x143150100, each with 0x80000000) [code, not followed further].
- **The server:** four factory vtables point at 0x1431C3F40 (0x141B027C0, 0x141B028C0, 0x141B02900, 0x141B02980;
  Research_Mission_Prefabs has three of them as the client's). The server's references are made by other code
  (0x143361260 calls 0x143167120 too), not read.

*What a second door at Dogen's still depends on [unknown].*
1. Whether a second bus from the same reference data under the same parent gets the same identity as the game's
   own door's (the registrations in 0x1431404A0). If it does, the two doors' networked parts get mixed up.
2. The server's side: its creation path, and whether a door made only on the client works (the prompts are enabled
   by server-realm logic).
3. Taking it down: whether the layer's bus destroys an extra blueprint entity made under it when the zone streams
   out, or leaves it pointing at freed data.
4. Whether Faith's Ant finds a door animatable made outside the level's own creation.

*So the door wasn't built [decision].* A wrong answer to 1 – 3 crashes the game as Faith nears Dogen's
place. **The fastest safe way on:** step 1's read-only
log, now aimed at exactly 1 – 4 (the client hook is the replay's `hCreateReference` in
`Camera/ReplayAssetLog.cpp`; it needs one call added), then the door build straight
after its log, with step 3's off switch.

### 6. Not checked

  - that the parts' bits are what the collision uses;
  - that Faith walks through;

  - that the door comes back solid;
  - that the in-memory member fields (+ 0x48 first part, + 0x50 parts per instance, read in 0x1431856E0) hold 290
    and 3. If they don't, the door simply isn't found and it's logged.
- Whether the inside is lit as in the cutscene [unknown].
- The lamps as spots: brightness, shadows.
- What the 30 m mission sphere beside it streams [unknown].

### 8. The lamps dimmer at night (2026-11-08)

- **The clock [code]:** the game's time of day as the tools' time of day menu reads it
  (`VisualsManager::GetCurrentTimeOfDay`, seconds from midnight, −1 with no level). It's read in the camera hook on
  the game's thread, where the door code runs too (`CameraManager::OnCameraUpdate`). Not known: the day's brightness.
- **The hours [data]:** the game's sun's. Its time of day logic (`pf_tod_sunmooncelectialandoutdoorlightlogic`) has the
  outdoor light 0.6 from 7:00 to 17:00 and 0 before 6:15 and after 17:45 (Research_Weather_2026-10-25.md, "The sun").
  So the lamps are at the day's brightness from 07:00 to 17:00, dim from 17:00 to 17:45 as the sun goes, stay at the
  night's from 17:45 to 06:15, and come back from 06:15 to 07:00, eased (smoothstep).
- **How much [chosen, not from the game]:** 40 % of the day's at night: 540 lm a lamp instead of 1,350, the same cone
  and reach. The panels' glow (DogenGlow.cpp) goes down with them by the same share, through its draw's blend factor
  (its constants and shaders are as they were).
- **How [code]:** read every 2 s while the lamps are lit; the lights are given the new intensity when it moved 2 % of
  the day's or more, or reached the night's or the day's (at most 6 updates every 2 s, only while it changes), and
  are made at the share of the time when Faith comes near. The new intensity goes through `LightManager::SetFixedLightIntensity`, added for this: it keeps it within 0 - 1e8, sends nothing when it's unchanged, and the game reads a light's intensity from its data (+ 0xA8) each time it builds the light [code].
- The log: "Dogen's kitchen: the ceiling lamps made / dimmed at N % of the day's (N lm; the game's clock hh:mm)", as the
  share reaches the night's or the day's or moves a tenth.
- **Not known:** how 540 lm looks at night with the game's night exposure; whether the game takes a light's
  new intensity from its data when it's sent again (the menu's looks do it that way: `ApplyLook`).

- **[inferred]** follows from the above but wasn't seen directly;
- **[unknown]** not found.

### 1. The answer in short

- **Her model can be scaled with the game's own pose math.** The animation system (Ant) has a uniform
  scale per bone. Two ways in work through the game's own code paths:
  - the pose override, the mechanism the game's ghost runners and the tools' replay already use;
  - the pose placement.

  A scale on her root bone (bone 1, AITrajectory, at her feet) would scale every bone below it about
  her feet: body, head, hands, feet, and her camera joint.
  **[decompile; that the drawn mesh follows is inferred, see 2.4]**
- **Her collision can't be resized safely with what's known.**
  - Her movement capsule is a value in the Ant data (CollisionDriver: radius, height, step-up). Its live
    copy wasn't found.
  - Her AI capsule body is a Havok shape built once at spawn.
  - Her parkour checks (vault, ledges, wall-run, floor, falls) each have their own fixed distances in the
    Ant data, and none of them would follow.

  So resizing collision would change what she fits through without changing how her moves work.
  **[decompile + data; the Ant data values: unknown]**
- **So only a model-only slider is possible now.**
  - Her moves keep their normal-size distances: she runs, jumps and climbs as far as before.
  - Her collision stays normal size.
  - A big Faith would push into walls and ceilings; a small one would stop short of walls.
  - Her hands would miss ledges by the size difference.

### 2. How her model is placed and drawn

#### 2.1 The chain
- **Entity.** Her soldier is `PamClientCharacterEntity` (ClientGameContext + 0x68 → + 0x568 → + 0x14A0).
  - Its transform rows live in its components (+0x38).
  - **[live: MEC_Reverse_Notes §9]**
- **Animatables.** She has two `ClientAntAnimatableEntity`s on the same skeleton and the same pose
  manager.
  - **Drawn body:** soldier + 0x248.
  - **Box pose:** soldier + 0x340. Its bones are PamCharacterEntityData.BoundingBoxBones = 179 CameraJoint,
    53 HeadEnd, 167 / 175 feet, 9, 117, 166, 174 **[data]**. They make her bounding box, so the drawn
    body is culled by them **[live: FaithReplay.cpp's comment]**.
- **Pose buffers.**
  - The pose object is at animatable + 0x158; its handle (+0x118) picks a page and slot in the manager
    (+0x1B8 / + 0x210).
  - Page + 0x00: local pose A. Page + 0x08: world pose B. Both 0x20 bytes per bone.
  - Page + 0x10: skinning matrices C, 3x4 rows = world pose × the inverse bind pose.
  - Page + 0x18 / + 0x20: Ant's own local pose (D, E), 0x30 bytes per bone.
  - **[live: MEC_Reverse_Notes 2026-10-23, SnowBodies.cpp]**
- **Her skeleton** (`characters/skeletons/skeleton_faith`, 182 bones) **[data]**:

| Bone | Name | Parent | Bind place (model space) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Reference | none | 0, 0, 0 |
| 1 | AITrajectory | 0 | 0, 0, 0 (her feet) |
| 2 | Trajectory | 1 | 0, 0, 0 |
| 4 | Hips | 1 | y 0.896 |
| 52 / 53 | Head / HeadEnd | | y 1.539 / 1.683 |
| 178 / 179 | CameraBase / CameraJoint | 1 / 178 | y 1.580, z 0.073 |
| 180 | Connect | 1 | 0, 0, 0 |

  Everything she is hangs off bone 1: hips, legs, spine, arms, head, camera.

#### 2.2 The scale that's already there (no tools needed to find it)
1. **Ant's pose record is (scale, rotation, translation).**
   - It's 0x30 bytes per bone: scale x y z w at + 0x00, rotation quaternion at + 0x10, translation at
     \+ 0x20.
   - The pose blend 0x142FD6180 writes the root record as scale (1, 1, 1, 1) and rotation (0, 0, 0, 1)
     (at 0x142FD63C3).
   - **[decompile; the layout also live, 2026-10-23]**
2. **The 0x20-byte format keeps the scale in the "1".**
   - The pose job's copy 0x142FD9D50 (loop at 0x142FD9DC0) packs each bone into the 0x20 format as
     translation (x, y, z, **scale.x**), then rotation.
   - So the "translation x y z 1" layout everyone reads holds her uniform scale in that 4th float. It's
     1.0 because nothing scales her. **[decompile]**
3. **Ant's math carries the scale down the skeleton.**
   - The whole-skeleton local → model pass is **0x142C1D5B0** (two bones per loop). For each bone:
     - scale = its own × its parent's;
     - translation = parent rotation × (parent scale × own translation) + parent translation.
   - The one-joint helpers 0x142C1A8F0 and 0x142C1B2D0 do the same.
   - **[decompile]**
4. **The game's pose override can set a bone's scale.**
   - The override is applied by 0x142FCF620 (called by the ANT pose job 0x142FCC7C0).
   - For each listed bone, rotation and translation are blended toward the override's by its weight
     (+ 0x18 of the override, job + 0x148).
   - **The override's 4th translation float (+ 0x0C) is written as the bone's scale, whatever the
     weight** (0x142FCFA5A – 0x142FCFA6F: broadcast into the record's + 0x00).
   - So an override with weight 0 and that float = s:
     - leaves the bone's animation as it is (translation exactly; rotation renormalised, a few float
       steps at most);
     - and gives it scale s.
   - **[decompile]**
   - The tools' replay writes 1.0 there for every bone (FaithReplay.cpp, `o[3] = 1.f` and the like).
5. **The pose placement takes a scale too.**
   - The placement setter **0x142FD8F20**(pose, 4x4, flag) passes the matrix to 0x142A63A30(out,
     matrix, 1).
   - 0x142A63A30 takes scale = the length of row 0, normalises the rows, and returns translation
     (x, y, z, scale) plus a quaternion.
   - 0x142FD8F20 then writes that scale into the root record's scale, unless pose + 0x12E forces 1.
   - The pose job's final step (end of 0x142FD9D50, 0x142FDA6C8 – 0x142FDA880) multiplies the root by
     the placement's scale (translation.w) when it puts it in the world.
   - **[decompile]**
   - **[unknown]** Which placement path Faith's body takes: mode animatable + 0x90 → 0x142FD8C30 (store
     only) or 0x142FD8F20, and whether + 0x12E is set for her. A live read needs the game running.

#### 2.3 What isn't a way in
- **Her entity's transform rows.** Scaled rows would reach the pose only through the placement path
  above, if hers is that one.
  - Many other readers take those rows as a pure rotation: the camera, attach targets, the AI capsule body
    (a Havok body moved by them), the tools' replay and snow code.
  - So scaling the entity rows isn't safe. **[inferred]**
- **A mesh or blueprint scale.**
  - No reflected class has a mesh, model or character scale field.
  - Ant's rig data has BindPoseScaleList and JointScaleAdjustDofIndices (names only).
  - **[decompile: strings and reflection]**

#### 2.4 Does the drawn mesh follow?
- **Skinning matrices.**
  - The skinning matrices C are "world pose × inverse bind pose" **[live]**.
  - With a scale on bone 1, every bone's world translation is scaled about her feet and its world scale
    (the 4th float) is s **[decompile, 2.2]**.
  - If C is built from those with the scale, the mesh is drawn scaled.
  - **The code that writes C wasn't found.** The only code indexing C by the manager's matrix stride is
    the reader 0x142FCEF00, which hands pointers out.
  - So "the mesh scales" is **[inferred]**, not verified. If C were built without the scale, the bones
    would spread apart while each part keeps its size. That would look broken.
- **The first-person camera.**
  - It sits exactly on CameraJoint (bone 179) **[live: FaithReplay.cpp]**.
  - CameraJoint hangs off bone 1, so the camera would rise and sink with her size: eye height 1.58 m × s.
    **[inferred]**
- **Hair.** It's cloth, and the cloth takes skinning matrices (string `ClothInstance::SkinningMatrices`).
  - **[inferred]** The hair is anchored to the scaled head.
  - **[unknown]** Whether its simulation copes with a scaled body.
- **Her box pose (+ 0x340)** must get the same scale. Otherwise the game culls a big Faith by her
  normal-size box. **[inferred from the culling finding in 2.1]**

#### 3.2 What else assumes her normal size
- **Movement.** Ant's movement drivers and processors are registered at 0x142F38B10 **[decompile:

- **Their distances are in her Ant data, not in code.** RayCastCollisionProcessor's defaults are

- **None of them would follow a size change.**
  - The animations' root motion moves her by the distances they were made with.
  - A ledge found at its real height would put a big Faith's hands above it and a small Faith's hands

  - **[inferred]**
- **Combat, hand plants, foot plants and the magrope** read her bones (PamHandPlantEntityData,

Her moves, speed, jump and climb distances and collision stay normal. A big Faith pushes into walls, doorways and ceilings; a small one stops short of walls. Hands miss ledges. Feet look like they slide at sizes far from 1 (normal-size steps, scaled legs). [inferred; mesh following: see 2.4] |
| B. Model + movement capsule | No, not with what's known | The live CollisionDriver assets weren't found, and where the default size comes from isn't known. Even then her moves stay normal size. |

### 5b. The first build's result, and the second build
- **The first build [seen in game]:** her body doesn't scale, only her hair; going back to 1.00 doesn't bring her hair
  back; the first-person camera doesn't shrink either.
- **Live, read only (size back at 1.00 after 0.50):**
  - **The game's world pose ignores the scale.** Bone 1's scale was 0.50 in the local pose (page + 0x00), the
    world pose (+ 0x08) and Ant's own records (+ 0x18 / + 0x20). Yet the hips stood 0.870 m from bone 1, which is
    the length of their local offset, and their world 4th float was 1.0. So the world pose is composed from
    translation and rotation only.
  - **The skinning matrices ignore it too.** Every row had length 1.0000.
  - **So 2.4's "inferred" was wrong** for the world pose and matrices. Ant's own composer (0x142C1D5B0) carries the
    scale, but the game's world pose isn't made with it. The hair cloth does follow bone 1's scale.
  - **The game never resets that scale.** It stayed 0.50 with the override gone, which is why 1.00 left her hair
    small.
  - **The render-side entry is the local pose.** [page + 0x40] + slot × 0x20 points to two buffers that hold Ant's
    local pose (scale, rotation, translation), not the drawn matrices.
- **Second build:**
  - **Sizing:** every frame from the camera hook, both slots' world pose and matrices are sized about bone 1, bones
    from the hips on, in the same way the replay already poses bodies the game doesn't update.
  - **Per bone:** a bone still holding the tools' values isn't sized again. A value the game wrote that's already
    nearer the sized length is left alone.
  - **At 1.00:** the bones still holding the tools' values get the game's values back. Bone 1's scale is handed 1.00
    until it reads 1.00 again.
  - **Still unknown:** whether the game writes her pose after the camera hook and before drawing. A diagnostic log
    line counts how often the game had written it anew between two hooks.

### 6. Her collision at her size (research, 2026-11-03)

Goal: make her collision work with her size. Offline (game image), plus what was seen in game. Labels as in the
rest of this file.

#### 6.1 How her movement meets the world
- **Ant's collision interface is `FrostbiteCollisionWorld`.**
  - It's 0x90 bytes, made by 0x142FD0D10 with constructor 0x142FC98B0 and vtable 0x141ABC7E8.
  - One is kept at animation manager + 0x150. It holds the physics world from 0x1434EE940 at + 0x88 (the same
    helper the game's own sweeps use).
  - Ant's drivers and processors ask it for queries; Havok answers them. **[decompile]**
- **The queries [decompile]:**

| Vtable slot | Function | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 6 (+ 0x30) | 0x142FCB200 | A shape cast: Ant shape, Ant transform, direction × distance. The transform is Ant's (scale, rotation, translation); the rotation rows are multiplied by the scale's x / y / z. Then cast 0x1434E2900 → 0x14351A3A0 (no body ignored, 0x7FFFFFFF). Hits go into Ant's result bus (0x142CC6350, 0x142FD0840) with two 16-bit ids from the caller (meaning **[unknown]**) |
| 7 (+ 0x38) | 0x142FCB5B0 | A second shape cast, the same transform handling |
| 14 (+ 0x70) | 0x142FCB8E0 → 0x142FD5BD0 | A sphere cast (sphere 0x1434DB570), or a ray (0x1434E27C0) |
| 13 (+ 0x68) | 0x142FCBA90 | The batched queries: jobs "antCollisionupdatejob" and "fbc_gatherresultsjob" |

- **Shapes are made anew for every query** (0x142FD0ED0), from Ant collision volume assets **[decompile]**:
  - **capsule** (type 0x5E4D2B70): Radius + 0x60, HalfHeight + 0x64. Made as the segment (0, ±HalfHeight, 0) with
    that radius, through 0x143514D80 → Havok capsule 0x143F6B310;
  - **sphere** (0xFEFFAA77): radius + 0x60;
  - **box** (0xFA1693D1): half extents + 0x60.

  **So a volume's numbers are read at each query:** changed at run time, they take effect at the next query.
  **[decompile; not verified in game]**
- **The collision volume assets** (CollisionVolumeAsset, registered at 0x142AF7AE0) have RuntimeKey, Scale,
  Quaternion, Translation and SurfaceId. CapsuleAsset (0x70 bytes, factory 0x142AF6CA0) has:
  - Scale + 0x20 (1, 1, 1, 1);
  - rotation + 0x30 (identity);
  - Translation + 0x40;
  - Radius + 0x60 (1.0);
  - HalfHeight + 0x64 (1.0).

  (Constructor defaults; offsets from the factory and the shape conversion.) **[decompile]** Faith's own volumes and
  their values are **[unknown]**: Ant's packages aren't decoded, and her live ones weren't found.
- **Her movement capsule.** `CollisionDriverAsset` has UseCustomCollisionSize, CustomCollisionCapsuleRadius / Height
  / StepUpHeight, UseCrouchCollision and EnableStepUp (§3.1). Its constructor defaults are radius 0.30, height 1.80,
  step-up 0.24. The driver's full constructor is 0x142EE2070 (vtable 0x141AAAAB8). **[decompile]**
  - **[unknown]** Which query its step uses.
  - **[unknown]** Where its size comes from when "custom" is off. Likely her capsule volume, not traced.
- **Her AI capsule body** (layer 20, 1.2 / 0.3, §3.1) is a Havok body whose shape is built once at spawn. It's what
  other characters' bodies meet, not her movement. **[data + decompile]**
- **Does Ant's scale already reach her capsule? [unknown]** The shape casts multiply the rotation rows by the
  transform's scale. If her movement capsule's transform carries bone 1's scale, the slider's sizes have already
  lengthened or shortened its segment. Havok adds a convex shape's radius after transforming its points, so the
  radius wouldn't follow. **[inferred, not verified in game]** Not settled offline.

- **Ant's movement drivers and processors** (the list in §3.2) each query with their own distances and heights from

#### 6.3 Ways to make her collision follow her size
| | What | Needs | What it does to her moves | Feasible? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Her capsule only** | Her capsule's Radius, HalfHeight and local Translation × size, and the CollisionDriver's custom radius / height / step-up × size. Either in her live volume assets (they're read at each query), or per query in a hook on the shape conversion 0x142FD0ED0 | Finding *her* volumes (other characters use the same interface and may share assets). Either a read-only live probe from her animatable, or a diagnostic that logs the shapes going through 0x142FD0ED0 with how far each query starts from her | Walls, ceilings and gaps meet her at her size: a big Faith can't pass normal doors, a small one fits small gaps. Every move still triggers and travels at normal size. A big Faith climbing a normal ledge has her capsule pushed into it while the animation lifts her normal-size distances, so she may stick or pop out **[inferred]** | Yes, with a find-her-volumes step first. Moderate risk: a wrong match would resize someone else |
| **B. Her moves too** | Her whole movement run in a world scaled by 1 / size about her: every query's start, end and shape × size about her and its hits mapped back; her root motion × size; and every piece of world move data Ant reads (ledges, splines, magrope targets, springboards, mission move volumes) mapped the same way | Each of those paths found and hooked; most aren't decoded | Moves would work at her size: she vaults a wall twice as high at size 2, runs twice as fast, and falls as if the world were small | Not as a slider: many separate paths, each a crash or desync risk. A project of its own |
| **C. Her AI capsule** | A new Havok capsule for her AI body at her size | A body-shape setter in hknp (**not located**), or remaking the body | KrugerSec bodies meet her at her size | Possible later; small gain |

**Recommendation:** A, as its own tick ("Collision follows size") next to the slider.
1. First a diagnostic. While she's sized, it logs each Ant shape the conversion sees: its pointer, type, Radius
   / HalfHeight, local translation and scale, and how far the query starts from her. That shows which volumes
   are hers and whether her movement capsule already gets bone 1's scale.
2. Then the tick: her volumes and her CollisionDriver's numbers × size while sized, and the game's own back at 1.00
   or unticked.

B isn't recommended.

#### 6.3b Option A, step 1: the diagnostic
- **More found while writing it [decompile]:**
  - **Slot 8 is a registration.** Slot 8 (0x142FCC1B0) doesn't query: it registers a collision object once.
    0x142FD1070 takes an Ant asset, or a list of volumes (type 0xC39365CD: count + 0x60, volumes + 0x68), makes each
    volume's Havok shape then, and keeps the record (0x7F0 bytes, ids at + 0x2C / + 0x2E) in the world's list
    (+ 0x08 .. + 0x18).
  - **So some Ant collision is baked at registration.** Changing a registered volume's numbers later wouldn't reach
    it.
  - **Slot 6 makes its shape per query.** Slot 7 takes a Havok shape made elsewhere.
- **The diagnostic** hooks slots 6, 7 and 8 and changes nothing. While she's sized, it tallies the casts near her
  feet: slot, shape, caller, sizes, the volume's own transform, the cast's transform, ids. It also logs every
  registration (the first 60 of a session).

#### 6.3c The diagnostic's first findings (size 0.09) [seen in game]
- **Registrations** (all by 0x142CD2B6D, per character; id1 4 – 10):
  - every character: two spheres (radius 0.16, 0.10 m up) and a capsule (radius 0.35, half height 0.60, 0.90 m up,
    a6 20);
  - id 7 (her checks carry it, below): capsules 0.20 / 0.20 at 0.15 m, **0.30 / 0.18 at 0.48 m** (a6 14), and spheres
    of 0.20.
- **Her casts** (all with ids 7 / 0, filter 0xE, **the cast's scale 1.000 at size 0.09**, so the size doesn't reach
  her collision):
  - **movement** (0x142F3C117):
    - slot 7: a ready-made capsule centred 0.48 m up, horizontal steps of about 0.24 m;
    - one centred 0.90 m up, sweeping down 0.63 m;
  - **ledge and obstacle probes** (0x142F4B1D8, slot 7): five capsules at 1.44 / 1.62 / 1.80 / 1.98 / 2.16 m sweeping
    2.5 m ahead, and casts from 0.48 m up 3 m or down 10 m (also 0x142F47756);
  - **box probes** (0x142F4B21A, slot 6): an Ant box, half extents 0.12 / 0.54 / 0.12, from 0.86 m, 2.5 m ahead.
- **What it means for option A [inferred from these findings]:**
  - Her body collision is ready-made Havok capsules: Frostbite shape wrappers, vtable 0x141BB19C0, the ones
    0x143514D80 makes. They're made at registration, not per query.
  - So her capsule can't be resized by changing volume numbers. The slot 7 cast would get a sized capsule of the
    tools' own, put in place of hers when id1 is hers and the caller is her movement (0x142F3C117). The sweep would
    stay, so her moves keep their normal distances.
  - Her ledge, obstacle and floor probes would stay normal size.
  - **[unknown]** How to tell her id other than by casts that start at her feet. And whether making Havok shapes from
    the tools is safe on the job threads the casts run on.
- **A crash** was in the crowd and traffic boids update (0x143B9BFA0 ← 0x143B9B7E0 ← 0x143B9BC10, a parallel-for item
  that checks CrowdBoidsComponent and CrowdPlacementBoidsEntity), with a garbage object pointer. There was no tools
  frame on that thread. **It came from the tools' road traffic code**, which reads those structures: hidden cars at
  y −10042 fell out of the game's node lists, and a despawn's list move then corrupted the member arrays. The fix puts
  hidden cars back at −10000.
