# 49. Faith's arm tattoo: how it's drawn and how the tools take it off (2026-11-08)

Goal: an option under Faith that removes her arm tattoo. Sources: the game's data on disk (fb tools: show_patched.py,
importers.py / importers_patched.py, chunkfind.py; new read-only scripts: mvdb_entries.py, mvdb_tex.py, meshlods.py,
uvcheck.py, texdump.py, bundles_of.py, rawshow.py) and the tools' log. No live reads of the game. **Nothing here was
tried in game.**

### 1. What it is: a texture switch (verified in data)

Not baked into the only skin texture, not a separate mesh part, not a decal, not a shader parameter.

- Her arms are one mesh, `characters/faith/arms/faith_arms_mesh` (SkinnedMeshAsset, MeshSet res 15549054755981171245).
  Materials: index 0 = `ca53e0d2` (ss_character_skin_02, the skin), index 1 = `09af1506` (ss_character, the glove).
  Sections per LOD (material index at section + 0x18): SkinUpper (0), Glove_M (1), and a UV-less depth section.
- `levels/sp/sp_maincity/sp_maincity/meshvariationdb_win32`, faith_arms_mesh:
  - variation 0 (the mesh's own): skin = Diffuse_AO `t_arms_dao`, NormalRS `t_arms_nrs`, Opacity_SSS_Metal_Trans
    `t_arms_ex`, MaterialMask `t_arms_m`, detail t_fuzz_*; glove = t_glove_d / _n / _rsm, AO t_arms_ao.
  - variation **4240144052** (`characters/faith/arms/faith_arms_notattoo`, ObjectVariation "Faith_Arms_NoTattoo", 4
    MeshMaterialVariations): skin = `t_arms_notattoo_dao`, `t_arms_notattoo_nrs`, `t_arms_notattoo_ex`, the same mask
    and detail; glove the same as variation 0.
  - The other level DBs with faith_arms_mesh (centralcityprops zs 170 / 172, droneworks, familymatters) have variation
    0 only.
- Texture res headers (format at + 0x0C): t_arms_dao fmt 67 (decodes as BC7), t_arms_notattoo_dao fmt 61 (BC3), both
  2048 x 2048, 12 mips; t_arms_ex / t_arms_notattoo_ex fmt 54 (BC1), 1024 x 1024.
- Decoded mip 0 and compared (Pillow's BCn decoder):
  - Colour: RGB differs by > 40 at 60,847 pixels, all in the tattoo, in one arm's part of the texture: bounding box
    x 169 – 1241, y 173 – 1352 (> 80: x 356 – 625, y 174 – 1097). Alpha (AO) the same everywhere. The dark band across
    that arm is the same in both, and covers part of the ink.
  - SSS map: only the green channel differs (up to 53), in the tattoo's shape.
- Which mesh draws those pixels (UV0, half2 at vertex + 52, triangles rasterized at 2048; V as stored, which puts
  100 % of SkinUpper on painted texels, 97.9 % flipped):
  - faith_arms_mesh SkinUpper: 60,840 of the 60,847 tattoo pixels at LOD 0 (the same at LODs 1 – 3).
  - faith_upperbody_mesh gloveArmguard (material 1 = `874650c4`, which uses t_arms_dao / t_arms_nrs / t_arms_m with
    ribbing detail): u 0.087 – 0.397, v 0.347 – 0.495, **0** tattoo pixels at LODs 0 – 2 (LOD 3 has no such section).
  - faith_prologue_upperbody_mesh Arms_Skin_M (material 2 = `e6560317`, its own t_faithprologue_arms_dao, but
    t_arms_ex for SSS): v 0.697 – 0.999 (the hands), **0** pixels of the SSS map's tattoo. Its LOD 1+ skin material
    has no t_arms_ex.
  - No other entry in the five DBs uses `characters/faith/upperbody/t_arms*`.

### 2. What picks it (data; code from Research_Faith_Outfit_2026-10-26 §2)

- The outfit. `gameplay/spawners/pf_spspawn_01` has seven CustomizeCharacterEntityData (Realm 1); its SelectEvent #113,
  driven by a progression flag, sends Apply (0x0C487271) to one; each links Characters -> #12 (the
  CharacterSpawnReference of characters/faithcharacter). Checked again for #43 and #47.
- #47 `C_Faith_WithTattoo` (Flags 1689729674; flag 7, RunnerWithTattoo, set at The Shard) lists 15 VisualUnlockAssets:
  hair_3pcloth_ingame, head, lowerbody, toolbag, upperbody_notattoo, lowerbody1p, toolbag1p, upperbody_notattoo_1p,
  headparts, **arms, arms1p**, magr_pickup_3, magr_pickup_3_1p, magrope, magrope_1p.
- #43 `C_Faith_NoTat_MagRope3` (Flags 1711066455; flag 6, RunnerWithPullDown) lists the same but **arms1p_notattoo,
  arms_notattoo**: VisualUnlockAssets whose OutObjectBlueprint is a MeshAndVariationPair {faith_arms_mesh,
  Faith_Arms_NoTattoo} (Unlock_Faith_Arms / Arms1p point at the ObjectBlueprint faith_arms, the plain mesh).
  "upperbody_notattoo" is just faith_upperbody, the same in both.
- Every other field of the two PamCustomizeCharacterData is the same (zeros printed too): Unlocks [],
  OverrideMaxHealth -1, OverrideCriticalHealthThreshold -1, RestoreToOriginalVisualState false, ClearVisualState true,
  the same 5 ImpactZoneMappings, the same WriteEnumerationGameState (d1466a63..., PropertyHash 0, Value 0).
- C_Faith_WithTattoo is imported only by the spawner (and the network registry); Unlock_Faith_Arms / Arms1p only by
  C_Faith_WithTattoo. So only the player's Faith ever has the tattoo. (`objects/props/cinematics/faithtattoo` is a
  separate model placed in centralcityprops_zs_zs_397; it isn't part of her.)
- Bundles: the textures (ebx and res), the variation, the unlocks, both outfits, the spawner and the main DB are all in
  `win32/levels/sp/sp_maincity/sp_maincity`, the main city's own bundle (Data and Patch sp_maincity.sb).
- In game the tools' log has shown the game dressing her in C_Faith_WithTattoo.
- How the engine turns MeshAndVariationPair into the arms' materials (inside the character's customize, slot + 0x340
  0x14336CF00) wasn't traced: not needed, the tools only send the game's own Apply.

### 3. What the tools do (2026-11-08)

GAME > Faith > **No arm tattoo** (under Outfit; saved as `[Misc] NoArmTattoo`, off by default):
- `faith_outfit::WantedOutfit` maps C_Faith_WithTattoo (index 6) to C_Faith_NoTat_MagRope3 (5) while ticked, after the
  replay's outfit and the menu's choice. The existing path does the rest: the game's own Apply on #47 is noted by the
  handler hook, and the next Server::update sends #43's Apply through its own handler (Dress). Unticking sends #47's.
- `WornOutfit` (what the replay records) tells 6 when she wears 5 in its place, so playback follows the tick.
- The tick works while a replay records or plays (the Outfit combo doesn't).

### 4. Not known / not verified

- Not tried in game. Whether the tools' own Apply (Dress) works: it has never shown up in the tools' log ("dressed
  in ... (Apply sent"); the game's Apply hook is proven by the logs.
- Whether the arms show the tattoo for a moment at a level load or a respawn (the game dresses her first, the tools at
  the next server update), and whether the no-tattoo textures show sharp at once or stream in.
- First person: the 1p arms are in both outfits (arms1p / arms1p_notattoo), so they should switch too; not seen.

# 50. A pose editor in the game: what's possible (2026-11-08)

Goal: find out whether a pose editor in the game is possible, to pose Faith and other characters (KrugerSec etc.), by
decompiling the systems it needs.

This research is an offline decompile of the game image and its data, plus earlier live reads written down elsewhere
(each one cited). Game build 0x5762E3B7.

How each claim is known:
- **[decompile]**: read in the game's code for this research (addresses given).
- **[decompile, earlier]**: read in the code earlier (file cited).
- **[data]**: read in the game's ebx files for this research.
- **[live, earlier]**: read in the running game earlier (where it's written down).
- **[log]**: the tools' log.
- **[inferred]**: follows from the above, not seen directly.
- **[unknown]**: not found.

### 1. The answer in short

| Who | Can be posed bone by bone? | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Faith** (third person with the free camera, and first person) | **Yes** | The game's own pose override on her body (soldier + 0x248) and her box pose (+ 0x340). This is the mechanism the Dash ghosts use. The replay poses her whole skeleton with it [log, live, earlier]. |
| **KrugerSec of every type, and named civilians** (any `PamClientCharacterEntity` whose body the game animates) | **Yes** | The same override on their body (+ 0x248). The replay poses people this way [log], and live KrugerSec have been posed with it [live, earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes]. |
| KrugerSec the game no longer animates (taken down / ragdoll, or far from Faith) | **Not with the override**: the game skips their pose job | The replay's other path (it writes their pose buffers itself and holds the game's update) exists, but it's harder and it had visibility bugs. Recommended for later. |
| **Crowds** (the walking city people, the road traffic's walkers) | **No, not one person** | A swarm's members share a few poses that the GPU reads from a texture [decompile, earlier: Research_Crowds_Textures §2]. |
| **Drones** (`PamClientDroneActorEntity`) | **[unknown]** | Whether a drone has an Ant body at + 0x100 was never read [FaithReplay.cpp:1938]. Their skeleton is skeleton_drone (49 bones) [data]. One read-only live check settles it. |

**One thing isn't known and matters most:** whether the game applies a pose override while *Freeze time* is on (time
scale 0, so no simulation ticks). The override is applied in the pose job's first step. That step only runs when the
body's "pose update" is due, and what makes it due while frozen wasn't traced (section 2.3). Section 7 has a fallback
that's already proven to draw, but it leaves her hair behind.

**What the first build would contain:** section 6.

### 2. Where a character's pose lives each frame

#### 2.1 The objects
- **Character:** `PamClientCharacterEntity`. Faith's is ClientGameContext + 0x68 → + 0x568 → + 0x14A0 [live, earlier:
  MEC_Reverse_Notes §15].
- **Body:** a `ClientAntAnimatableEntity` (TypeInfo 0x1427EEE10) at character + 0x248. Faith has a second one at
  \+ 0x340: her box pose. Its bones make her culling box (PamCharacterEntityData.BoundingBoxBones) [live, earlier:
  FaithReplay.cpp:69–96].
- **Pose object:** animatable + 0x158.
  - + 0x118 is its handle: byte 3 a page, byte 0 a slot.
  - + 0x1B8 is its pose manager.
  - + 0x12C is "pose update on"; it's the slot object's + 0xBC.
  - [live + decompile, earlier: FaithReplay.cpp:40–66, MEC_Reverse_Notes 2026-10-24]
- **Pose manager:** one per skeleton asset, shared by every body of that skeleton (Faith and the Dash ghosts share one)
  [live, earlier: §15].

| Manager field | What | How known |
|---|---|---|
| + 0x08 | bone count | [decompile] 0x142FD7814: copied into the transform job's + 0x28, its loop count |
| + 0x88 | 0xB8 for Faith; copied into the job's + 0x164 | [live, earlier: §15] [decompile] 0x142FD798E |
| + 0x8C | local/world pose stride per slot (bones × 0x20) | [live, earlier] |
| + 0x90 | skinning matrix stride per slot (bones × 0x30) | [live, earlier] |
| + 0x94 | 0x2D80 for Faith (182 × 0x40); what uses it isn't known | [live, earlier: §15] |
| + 0x98 | stride of Ant's two animation steps (page + 0x18 / + 0x20): 0x2280 for Faith, 182 × 0x30 + 0x60 | [live, earlier: §15; FaithReplay.cpp:944–954] |
| + 0xA0 | inverse bind pose, 0x20 per bone (translation, quaternion), used for the skinning matrices | [decompile] 0x142FD7959 → job + 0x20, read at 0x142FD01A0 with a 0x20 step. That it's the inverse bind: the replay found matrices = world × a fixed transform per bone, the same in every body of a skeleton [live, earlier: FaithReplay.cpp:944–954] |
| + 0xA8 | inverse bind pose as 4×4 matrices (0x40 a bone), used by the hair cloth | [decompile] 0x142FD7DD2, 0x142FDA6AA (`shl r9, 6`); [decompile, earlier: Research_Faith_Size §6.5] |
| **+ 0xF0** | **parent index per bone** (u32, −1 for none): the skeleton's hierarchy | [decompile] 0x142FD77E8 → job + 0x08, read as the parent at 0x142FD021C |
| + 0x190 | the root bone (AITrajectory, bone 1) | [decompile] 0x142FD7807 → job + 0x18 |
| + 0x210 | pages (vector) | [live + decompile, earlier] |
| + 0x2B8 / + 0x2B9 | has render entries / has matrices | [decompile, earlier] |

| Page field (one page holds many slots) | What |
|---|---|
| + 0x00 | **local pose A**, 0x20 a bone: translation x y z, the bone's scale as the 4th float, then a rotation quaternion, each relative to the bone's parent [live + decompile, earlier; decompile 0x142FD9DE0–0x142FD9E08] |
| + 0x08 | **world pose B**, same layout, 4th float always 1.0 [decompile] 0x142FCFF7D–0x142FCFFA3 |
| + 0x10 | **skinning matrices C**: 3 rows a bone (rotation, translation in the 4th column) = world × inverse bind [decompile] 0x142FD018F–0x142FD01A0 |
| + 0x18 / + 0x20 | Ant's two animation steps (0x30 a bone: scale, rotation, translation) [live, earlier] |
| + 0x28 | per-slot objects (+ 0xBC pose update on; the first 0xE0 bytes are copied into each job) [decompile] 0x142FD7C9F–0x142FD7D17 |
| + 0x30 | **the override per slot** (a pointer, 0 for none) [decompile] 0x142FD7D6B–0x142FD7D7A |
| + 0x38 | per-slot buffer descriptors, 0x20 apart, 0x40 bytes copied: + 0x08 local, + 0x10 world, + 0x18 matrices [decompile] 0x142FD78CA–0x142FD7907 |
| + 0x40 | render-side entries (+ 0x14 on) [decompile + live, earlier] |

#### 2.2 The order in a frame (decompiled)
1. **Ant's own evaluation** writes Ant's records (scale, rotation, translation, 0x30 a bone).
   - This is the animation graph. Its node types include `antqTwoBoneIKNode`, `antqSetDofNode`, `antqApplyPoseNode`
     and the blends (strings at 0x141A12C20–0x141A23A38).
   - Ant's scene ops are part of it: `PamplonaFootplantSceneOpAsset`, `PamplonaHandplantSceneOpAsset` (hand IK), and
     `PamplonaCopyPoseSceneOp`. So are its subsystems: IK rig 0x142E64300, physics pose 0x142ECAA00, particle IK
     0x142F53E70 and PA2 facial (GridNode's ant.yaml / ant_runtime.yaml).
   - **[inferred]** All of these run inside Ant, before Ant hands the pose to Frostbite's pose jobs (step 2). The code
     is in Ant's address range, and the pose job is reached from Ant's scene driver (step 2). Their exact place in the
     frame wasn't traced.
2. **The Ant pose job 0x142FCC7C0**, reached through slot 13 (0x142FCE080) of the table at 0x141ABCA30 [decompile].
   - **Step 1**, when request + 0x80 is set and the slot's pose update (+ 0xBC) is on:
     - 0x142FD7C60 copies into the job: the slot object (job + 0x00), the slot's buffer descriptor (+ 0xF0), and the
       override if there is one (0x28 bytes at + 0x130, its bone list's data at + 0x158).
     - **0x142FCF620 applies the override** into Ant's records (job + 0xA0):
       - it does nothing if the override's handle (job + 0x150) is −1 (0x142FCF62D);
       - it loops over the override's count (job + 0x14C);
       - it blends each listed bone toward the override by the weight (job + 0x148);
       - it writes the 4th translation float as the bone's scale whatever the weight (0x142FCFA5A).
       - [decompile; the blend and the scale, decompile, earlier: Research_Faith_Size §2.2]
   - **Step 2**, when request + 0x81 is set and the slot's render entry is on: 0x142FCFB10, 0x142FD7A10, then
     0x142FD6180 [decompile].
     - 0x142FD7A10 picks the interpolation mode by distance [decompile, earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes §16].
     - 0x142FD6180 is the pose blend [decompile, earlier: Research_Faith_Size §2.2]. That it blends the two animation
       steps (page + 0x18 / + 0x20) is **[inferred]**.
3. **`antFbUpdateLocalPose`** (registered at 0x142FC9770: job 0x142FD9CF0 → 0x142FD9D50 for each 0x170-byte item).
   - It turns Ant's records into the slot's local pose (descriptor + 0x08, the page + 0x00 slot), in the 0x20 layout.
   - The 4th float is the record's scale.x (0x142FD9DE0–0x142FD9E08) [decompile].
4. **`antFbPrepareBuildRenderTransformsData`** (0x142FD77B0 → 0x142FD77E0) fills a job item [decompile]:
   - + 0x08 parents (manager + 0xF0), + 0x18 root bone, + 0x20 inverse bind, + 0x28 bone count;
   - + 0x30 – + 0x10F the slot object (her placement);
   - + 0x128 / + 0x130 / + 0x138 the local, world and matrix pointers;
   - + 0x160 mode: 2 with matrices, 1, or 0 with a render entry.
5. **`antFbBuildRenderTransforms`** (0x142FCFBA0 → 0x142FCFBB0 → **0x142FCFC30**) [decompile]:
   - **This is the writer of the world pose and the skinning matrices** that Research_Faith_Size §2.4 hadn't found.
   - It goes over the bones in index order. For each bone:
     - world = parent world ∘ local, the parent from + 0x08;
     - the root bone (+ 0x18) or a bone without a parent takes its local as world;
     - before the loop, the root's local is set from her placement (0x142FCFC80–0x142FCFE04, when + 0xF4 and + 0xEF);
     - the translation's 4th float is set to the constant 1.0 (0x142FCFF7D, 0x142FD0247);
     - with matrices (+ 0x138 not 0): matrix = world ∘ inverse bind as 3 rows (0x142FD018F, 0x142FD04E6).
     - After the loop: 0x142FD8660 on the root's world.
     - **Correction (2026-11-08, live, read only, Faith):** the root's entry in the world pose isn't the frame its
       children are built on.
       - Its stored rotation is a quarter turn about up from its local rotation: local (0, −0.718, 0, 0.696), world
         (0, −0.016, 0, 1.000).
       - Its children (Hips, CameraBase, Connect, Trajectory) are built on its local rotation. With the stored one,
         Hips came out 10.6 cm off.
       - Chaining the local poses down from bone 0's world gave every bone's world pose to within 2 mm, all but that
         one entry's rotation.
       - **[inferred]** 0x142FD8660 rewrites that entry after the loop.
       - Built on the stored entry, the editor's bone dots came out turned a quarter turn about her feet, and its pose
         check never matched (seen in game).
   - **So bone scale never reaches the drawn mesh.** The rotation comes from quaternions only and the 4th float is
     forced to 1. That matches the live finding (her world 4th float 1.0, matrix rows of length 1.0000;
     Research_Faith_Size §5b).
   - Every bone's parent has a lower index in all 12 character skeletons [data], so one pass in index order is right.
6. **0x142FCCB70** is the same work done in one go: the copy (0x142FD7C60), 0x142FD9D50, then 0x142FD77E0. It starts
   the two jobs by name (0x142FCCE75, 0x142FCCF2D) [decompile].
7. **The tools' camera hook runs after all of that, on the game thread.** Live: the game had written Faith's world pose
   and matrices anew before every camera hook [live, earlier: Research_Faith_Size §5c].
   - What the tools write there is what's drawn. Sizing her world pose and matrices there sized her drawn body
     [live, earlier].
8. **The renderer:**
   - A skinned draw's vertex shader reads its bones from `t0 instanceVectorBuffer`: the instance's header rows, then 3
     rows per palette bone [live, earlier: ReplayGameDraws.cpp:36–43, ReplayGameDraws.h:114–130].
   - The palette is the mesh section's + 0x44: a u16 skeleton bone per palette entry, count at + 0x41 [live, earlier:
     ReplayShapes SectionBones].
   - **[unknown]** Where page + 0x10 is copied into that buffer. It happens after the camera hook (point 7).

#### 2.3 The open point: does step 1 run while time is frozen?
- Step 1 (the override) needs request + 0x80 and the slot's pose update.
- The pose update is switched on by 0x1432EAD70 when the body's per-distance interval fires (0x1432E98D0) [decompile,
  earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes 2026-10-24].
- The frame's world pose is rebuilt every frame (2.2 point 7), faster than the 30 Hz ticks. **[unknown]** whether step 1
  also runs every frame, or only on a tick, and so whether it runs at all with *Freeze time* (no ticks; Research_GameSpeed).
- The replay can't tell us: it stands still while frozen (`SetPlaySpeed` 0; Research_Combined).

### 3. Overriding the pose

#### 3.1 The override (the way to use)
- **Layout:** + 0x00 bone buffer (0x20 a listed bone, the local layout), + 0x08 list (vector of skeleton bones held),
  \+ 0x10 map (per skeleton bone, its place in the buffer, −1 for none), + 0x18 weight, + 0x1C count, + 0x20 handle.
  - The vectors are {allocator 0x142364F80, data, count, capacity}.
  - [live + decompile, earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes §15; FaithReplay.cpp:239–257; decompile: job + 0x130 … + 0x150 as above]
- **Registering:** write the slot's handle into + 0x20 and the override's address into page + 0x30 [slot]. That's what
  0x142FCEE50 does for the ghosts; FaithReplay.cpp:307 does the same.
- **Releasing:** the game clears it itself when it releases a slot (0x142FD8420) [decompile, earlier].
- **Any subset of bones works.** The ghosts list 23; Faith's size override listed bone 1 only, and its scale reached
  her local pose [live, earlier: Research_Faith_Size §5b].
  - Bones not listed keep their animation. So "pose one arm, the rest keeps moving" is possible.
- **One weight for all listed bones.** There's no per-bone weight [decompile: one float, job + 0x148].
- **Two buffers in turn.**
  - The job copies the override's 0x28-byte header but reads its bone buffer while it runs [decompile: 0x142FCF70B reads
    the bones' pointer, then the loop reads through it].
  - So the bone buffer being read mustn't be rewritten during the frame's jobs.
  - The replay fills one buffer while the other is registered, and swaps each frame at the camera hook
    (OverrideSet, FaithReplay.cpp:259–304). The editor would do the same.
- **The 4th float must be 1.0** (or the bone's own scale).
  - It becomes the bone's scale whatever the weight, and the game never puts it back. Her hair stayed small after the
    size override went [live, earlier: Research_Faith_Size §5b].
  - It isn't drawn (2.2 point 5), but the hair cloth reads it [decompile, earlier: §6.5].

#### 3.2 Which bones to hold
- **Never bones 0 – 3** (Reference, AITrajectory, Trajectory, TrajectoryEnd).
  - Bone 1 is where the character is. Its world is her placement, not parent × local (2.2 point 5; the replay's learnt
    hierarchies list bones 1 and 2 without a parent [log]).
  - **A body the game animates takes its client entity along with its pose's root.** Parked KrugerSec went 10 km down
    with their bodies and stayed under the map [live, earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes].
  - So posing in place means leaving 0 – 3 to the game. The posed body then stands where the character stands, and
    follows it if it moves.
- **Faith's camera bones (178 CameraBase, 179 CameraJoint) stay hers on her box pose.**
  - With them moved, the level took the player to be where the replayed Faith was, and KrugerSec went after that place
    [live, earlier: FaithReplay.cpp:87–96].
- **Hold Hips (bone 4) and every bone below it, and nothing else.**
  - On every human skeleton Hips is bone 4. The only bones outside its branch are 0 – 3, CameraBase / CameraJoint,
    Connect / ConnectEnd, and on the male and female_heels skeletons bone 161 (BlendshapeDriver / FacePosesAnimation)
    [data]. Those stay the game's on the body as well as on the box pose.
  - The branch includes the face bones (Jaw, lips, eyelids, eyes). They're ordinary bones of the skeleton [data], with a
    place in the local pose like any other.
  - The replay's recorded-pose check found 0 of 159 bones off [log, earlier: Research_Replay_Screens_Cloth_Face §8].
    Being 159 of a 162-bone skeleton, they include the face bones **[inferred]**.
  - **[inferred]** The override wins over Ant's facial animation, as over every other Ant writer (2.2 point 1).
- **Moving the whole body:** the Hips' translation (bone 4) moves everything below it.

#### 3.3 Other writers of a character's bones
| Writer | When | Effect on an override |
|---|---|---|
| Ant's graph, IK nodes, foot / hand plant scene ops, IK rig, particle IK, physics pose, facial | inside Ant, before the pose job [inferred, 2.2 point 1] | The override replaces their result for the bones it lists, with weight 1. The replay's playback shows the recorded pose. No report of IK fighting it was found in the notes read for this research. **Not specifically checked for feet on uneven ground.** |
| **Hair / hoodie cloth** (EA SimpleCloth, jobs eacloth*) | its own jobs; it reads her pose before the camera hook | It builds its anchors from her **local** pose records (0x142FA45D0 for Faith) or her world pose (0x142FA42C0) [decompile, earlier: §6.5]. Both are made from what the override wrote. So **the hair follows a posed head** [inferred]. It did follow the override's scale on bone 1 [live, earlier: §5b]. Whether the cloth simulates while time is frozen is **[unknown]**. If it doesn't, hair stays where it was when the head is turned while frozen. |
| Ragdoll of a taken-down KrugerSec | the game stops animating that body ("always update" off, 0x143981A80) | Something writes its world pose and matrices each frame [live, earlier]. The writer wasn't found. The override isn't taken: four bodies with the override in their slot didn't move [live, earlier], and the body update gate skips the pose job for such bodies [decompile, earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes, 2026-10-24 ghost system section]. |
| Replay | while it plays | It registers its own override on Faith and on the people it plays. **One override per slot**: the editor must step aside while the replay is busy (`m_Replay.IsBusy()`), as Faith's size did. |
| Dash ghost runners | each time their pose listener is called | The ghost player component's listener registers its override again each time (0x14394D6B0 → 0x142FCEE50) [decompile, earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes §15]. Ghosts can't be posed. |
| The tools' Faith size | switched off now | If it comes back, it uses the same override slot. |

#### 3.4 Pausing while posing
- **Freeze time** (`GameTimeSettings.TimeScale` = 0) stops every simulation tick: gameplay, AI, physics and animation
  [decompile, earlier: Research_GameSpeed]. It's the natural way to hold a whole scene, so KrugerSec don't walk off or
  shoot.
  - Whether the override is still applied then is the open point in 2.3.
- **Game speed 0.05x** (1.5 ticks a second) is the existing fallback if the override needs ticks.
- **Per character, without freezing:**
  - Holding one KrugerSec's AI wasn't found. The server brain's per-frame update slot isn't traced
    (Research_KSec_Systems).
  - With time running, a posed KrugerSec keeps its AI. It walks (the pose slides with its root), aims and fights, and its
    gun is a separate actor (3.5).
- **Faith:** *Freeze Faith* already stops the game's input from moving her (CameraManager.cpp:7248).

#### 3.5 What a pose doesn't carry along
- **KrugerSec's guns.**
  - A gun is its own actor (`PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity`) with its own 26-bone body at + 0x100; its bone 1 is where
    the gun is. The game updates it every frame [live, earlier: FaithReplay.cpp:1932–1937].
  - **[unknown]** Whether a held gun follows the *posed* hand or the animated one ("not known", Research_AI_Replay §2).
    If it follows the animation, a posed KrugerSec's gun floats where the hand would have been.
- **The culling box.** Faith's comes from her box pose's bones; the editor poses that too (3.2). An NPC's box is made by
  0x14391C700 from its box bones.
  - A pose that reaches far outside it could be culled at the screen's edge [inferred].
  - util::hooks::SetCullBox exists for that (the replay uses it).
- **Bone scale:** not drawn (2.2 point 5).

### 4. Bone identity
- The skeletons, from the game's data [data]. Each `SkeletonAsset` has BoneNames, Hierarchy (parents), LocalPose and
  ModelPose. The reflected fields: BoneNames + 0x18, BoneNameHashes + 0x20, Hierarchy + 0x28, LocalPose + 0x30, ModelPose
  \+ 0x38 (classfields, size 0x68).

| Skeleton | Bones | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| characters/skeletons/skeleton_faith | 182 | Faith (masterske_faith) |
| skeleton_enemy | 163 | KrugerSec (masterske_enemy → skeleton_enemy; the KSec dump) |
| skeleton_male | 162 | men |
| skeleton_female_heels | 162 | women in heels; same parents as male; only bone 161 is named differently (BlendshapeDriver / FacePosesAnimation) |
| skeleton_female | 169 | women; male's bones without BlendshapeDriver (male's last, 161), plus ponyTail_ROOT, ponyTail_01–05 and LeftAnkle / RightAnkle |
| skeleton_enemy_balc | 83 | low-detail KrugerSec |
| skeleton_male_balc = female_balc = female_heels_balc | 82 | low-detail people (identical lists) |
| skeleton_pedestrian | 28 | crowds (masterske_crowd) |
| skeleton_drone | 49 | drones (masterdronesecurity_ske) |
| skeleton_kumabear01 | 47 | the bear mascot |

- **The replay's 162 / 169 / 163-bone people are these.** The bone counts the replay logs match [log].
- **The data settles the replay's hierarchy ties.** The replay's learnt ties, e.g. 45 (44 46), are between two possible
  parents that sit at the same place: Head (44) and Face (46) have the same bind place in the male skeleton, 1.651 m up
  [data]. The data gives the right ones: 45 HeadEnd < 44 Head, 46 Face < 44, 47 Jaw < 46.
- **Key bones:**

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hips | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| Neck / Head / HeadEnd | 50 / 52 / 53 | 42 / 44 / 45 | 42 / 44 / 45 | 42 / 44 / 45 |
| Jaw | 55 | 47 | 47 | 47 |
| LeftHand / RightHand | 15 / 123 | 15 / 112 | 15 / 112 | 15 / 118 |

- The full lists (index, name, parent) are in the appendix.
- **For the build:** ship these tables, made from the data. At run time, pick a table by bone count and check it against
  the live parent array (manager + 0xF0, 2.1).
  - Reading BoneNames live from the character's SkeletonAsset would also work, but the path from a character to its
    asset wasn't traced.
    - The ghost setup finds its manager with 0x142FC2A30([character + 0x368] + 0x148, …, data + 0x80)
      [decompile, earlier: MEC_Reverse_Notes §14].
    - 0x142FC2A30 passes its third argument through 0x142FC5240 to the manager map 0x142FC3770 [decompile].
- **Mirroring:** the names pair as Left… / Right… on every skeleton above but the drone (Arm1/2/3).

### 5. Interaction: what exists to build on
- **Projection:** LightManager.cpp:301 `ToScreen`: a world point to pixels, Panini-aware, from the main render view
  (`ReadMainView`, GameRenderer + 0x58: + 0x40 transform, + 0x360 projection). CameraManager::ProjectToScreen does the
  same.
- **Dragging:** LightManager.cpp:327 `DragPlace`. Newton steps on ToScreen put a point under the cursor across the
  picture, along the ground, or up and down.
- **Dots, handles, undo:** the Lights tab has draggable dots (F5), an aim handle, Ctrl+wheel radius and Undo. The camera
  path has orbit dots, arch diamonds and a right-click popup. All of it is drawn with ImGui draw lists.
- **ImGui is 1.61 WIP** (imgui.h:24), with no gizmo library. A rotation gizmo would be the tools' own: three rings around
  the selected bone, drawn from ToScreen points, with the angle swept along a ring as the rotation.
- **Bone dots:** each bone's world place is in the world pose (page + 0x08), read at the camera hook. Picking means the
  nearest projected bone within a few pixels.
- **Threads:**
  - The camera hook (`hCameraUpdate` → `CameraManager::OnCameraUpdate`) runs on the game thread once a frame, after the
    pose jobs (2.2 point 7). The replay runs there (CameraManager.cpp:4417).
  - The menu is drawn at Present.
  - So the menu changes the editor's pose under a lock, and the camera hook copies it into the override buffer that isn't
    registered, then swaps.

### 6. Recommended design, and what the first build would contain

#### 6.1 How it works
- **Take:** copy the target's local pose (page + 0x00 slot) as the editor's pose.
- **Hold:** an override listing Hips and the bones below it (3.2), weight 1, 4th float 1.0, two buffers swapped each
  frame at the camera hook. Faith also gets it on her box pose (the same bones, so not 178 / 179).
- **Edit:** each bone is a rotation in its parent's frame, the taken rotation times the turn made in the editor. The Hips
  also have a translation.
  - On-screen turns are about world axes: local = parent world⁻¹ × turn × parent world × local. The parent world comes
    from the editor's own pose and the chain of the game's local poses from bone 0. Not from the world pose's entry for
    bone 1: see the correction in 2.2 point 5.
- **Release:** take the override out of the slot. The game's animation is back the next frame.
- **Every frame:** find the slot again (same entity, manager, handle and bone count). If it changed, or the entity went,
  drop the target and log it. All game reads go in `__try`.

#### 6.2 The first build (GAME > Pose, or a POSE tab)
1. **Target list:** Faith, plus the characters within 30 m of the camera whose bodies the game animates.
   - Each one labelled by skeleton (Faith / KrugerSec / man / woman) and distance.
   - Characters it can't pose are listed greyed out with the reason: not animated by the game, replay busy, slot held by
     another override.
2. **Take pose / Release / Release all.**
3. **Bone tree** from the data's hierarchy with names, a search box and the face folded.
   - Selected bone: X / Y / Z degree sliders in its parent's frame, relative to the taken pose.
   - Hips: translation sliders.
   - Reset bone / branch / all. Mirror left ↔ right. Undo (Ctrl+Z, as in the Lights tab).
4. **On screen** (with the free camera):
   - the target's bone dots, and click to select;
   - three rotation rings on the selected bone, drag to turn;
   - the selected bone's name next to it.
5. **Save / Load** in `Cinematic Tools\Poses\<name>.txt`.
   - By bone name, so a pose loads onto any skeleton with the same names (Faith → KrugerSec covers the body bones).
   - Each bone's local rotation, plus the Hips translation.
   - Apply a pose to another character.
6. **Self-checks in the log:**
   - the code bytes it relies on, with the PE timestamp: 0x142FCF62D, 0x142FCFA5A, 0x142FD7D7A, as Faith's size did;
   - **every second, whether the game took the override**: the world pose of the edited bones against the editor's
     pose, with time running and with *Freeze time* (settles 2.3);
   - a KrugerSec's gun bone 1 against its posed Wep_Root (settles 3.5);
   - slot changes and targets lost.

#### 6.3 Later builds
- **Poses on the camera track.** Pose keyframes, each bone slerped between them, played with the track
  (TrackPlayer / CameraManager keyframes).
- **Two-bone IK handles** for hands and feet. Drag a hand dot with DragPlace and the arm solves (upper arm, forearm).
- **Bodies the game doesn't animate:**
  - alive but far: the replay's ForceBodyUpdate (only for bodies the distance switch turned off; never dead ones, see 8);
  - taken down: the replay's direct writes (DrawBody, HoldBodyUpdate, SetCullBox, entity rows). These have the most
    history of problems.
- **Drones,** once a live read shows whether they have an Ant body.
- **A whole crowd swarm's shared pose**, through its two `AntAnimatableEntity`s. **[inferred, not tried]**: every member
  showing that pose slice would change. Low value.

#### 6.4 Shared files
- Camera/PoseEditor.cpp / .h would be new.
- Shared edits: one call in CameraManager::OnCameraUpdate, the menu entry, Main.cpp init, the vcxproj and filters, and
  CHANGELOG.md.
- The override helpers (OverrideSet, RegisterOverride, SlotOf) are in FaithReplay.cpp, the replay's file. The editor
  would have its own copy, or they could move to a shared header.

### 7. If the override isn't taken while frozen: the fallback
- **Write the target's world pose and matrices at the camera hook** from the editor's pose: world composed in index order
  with the live parents (manager + 0xF0), matrices = world ∘ inverse bind.
  - The inverse bind is manager + 0xA0, or worked out from the live slot the way the replay's ReadUnbind does
    (FaithReplay.cpp:1396).
- **Proven to draw** for Faith's body (by the tools' Faith size) [live, earlier].
- **What it misses:**
  - **The hair and hoodie cloth.** They read her local pose and run before the hook, so they'd stay on the animated head
    (2.2, 3.3). Faith's size met exactly this.
  - Her box pose, unless that's written the same way.
- So the fallback is for frozen shots of bodies without cloth, or with the hair hidden. The override stays the main way.

### 8. Risks
- **Crashes to avoid** (all seen before):
  - **Switching "always update" on for a dead or reset body** crashed the game in an animation job [live, earlier:
    FaithReplay.cpp:927–931, Hooks.cpp:6822–6826]:
    - 0x142CF7ABB reading a freed list, six dead bodies;
    - a body that came back from a respawn switched off.

    The editor only poses bodies the game already animates.
  - **Characters going away:** the AI's unspawn, a level unload, a respawn. The slot is released and the override entry
    cleared by the game (0x142FD8420). The editor checks its entity every frame (the replay's StillCharacter) and never
    writes to a gone slot.
  - **A slot held by someone else** (replay, ghosts): never overwritten.
- **Threads:** the override's bone buffer is read on Ant's job threads during the frame. Two buffers, written only at
  the camera hook, as the replay has done for weeks. The menu's edits go through a lock.
- **Moving the root moves the entity** (3.2): never hold bones 0 – 3. For Faith's box pose, never 178 / 179.
- **The 4th float sticks** (3.1): always write 1.0.
- **With time running,** posed KrugerSec keep their AI. They slide with their root and may shoot, and their guns may not
  follow (3.5). *Freeze time* is the intended way to pose people.
- **What can't be done (with what's known):**
  - one crowd member alone;
  - bone scale on the drawn mesh through the game's path;
  - ghost runners;
  - KrugerSec's AI held per person;
  - Faith's first-person camera following a posed head (it's on CameraJoint, under bone 1, not the head).

### 9. Open questions
1. **Is the override applied while *Freeze time* is on?** (2.3)
2. **Does a KrugerSec's held gun follow the posed hand?** (3.5)
3. **Does the hair cloth simulate while frozen?** (3.3)
4. **Do drones have an Ant body at + 0x100?** One read-only live read.
5. **Foot and hand IK:** do any of Ant's plant scene ops act after the pose job? Not traced. A posed foot on a slope
   would show it.
6. **Where page + 0x10 goes into the instance buffer** (2.2 point 8). Not needed for the editor.

### 10. Tools used (read-only)
- `run.py` runs the shared tools (dfn, dis, callers, classfields, fieldsby, vt_of) without their folder shadowing
  Python's own `dis`;
- `ripfast.py`: rip-relative references by a numpy scan;
- `skeletons.py`: every SkeletonAsset's names and parents into `skel\*.tsv`;
- `f_142FCFC30.txt`, `f_142FD9D50.txt`: the disassemblies.
- Shared: the decrypted game image and its tools, fb\ (cas, ebx, patched), GridNode's annotations.

### Appendix: the skeletons' bones (index:name<parent), from the game's data

Made by skeletons.py from the SkeletonAssets' BoneNames and Hierarchy. A parent of -1 is none. skeleton_male_balc's list is also female_balc's and female_heels_balc's (identical); skeleton_female_heels is skeleton_male's with bone 161 named FacePosesAnimation.

### 11. The first build (2026-11-08)

- **The first build, as section 6.2 planned, with these differences:**
  - **Mirror left ↔ right is left out.** Mirroring a bone's turn needs its rest frame, which wasn't checked.
  - **Undo is a button** (as in the Lights tab), not Ctrl+Z.
  - **Drones are listed only if they turn out to have a body.** The log says once how many near the camera have one.
- **What it reports:**
  - "Pose: holding …" in the log when a pose is taken.
  - Every 10 s in the log: "the game took the pose in N of M frames with time running, N of M with time frozen"
    (open question 1).
  - In the menu: "Its gun: N cm from where the posed hand holds it" (question 2).
  - "Pose: N drones … with an Ant body" in the log (question 4).

### 12. Bone dots a quarter turn off, and the fix (2026-11-08)

- **Why [live, read only]:** the editor built the held bones from the world pose's entry for bone 1. Its rotation is a
  quarter turn from the frame the game builds Hips and the other children of bone 1 on (2.2 point 5, the correction).
  - So the dots and the rings' frames were turned 90° about her feet.
  - The check failed on Hips every frame.
  - Whether the game took the pose wasn't measured correctly at all.
- **The fix:**
  - Each bone's world pose is the chain of the game's local poses from bone 0 (the held bones from the pose). The dots,
    the rings, the parent frames of the turns and the check all use it.
  - The rings turn about the bone's own axes by default ("Rings on the bone's own axes"; unticked, the world's).

### 13. Whether the game takes the pose while frozen

- **Open question 1 is answered: the game takes the pose with Freeze time on [log].**
  - Faith, frozen: taken in every frame, the most a held bone was off 0.0 cm.
  - A woman, with time running: taken in every frame while the pose stayed the same, and in most while it changed (the
    most off 0.8 cm). The check compares this frame's world pose with the pose handed the frame before, so a changing
    pose misses some frames.
- Still open: questions 2 (guns), 3 (hair while frozen), 4 (drones), 5 (foot / hand IK after the pose job).

### 14. Dragging a bone

Goal: grab a bone with the mouse and move it anywhere.
- **The drag:** press on a dot, then drag it.
  - The target is the point under the cursor on the plane across the picture through the bone. It's found by Newton
    steps on the same projection the dots use (LightManager's DragPlace way), so the Panini view works too.
  - The mouse wheel moves that plane nearer or farther.
- **The solve:** each frame, from the pose as it was pressed in.
  - **Hips:** the whole body moves (the held root's translation in bone 1's chain frame).
  - **1 bone:** the bone above it turns to point at the target.
  - **2 bones (default):** a two-bone solve. The joint's new place is in the plane of the target line and the joint's
    old bend direction, so the elbow or knee keeps its side. Then each of the two bones turns the shortest way onto
    it.
  - **3 – 4 bones:** cyclic coordinate descent, 16 passes, or until within 1 mm.
  - No joint limits: a knee can be pulled backwards with 1, 3 or 4 bones.
- **The solve's results (offline, the C++'s formulas):**
  - Reachable targets are hit exactly, and the bend side never flips.
  - An out-of-reach target gets the limb at full reach on the line to it.
  - A world turn applied through the parent frame turns the child exactly.

### 15. The face in groups [not verified in game]

Goal: a tick that groups most facial bones (cheeks, mouth, eyes etc.).
- **The face bones [data]:** the same 57 in skeleton_faith, _enemy, _male and _female, under Face (54 on Faith, 46 on
  the others). The lower lip and the low cheeks hang from Jaw; the rest of the face's from Face.
- **The groups, by name:**
  - Eyes (2), Upper eyelids (2), Lower eyelids (4, with the eyelid creases), Eyebrows (10), Upper lip (3), Lower lip (3),
    Mouth corners (2), Cheeks (10, with the nose-to-mouth creases), Nose (4).
  - Single: Face, Jaw, Tongue (TongueTip under it) and Chin.
  - Going with their group: the inner lips, the irises, and the mouth's inner corners and middle creases.
- **A group's edit:** each member gets the same turn (in its parent's frame, about its own place) and the same move.
  - A ring turns each member by the same world turn.
  - A drag moves each member by the same world offset.
  - No left/right mirroring: a sideways move sends both mouth corners the same way.
- **Face bones are moved, not bent.** A dragged face bone changes its own translation (each bone now has a move in its
  parent's frame, at most 0.15 m; the Hips' 2 m), since bending the head and neck for a lip makes no sense.
- **Whether the game draws a face bone's moved translation** isn't proven, only expected: the override carries
  translation like rotation (0x142FCF620 blends both), and the face skin is skinned to those bones.

### 16. Faith's hair while paused

Goal: Faith's hair keeps moving while the game is paused.

**Why it stops [decompiled offline from the game image, PE 0x5762E3B7]:**
- Freeze time writes 0 to the time scale (GameTimeSettings + 0x48). The game's 30 Hz sim ticks and physics steps stop.
- Every cloth is stepped from the physics step. EAClothSimUpdater (vtable 0x141AB68D8, made by 0x142F9A2D0) slot 3
  is 0x142FA2720. On a step's last substep (record + 0x2C == + 0x30) it hands the cloth manager ([0x1423DCA90]) and
  the step record to the scheduler 0x142FA3A10.
- **The scheduler (0x142FA3A10):**
  - It handles the manager's add and remove lists (0x142FA0A90, 0x142FA0BE0).
  - It runs the pre-update over the list (job 0x142FA06C0, "eaclothPreUpdateJob"; the leftovers inline). Each cloth
    gets 0x142FA2760 (instance, record): its root's matrix from its pose provider (slot 0x68) into + 0xD0 (the one
    before at + 0x110) and the root's speed into + 0x150 over (record + 0x30 + 1) x record + 0x10. Then + 0x18D is
    set from provider slots 0x20 / 0x48.
  - It sets the LOD from the activation points (0x142FA0D20) and switches LOD (0x142FA29F0).
  - If the cloth settings ([0x1423DCCA8] + 0x2E) are on, it copies the record (64 bytes) into manager + 0xA0 and the
    count and list into + 0x94 / + 0x98. It then schedules the sim job 0x142FA07A0 ("eaclothSimJob") on manager +
    0x90, with its sync at + 0xE0. It doesn't wait for it.
- **The sim job (0x142FA07A0)**, on a record { + 0 next batch (lock xadd, 4 cloths a batch), + 4 count, + 8 list,
  \+ 0x10 the step record }. Its time is ([+ 0x40] + 1) x [+ 0x20]. For each cloth:
  - 0x142FA5020: the palette from her pose (FaithSize.cpp's research: from her local pose, through 0x142FA45D0).
  - At LOD 0 and + 0x18B clear: a reset first if + 0x18A is set (0x143B787A0), then the world's collision
    (0x142F9FA80), then the EA step 0x143B7C5A0 (simulation, time). At LOD 1 it's a reset only.
  - The result goes to the drawn mesh (+ 0xA8, 0x1430503C0), or 0x142FA57A0.
- **Each frame, time frozen or not:** EAClothUpdater (vtable 0x141AB6838, slot 14 = 0x142FA26B0, its pass 2)
  interpolates the last two steps (0x142FA1960 -> job 0x142FA0600 -> 0x142FA28F0). It schedules after the sim sync
  (+ 0xE0) and keeps its own sync at + 0xF8. It moves no particle. So a head posed while frozen left her hair where it
  was.
- **The EA step keeps its last step's time** (0x143B7C5A0: [simulation + 0xE0] handed to 0x143B7C5F0 with the new
  time, then the new time stored there). A step of another length than the last is the EA code's own case, so the
  tools can step at their own rate.
- A sync handle is done when [+ 8] is 0 or [[+ 8] + 8] != [+ 0x10] (0x142FBAB50, reads only).

**What the tools do: PausedHair.cpp/.h, GAME > Pose > "Her hair moves while paused"** (ticked by default, not saved):
- **When it runs:** while time is frozen (the tools' Freeze time), every frame on the game's thread, from
  pose_editor::Update. Once at least 1/60 s of real time has passed since its last step (at most 1/30 s a step), it
  steps.
- **Which cloths:** Faith's cloths, found as CameraManager.cpp's hair code finds them: her customization component's
  ClothEntities (vtable 0x141AD2998) + 0x68, each checked to be an EA cloth instance (vtable 0x141AB6380). Each must
  be in the manager's list, at LOD 0 with + 0x18B clear: the cloths the game itself would step.
- **Never with the game's own cloth jobs running:** if the sim sync (+ 0xE0) or the interpolation's (+ 0xF8) isn't
  done, the step waits for the next frame. The tools never wait on a job.
- **The step is the game's:**
  - 0x142FA2760 for each cloth, then 0x142FA07A0 on the tools' own job record listing her cloths only.
  - The step record is a copy of the manager's last (+ 0xA0), with + 0x10 = the step's time and + 0x2C / + 0x30 = 0.
    Only + 0x10 and + 0x30 are read on these paths: 0x142FA2760 and the job; 0x142FA53A0 hands it to 0x142FA34F0,
    which doesn't read it.
  - Not run: the add and remove lists, the LOD (kept from the last real step), the scheduler's + 0x18D (provider
    state, unchanged while frozen).
- **Checked at the first frozen frame:** 13 pieces of the game's code byte for byte. These are the updater slot with
  the manager's global, the pre-update and its record reads, the sim job and its list and LOD reads, the done check,
  the settings' global and + 0x2E, the record copy, the job's count and list, both sync handles and the EA step. If one
  differs, the tick does nothing and the log says which.
- **Faults:** each step runs under SEH. A fault switches it off until the game restarts (logged).
- **Log:** "Paused hair: stepping N cloth(s) of Faith's ... the EA step's time before / now" once per change of
  count. Every 10 s while frozen: steps and skips (cloth jobs running, not at full detail, not listed). On unfreezing:
  the totals.

**Not known:**
- Whether her hair visibly follows a head posed while frozen. Her palette is made from her local pose, and with time
  frozen the game takes the pose override (section 13). So it should.
- Whether her pose page is ever mid-write by the game's pose job when the camera hook steps. If it is, the anchors
  would be off for one step.
- How often the game's cloth jobs are still running at the camera hook (the "skipped" count in the log).
- How the hair looks at 60 steps a second. The game steps it 30 times a second at 1x.
- The interpolation's blend stays where it was at freezing, so the drawn hair sits between the last two steps by that
  same amount.
- **Seen in game:** the game's last step before freezing was 1/30 s, and the tools' steps are taken, with no skips of
  either kind and no fault. Unfreezing stops them. Whether the hair looks right isn't known yet.

### 17. Weapons going with the posed hands

Goal: a baton or gun a KrugerSec holds moves with its posed bones.

**Read live** (targeted reads of 2 posed KrugerSec and the 4 weapon entities in the instance lists). Time was frozen
and both were posed.

- **Batons and guns are the same class.** Each is a `PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity` (vtable 0x141C39980). Each has
  its owner at + 0x120, its data at + 0x30, and the data's Mesh at + 0x90 (MeshAsset name at + 0x10). The level had 2
  `cpf_shotgun_Mesh` and 2 `cpf_baton_Mesh`.
- **A weapon's pose (26 bones):**
  - Bone 0 is the identity.
  - Bone 1's local pose is the entity's transform. Its rotation as XMMatrixRotationQuaternion's rows equals the
    entity's rows, checked row by row.
  - Bone 1's world pose has the same place, but its rotation is turned. The body's placement rows (body + 0x50) are
    that turned rotation.
  - Bone 2's world pose is bone 1's local pose, as on a character.
- **Where they were:**
  - Shotgun: 0.336 m from its owner's posed Wep_Root. Its nearest bones were the right forearm's (0.20 m).
  - Baton: 1.034 m from its owner's posed Wep_Root. Its nearest bones were the right thigh's (0.18 m), probably where
    the unposed hand hung.
  - So the game doesn't move them with the posed hand. Which hand it does use wasn't read.
- **Their bodies (animatable + 0x70):**
  - The shotgun's had + 0xB8 = 1 (placement on), + 0xC0 = 0 (no physics part), + 0x90 = 1.
  - The baton's had + 0xB8 = 0, + 0x90 = 0.
  - 0x1432E06B0 returns false at + 0xB8 = 0, so the placement hook only reaches the shotgun.

**What the tools do:**
- **At Take pose:** each weapon is put on the grip (Wep_Root) if within 0.25 m, else on the nearest held body bone
  within 0.4 m (no face, finger or helper bones), else left alone. Two offsets are kept in that bone's frame: its
  local bone 1 and its world bone 1, from the game's world pose then.
- **Each handed frame:**
  - Local offset -> the entity's rows (the rows' 4th floats kept) -> MoveActorDrawn. The physics and queued flags
    are off for the call. The entity is held in the pose's own list (PoseHoldActor), so the game's own setTransform
    calls for it are dropped.
  - World offset -> PlaceBody.
  - Once a second: the gap between where the pose has it and its local bone 1 now. It's in the menu and logged every
    10 s.
- **Let go:** on release, replay busy, override refused, unticked, or not the character's any more.

**Not known:**
- Whether, with time frozen, the game rebuilds a weapon's pose from its moved entity.
- Whether the shotgun's turned world bone 1 comes out right from the placement rows.

### 18. Why the weapons didn't follow, and the tools drawing them

Goal: weapons that move with the posed hands or on their own (with section 17's way they didn't, seen in game), and no
±2 m limit on the Hips' move.

**Live** (targeted read-only reads; time frozen; one KrugerSec, its cpf_baton and the baton's body):
- The entity was at the posed grip (0.000 m).
- Local bone 1, world bones 1 – 3 and the 3x4 matrices (page + 0x10, 48 bytes a bone) agreed with each other, but
  stood 14.5 cm away, where the baton was before. They didn't change over 1 s.
- The weapon manager: + 0x8C 0x340, + 0x90 0x4E0, + 0x98 0x4E0, + 0x2B9 = 1.

**Offline:**
- **No game code carries a moved weapon entity into its body.**
  - ActorEntityData.MoveAnimatableWithActor (+ 0x98) is read by ClientActorEntity slot 75 (0x142D4AB50). It hands the
    rows to slot 76 (0x142D4A9A0: a placement request on the body).
  - PamClientCharacterWeaponEntity (vtable 0x141C33FE0) has slot 76 = 0x142A1C590 (ret 0). The replay's note "bone 1
    of its local pose is set to the entity's transform" holds for drones, not weapons.
  - A weapon's own update (0x143901F10) places its body from the entity at weapon + 0x130 (contents unknown), not from
    itself. The setTransform change handler (slot 28) never reaches the body.
  - 0x141C39980 is PamCharacterWeaponEntityData's vtable, not the entity's. Section 17 had it wrong.
- **In game, the weapon never followed.** Time was frozen before the pose was taken, and the gaps only changed with
  the pose's edits.
- **The page's step buffers.** + 0x18 and + 0x20 are Ant's last two pose steps, in the local layout (0x30 a bone:
  scale, rotation, translation; bone 1 is local bone 1).
  - The render-side entry at [page + 0x40] + slot x 0x20 is {from, to, factor, on}, pointing at those two buffers.
    This was read live on Faith; an older note had taken it for separate world-space buffers.
  - The world pose and the matrices are built from the local pose only (0x142FCFC30).
  - A skinned draw takes the matrices (Faith's size; the replay's DrawBody). Weapons are skinned meshes.
- **Holding a body's update is unsafe.** With a pose slot, the update job queues the held body (0x142FD1B00) onto the
  not-updated list (0x142FD1CD0). Nothing found puts it back.
- **With time running, the game rebuilds the steps.** On a frame with request + 0x80 set, the pose job copies Ant's
  output (with the override applied, 0x142FCF620) over the "to" step, blends, and rebuilds local, world and matrices.
  Whether a weapon's job runs before or after the camera hook isn't known.

**What the tools do:**
- Each held weapon's body is drawn by the tools at the camera hook. It's a rigid move of a kept snapshot: local bone 1,
  bone 1 of both steps, and the world pose and matrices of bones 1 – n. The body update is not held.
- The snapshot is taken afresh whenever the game rebuilt the buffers since the tools' last write.
- The weapon body also gets the game's own pose override (bone 1, weight 1, two buffers in turn), so a pose job of the
  game's rebuilds it in the same place.
- The entity is moved, with the game's own moves held back.
- Let-go puts back what was kept only into a weapon checked that frame, and only if time didn't run meanwhile.
- **Weapon handles.** Weapons have squares on the picture (drag; rings), their own section in the menu (goes with a bone
  or is put down; Turn, Move, Reset), and Undo.
- **The Hips' move: up to 100 km** (was 2 m; a finite cap so nothing overflows).
- **Defects found and fixed:** let-go into a freed weapon, a late Rows0, a stale put-back, the frozen weapon animation,
  a dropped weapon brought back by Undo, stale log lines, and typed text carried to the next pick.

**Not known:**
- Whether the drawn weapon follows. In the replay, guns' slot matrices were found 1.2 km from where they were drawn;
  the world pose is written too.
- The weapon's culling box.
- Whether a game job writes a weapon's buffers after the camera hook.
- **Later, seen in game:** the guns work with the pose, with no problems found.

### 19. Idle movement over a pose

Goal: a tick that brings back her micro movements (idle animation) over a pose.

**Where the animation still is [offline, 2026-11-09; f_142FCF620.txt]:**
- The game blends a pose override in 0x142FCF620. Its only call is in the pose job, at 0x142FCC9A7: rdx = the item,
  r8 = a map struct, r9 passed on, rcx unused. It takes no stack arguments.
- It returns at once if item + 0x150 (the handle) is -1 or item + 0xA0 (the records) is 0.
- For n < item + 0x14C, it takes bone = [item + 0x158][n] and rec = [r8 + 0x20][bone]. It reads Ant's record at
  [item + 0xA0] + rec x 0x30: rotation at + 0x10, translation at + 0x20, scale at + 0x00. It blends that with the
  override's bone ([item + 0x130] + n x 0x20) by the weight (item + 0x148) and writes the result through r15.
- The blend is in place. r15 is the same records: step 2 copies [item + 0xA0] into the step afterwards, and the local
  pose is made from them. This is inferred from the job's code; a first draft had said "elsewhere".
- So at the blend's entry, the records are Ant's output for that frame, under the pose. With time running Ant
  rewrites them before each pose job; whether it does while frozen isn't known. A guard skips a capture whose records
  equal the override's bones (the tools' own pose read back).

**What the tools do:**
- **The hook** (`util::hooks::CreateGameHook`, made the first time the tick is used). It is made only after 8 pieces of
  the function and its call are checked byte for byte. It copies, inside a seqlock, the records of held poses that want
  it: their override bone buffer is item + 0x130, and the body's slot is item + 0x150 (Faith's box pose shares the
  buffers).
  - A generation number per wanting keeps an earlier pose's capture, in the same held slot, from being used.
- **On the game thread:**
  - Each held bone's animation is smoothed over 3 s (an EMA per bone, its reference taken from its first good record).
  - The movement about that (a turn in the bone's own frame, then a move in its parent's) is scaled by Amount and
    capped at 15 degrees and 8 cm.
  - It's laid over the handed locals by a weight that fades in and out in 0.4 s. The weight is 0 when: the tick is
    off, no capture came for 0.5 s, any body bone (not face, finger, eye or helper) is more than 10 degrees off its
    smoothed animation, or the character's root moves faster than 0.3 m/s.
- **Defects found and fixed:**
  - a stale capture after a re-take in the same slot;
  - one reference flag per pose instead of per bone;
  - a shiver at step rate on walking characters;
  - a pop on untick.
  The in-place blend gave the read-back guard.

**Not known:** how it looks, and whether Ant writes the records while frozen (it doesn't matter there: the animation
doesn't advance).

### 20. Free-moved bones staying moved after Let go

Goal: free-moved bones go back to their original position after Let go.

**Why [offline, from section 19's reading of the blend]:**
- The blend writes the pose into Ant's own records, in place. Ant rewrites only the channels it animates.
- A channel it doesn't animate keeps the last value the blend wrote after the override goes. That's most bones'
  translations, and some face and helper bones' rotations. So the bone stays where the pose put it, and the next Take
  pose starts there. The size override's scale behaved the same (Research_Faith_Size).
- Idle movement made it worse on those channels. Its capture took the tools' own previous value as the game's
  animation, so the movement fed on itself.
- A first fix (the override at weight 0 for a few frames while the hook puts channels back) was replaced.

**How the pose job fills the blend's arguments [offline, 2026-11-09; f_142FCC7C0.txt, rev_f_142FD7C60.txt]:**
- The item is on the pose job's stack (rbp - 0x70). 0x142FD7C60 copies the slot's own data into item + 0 - 0xEF
  (the records pointer at + 0xA0). The override, if the slot has one, goes into + 0x130 - 0x157.
- With no override, + 0x130 stays null and + 0x150 stays -1, as the caller set them (0x142FCC935, 0x142FCC981). The
  blend is still called (0x142FCC9A7) and returns at once.
- The map is at rsp + 0x40 (0x142FCC8EF):
  - + 0 the manager;
  - + 0x20 the bone -> record map ([manager + 0xB0]);
  - + 0x2C the bones ([manager + 8]);
  - + 0x30 [manager + 0x88]. Step 2 copies the records by that count (0x142FCCB05: count x 0x30 bytes), so it's the
    record count.
- Step 1 ran 30 times a second with time running, fewer times than frames were drawn [log].
- **[live, read-only, 2026-11-09]** Faith's body slot object + 0xA0 stayed the same over 3 s of samples.

**What the tools do (PoseEditor.cpp, BlendWatch):**
- The hook is made at Take pose, after 13 pieces of code are checked (the 8 before, plus the map fill, the item's
  override part and the item fill).
- For each slot (the body; Faith's box pose), the hook keeps per held bone:
  - **Seen:** the record as the slot's last pass left it (copied after the game's blend, on every pass of the slot).
  - **Game:** the game's own latest value. First the record just before the pose's first blend, then any channel that
    changed since Seen at a pass's start.
- A pass of the slot without the tools' override is known by the item's records pointer and the map's manager, learnt
  at the tools' passes.
- **While the override is out** (Let go, stepped aside for a replay, the slot holding another override): at each pass,
  each channel still bit for bit as Seen is put back as in Game, before the game's blend.
- **Let go** takes the overrides out at once. The pose stays listed as being let go (not editable, can't be taken
  again) until each slot it was blended into has had such a pass. The box counts only while it's still the same box.
  - It waits while AnimatedByGame isn't 1, and the menu says so.
  - A dead body (util::hooks::IsBodyDead) is let go at once, as posed.
  - With the game animating it and no pass in 3 s, it's let go as posed, logged.
  - Let go of all ends a waiting one at once.
- **Idle movement:** the capture marks each bone's rotation and translation that is still as Seen. UpdateIdle gives
  those no movement and leaves their reference alone. A pass where the game wrote nothing is no capture. That replaces
  the read-back guard, which compared with the current override instead of with what the last pass left. The capture
  copies the game's memory into a scratch before its seqlock opens.
- The game thread waits for the hook to be out of a watch before it reuses or frees it (Busy / On, seq_cst).

**Defects found and fixed:**
- the timer wrapping round in Let go's first frame;
- giving up after 3 s on a body the game wasn't updating;
- the capture's seqlock left open by a fault;
- the "blended" flag cleared for a moment on every pass (a Let go then skipped the put back);
- a waiting pose that was hidden and couldn't be ended.

What's put back changed from the Take-time value to the game's latest value. It makes little difference with time
running, because the blend runs at the game's tick. It matters when time ran and was then frozen.

**Not known:**
- How it looks.
- Whether the game updates a body with no override while time is frozen. If not, Let go while frozen gives up after
  3 s, and the log says so.
- Whether bones left moved before this fix come back on a level reload.
- The weapons' own override (a gun body's bone 1) isn't covered. Whether the game animates that bone, and so whether a
  gun moved by hand stays there after Let go, isn't known.
